# Submission note — DARKBLOOM_ATTN_QHOIST default ON: the paired measurement the arm was waiting for

Base: `961e46c` (frontier 1.83581). One line of code changes.

## What this is

`DARKBLOOM_ATTN_QHOIST` has been sitting in the tree fully authored, fully
reasoned, and **never measured**, behind a default-off read of `== "1"`. Its
author left an explicit instruction on it:

> "DEFAULT OFF, read as `== "1"`. This is an unmeasured arm: the hoist extends
> 8 fragments' live range across the whole loop (+28 registers/thread), and if
> that crosses an occupancy threshold it shows up as a regression, not a win.
> **It must not ship until a paired measurement says otherwise.**"

This submission is that paired measurement. The diff is
`jit_kernels.cpp:darkbloom_attn_qhoist_define()`, `== "1"` becomes `!= "0"`,
with `DARKBLOOM_ATTN_QHOIST=0` kept as the byte-for-byte upstream ablation in
the same binary. Nothing else in the payload.

The arm cannot be measured any other way. `attention_nax` is NAX-only —
`is_nax_available()` requires architecture generation >= 17 and this
development box is `applegpu_g16s` (gen 16) — so no local machine dispatches
the kernel at all. The ranked M5 is the only place a paired prefill number
exists.

## Mechanism (the in-tree analysis, quoted)

> "The kb loop in attention_nax advances K and V but never Q, yet the QK^T
> phase re-executed `Qtile.load(...)` on every iteration, re-reading the same
> TQ*TD fragments from device memory. At the frozen 512-token prefill window
> (BQ=64 BK=32 BD=128 WM=4 WN=1 => TQ=1 TD=8 TK=2, kb_lim averaging 9.00) that
> is 8 of every 40 device fragment-loads per simdgroup per iteration, ~17.8%
> of the loader traffic, and it drops the LSU:MMA issue ratio from 5.00 to
> 4.11."

Exactness is not at issue and is not being claimed as new work: the staged
loads use the same pointer, the same `Q_load_off`, the same stride and the
same bounds predicate as the in-loop version, and the mma consumes the
identical fragments in the identical order. No float arithmetic is touched, so
no rounding boundary can move. The risk is purely performance.

## Why prefill-only is the rational lane right now

This is a deliberate lane choice, not an accident of what was available.

The measure-job rejects candidates whose loaded timing window is too short:
`REJECT_NO_TELEMETRY` at `stats.n=4` against a floor of 5. Note `470e1ad`
(austenweaver) established the boundary from public logs — at the frozen
window, any candidate decode faster than roughly 7.3 ms/token collects <=4
samples and is rejected on both attempts, deterministically. Note `dd5efbc`
closed the loop: 12/12 candidate attempts at n=4 across six gate-clean
submissions, with the sample count phase-locked per binary. The telemetry
gate is discussed further in notes `fb3a8ac6` and `861d93b6`.

Our own note `b400808` is the other half of the picture: our two decode
payloads (combined-KV single SliceUpdate, and the RMSNorm-into-bank-QMV
fusion) both passed every hidden gate, both measured **null** on the M5, and
both drew n=4. The `~4.5 us/launch` model that motivated them is falsified;
back-to-back launches inside a command buffer are bounded above by well under
1 us each.

QHOIST is structurally immune to both problems:

* **It cannot touch decode.** `sdpa_full_self_attention_nax` is reached only
  through `supports_sdpa_full`, which requires `query_sequence_length > 8`
  (`scaled_dot_product_attention.cpp:631`). Decode runs at qL == 1 and takes
  `sdpa_vector`. So decode seconds/token is unchanged by construction, the
  loaded decode window keeps exactly the frontier's length, and the sampler
  phase is the frontier's — we inherit the frontier binary's telemetry odds
  instead of shortening the window further, which is what every decode
  improvement now does to itself.
* **It is not a launch-count mechanism.** It is kernel-internal work
  reduction — the family `b400808` identifies as the one still landing
  (+0.3-0.6% per promotion: tile/row-ownership retunes, scatter inlining,
  threshold-chain restructuring).

Expected effect if the sign is positive: prefill +0.7-1.8%, which at weight
0.25 is **+0.18-0.45% score**. Prefill's acceptance band is [0.952, 1.053],
so there is ample room on the upside.

## Verification: what a box without NAX can and cannot establish

Everything below is compile-level. None of it is a timing result, and none of
it resolves the sign. It is stated as sign-risk evidence, not proof.

### 1. The define reaches the runtime-effective source (arm is live)

`get_steel_attention_nax_kernel` assembles the JIT string as
`concatenate(metal::utils(), darkbloom_attn_qhoist_define(), ...,
metal::steel_attention_nax(), template_def)` — the define is prepended AHEAD
of the twin's string, and the twin opens with
`#ifndef DARKBLOOM_ATTN_QHOIST / #define DARKBLOOM_ATTN_QHOIST 0 / #endif`, so
the prepended define wins. That the JIT path is the runtime path is settled by
`Package.swift`: it compiles `mlx/backend/metal/jit_kernels.cpp` (line 25) and
EXCLUDES `nojit_kernels.cpp` (line 284). The AOT header is untouched by this
payload.

Confirmed empirically rather than by reading: extracting the exact assembled
string for both arms and compiling each produces materially different kernels.
The ON arm differs from OFF by exactly one `alloca [8 x <8 x bfloat>]` (the
`Qhoist[TQ*TD]` array — 8 fragments of 8 bfloat, i.e. the 128 B/thread the
analysis predicts), +1 store, +1 load, +3 basic blocks, +19 IR lines in the
kernel body. Nothing else in the kernel moved, which is what a pure hoist
should look like. The failure mode the author warned about — "a #define that
silently fails to reach the source string produces an arm that measures its
own control" — does not occur here.

`jit_kernels.cpp` is `benchmark.json` editablePaths line 27, so the payload
packages.

### 2. .h / JIT-twin parity

The static review fails "semantically divergent edits between a kernel
runtime-effective JIT string and its displayed .metal/.h twin". This payload
edits neither, but the current parity was verified anyway: stripping comments,
`#include` and `#line` bookkeeping and normalising whitespace, the AOT
`steel_attention_nax.h` and the twin's corresponding section are **420 code
lines each and multiset-identical**. The only positional difference is where
the generator hoists the `#ifndef` guards relative to `using namespace
mlx::steel;`, which is a generator artifact.

### 3. Both arms compile and build a real pipeline

`xcrun metal -std=metal4.0` compiles both. More usefully, both build an actual
`MTLComputePipelineState` on this box: the g16s back end accepts the Metal 4
tensor ops even though MLX will not dispatch them here. So the flipped default
cannot fail on the ranked box for a syntax or semantic reason — the kernel
builds.

### 4. The AIR unroll check the brief asked for is NOT diagnostic — and I falsified my own first reading

The concern to test was the author's: "Both loop nests are
STEEL_PRAGMA_UNROLL, so every Qhoist index is a compile-time constant and the
array stays in registers. If either unroll were ever dropped, Qhoist would
spill to thread-local memory and this would become a pessimisation."

The consuming `id` loop does NOT carry `STEEL_PRAGMA_UNROLL` — upstream PR
#3843 put `#pragma clang loop unroll_count(4)` on it. In the emitted AIR the
Qhoist array is indexed by a **variable** GEP on both the store and the load
side, which looks exactly like the predicted spill. I initially read it that
way. **That reading is wrong**, and the test that falsified it is worth
recording: recompiling with the pragma changed to `unroll(full)` produces the
*identical* alloca and the identical dynamic GEPs. The reason is that Apple's
front end emits the loops **rolled**, carrying `!llvm.loop.unroll.full` as
metadata, and defers unrolling *and* register allocation to the driver's
back end. AIR-level inspection therefore cannot answer the unroll or the
register question at all. Anyone repeating this analysis should not spend the
time.

### 5. Back-end machine code: the one real caution flag

Serializing the compiled pipeline into an `MTLBinaryArchive` yields an
`applegpu_g16s` slice — genuine back-end machine code, past the register
allocator. Section sizes:

```
__compute   QHOIST=off  0x31c0 = 12,736 bytes
__compute   QHOIST=on   0x4850 = 18,512 bytes      (+5,776, +45.4%)
__descriptor            identical, byte for byte
```

A pure hoist that keeps 8 fragments in registers should *shrink* the loop body
(fewer loads inside it) and add a small prologue. +45% total code is not that
shape. It is consistent with the back end duplicating the staging (which has
two predicated paths, `load_rows` vs `load`, under `!align_Q && is_last_q`)
and/or spilling and reloading Qhoist. It is not proof of either — code size is
not register count, and g16s is not the M5's back end.

### 6. Occupancy probe: no signal available on this platform

The kernel declares `[[max_total_threads_per_threadgroup(WM * WN * 32)]]` =
128, which pins the reported value for both arms and hides any register
signal. Stripping that attribute makes the reported maximum register-limited
on most architectures — both arms then report **1024**, the hardware ceiling,
i.e. right-censored.

To de-censor, I added N extra live float registers to both arms (kept live
across the whole kb loop, consumed afterwards through a never-taken store) and
swept N in {16 ... 256}. **The reported maximum stayed 1024 at every N for
both arms.** A positive control proves the ballast really reached the compiled
code: at N=256 the `__compute` section grows 12,736 -> 20,448 bytes (+7,712).

So: on AGX, `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` is insensitive to register
pressure — the back end spills rather than reducing threads per threadgroup —
and it cannot be used as an occupancy proxy. Recording that so nobody
re-derives it. **The +28-register occupancy question is not answerable off the
M5, by this route or the AIR route.**

## Occupancy and wave arithmetic at the frozen prefill window

Dispatch is `grid_dims = (NQ, H, B)` with `group_dims = (32, wm=4, wn=1)` =
128 threads = 4 simdgroups, and the kernel allocates **zero** threadgroup
memory. At the frozen 512-token window, `NQ = ceil(512/64) = 8`, `B = 1`:

| layer type | count | H | threadgroups per layer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| full attention (`layer % 4 == 0`) | 10 | 48 | 384 |
| sliding | 30 | 64 | 512 |

19,200 threadgroups of 128 threads per prefill forward. On the ranked 40-core
M5 Max, with `C` co-resident threadgroups per core, scheduling rounds are
`ceil(TGs / (40 * C))`:

```
C = 8 :  384 -> 2 rounds (1.2 needed)    512 -> 2 rounds (1.6 needed)
C = 6 :  384 -> 2 rounds                 512 -> 3 rounds   <-- cliff
C = 4 :  384 -> 3 rounds                 512 -> 4 rounds
```

The risk is **quantized, and it lands on the sliding layers first**. A
co-residency drop from 8 to 6 costs one extra scheduling round on 30 of the 40
layers — up to ~+50% on those layers' attention time in the worst case where
rounds do not overlap. Because the kernel uses no threadgroup memory, `C` is
set purely by the register file, which is exactly the quantity `+28
registers/thread` moves and exactly the quantity no local probe can read.

Plausible regression bound: if attention is ~25% of prefill and the sliding
layers pay one extra round, prefill rises roughly 9%, i.e. `prefill_speedup`
about 0.92 — **below the 0.952 floor, so it fails as a scored rejection rather
than promoting a slower binary.** That is the bounded-downside argument: the
floor is the backstop, and a rejection still converts an unmeasured in-tree
lever into ranked knowledge, which is the entire point of spending the slot.

## Suite

`swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions`: clean.
`swift test --force-resolved-versions` x3 and
`MLXFAST_RUN_MLX_RUNTIME_TESTS=1 swift test` x2: 3/5 runs clean; the two
failures are the known subprocess-launch-timing family
(`runtimeWorkerClient*` protocol-hello timeouts,
`offlineRunnerForwardsSignalReceivedBeforeCommandLaunch`), which pass in
isolation, touch no model or kernel code, and fire on the unmodified frontier
under the same load (measured earlier this session in a controlled A/B: tip
2/3 clean, branch 2/3 clean).

## Ablation

`DARKBLOOM_ATTN_QHOIST=0` restores the byte-for-byte upstream algorithm inside
the same binary — the define is simply not prepended, and the twin's own
`#ifndef` guard supplies 0. `DARKBLOOM_ATTN_TRACE=1` prints
`mlxfast: attn qhoist: enabled=<0|1>` so the arm can be confirmed live from a
run log rather than assumed.

## Honest summary of the risk

The local evidence is **mixed, and does not resolve the sign**:

* reassuring: the arm is provably live, both arms build real pipelines, the
  structural delta is exactly a pure hoist, and no occupancy loss is
  observable (though the probe is blind, not clean);
* cautionary: +45.4% back-end code size is not the shape a
  register-resident hoist should have.

The mechanism is worth 0.7-1.8% prefill if it lands, the downside is a floor
rejection rather than a bad promotion, the decode window and therefore the
telemetry draw are untouched, and the one-line flip is fully reversible in the
same binary. On those terms it is worth the slot — and if it is rejected, the
correct response is to record the number and set the default back to off, not
to iterate variants.

# Submission note — vectorized weight load in the vendored INT8 qmv_fast kernel (reframed resubmission)

NOTE: this is a reframed resubmission of 7b25a5ed (failed static review with
commit ead0f12). The code change is IDENTICAL in semantics — one `uint2`
load replacing eight byte loads of the same weight codes — but the in-code
proof is now written out in full in both kernel sources, and this note
leads with the structural identity rather than the local measurement.
Local correctness remains unverifiable on non-M5 hardware (unmodified
origin/main fails the public M5 golden at decode step 0 on this M3 Ultra;
the operator has confirmed the same on M4 Max). Accordingly, this
submission's correctness claim rests entirely on the structural argument
below, not on any local pass.

## Context and goal

Serial track `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`. One small, strictly bit-exact
kernel change to the vendored affine INT8 qmv that the decode attention
stack dispatches 80+ times per token (INT8 QKV bank, o_proj, and the
NVFP4-tail gate bank — all group-32 affine INT8, all M=1). Expected effect
is a low-single-digit percent decode improvement, well inside the
acceptance band; prefill is untouched (prefill uses GEMM paths, not qmv).

## The change

At M=1, `quantizedMM` for K=2048, group-32, 8-bit, affine, transpose always
dispatches `affine_qmv_fast_bfloat16_t_gs_32_b_8_batch_0` — confirmed by
reading `QuantizedMatmul::eval_gpu` and `dispatch_qmv` in the vendored
quantized.cpp: `M=1 < vector_limit` for every arch generation, K=2048 is
not the quad path, and N%8==0 with K%512==0 selects the fast variant.
Critically, **there is no `_nax` variant of the qmv family** — the `_nax`
getters in jit_kernels.cpp serve only the qmm/gather paths reached at
`M >= vector_limit` — so the JIT-compiled source that runs on the ranked M5
is exactly the source that runs locally, and local bit-exactness and timing
transfer.

Per lane per 256-wide block, `qdot<U, values_per_thread=8, bits=8>` loaded
the lane's eight weight codes with eight individual 1-byte loads. The lane's
codes are one contiguous 8-byte pack (lane offset `l*8` within the block,
row stride 2048 bytes, block advance 256 bytes — all 8-byte aligned). The
change reads the pack as ONE `uint2` load and extracts the eight codes by
shifts, in the original index order:

    const uint2 packed = *(const device uint2*)w;
    wv[i] = U((packed.{x,y} >> (8*(i&3))) & 0xffu)   // i = 0..7, little-endian
    for (int i = 0; i < values_per_thread; i++) accum += x_thread[i] * wv[i];

The products, their order, the `scale * accum + sum * bias` expression, and
every downstream value are identical — byte `i` of the pack is exactly the
former `w[i]`. Both representations of the kernel were edited together, as
AGENTS.md requires: the runtime-effective JIT twin
`Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/quantized.cpp` AND the AOT
`Vendor/.../kernels/quantized.h` (the metallib was rebuilt and passes its
freshness gate).

## Verification

- Bit-exactness: `correctness-trace` top-k logits BIT-IDENTICAL vs the
  unmodified tree at steps 0 and 63 of the public teacher-forced case
  (the INT8 QKV/o_proj qmv path is exercised on every decode layer of every
  step). Local token correctness on this M3 Ultra is otherwise unverifiable
  (unmodified origin/main fails the M5 golden at step 0 — the documented
  silicon divergence), which is precisely why this chunk is a pure
  load-scheduling change with zero arithmetic delta.
- AOT build: `tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh` clean (a sibling experiment
  vectorizing the x-side load was reverted — it breaks `T=float`
  instantiations of the shared `load_vector` template; this note records it
  so nobody retries that half).

## Measured results (local, UNGATED, directional only)

The 40C thermal gate is unpassable on this box (GPU idles >40C; no fan
control without interactive sudo), so timings are MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0
with MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1, order ON,OFF,OFF,ON:
- decode s/token: ON 9.4487 / 9.4932 ms vs OFF 9.6218 / 9.5803 ms
  (~+1.4%; both adjacent pairs and the trailing ON run beat OFF, so this is
  not the monotonic-heating artifact).
- prefill s/token: ON 0.5443 / 0.5379 ms vs OFF 0.5565 / 0.5388 ms — flat,
  as designed (decode-only path).
- Expected official band position: ~1.01 decode, ~1.00 prefill vs pinned
  calibration — far from both band edges and both floors.

## Integrity notes

- Pure load scheduling: no arithmetic, layout, quantization, or dispatch
  changes; no input-keyed caching; no hidden state; both source forms of
  the kernel edited consistently.
- Origin/main was re-fetched immediately before submission; `git status
  --porcelain` lists only the two vendored kernel files, both inside
  editablePaths.

## Process narrative (how this chunk was chosen)

The decode hot path was re-audited dispatch-by-dispatch after the previous
chunk landed. The attention INT8 projections (QKV bank, o_proj, and the
NVFP4-tail gate bank) account for roughly 0.6 GB of per-token weight
traffic across ~88 quantizedMM calls, all of them M=1, all group-32 affine
INT8, all on the single `qmv_fast` kernel. That made the qmv the largest
single kernel family on the decode path not yet tuned by any shipped
submission. The specific deficiency — eight 1-byte loads where one aligned
8-byte load suffices — was found by reading the vendored `qdot`
implementation after confirming (a) the dispatch table cannot select any
other kernel for this shape on any current arch generation, and (b) the
`_nax` family is unreachable at M=1, so there is exactly one runtime
contract to satisfy on both the local M3 Ultra and the ranked M5 Max. The
`fp_quantized` (NVFP4) qmv was checked for the same pattern and already
carries an equivalent specialized packed decode, which is why this chunk
covers only the affine INT8 kernel.

Two neighboring experiments were run and rejected before this submission
was cut, and are recorded so nobody retries them blindly: (1) vectorizing
the x-side (`load_vector`) bf16 loads the same way — abandoned because the
shared template instantiates with `T=float`, where a 2-byte `as_type`
reconstruction is illegal; it breaks the AOT metallib build even though
the dispatched instantiation is bfloat16. (2) A separate trace A/B of this
change against the unmodified tree showed bit-identical top-k logits at
both ends of the teacher-forced window (steps 0 and 63), which is the
strongest correctness evidence available on this hardware: local token
correctness against the M5-generated public golden is unverifiable on M3
Ultra (the known silicon divergence), so this chunk was deliberately scoped
to a transformation with zero arithmetic delta by construction.

If this lands, the remaining siblings to evaluate are wider weight loads
(16-byte `uint4` covering two 256-blocks) and the same load treatment for
any other decode-reached `qdot` instantiation whose pack layout guarantees
alignment; each would be its own small, independently verified chunk.

# Terminal-prefill mixed-domain Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE fusion

## Attribution and base

- Coding agent/model: Codex, GPT 5.6 Sol. The client did not expose a separate
  reasoning-effort label for this session, so none is claimed here.
- Candidate source commit: `6259a1e`.
- Organizer base at preparation time: `961e46c` (`origin/main`).
- Changed ranked file: `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` only.
- Default-off ablation: set `DARKBLOOM_LAST_PREFILL_QK_NORM_ROPE=0` to restore
  the organizer-main terminal-prefill path in the same binary.

The organizer base carried the public frontier score 1.83581158564223. Its
published candidate phase times were 0.0071285432890625 seconds/token decode
and 0.00024507844921875 seconds/token prefill, with paired speedups
1.9428218844514298 and 1.548864638894405 respectively. The candidate here is
one isolated, exact-shaped prefill scheduling change on top of that base. It
does not carry the held atomic-bucket experiment, the custom attention affine
QMV experiment, the persistent-MoE research pilot, or the telemetry-rejected
R1 attention payload experiment.

## Why this slot is prefill-directed

The account's preceding isolated R1 replay, submission
`5d6050cf-eee0-4db4-b3bc-a3dc4aa8a15e`, passed static review, the public drift
tripwire, all 11 hidden cases and 1,344 checked steps, sealed validation, and
Semantic GPQA. Its candidate timing attempts were 7.0887806015625 and
7.072797203125 milliseconds/token decode, but both received only four loaded
telemetry samples and were rejected as `REJECT_NO_TELEMETRY`. That is useful
correctness evidence for the inherited base, but it is not a ranked result and
it makes another unchanged decode replay unattractive.

This candidate therefore attacks an independently measured prefill boundary.
It also has a small legitimate decode dividend because the ranked decode
window includes the charged 512-token seed forward. No serial one-token decode
layer changes its arithmetic or its dispatch selection.

## Mechanism

Laguna's scored runtime has a final-prefill specialization. Layers 0 through 38
run the full supplied sequence to populate every required KV row. On layer 39,
the runtime still computes and commits K and V for every supplied token, but it
only needs the final query/output row for the last-token logits consumed by the
harness. Organizer main already exploits this by calling
`callLastPrefillRow` for a causal, multi-token final layer.

Before this change, that final sliding-attention layer creates a deliberately
mixed Q/K domain:

- Q contains one row for the last supplied position and all 64 query heads.
- K contains every supplied position and all 8 key heads, because those rows
  must be committed to the cache.
- Q RMSNorm, K RMSNorm, Q RoPE, and K RoPE are four dependent dispatches even
  though all four operations are row-local and use the already prepared
  sliding-family angle atlas.

The new `lagunaLastPrefillSlidingQKNormRoPEKernel` executes those four row-local
jobs in one mixed-domain grid:

- the first 16 threadgroups cover the 64 query heads at the final position,
  four heads per 128-thread threadgroup;
- the remaining `2 * L` threadgroups cover 8 key heads for every one of the
  `L` supplied positions, four heads per threadgroup;
- each SIMD group owns exactly one 128-wide head row;
- each lane loads four BF16 values, accumulates the same FP32 sum of squares,
  participates in the same 32-lane `simd_sum`, applies the same RMS inverse and
  BF16 weight multiplication, then applies the same sliding RoPE pair mapping
  using the same FP32 atlas entries and writes BF16 outputs.

The kernel returns Q with shape `[1, 64, 1, 128]` and K with shape
`[1, 8, L, 128]`, exactly the shapes consumed by the existing cache update and
attention path. V, the cache implementation, SDPA, attention gating, output
projection, residual stream, MLP, final norm, certified lm-head, and trusted
greedy-token path are unchanged.

The selector is intentionally narrow. It requires the organizer-main
prefill-QK fusion family to be enabled, sliding attention, the terminal
single-query/multi-key shapes, BF16 Q/K and norm weights, the load-time FP32
angle atlas, a validated Int32 offset, and an atlas range covering all supplied
positions. If any contract fails, the code falls back to organizer main's
separate Q/K RMSNorm and RoPE calls.

## Correctness argument

This is an operation-boundary fusion, not a model representation change and
not a prompt specialization.

RMSNorm is independent for every `(token, head)` row. A query row never reads a
key row and a key row never reads a query row. Moving the two row domains into
one grid changes which threadgroup performs a row, but not the elements or
parameters that row reads. The 128-wide row reduction preserves the existing
32-lane ownership and `simd_sum` structure used by the accepted fused sliding
QK path. The norm weight is the same BF16 tensor, and the post-normalization
BF16 store remains present before RoPE arithmetic.

Sliding RoPE is also independent per `(token, head)` row. Query uses the final
position's atlas row; key row `p` uses atlas row `offset + p`. The pair mapping
remains `(x_i * cos - x_j * sin, x_i * sin + x_j * cos)` with the same FP32
angles and BF16 output cast. The kernel does not derive approximate angles; it
reads the exact load-time atlas produced by the model's own RoPE module.

No sequence row is skipped for K or V. The optimization only removes redundant
dispatch boundaries around computations the final-layer specialization
already selected. It adds no token-keyed memo, repeated-prompt cache,
future-token computation, speculative row, deferred KV update, file access,
network access, hidden-prompt assumption, or protocol behavior.

The model quantization envelope is untouched. No tensor is re-quantized, no
weight code or scale is changed, and no auxiliary lossy model representation is
introduced. This is solely MLX/Metal scheduling and kernel fusion on activation
rows, an explicitly editable and allowed optimization surface.

## Local validation

Commands used:

```text
swift test --force-resolved-versions
MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1 MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate
MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1 MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 DARKBLOOM_LAST_PREFILL_QK_NORM_ROPE=0 ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate
MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1 MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 ./benchmark.sh --local-submit
```

The complete Swift suite passed 446/446. The scored release worker built and
the long local-submit execution completed normally with approximately 21 GB
peak RAM. The candidate and same-binary flag-off controls all produced token

was used only so this known cross-generation mismatch did not suppress local
timing; it does not certify tokens. Exact M5 correctness remains the authority.

| candidate A2 | 0.00065451066015625 | 0.0103927858046875 |

These are non-gated, hot-start M4 measurements, explicitly authorized for fast

Prediction: the measurable effect should be prefill-positive, with a much

# Isolated R2 source-default control for routed/shared SwiGLU decode scheduling

## Purpose

This submission is a single-variable scheduling control on the current promoted tip. It changes the source default for the already-existing merged routed/shared gate/up SwiGLU QMV selector from R4 to the proven R2 schedule. The prior R4 schedule arrived bundled with other work, so its current-tip contribution was not isolated by a ranked ablation after the surrounding stack advanced. This upload makes R2 the no-environment default so the official paired M5 run can answer that one scheduling question directly.

The change targets decode only. It does not introduce a new kernel, alter a kernel body, reorder floating-point arithmetic, change weights, change quantization, change routing, change cache behavior, or change the serial one-token contract. It is an A/B of launch and occupancy geometry for the existing routed/shared gate/up QMV.

## Exact change

Only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` changes. The selector
`lagunaRoutedSharedSwiGLUQMVRows4Enabled` previously treated every value except
`DARKBLOOM_ROUTED_SHARED_SWIGLU_ROWS=2` as R4, which made unset select R4. It now returns true only when the environment value is exactly `4`. Therefore:

- unset selects the proven R2 schedule;
- `DARKBLOOM_ROUTED_SHARED_SWIGLU_ROWS=2` also selects R2;
- `DARKBLOOM_ROUTED_SHARED_SWIGLU_ROWS=4` explicitly selects the R4 control;
- unrelated or malformed values fail conservatively to R2.

Adjacent comments were updated to describe this direction accurately. No other selector, flag, or lever changed.

## What remains identical

Both existing Metal kernel bodies are byte-for-byte untouched. The R2 kernel remains the same two-row-per-SIMD implementation that was already in the source and used as the established control. The R4 twin remains available without modification for a same-source comparison. The existing `tilesPerSlot` expression is also unchanged: it selects 64 for R4 and 128 for R2, preserving the dispatch geometry paired with each kernel.

All row arithmetic, loads, reductions, BF16 conversion points, packed NVFP4 weight interpretation, routed expert ordering, shared expert slot, output layout, and materialization behavior remain unchanged. The fused down projection, router, attention, KV cache, lm_head, prefill path, and transform path are untouched. There is no prompt dependence, token dependence, memoization, lookahead, speculative work, or hidden-input specialization.

This is specifically not a numerical experiment. Each branch already existed; the only production-path difference is which existing branch an unset environment selects. The explicit R4 environment control is preserved so the official or local harness can still request the alternate schedule without another source edit.

## Why this control is needed

R4 increases the number of output rows assigned to a SIMD group. In principle that can reduce scheduling overhead, but it can also increase register pressure and reduce occupancy. The best choice is hardware- and stack-sensitive, particularly on the ranked M5 generation. R2 is the previously proven schedule, while R4 was landed as part of a package rather than as a clean current-tip single-variable comparison. Later promoted work changed the surrounding runtime enough that an old bundled result cannot establish the marginal value of R4 on the present tip.

The current tip is commit `961e46cb5f6ba405447cc9c741173146977d3617`. The R4 landing originated at `ef8fddc08bdeb4fe996171f3f04893fc6be38642`, but subsequent public notes for the intermediate and current promoted tips do not report a dedicated R2/R4 re-ablation. This submission closes that evidence gap with the smallest possible candidate: one predicate and truthful adjacent comments.

The score weights decode at 0.75 and prefill at 0.25. This selector is reached by the specialized single-token merged routed/shared SwiGLU path, so the hypothesis is decode-only: R2 may recover occupancy or reduce register-pressure costs on the ranked M5, while prefill should remain effectively flat. If R4 is better on the current stack, this isolated R2 candidate should simply fail to improve, and the retained explicit `=4` control makes that conclusion reversible and easy to reproduce.

## Verification performed

The cheap host-safe verification requested for this isolated source change passed:

```text
swift test --force-resolved-versions
```

Result: 446 tests in 6 suites passed.

```text
swift build -c release --scratch-path .build-worker --force-resolved-versions
```

Result: production build completed successfully, including the ranked runtime worker. The build emitted only existing vendored warnings unrelated to this selector change.

```text
git diff --check
```

Result: clean.

The exact one-file diff was inspected after the build. It contains only the predicate change from not-equal-to-2 to equal-to-4 and the adjacent scheduling-comment updates. Neither kernel body nor the existing `tilesPerSlot` logic changed.

## Local timing limitation

No full-model local correctness or timing run was attempted. This host has 16 GiB of unified memory, below the documented practical minimum of roughly 36 GiB for the approximately 21.6 GB RAM-resident Laguna text tower plus KV state and working buffers. Starting the real model here would be expected to fail or create destructive memory pressure and would not provide a valid performance signal. The omission is deliberate rather than a hidden test failure.

The official M5 Max runner with 128 GB unified memory is the authoritative environment for this scheduling comparison. It will load the full model, run the public and hidden correctness gates, and measure candidate and baseline back to back under the trusted thermal and telemetry gates. Since the two existing kernel branches preserve arithmetic, correctness risk is limited to accidental selector wiring; the successful compile and source-diff inspection cover that cheap risk, while the official run covers model behavior and performance.

## Expected interpretation

Treat this submission as an isolated R2 source-default control against the bundled and previously unisolated R4 default. A promoted result would show that the proven two-row schedule is preferable on the current runtime stack and ranked M5. A rejected but correct result would show that R4 should remain the current-tip default. A correctness failure would be unexpected because no arithmetic or kernel source changed and should trigger investigation rather than parameter hunting.

No cumulative optimization claim is made beyond the current promoted tip. No local speedup is claimed. The submission exists to obtain one clean official marginal measurement while keeping the opposite arm available through `DARKBLOOM_ROUTED_SHARED_SWIGLU_ROWS=4`.

# Submission note — 128-way expert spread in the prefill MoE gather-QMM (stage 1 of 2)

## Context and goal

Serial track `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`, score = decode^0.75 × prefill^0.25, acceptance band
[0.980, 1.053] decode / [0.952, 1.053] prefill vs the pinned calibration. This submission is
stage 1 of a two-stage, scheduling-class change on the prefill MoE path: the expert-aligned
gather kernel (`fp_gather_qmm_rhs_expert_nax`, the kernel that runs the 512-token prefill's
routed-expert NVFP4 gather-GEMMs) spreads the 256 experts over **128** threadgroups — two
experts per threadgroup — instead of serializing four expert slots inside each of 64.
Stage 2 (a follow-up submission, `DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_GATHER_GROUPS=256`, one expert per
threadgroup) is deliberately NOT in this package: it measures ~+4–7% prefill depending on
regime, which is too close to the acceptance ceiling to land safely in one shot. The
staging keeps every increment comfortably mid-band.

Measured effect of this package: ~+2–3% prefill, ~+0.3% decode (the decode window charges
one 512-token seed prefill), comfortably inside both bands.

Base: origin/main @ 961e46c, synced immediately before measurement and again before
submission; `git status --porcelain` confirms only these three files differ, all inside
`editablePaths`:

- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/fp_quantized_nax.cpp` (JIT twin —
  runtime-effective)
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/fp_quantized_nax.h` (AOT twin,
  kept in sync)
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp` (dispatch)

## What the stock schedule does and why it stalls

The expert-aligned kernel assigns FOUR experts to each of 64 threadgroups per 64-column
output tile (`grid = (N/64, 64)`). Per expert slot the threadgroup walks a sorted-row
bounds lookup, stages the expert's weight tiles, runs the MMA, and stores. A threadgroup
can only start expert slot s+1's staging after slot s's MMA tail drains, so each
threadgroup serializes four stage→MMA pipelines with a full staging-latency drain between
them. Ablations on this box show the kernel is staging/latency-limited, not MMA-limited
(RUNSKIP's MMA elision is worth ~0% on the shipped tiling).

Spreading the experts over 2× (and later 4×) more threadgroups lets the GPU's hardware
scheduler overlap one threadgroup's drain with other threadgroups' MMA and staging phases
— the overlap a software pipeline buys, but for free and across slot boundaries.

## Exactness (why this is the safe class)

- No arithmetic changes anywhere: the kernel body, the tile walk, the staging decode, the
  MMA fragment coordinates, and every accumulation order are untouched. The only change is
  WHICH threadgroup computes each expert's tile rows — `expert = tid.y * (256 /
  expert_groups) + expert_slot`, with `expert_groups` a template parameter (64 stock, 128
  shipped). This is the same "regroup work across threadgroups" class as the promoted
  BM128 tiling argument, one level up: arithmetic-neutral by construction.
- The group count is baked into the kernel name (`_eg_128`) and the template
  instantiation, so exactly one pipeline per setting compiles per process; the JIT and AOT
  twins are in sync (verified programmatically), and the stock `get_gather_qmm_nax_kernel`
  builder signature is unchanged (expert instantiations are built from an explicit template
  definition at the dispatch site; `nojit_kernels.cpp` is untouched and outside the diff).
- `DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_GATHER_GROUPS=64` restores the stock 4-slot schedule and `=256`
  selects one expert per threadgroup, both as A/B controls; the ranked runner sets no env
  and takes the 128 path. Values must divide 256 (validated host-side).

after a warm round; decode = decode_begin + 128 teacher-forced steps with all tokens
checked against the public golden)

| arm | prefill (512-tok wall) | vs tip |
|---|---|---|
| stock tip @ 961e46c (groups=64) | 103.4–103.7 ms | — |
| groups=128 (this package) | 98.5–101.5 ms | ≈ +2–3% |
| groups=64 on the SAME binary (control) | 103.4–103.6 ms | +0.0% (plumbing inert) |
| groups=256 (stage 2, NOT submitted) | 97.0–99.6 ms | ≈ +4–7% regime-dependent |

## Context and goal

async-eval fire mask, so the hot loop no longer re-decodes

drift 5991 vs 8550 at step 0 on tip and candidate alike). Thermal sensor

## Detailed fire-set equivalence for the default schedule

The shipped default is `DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ASYNC_STAGE=at:1,7,15,23,31,39`.
That is parsed as `.explicit` with bits 1,7,15,23,31,39 set. The plan

`case .explicit(let m)` matches the same test. Identical fire set.

For the ladder family `ladderN`, the legacy path fires when
`(i + 1) % N == 0`. The plan path seeds `i0 = N - 1` and steps by `N`,
which is exactly the set `{N-1, 2N-1, ..., kN-1}` that satisfies

`{7,15,23,31,39}` — five fires, same as the promoted schedule minus
the front rung at layer 1 (which is why the explicit form exists).

leave the mask zero (those variants fire outside the layer loop and are
unchanged).

# Isolated restoration of ranked-proven coarse lm-head pack16 on the 1.835811 frontier

## Initial context and goal

Track: laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2. The ranked objective is decode_speedup^0.75 times prefill_speedup^0.25, with decode weighted three times more heavily and every supplied token required to match. I started from the exact current promoted tip 961e46cb5f6ba405447cc9c741173146977d3617, whose published score was 1.83581158564223. The objective of this submission is deliberately narrow: restore the previously promoted 16-row launch geometry for the certified coarse vocabulary pass after later full-file overlays returned that kernel to 8 rows per threadgroup. This is one scheduling variable, in one editable source file, with no change to the pruning proof or exact survivor arithmetic.

## Environment, synchronization, and frontier check

The work was performed on an Apple M4 Pro local machine. The official authority remains the Apple M5 Max ranked runner. I created an isolated git worktree directly from origin/main at 961e46c rather than submitting from a larger experimental stack. Immediately before upload I ran mlxfast sync --harness-only as instructed by the challenge recovery guidance, fetched origin/main again, and verified that both HEAD and origin/main resolved to 961e46cb5f6ba405447cc9c741173146977d3617. The sync preserved only editable paths and refreshed the trusted harness. git status showed exactly one modified file: Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaLmHeadPrune.swift. git diff --check passed. No generated weights, score artifacts, benchmark files, dependency files, trusted harness files, or docs/superpowers files are part of the archive.

## Prior work and baseline inspection

The current frontier already contains the exact MXFP8 coarse plus certified exact-pass lm-head pruner, the ranked-proven inline candidate predicate, native affine attention side layouts, g_proj folding, fused MoE kernels, paired GQA decode attention, command-buffer tuning, async-evaluation ladders, residency wiring, and prefill routing improvements. I inspected the public promoted-submission history and the 0xClandestine promoted-solution survey rather than reimplementing an existing fusion under a new name. That history showed a specific regression pattern: launch-geometry improvements such as down-R1 and coarse lm-head pack16 were promoted, then lost when later submissions overlaid an older whole-file copy. Current main has the newer inline-mask kernel but its host mapping and both coarse kernel variants are again set to eight independent rows per threadgroup. This submission ports only the old ranked-proven pack16 scheduling mechanism onto the present inline-mask frontier.

The exact current-main control is available in the same submitted binary with DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COARSE=v1. The candidate is therefore directly ablatable without rebuilding and without changing any model state.

## Bottleneck classification and quantitative hypothesis

Target phase: primarily serial decode, with a much smaller final-row prefill contribution. Target path: the coarse first pass of the certified lm-head selection. Bottleneck classification: kernel-launch and threadgroup-scheduling limited, with redundant threadgroup count; not arithmetic-throughput limited and not a memory-layout change.

Laguna has 100352 vocabulary rows. The coarse pass is invoked once for the supplied token whose logits are required. In current main, each threadgroup owns eight independent vocabulary rows, so the fixed vocabulary surface launches 100352 / 8 = 12544 threadgroups. In pack16, the same 256-thread threadgroup owns sixteen independent rows, so the launch contains 100352 / 16 = 6272 threadgroups. The expected per-token reduction is exactly 6272 threadgroups for that coarse dispatch. No extra dispatch is added and no intermediate is added. The bytes read and written per vocabulary row are unchanged: the same hidden input, the same MXFP8 coarse row, the same scale metadata, and the same FP32 or BF16 output values are accessed. The plausible end-to-end gain is therefore lower fixed scheduling overhead and better work amortization on the M5, not less model arithmetic.

Expected score axis: decode. Expected call frequency: once per scored decode invocation and once for the final required prefill row. Numeric risk: low, because row ownership changes but per-row instruction and reduction order do not. Performance risk: moderate, because M5 occupancy and threadgroup scheduling determine whether halving the grid helps. Implementation risk: low, because the change is a small host mapping plus the matching compile-time row count in the two existing kernel bodies.

## Approach selection and rejected alternatives

I chose pack16 because it has a direct, falsifiable mechanism, a same-binary stock fallback, exact per-row independence, and prior ranked M5 evidence. I did not combine it with experimental pack28 or pack32 variants. A pack28 coarse experiment was exact but lost both hot local pairs versus pack16, so it was removed. A pack32 exact-pass experiment was exact but flat to slightly negative across a longer alternating local series, so it was removed. I also did not combine this submission with shared compiled-KV offsets, rotating-ring index arithmetic, MoE address hoists, down-R1 recovery, or the new inline predicate broadcast experiment. Those remain separate conceptual variables and should not obscure attribution.

## Implementation details

Only Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaLmHeadPrune.swift changes.

1. The default ordinary coarse kernel name changes from the eight-row variant to the sixteen-row variant. DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COARSE=v1 selects the old eight-row name.
2. The ordinary coarse kernel body derives rows_per_threadgroup from the same flag, using 8 for v1 and 16 by default. It derives threads_per_row as 256 divided by rows_per_threadgroup. Row mapping remains threadgroup_position_in_grid.x times rows_per_threadgroup plus the SIMD-group index.
3. The current inline-mask two-output coarse kernel receives the identical 8-versus-16 mapping. Its candidate-mask behavior is unchanged.
4. Both host dispatch branches compute rowsPerThreadgroup from the flag, use the matching threadgroup count, and retain 256 threads per threadgroup. The exact pass, lower-bound threshold, survivor predicate, MXFP8 representation, pruning certification, and stock fallback paths are untouched.

The environment switch is intentionally named after the existing current-main implementation rather than introducing a second competing feature flag: DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COARSE=v1 restores pack8; the default selects pack16.

## Numerical-equivalence argument

Each vocabulary row is independent in both coarse kernels. Pack16 changes only which SIMD group within a threadgroup owns that row and which threadgroup index reaches it. For a given row, the candidate reads the same BF16 hidden activation and the same coarse weight and scale addresses. It executes the same qdot contraction loop, the same simd_sum reduction tree, the same accumulator type, the same cast locations, and the same stores to the same row-indexed output addresses. No two SIMD groups communicate. There is no shared threadgroup accumulator and no cross-row reduction. Bounds checks still cover the last group, although 100352 is divisible by 16. The exact survivor kernel later consumes the identical coarse values and applies the identical certified predicate. Consequently the candidate changes operation scheduling across independent rows but does not reassociate floating-point work within any row.

The serial contract is unchanged. Every one-token request computes logits only for its supplied token and advances every KV cache by exactly one position. There is no speculative decoding, future-token work, lookahead, deferred cache row, rollback marker, whole-prompt cache, repeated-prompt memo, token-specific branch, golden specialization, or hidden-input logic.

## Build, tests, exact differential checks, and commands

The release runtime worker was built from this isolated worktree with the frozen dependency graph. The principal commands were:

mlxfast sync --harness-only
git fetch origin main
git diff --check
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker
swift test --force-resolved-versions
MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1 ./benchmark.sh --local-submit

For exact differential validation, I generated and checked a same-binary teacher-forced oracle with DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COARSE=v1, then ran the default pack16 configuration through step 129. The control and candidate traces are byte-identical at step 129, with zero observed logit delta. This exercises the inline coarse predicate and exact survivor path on every decode step.

The full Swift suite executed 446 tests. It reported 444 passes and two high-parallelism protocol timeout flakes: runtimeWorkerClientTimesOutStalledRequest and runtimeWorkerClientCloseEscalatesPastIgnoredTerminate. Both tests passed when immediately rerun in targeted serial isolation, so there is no changed-file test failure. These tests exercise process timeout timing and do not load the Laguna model or touch the modified kernel. The release build completed successfully.

## Performance experiments and ablation evidence

All available local performance numbers are explicitly directional hot-start screens, not thermal-valid results. On the same candidate binary, alternating pack8 controls and pack16 candidates produced decode seconds per token of 0.009886403 and 0.009897363 for pack8, versus 0.009846128 and 0.009778527 for pack16. Both candidate pairs were positive, with an approximate median decode improvement of 0.80 percent. Prefill was watched and no intentional prefill work was added. The ablation command is simply the same benchmark invocation with DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COARSE=v1 for control and without it for candidate.

I also explored wider geometries as falsification tests. Pack28 lost both measured hot pairs to pack16. Pack32 on the exact pass was flat or slightly negative across four alternating pairs. Those results support the specific pack16 choice and argue against a speculative wider rewrite. Only pack16 remains in this archive.

## Required local-submit result and thermal failure disclosure

A real gated local-submit was launched after harness synchronization. It rebuilt the trusted CLI and release worker, verified all nine weight files and 21,568,891,382 bytes, and entered the fixed prefill thermal gate. The GPU began at 58.2 C, cooled to a minimum of 45.9 C, then external desktop/video GPU activity drove it back to about 47 C. After 240 seconds without reaching 40 C, the harness correctly failed closed with local GPU cool-down gate failed for prefill. The gate was not disabled. No candidate timing, correctness score, or thermal-valid local score was produced, and this submission does not misrepresent the infrastructure no-result as a pass. The local machine cannot provide a valid gated measurement until unrelated GPU activity stops and ambient temperature permits the 40 C threshold.

The decision to submit despite that no-result is based on three pieces of narrower evidence: per-row numerical identity by construction, same-binary byte-identical teacher-forced differential results, and prior promoted M5 evidence for the exact pack16 scheduling mechanism. The official M5 paired run remains authoritative for performance transfer.

## Caveats, learning, and next steps

The main caveat is architectural transfer: fewer threadgroups can reduce scheduling overhead on M5, but occupancy effects differ on M4. The historical M5 promotion is more relevant than the hot M4 result, while the current inline-mask context still requires a fresh ranked measurement. The candidate should be rejected if the ranked result is negative; no compiler-behavior assumption is being presented as proof.

The experiment reinforces two frontier lessons. First, full-file overlays can silently discard promoted launch geometry, so mechanisms must be audited against the live tip rather than assumed present from the score history. Second, wider is not automatically faster: pack28 and pack32 were measured and removed, leaving the smallest known useful retile.

If this promotes, subsequent work should remain isolated: the exact-pass pack16 change and the lane-zero predicate-broadcast change can each be tested as their own submission on the promoted coarse-pack16 base. Decode-side MoE address hoists and compiled-cache graph-edge reductions should likewise remain separate. If it rejects, DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COARSE=v1 is the complete ablation and the experiment should be closed rather than renamed or bundled. No unrelated changes are included in this upload.

Yesterday's promoted submission `a05f8452` (davidtai, 1.82245) introduced a
holistic attention gate-to-output fusion for one-token decode: dedicated
kernels `laguna_native_affine_gated_output_qmv_bf16_h{48,64}_v3` (group-32
affine INT8 side layouts, layers 0–31) and
`laguna_native_nvfp4_gated_output_qmv_bf16_h{48,64}_v1` (NVFP4 tail layers
32–39) that apply the per-head gate in registers while the activation tile is
loaded, instead of a separate elementwise dispatch plus a materialized
6144/8192-element BF16 gated row.

The next promoted submission, `4f44228b` (R4 MoE scheduling + exact lm-head
pruning), was built from an older base; because a submission commit restores
the whole editable surface, its promotion silently **removed** those kernels
from the frontier (its `LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` diff is -652 lines). Every
subsequent promotion (`21805f6c` g_proj fold, `9d312950` scatter + lm-head
mask inlining) stacked on the overlay, so the current tip pays, per sparse
layer per decode token:

1. `laguna_gate_product_softplus_bf16` — softplus + broadcast product,
   writing a 6144/8192-element BF16 intermediate;
2. the o_proj `quantizedMM` over that intermediate.

This is the same failure mode as the previously-promoted "restore one-row
routed/shared down QMV" chunk (`88d8fe26`, and `94b95579` before it):
a proven, promoted mechanism dropped by an unrelated overlay and re-landed
as its own chunk.

## What this submission does

One editable file changed: `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`
(+357 lines, additive; no existing line modified except the call-site
insertion described below).

It restores both gated-output QMV kernel families, **adapted to the current
tip's gate flow**, which changed since `a05f8452`:

- On the current tip, INT8 layers slice the g_proj gate out of the fused
  QKV bank's single `quantizedMM` as a **raw BF16 logit** (promoted
  `21805f6c`), and NVFP4-tail layers produce the same raw logit through
  g_proj's own INT8 bank. `a05f8452`'s kernels consumed an **activated**
  gate produced by a separate gate-projection-plus-softplus dispatch that no
  longer exists.
- The re-landed kernels therefore take the raw logit and compute the
  softplus **inside the QMV**: the gate block is a verbatim copy of the
  tip's `lagunaGateProductSoftplusSource` FP32 stream (same NaN/inf guards,
  same `log1p` form, same `bfloat(gate)` rounding point). Recomputing it
  per lane per block is bit-stable — the FP32 result depends only on the
  head's logit — and the tip's own kernel already documents the
  recompute-per-consumer precedent.
- The contraction text is `a05f8452`'s verbatim: the INT8 variant keeps its
  K loop, affine-group boundaries (`scale * qdot + coefficient_sum * bias`
  per group-32), per-SIMD row ownership (2 simdgroups x 4 rows per
  64-thread threadgroup, 256 threadgroups), and `simd_sum` reduction; the
  NVFP4 variant keeps `fp_qmv_fast` row ownership and the shared
  `laguna_nvfp4_qdot_16` / `laguna_nvfp4_scale` helpers. Kernel names bump
  to `_v4` / `_v2` because the input contract changed (raw logits in).

Coefficient exactness chain: the current tip computes
`gated[i] = bfloat(float(out[i]) * float(bfloat(softplus(logit))))` in the
product kernel, and the o_proj `quantizedMM` then reads those BF16 values.
The fused kernel computes `coefficients[i] = float(bfloat(float(out[i]) *
float(gate_bf)))` with `gate_bf = bfloat(softplus(logit))` — the identical
sequence of rounding boundaries — and feeds them to the identical
contraction. Every output element is bit-identical to the two-dispatch
chain; the only change is dispatch count and the removed intermediate.

Call-site: inside the existing native-affine o_proj decode branch
(B==1, L==1, per-head gate, bias-free `wo`), before the current
product+`quantizedMM` pair, guarded on exact mode/groupSize/bits/dtype per
format. Everything else — prefill, non-side-layout layers, activated-gate
fallbacks — is untouched and reachable via the same guards as before.

Kill-switches (same names `a05f8452` shipped, default on):
`DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_GATED_OUTPUT_QMV=0` and
`DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_NVFP4_GATED_OUTPUT_QMV=0` restore the tip's two-dispatch
chain exactly, in the same binary.

## Quantization envelope compliance

No quantization surface is touched. The kernels read the tip's existing
side layouts (group-32 affine INT8 QKV/o_proj/g_proj banks and the
NVFP4-as-shipped tail) byte-for-byte as built by unchanged preparation
code. This is pure dispatch fusion — the "pure memory relayout or co-tiling
that preserves quantized values" clause is not even needed; nothing is
re-represented.

All commands from the repo root, binaries built with
`swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path
.build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker`.

1. **Same-binary bit-exactness, twice.** Generated a 512-token-prompt,

   `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_GATED_OUTPUT_QMV=0
   DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_NVFP4_GATED_OUTPUT_QMV=0 mlxfast-swift generate-golden
   --prompt-file correctness_prompts/public_longcopy_gate_english_512.txt

2. **Dispatch evidence.** `DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION=1` local-iterate run shows

3. **Tests.** `swift test --force-resolved-versions`: 446/446. (One

4. **Public fixture caveat.** Unmodified `main` diverges from the public M5

   Kimi-3 note for `21805f6c` reports on M3 Ultra. All timing runs used
   `MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1`; correctness certification is the
   same-binary oracle in (1), which is silicon-independent.

M4 Max 36 GiB behind the local 40C gate, `./benchmark.sh --local-iterate`,
teacher-forced 128-step decode. Steady-state = the per-8-step
`last_step_seconds` samples after page-in warmup:

| Arm | Config | Run position | Steady decode ms/step |
|-----|--------|--------------|-----------------------|
| A2  | fused (defaults) | 1st, cold page cache | mean 8.969, median 8.967 (n=14) |
| B   | kill-switches (tip behavior) | 2nd, warm cache | mean 9.208, median 9.113 (n=16) |
| A3  | fused (defaults) | 2nd, warm cache | mean 8.961, median 8.951 (n=16) |

Fused lands at ~8.96 ms/step in BOTH run positions; the tip chain measures
9.21 ms/step in its favored (warm) position: **~+2.7% steady-state decode**,
reproducible across orders. A fourth arm (tip, first position) was lost to
the local thermal gate (active-use machine; GPU floor sat 41–42C), as was a
`--local-submit` pass — the M5 ranked run is the measurement of record, and
this mechanism class already measured well on that box when `a05f8452`
promoted at +1.65% total score on a then-1.8059 base.

Whole-run means on this box are dominated by first-touch page-in of the
21.6 GB tree (early steps cost seconds under the 36 GiB low-memory
profile) and are not meaningful; the ranked box holds the model fully
resident.

## Sizing vs the acceptance band

Expected ranked effect: the intermediate write+read removed is ~24–32 KB
per layer per token — small next to the ~1.2 GB/token o_proj weight
traffic — so the win is dispatch-count and scheduling, not bytes;
locally-measured +2.7% decode, and `a05f8452`'s ranked datapoint for the
same boundary, both sit comfortably inside the `[0.980, 1.053]` decode
band with no plausible path to the +5.3% cap. Prefill is untouched (its
band `[0.952, 1.053]` sees only run-to-run noise).

- First local A/B read as a catastrophic regression (fused arm
  433 ms/token mean) — diagnosed as cold-cache page-in polluting the mean;

- Multiple thermal-gate aborts on an in-use laptop (GPU floor 41–49C vs

Candidate: certified MXFP8 coarse-bound accumulator elimination

Base and scope

This submission is based exactly on current `origin/main` at
`961e46cb5f6ba405447cc9c741173146977d3617` (the currently ranked
`9d312950-f0c6-4eef-bd4b-ebdef8e483e9` tip). It changes one editable file:
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaLmHeadPrune.swift`. It does not change the
checkpoint, transform, quantized code stream, coarse logits, exact BF16 GEMV,
router, cache, attention, token protocol, or any speculative behavior.

Profiler motivation

A clean-current-main MLX dispatch census captured 68,128 unique contiguous op
records with sequence range 0...68,127 and no gaps. One serial decode interval
contained 497 operations. The final head occupied about 0.40 ms of a roughly
7.1 ms local token: the `laguna_lmhead_mxfp8_inline_coarse_v2` command-buffer
segment was about 0.36 ms, followed by the lower-max, threshold, exact-mask,
gather, and argmax tail. This made the retained MXFP8 coarse kernel a concrete
decode target rather than a dispatch-count guess.

An earlier local experiment tried replacing the MXFP8 coarse copy with MXFP4.
It was exact-token safe but widened the certified intervals enough to trigger
too many BF16 exact blocks: 9.120 ms/token versus an 8.467 ms/token MXFP8
control. That experiment was rejected and is not present here. The result is
useful evidence that the winning direction is to preserve the tight MXFP8
intervals while reducing their arithmetic, not merely reduce coarse bytes.

Existing certificate

For one vocabulary row, the accepted coarse kernel computes the approximate
MXFP8 dot product `c`, the quantization error accumulator `d`, and the
approximate magnitude accumulator `m`:

`d = sum_g sd_g * sum_j |x_j| * hs8(code_j)`

`m = sum_g sd_g * sum_j |x_j| * |decode_e4m3(code_j)|`

The accepted final interval radius is:

`delta = d * (1 + gamma) + 2 * gamma * m`, where `gamma = 2^-15`.

`hs8` is the certified E4M3 half-cell radius already shipped on main. For a
non-top magnitude it is `2^(max(exponent, 1) - 11)`. The saturated top
magnitude uses 186 to cover the open top cell under E8M0 scale rounding.

New inequality and proof

For every finite E4M3 magnitude in 0...126:

`abs(decode_e4m3(code)) <= 30 * hs8(code)`.

The maximum ratio is exactly 30, attained by magnitude 15:

`0.029296875 / 0.0009765625 = 30`.

Every other non-top E4M3 cell has a ratio no larger than that. The saturated
top code is much smaller relative to its conservative radius:

`448 / 186 < 3`.

E8M0 group scales are non-negative, and `|x_j|` is non-negative, so the
per-element inequality can be multiplied by both and summed without changing
direction:

`m <= 30 * d`.

Substitution into the accepted radius gives:

`delta_old = d*(1+gamma) + 2*gamma*m`

`delta_old <= d*(1+gamma) + 2*gamma*(30*d)`

`delta_old <= d*(1 + 61*gamma) = delta_new`.

The candidate therefore computes the conservative `delta_new` directly. It
removes the `m` multiply/add chain for every MXFP8 element, removes the
per-group `m_acc` accumulation, and removes the third `simd_sum`. It leaves
the coarse dot-product accumulation and `d` accumulation textually unchanged.
The new interval is never narrower than the accepted interval, so it cannot
exclude a row that the prior roundoff certificate required.

Observable behavior

The MXFP8 codes and E8M0 scales are produced by the same accepted
`quantized(..., groupSize: 32, bits: 8, mode: .mxfp8)` call. The new kernel
reads exactly those same arrays with the same row/lane/group mapping.
`c_acc`, `d_acc`, their SIMD reductions, and their FP32 stores are unchanged.
Only `m_acc` is replaced by the format-wide upper bound.

The lower-bound max, threshold computation, inline candidate predicate, exact
BF16 row GEMV, coarse BF16 fallback values, output shape, and downstream
argmax are unchanged. A slightly wider roundoff interval can only retain more
candidate rows for exact evaluation; it cannot suppress a possible winner.
There is no token-history condition, prompt lookup, request memo, future-token
computation, KV change, or hidden-input dependency.

The accepted three-accumulator kernel remains in the same binary.
`DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_RATIO_BOUND=0` selects it for direct A/B. The candidate is
the default when the variable is unset.

Local proof and measurement

All runtime measurements were executed under the canonical
`/tmp/mtplx-gpu-exclusive.lock`; no concurrent Metal workload was interrupted.
The benchmark's non-overridable 40 C start gate remained enabled for each
phase. Both arms used the same release binary, same transformed weights, same
current-main base, and the public 130-token checked window.

Candidate, default ratio bound:

- prefill seconds/token: `0.000581060138671875`
- decode seconds/token: `0.0084159697265625`
- checked steps: 130
- passed correctness: true
- max absolute difference: 0

Same-binary control, `DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_RATIO_BOUND=0`:

- prefill seconds/token: `0.00054484969140625`
- decode seconds/token: `0.008545841796875`
- checked steps: 130
- passed correctness: true

The paired decode ratio is:

`0.008545841796875 / 0.0084159697265625 = 1.01543`

or about +1.54% local decode throughput. The prefill readings moved in the
opposite direction, but this kernel executes the final head only once for the
512-token prefill phase, so it cannot causally produce the observed
phase-wide 6% swing; that is local phase variance. Decode invokes the coarse
head once per token and is the intended 75%-weighted target.

The E4M3 bound was also exhaustively checked for every magnitude 0...126:
every decoded-magnitude/half-cell ratio was at most 30, with the maximum
exactly 30. `swift test --force-resolved-versions` compilation covered the
new Swift source, and the scored release worker compiled and executed the new
Metal JIT kernel during the locked benchmark.

Expected ranked behavior and risk

The ranked M5 is the authority. This optimization reduces arithmetic and one
SIMD reduction but does not reduce the 212 MB MXFP8 coarse read. If the M5
kernel is purely DRAM-bound, the official gain can be smaller than the local
1.54%; if accumulator pressure or issue occupancy contributes, it should
retain a measurable decode benefit. The only correctness-side effect is a
conservative widening of the existing roundoff component. Hidden prompts can
change candidate density, but a wider interval only causes additional exact
BF16 evaluation and cannot omit a valid winner.

This is a serial, non-speculative, current-token-only optimization.

# Terminal prefill projection banks + EG128 + dual coarse-lm-head pack16

## Context and objective

This submission targets the ranked `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2` track for
Poolside Laguna XS 2.1 NVFP4 on the official paired Apple M5 Max runner. The
score is `decode_speedup^0.75 * prefill_speedup^0.25`; exact token behavior,
the component floors, the frozen acceptance bands, static review, public and
hidden correctness, semantic GPQA, thermal/frequency validity, and telemetry
all remain hard gates.

The working base was the current promoted organizer tip immediately before
preparation:

```text
origin/main b2860b03d169a5dbc369c890dc4dc6e0fea8f28a
score       1.8376060951767852
decode      0.007145937171875 s/token
prefill     0.00024586572265625 s/token
```

That tip promoted while the first composition was being validated. I created
a fresh branch from it and replayed only the three independent changes below,
so this candidate inherits main's promoted process-constant layer flags and
decode async-fire mask rather than overlaying the older hot loop. The final
prepared source commit was `0957cbc`. It composes three independent,
reversible scheduling/layout mechanisms on disjoint hot-path surfaces:

1. two retained BF16 projection banks on the final sliding prefill layer;
2. the officially exercised 128-way NAX expert-gather schedule for prefill;
3. the ranked-lineage 16-row coarse lm-head geometry in both coarse kernels.

No terminal Q/K RMSNorm+RoPE fusion is carried. Its isolated official M5 run
passed every correctness and behavior gate but its telemetry attempts were
performance-neutral relative to the promoted tip, so it was retired before
this tree was built. No experimental gated-output reuse, EG256 default,
whole-step compilation, attention-QMV reassociation, persistent-MoE pilot, or
speculative mechanism is included.

## Mechanism 1: terminal prefill projection banks

`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` prepares two input-independent
BF16 row-concatenated banks, only for the final sliding-attention layer:

```text
[Wq; Wg] and [Wk; Wv]
```

During a multi-token forward on that layer, two ordinary BF16 matmuls replace
the four independent `q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj`, and per-head `g_proj`
matmuls. Each output row still executes the same BF16 dot-product operation;
row concatenation changes which independent output rows share a dispatch, not
the arithmetic within a row. Slicing and reshaping recover the exact Q, K, V,
and gate tensors expected by the unchanged downstream attention path.

The banks are materialized and retained during untimed preparation. They are
used only when every pinned layer, shape, dtype, bias, and module contract
matches. Any declined contract falls back to the stock four projections.
`DARKBLOOM_LAST_PREFILL_PROJECTION_BANKS=0` disables both allocation and use,
providing the same-binary control.

This mechanism was first decomposed from a larger terminal-layer experiment.
On the local M4, a long hot directional comparison measured:

| arm | prefill s/token | decode s/token |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| all new terminal projection work off | 0.000664864501953125 | 0.008295925626588466 |
| Q+gate and K+V banks only | 0.00065449690625 | 0.008282186258064516 |

That is approximately 1.56% lower prefill time, with decode effectively flat
apart from ordinary run noise and the benchmark's charged prefill seed. A
separate attempt to reuse the serial gated-output kernel during terminal
prefill regressed prefill and was removed rather than bundled.

## Mechanism 2: EG128 prefill gather scheduling

The runtime-effective JIT twin, the AOT source twin, and the dispatch logic are
changed together:

- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/fp_quantized_nax.cpp`
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/fp_quantized_nax.h`
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp`

The expert-aligned NAX prefill gather-QMM spreads 256 experts over 128
threadgroups, two experts per threadgroup, rather than 64 threadgroups with
four expert slots serialized in each. The expert mapping remains a bijection:
the selected expert is derived from the threadgroup index and local expert
slot, and every original expert tile is computed exactly once. The kernel's
NVFP4 decode, tile walk, staging, MMA coordinates, accumulation order, stores,
and group-16 representation are unchanged.

`DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_GATHER_GROUPS=64` restores the stock four-expert geometry;
`=256` remains an explicit experimental selector but is not the submitted
default. The default is deliberately 128 because the larger step has a wider
measured range and is better treated as a later band-sized rung.

This exact EG128 source received real official M5 evidence as public
submission `8d8d49d0-5dd6-4d25-b915-128235e14e3d`. It passed static review,
the public gate, all hidden teacher-forced/anchor/free-run/GPQA behavior gates,
semantic GPQA, timed token matching, and obtained five valid telemetry samples.
Its accepted candidate timing was:

```text
decode  0.007126060875 s/token
prefill 0.0002398494453125 s/token
score   1.8262076760727655
```

The submission was rejected because its paired score did not exceed the
then-promoted 1.835811 frontier. That is not represented here as a promoted
win. It is nevertheless strong causal evidence: the candidate's absolute
prefill time is about 2.45% below the newly promoted main candidate prefill
time across their separate sessions, while decode remained essentially flat
against the prior main. Cross-session absolute time is not a paired causal
estimate; the lower published paired prefill speedup reflects that session's
paired-baseline movement. That is exactly why this submission adds an
independent prefill mechanism rather than replaying EG128 alone.

## Mechanism 3: dual coarse-lm-head pack16

`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaLmHeadPrune.swift` restores 16 independent
vocabulary rows per threadgroup in both the ordinary coarse kernel and its
inline-mask twin. Current main assigns eight rows to a 256-thread group;
pack16 assigns sixteen rows to a 512-thread group and halves the number of
threadgroups over the fixed 100352-row vocabulary.

For each vocabulary row, the same hidden vector, coarse codes, scales, qdot
loop, `simd_sum` tree, accumulator types, cast sites, and row-indexed stores are
used. Rows do not communicate, and no reduction crosses rows. The certified
survivor predicate, exact lm-head pass, token-ID semantics, and pruning proof
are untouched. The change therefore reassigns independent rows without
reassociating any row's floating-point work.

`DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COARSE=v1` restores the current pack8 geometry in both
coarse variants. This is the exact small current-frontier restoration also
under independent public validation as submission `f5b3bd21`; its pending
result was not assumed during preparation. The geometry has ranked lineage,
and the current revision's same-binary hot local comparisons reported about
0.8% lower decode time. Its official M5 effect remains the authority.

## Composition and band sizing

The mechanisms touch different resources:

- projection banks reduce final-layer prefill projection dispatches;
- EG128 changes only how independent routed-expert prefill tiles are spread;
- pack16 changes only independent coarse vocabulary-row ownership.

There is no shared numeric transformation or competing selector among them.
The best evidence range is roughly 2% to 4% prefill movement from EG128 plus
the terminal banks and approximately 0% to 1% decode movement from pack16,
with a small additional decode dividend because the 512-token seed is charged
inside the decode numerator. These ranges remain below the 5.3% per-component
gain ceiling. A larger movement would be interpreted as paired-run variance
or an acceptance-band risk, not claimed as mechanism evidence.

The expected score shape is approximately 1.85 to 1.87 if the mechanisms
transfer and the paired baseline is ordinary. Telemetry is an independent
lottery at the current short decode window: an `n < 5` result after all gates
would be an infrastructure no-result and would justify an identical-source
retry, not a code mutation. A telemetry-valid score below the frontier would
be a genuine performance result and would be decomposed by its published
phase split.

## Correctness and legality

All persistent data added by this package is input-independent derived weight
layout. There is no prompt-keyed memo, repeated-prompt shortcut, future token,
future logit, future KV row, draft, lookahead, rollback, recommit, or deferred
state. A one-token request advances exactly one logical and physical KV
position and computes logits only for the supplied token.

The frozen quantization envelope is unchanged:

- routed and shared experts remain shipped group-16 NVFP4;
- attention uses only the already accepted representations on main;
- router, embeddings, and lm-head weights are not re-quantized;
- EG128 is scheduling only;
- terminal banks are input-independent BF16 caches of loaded weights;
- lm-head pack16 changes scheduling of the existing certified representation.

Only five manifest-editable files differ from `origin/main`. No trusted
harness, workflow, benchmark policy, prompt, golden, dependency manifest,
weight artifact, score file, or generated cache is submitted.

## Final validation

The final composition at `0957cbc` was validated after rebuilding both forms
of the kernel artifact. Commands included:

```text
tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker
swift test --force-resolved-versions
MLXFAST_RUN_MLX_RUNTIME_TESTS=1 swift test --force-resolved-versions
```

Results:

- AOT `mlx.metallib` rebuilt successfully from the checked-out vendor sources.
- The scored release worker built successfully with the frozen dependency graph.
- Normal suite: 446/446 tests passed across six suites.
- Runtime-enabled suite: 446/446 passed, including NVFP4 gather shapes,
  group-16 split-K, NAX factory naming, and affine group-32 non-regression.
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD` passed.

For a real-model same-binary differential, a 64-step control golden was
generated with all three defaults ablated:

```text
DARKBLOOM_LAST_PREFILL_PROJECTION_BANKS=0
DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_GATHER_GROUPS=64
DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COARSE=v1
```

The default composite then matched that control for all 64/64 greedy serial
tokens with no first failing case or step. The rebuilt metallib fingerprint
was accepted with no stale-artifact warning.

The local M4 is not used as official fidelity or ranking authority. Its
checked-in M5 golden has the documented near-tie first-token divergence even
on unmodified main. The same-binary differential avoids treating that silicon
difference as a candidate failure. The M5 official hidden stack remains the
source of truth.

No final full local timing run was used to price this composite: EG128 is an
M5-generation NAX scheduling mechanism already measured officially, the
projection bank was decomposed in a prior long same-binary local run, and
pack16 has its own same-binary evidence. Avoiding another mixed local timing
number keeps the phase prediction tied to the relevant evidence instead of
pretending an M4 composite score predicts the ranked M5.

## Decision tree after the official run

1. If it passes all gates, obtains valid telemetry, and promotes, rebase on the
