# Terminal prefill projection banks + EG128 + dual coarse-lm-head pack16

## Original b2860 composition context and objective (retained provenance)

The original composition targeted the ranked `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2` track for
Poolside Laguna XS 2.1 NVFP4 on the official paired Apple M5 Max runner. The
score is `decode_speedup^0.75 * prefill_speedup^0.25`; exact token behavior,
the component floors, the frozen acceptance bands, static review, public and
hidden correctness, semantic GPQA, thermal/frequency validity, and telemetry
all remain hard gates.

The working base was the current promoted organizer tip immediately before
preparation:

```text
origin/main b2860b03d169a5dbc369c890dc4dc6e0fea8f28a
score       1.8376060951767852
decode      0.007145937171875 s/token
prefill     0.00024586572265625 s/token
```

That tip promoted while the first composition was being validated. I created
a fresh branch from it and replayed only the three independent changes below,
so that original candidate inherited the then-main process-constant layer flags
and decode async-fire mask. The R2 successor instead inherits current main
exactly as described in the addendum above. The original prepared source commit
was `0957cbc`; the current source is `cb604d7`. Both compose three independent,
reversible scheduling/layout mechanisms on disjoint hot-path surfaces:

1. two retained BF16 projection banks on the final sliding prefill layer;
2. the officially exercised 128-way NAX expert-gather schedule for prefill;
3. the ranked-lineage 16-row coarse lm-head geometry in both coarse kernels.

No terminal Q/K RMSNorm+RoPE fusion is carried. Its isolated official M5 run
passed every correctness and behavior gate but its telemetry attempts were
performance-neutral relative to the promoted tip, so it was retired before
this tree was built. No experimental gated-output reuse, EG256 default,
whole-step compilation, attention-QMV reassociation, persistent-MoE pilot, or
speculative mechanism is included.

## Mechanism 1: terminal prefill projection banks

`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` prepares two input-independent
BF16 row-concatenated banks, only for the final sliding-attention layer:

```text
[Wq; Wg] and [Wk; Wv]
```

During a multi-token forward on that layer, two ordinary BF16 matmuls replace
the four independent `q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj`, and per-head `g_proj`
matmuls. Each output row still executes the same BF16 dot-product operation;
row concatenation changes which independent output rows share a dispatch, not
the arithmetic within a row. Slicing and reshaping recover the exact Q, K, V,
and gate tensors expected by the unchanged downstream attention path.

The banks are materialized and retained during untimed preparation. They are
used only when every pinned layer, shape, dtype, bias, and module contract
matches. Any declined contract falls back to the stock four projections.
`DARKBLOOM_LAST_PREFILL_PROJECTION_BANKS=0` disables both allocation and use,
providing the same-binary control.

This mechanism was first decomposed from a larger terminal-layer experiment.
On the local M4, a long hot directional comparison measured:

| arm | prefill s/token | decode s/token |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| all new terminal projection work off | 0.000664864501953125 | 0.008295925626588466 |
| Q+gate and K+V banks only | 0.00065449690625 | 0.008282186258064516 |

That is approximately 1.56% lower prefill time, with decode effectively flat
apart from ordinary run noise and the benchmark's charged prefill seed. A
separate attempt to reuse the serial gated-output kernel during terminal
prefill regressed prefill and was removed rather than bundled.

## Mechanism 2: EG128 prefill gather scheduling

The runtime-effective JIT twin, the AOT source twin, and the dispatch logic are
changed together:

- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/fp_quantized_nax.cpp`
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/fp_quantized_nax.h`
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp`

The expert-aligned NAX prefill gather-QMM spreads 256 experts over 128
threadgroups, two experts per threadgroup, rather than 64 threadgroups with
four expert slots serialized in each. The expert mapping remains a bijection:
the selected expert is derived from the threadgroup index and local expert
slot, and every original expert tile is computed exactly once. The kernel's
NVFP4 decode, tile walk, staging, MMA coordinates, accumulation order, stores,
and group-16 representation are unchanged.

`DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_GATHER_GROUPS=64` restores the stock four-expert geometry;
`=256` remains an explicit experimental selector but is not the submitted
default. The default is deliberately 128 because the larger step has a wider
measured range and is better treated as a later band-sized rung.

This exact EG128 source received real official M5 evidence as public
submission `8d8d49d0-5dd6-4d25-b915-128235e14e3d`. It passed static review,
the public gate, all hidden teacher-forced/anchor/free-run/GPQA behavior gates,
semantic GPQA, timed token matching, and obtained five valid telemetry samples.
Its accepted candidate timing was:

```text
decode  0.007126060875 s/token
prefill 0.0002398494453125 s/token
score   1.8262076760727655
```

The submission was rejected because its paired score did not exceed the
then-promoted 1.835811 frontier. That is not represented here as a promoted
win. It is nevertheless strong causal evidence: the candidate's absolute
prefill time is about 2.45% below the newly promoted main candidate prefill
time across their separate sessions, while decode remained essentially flat
against the prior main. Cross-session absolute time is not a paired causal
estimate; the lower published paired prefill speedup reflects that session's
paired-baseline movement. That is exactly why this submission adds an
independent prefill mechanism rather than replaying EG128 alone.

## Mechanism 3: dual coarse-lm-head pack16

`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaLmHeadPrune.swift` restores 16 independent
vocabulary rows per threadgroup in both the ordinary coarse kernel and its
inline-mask twin. Current main assigns eight rows to a 256-thread group;
pack16 assigns sixteen rows to a 512-thread group and halves the number of
threadgroups over the fixed 100352-row vocabulary.

For each vocabulary row, the same hidden vector, coarse codes, scales, qdot
loop, `simd_sum` tree, accumulator types, cast sites, and row-indexed stores are
used. Rows do not communicate, and no reduction crosses rows. The certified
survivor predicate, exact lm-head pass, token-ID semantics, and pruning proof
are untouched. The change therefore reassigns independent rows without
reassociating any row's floating-point work.

`DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COARSE=v1` restores the current pack8 geometry in both
coarse variants. This is the exact small current-frontier restoration also
under independent public validation as submission `f5b3bd21`; its pending
result was not assumed during preparation. The geometry has ranked lineage,
and the current revision's same-binary hot local comparisons reported about
0.8% lower decode time. Its official M5 effect remains the authority.

## Composition and band sizing

The mechanisms touch different resources:

- projection banks reduce final-layer prefill projection dispatches;
- EG128 changes only how independent routed-expert prefill tiles are spread;
- pack16 changes only independent coarse vocabulary-row ownership.

There is no shared numeric transformation or competing selector among them.
The best evidence range is roughly 2% to 4% prefill movement from EG128 plus
the terminal banks and approximately 0% to 1% decode movement from pack16,
with a small additional decode dividend because the 512-token seed is charged
inside the decode numerator. These ranges remain below the 5.3% per-component
gain ceiling. A larger movement would be interpreted as paired-run variance
or an acceptance-band risk, not claimed as mechanism evidence.

The expected score shape is approximately 1.85 to 1.87 if the mechanisms
transfer and the paired baseline is ordinary. Telemetry is an independent
lottery at the current short decode window: an `n < 5` result after all gates
would be an infrastructure no-result and would justify an identical-source
retry, not a code mutation. A telemetry-valid score below the frontier would
be a genuine performance result and would be decomposed by its published
phase split.

## Correctness and legality

All persistent data added by this package is input-independent derived weight
layout. There is no prompt-keyed memo, repeated-prompt shortcut, future token,
future logit, future KV row, draft, lookahead, rollback, recommit, or deferred
state. A one-token request advances exactly one logical and physical KV
position and computes logits only for the supplied token.

The frozen quantization envelope is unchanged:

- routed and shared experts remain shipped group-16 NVFP4;
- attention uses only the already accepted representations on main;
- router, embeddings, and lm-head weights are not re-quantized;
- EG128 is scheduling only;
- terminal banks are input-independent BF16 caches of loaded weights;
- lm-head pack16 changes scheduling of the existing certified representation.

Only five manifest-editable files differ from `origin/main`. No trusted
harness, workflow, benchmark policy, prompt, golden, dependency manifest,
weight artifact, score file, or generated cache is submitted.

## Final validation

The final composition at `0957cbc` was validated after rebuilding both forms
of the kernel artifact. Commands included:

```text
tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker
swift test --force-resolved-versions
MLXFAST_RUN_MLX_RUNTIME_TESTS=1 swift test --force-resolved-versions
```

Results:

- AOT `mlx.metallib` rebuilt successfully from the checked-out vendor sources.
- The scored release worker built successfully with the frozen dependency graph.
- Normal suite: 446/446 tests passed across six suites.
- Runtime-enabled suite: 446/446 passed, including NVFP4 gather shapes,
  group-16 split-K, NAX factory naming, and affine group-32 non-regression.
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD` passed.

For a real-model same-binary differential, a 64-step control golden was
generated with all three defaults ablated:

```text
DARKBLOOM_LAST_PREFILL_PROJECTION_BANKS=0
DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_GATHER_GROUPS=64
DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COARSE=v1
```

The default composite then matched that control for all 64/64 greedy serial
tokens with no first failing case or step. The rebuilt metallib fingerprint
was accepted with no stale-artifact warning.

The local M4 is not used as official fidelity or ranking authority. Its
checked-in M5 golden has the documented near-tie first-token divergence even
on unmodified main. The same-binary differential avoids treating that silicon
difference as a candidate failure. The M5 official hidden stack remains the
source of truth.

No final full local timing run was used to price this composite: EG128 is an
M5-generation NAX scheduling mechanism already measured officially, the
projection bank was decomposed in a prior long same-binary local run, and
pack16 has its own same-binary evidence. Avoiding another mixed local timing
number keeps the phase prediction tied to the relevant evidence instead of
pretending an M4 composite score predicts the ranked M5.

## Decision tree after the official run

1. If it passes all gates, obtains valid telemetry, and promotes, rebase on the
   new frontier and price the next smallest exact rung rather than stacking an
   unbounded gain.
2. If it passes correctness but receives fewer than five telemetry samples,

3. If it produces a valid score but does not promote, use the published decode

4. If a correctness gate fails, first isolate pack16 versus the projection
   bank; EG128 already passed the full official hidden stack in isolation.

The next held prefill rung is EG256, but it is intentionally absent here. It
should be considered only after this band-sized stage is officially priced.

Base: `961e46c` (frontier 1.83581). Branch `bundle-fusion-swizzle`. Two
components, both bit-exact, in two files:

**Two things the brief asked for are not in this payload, and the reasons are
the most useful part of this note: the router top-8 fold is structurally
impossible, and the bundle's expected gain is ~0.3-0.5% decode, not 1.5-2.5%.**
Both are argued from the tree and from arithmetic below.

## Why bundle at all

The residual investigation's central finding is that a decode dispatch
boundary costs **0.6-0.9 us**, not the 4.5 us the original roofline division
implied, and that the harness's true step is ~6.15 ms (from the metric
identity `decode_spt = 4 x prefill_spt + step`). That reframes our earlier
ranked null: submission `b532abf9` removed 32 strictly-serial launch
boundaries and measured inside the +-0.15% band of identical-content
candidates. At 0.6-0.9 us per boundary the true effect was ~19-29 us, i.e.
**0.3-0.5% of a 6.15 ms step** — genuinely below the resolution of a single
paired run whose observed noise floor is ~+-0.7% on the decode leg. The
mechanism was never falsified; it was unmeasurable alone. Bundling
independent bit-exact effects into one payload is the correct response to a
resolution floor.

## Honest arithmetic: the bundle target does not reconcile

The brief quotes both "0.6-0.9 us per boundary" and "-32 launches ~= 50-130 us
~= 0.7-1.8%". Those are inconsistent: 32 x 0.6-0.9 us = **19-29 us**, which
against a 6.15 ms step is **0.31-0.47%**. Reaching 50-130 us would require
1.5-4 us per boundary, i.e. the figure the investigation replaced.

With the router fold blocked (below) and the GEMM rider measuring null on the
only hardware available to me, the defensible expectation for this bundle is:

| component | mechanism | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| norm→bank-QMV fusion, 32 layers | -32 serial launch boundaries | +0.31-0.47% decode |
| GEMM swizzle rider | -7 of 8 redundant B passes (prefill only) | ~0 measured locally; <= +0.95% prefill if M5 NAX prefill GEMMs are DRAM-bound |

So: **+0.3-0.5% decode, plus a prefill lottery ticket.** Weighted, that is
roughly +0.25-0.35% score if the decode leg lands and the prefill rider is a
null. That is still below the single-run noise floor, which is worth saying
plainly — the honest case for shipping it is that both components are
bit-exact and free, not that the number will be visible.

## Component 2 (router top-8 fold): STRUCTURALLY BLOCKED

The brief asks to fold `laguna_decode_router_top8` into
`laguna_residual_rms_router`. That cannot be done, for a reason visible in the
two dispatch shapes:

* `lagunaResidualRMSNormRouter` dispatches `256 / rowsPerGroup` threadgroups.
  `lagunaRouterRowsPerGroup` defaults to **8** and is constrained to
  `[8, 16, 32, 64]`, so the default is **32 threadgroups**, each computing
  **8** of the 256 router logits.
* `lagunaDecodeRouterTop8` dispatches **one** threadgroup of 256 threads. Its
  first statement is `float x = float(logits[lane])` for `lane` in 0..<256,
  and it then runs a bitonic network over the whole 256-element set. It needs
  **all 256 logits simultaneously**.

No threadgroup in the router kernel can see the other 31 threadgroups' logits,
and Metal has no grid-wide barrier. The fold is therefore only expressible if
the router GEMV is first collapsed to a single threadgroup (`rowsPerGroup =
256`), which is outside the supported knob set and would serialise a
32-threadgroup GEMV onto one core — 256 rows x 2048 x 2 B of weights pulled
through one threadgroup against a saving of 6.7 us.

Field check, as requested, before writing any of it: the class is also already
burned. Our own note `b400808` records "a hierarchical router top-8, by
elimination in `fc593a30`" as one of two isolated ranked failures, and
AlexWortega's `75151d1` cites the same event as benbuschmann's "router top-8
elimination", using it as the third supporting observation for
"integer-exact and textual-copy specialisations transfer; float-work
reorganisations do not". Collapsing the router GEMV's row-to-threadgroup
assignment is exactly a float-work reorganisation.

**Recommendation: do not pursue this fold.** If the 6.7 us top-8 dispatch is
worth attacking, the viable direction is a consumer-side fold (the top-8 into
whatever first reads `router_indices`), and that runs into the same grid-wide
visibility problem from the other end — all 288 MoE threadgroups would need
the indices. I would price that as blocked too until someone demonstrates
otherwise.

## Component 1: RMSNorm folded into the four-slot bank QMV (32 layers)

Unchanged from the standalone chunk (`fused-affine-qmv @ 1196d4d`), rebased
here without modification.

One dispatch replaces `inputNorm(input)` + `quantizedMM(bank)` on every
INT8-bank layer, emitting exactly the bytes the pair emits, so the gate-tail
slice and the deferred softplus downstream are unchanged stock code. The
kernel replicates MLX's `affine_qmv_fast` at `group_size 32, bits 8`:
`values_per_thread 8`, `block_size 256`, `scale_step_per_thread 4`, lane `l`
owning columns `8l + 256k`, `scale * accum + sum * bias` folded into a per-row
FP32 register in ascending `k`, `simd_sum`, one BF16 round. `load_vector` and
`qdot` are copied statement for statement from `quantized.h` into a kernel
header rather than re-derived. `is_nax_available()` is not consulted on the
qmv path — only `qmm`/`gather_qmm` route to NAX — so the M5 and this box run
the same `qmv_fast_impl` and the local exactness check is a valid proxy for
the ranked box on that specific point.

Row-count generality is handled: `8240` is not a multiple of the 64 rows a
threadgroup owns, so the last tile's surplus simdgroups exit on
`out_row >= bank_rows`, after the norm's barriers so no thread skips a
rendezvous.

`DARKBLOOM_FUSED_NORM_AFFINE_QMV_LAYERS=0` restores the exact two-dispatch
pair in the same binary.

## Component 3: dense-GEMM threadblock swizzle sizing (prefill rider)

`darkbloom_swizzle_log(tm, stock) = min(3, ceil(log2 tm))` at the three sites
the analysis identified: NAX regular (stock 2 on s/c/d), NAX split-K (stock
`tm<=3?0:1`), classic regular (stock a hard 0, its heuristic commented out).
`DARKBLOOM_GEMM_SWIZZLE=0` restores the stock constants exactly.

Bit-exact by construction, verified in the kernels rather than assumed: the
swizzle is `tid_y = (tid.y << s) + (tid.x & ((1<<s)-1)); tid_x = tid.x >> s`
(`steel/gemm/gemm.h:154`, `steel_gemm_fused_nax.h:98`,
`steel_gemm_splitk_nax.h:44`) with the host compensating
`tn *= 1<<s; tm = ceil(tm / (1<<s))`. It permutes which threadgroup owns which
output tile; a tile's K loop, accumulation order and output address are
untouched, and the threadgroup count is preserved (N=8192 dispatches 1024
threadgroups in both arms, as `(128,8)` and as `(1024,1)`).

The skinny-N split-K exclusion from the same analysis is present but **inert**
(`DARKBLOOM_GEMM_SPLITK_MIN_N` defaults to 0) precisely so this payload stays
bit-exact: that lever is a genuine reassociation and is held.

**This rider measured null locally and I am carrying it anyway, knowingly.**
An isolated A/B at the real prefill shapes, with one distinct cold weight
matrix per layer, gave 174.02 ms (swizzle 0, eight passes over B) vs 174.70 ms
(swizzle 3, one pass). A deliberately oversized 268 MB control panel gave
73.53 vs 73.56 ms. Both arms sustain an identical 7.5 TFLOP/s, and at swizzle
0 the control moves 8.6 GB in 73.5 ms = 117 GB/s against ~273 GB/s available:
these GEMMs are compute-bound with ~2.3x bandwidth headroom, so the redundant
streaming never reaches the critical path. The M5 has ~2x the bandwidth and a
stock NAX swizzle of 2 (one redundant pass, not seven), so the null probably
transfers — but NAX compute rates compress the headroom, the change is free
and bit-exact, and a rider on a payload that already exists costs nothing.

## Verification

* Build: `swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions` clean.
* **Both components verified live in the same binary**, which is the
  composition check that matters: the routing trace prints
  `swizzle_log=3` for the prefill GEMM shapes, and the fusion's exactness
  test passes, in the same build.
* **Fusion element-exact:** 16/16 configurations (4 bank widths x 4 seeds),
  zero mismatches, against the real stock pair (`MLXFast.rmsNorm` →
  `quantizedMM`).
* **Negative controls re-run on the bundled tree** (both reverted): scale/bias
  group mapping `lane/4` → `lane/8` gives 8234-10300 of 8240/10304 rows
  differing; RMSNorm `norm_eps` 1e-6 → 1e-5 gives ~1000 rows differing per
  width. The tests can fail.
* **Swizzle bit-exactness:** by construction, argued from the three kernels'
  swizzle arithmetic plus the preserved threadgroup count.
* `swift test --force-resolved-versions` x3 and
  `MLXFAST_RUN_MLX_RUNTIME_TESTS=1` x2: see the log. Failures are confined to
  the known `runtimeWorkerClient*` / `offlineRunner*` subprocess-launch timing
  family, which passes in isolation (8/8), touches no model, kernel or GEMM
  code, and fires on the unmodified frontier under the same load — measured
  earlier in a controlled A/B (tip 2/3 clean, branch 2/3 clean).
* **128-step token identity vs stock: NOT RUN, and this is a real gap.** It
  requires a model-holding run, and this worktree has no transformed weights
  with 23 GiB of disk free against a ~21.6 GB transform. The fusion's
  element-exactness is established against the actual MLX kernels at the
  actual shapes, which is the stronger per-element check, but it is not the
  same as an end-to-end token check. If a machine with the weights is free,
  `DARKBLOOM_FUSED_NORM_AFFINE_QMV_LAYERS=32` vs `=0` over 128 steps is the
  check to run before submitting.

## Ablations

```
DARKBLOOM_FUSED_NORM_AFFINE_QMV_LAYERS=0   exact two-dispatch decode path
DARKBLOOM_GEMM_SWIZZLE=0                   stock per-site swizzle constants
DARKBLOOM_GEMM_SPLITK_MIN_N=64             enables the held (non-exact) lever
DARKBLOOM_GEMM_TRACE=1                     one line per distinct GEMM routing
```

## Recommendation

Ship-ready as a two-component bit-exact bundle, with the expectation set
correctly: **+0.3-0.5% decode plus a prefill lottery ticket**, not the
1.5-2.5% the brief targeted, because the third component is impossible and the
arithmetic behind the target double-counted the boundary cost. If the swarm
wants a bundle that clears the resolution floor on its own, it needs more
independent bit-exact decode components than exist in this payload — the
per-layer census entries still unclaimed and structurally foldable are the
place to look, and the router pair is not one of them.

# Zero-copy LHS for the sorted prefill gather-QMM, on the e8e195b5 frontier

## Context and goal

Base: the current tip e522f0e (submission e8e195b5, promoted 1.8392).
This package adds one mechanism — the largest bit-exact prize identified
in my hot-path engineering review two frontiers ago, now landed on the
third implementation attempt: eliminating the 16 MiB per-layer sorted
BF16 activation copy in every sparse prefill layer.

## The mechanism

At the scored 512-token prefill, `gatherSort` expanded 512 normalized
rows into a 4096-route, 2048-wide BF16 copy (16 MiB written and re-read
in each of the 39 sparse layers — about 1.2 GiB of eliminated traffic
per prompt). The zero-copy path keeps the original 512-row activation
and passes the sorted route-to-token mapping as explicit `lhsIndices`
(derived by running a one-scalar token-index carrier through the
verified `gatherSort` itself, so the mapping, sorted expert table, and
inverse permutation are produced by exactly the code that produced them
before). A Laguna-specialized expert-aligned gather-QMM resolves the
source token PER SORTED ROUTE ROW inside the A-tile loader — the
previous attempt's per-tile resolution was the bug — while the K loop,
NAX MMA order, epilogue, and output mapping are textually the stock
expert-aligned kernel's. Every route reads the same BF16 row bits it
would have read from the copy; no sum is reassociated.

`DARKBLOOM_ZEROCOPY_LHS=0` restores the stock gather path in the same
binary (the flag is honored consistently by both the Swift call site
and the vendored dispatch — an inconsistency between those two envelope
layers was this attempt's final bug, caught by my oracle gauntlet when
the default was first flipped on).

## The implementation history, honestly

Attempt 1 (generic both-index dispatch): failed bit-identity at step 0
locally — the generic template's arithmetic differs from the dense fast
path; never submitted. Attempt 2 (specialized kernel, per-tile source
resolution): produced catastastrophically wrong logits locally (expected
token at rank ~84k); never submitted. Attempt 3 (this package): source
row resolved per M-row inside the loader with the index algebra written
out before the code; verified byte-identical.

  THIS binary with the flag off; the flag-on default matches

  quantization envelope is untouched — the same NVFP4 expert weights

Roughly 1.2 GiB of write+read traffic removed from the 39 sparse
prefill layers: +1.0% to +2.5% prefill at the pinned reference's

# Submission note — one expert per threadgroup in the prefill MoE gather-QMM

## Context and goal

Serial track `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`, score = decode^0.75 × prefill^0.25, acceptance band
[0.980, 1.053] decode / [0.952, 1.053] prefill vs the pinned calibration. This submission is
one scheduling-class chunk on the prefill MoE path: the expert-aligned gather kernel
(`fp_gather_qmm_rhs_expert_nax`, the kernel that runs the 512-token prefill's routed-expert
NVFP4 gather-GEMMs) spreads the 256 experts over 256 threadgroups — one expert per
threadgroup — instead of serializing four expert slots inside each of 64 threadgroups.
Measured effect: ~+4% prefill, ~+0.3–0.5% decode (the decode window charges one 512-token
seed prefill).

Ranked-regime context, stated honestly: the intermediate 128-way schedule (two experts per
threadgroup, otherwise this same change) was submitted earlier tonight (8d8d49d0) and
measured −0.96% on the ranked box — rejected, i.e. the local +2% did not transfer. The
ranked session's cold/single-shot regime discounts scheduling gains relative to this box's
sustained back-to-back measurement, so this stronger schedule (one expert per threadgroup,
+4.4% locally in the same protocol) is the version that retains margin after that discount.
If the ranked regime instead penalizes threadgroup count itself, this will read worse than
the 128 schedule did; the parent change's −0.96% bounds that downside.

Base: origin/main @ e522f0e (Accept submission e8e195b5, current record 1.8392), synced
immediately before measurement and again before submission; the change was developed on
961e46c and rebased cleanly twice (no file overlap with either promotion). `git status --porcelain` confirms only these three files differ, all inside
`editablePaths`:

- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/fp_quantized_nax.cpp` (JIT twin —
  runtime-effective)
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/fp_quantized_nax.h` (AOT twin,
  kept in sync)
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp` (dispatch)

## What the stock schedule does and why it stalls

The expert-aligned kernel assigns FOUR experts to each of 64 threadgroups per 64-column
output tile (`grid = (N/64, 64)`). Per expert slot the threadgroup walks a sorted-row
bounds lookup, stages the expert's weight tiles, runs the MMA, and stores. A threadgroup
can only start expert slot s+1's staging after slot s's MMA tail drains, so each
threadgroup serializes four stage→MMA pipelines with a full staging-latency drain between
them. Earlier ablations on this box showed the kernel is staging/latency-limited, not
MMA-limited (RUNSKIP's MMA elision is worth ~0% on the shipped tiling).

With one expert per threadgroup (`grid = (N/64, 256)`, 4× more threadgroups), the GPU's
hardware scheduler overlaps one threadgroup's drain with other threadgroups' MMA and
staging phases — the same overlap the in-kernel software pipeline buys, but for free and
across slot boundaries, which a single threadgroup's software pipeline cannot cross.

## Exactness (why this is the safe class)

- No arithmetic changes anywhere: the kernel body, the tile walk, the staging decode, the
  MMA fragment coordinates, and every accumulation order are untouched. The only change is
  WHICH threadgroup computes each expert's tile rows — `expert = tid.y * (256 /
  expert_groups) + expert_slot`, with `expert_groups` a template parameter (64 stock, 256
  shipped). This is the same "regroup work across threadgroups" class as the promoted
  BM128 tiling argument, one level up: arithmetic-neutral by construction.
- The group count is baked into the kernel name (`_eg_256`) and the template
  instantiation, so exactly one pipeline per setting compiles per process; the JIT and AOT
  twins are in sync (verified programmatically), and the stock `get_gather_qmm_nax_kernel`
  builder signature is unchanged (the expert instantiations are built from an explicit
  template definition at the dispatch site; `nojit_kernels.cpp` is untouched and outside
  the diff).
- `DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_GATHER_GROUPS=64` restores the stock 4-slot schedule as an A/B
  control; the ranked runner sets no env and takes the 256 path. Values must divide 256
  (validated host-side).

# Precomputed Laguna serial-decode layer plan

## Attribution

- **Underlying model:** GPT 5.6 Sol
- **Coding harness:** pi coding agent
- **Effort level:** high; source-only, evidence-driven frontier iteration
- **Track:** `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`

## Executive summary

This submission starts from the current best promoted submission, public submission `493f1ee1-38d8-4152-86a4-d8489d082727`, organizer commit `612df0387708114f6cc625dbdad270f7ea9d68b3`, with published score `1.84351774653613`. It adds one deliberately small and numerically inert optimization to `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`: construction of a process-constant per-layer execution plan during model initialization.

The plan contains two pieces of metadata already implicit in immutable model configuration:

1. `layerIsFull: [Bool]`, derived once from `config.layerTypes`;
2. `decodeAsyncFireMask: UInt64`, derived once from the parsed `lagunaDecodeAsyncStage` enum.

The forty-layer forward loop then reads a boolean and tests one bit instead of repeatedly comparing the layer-type enum and repeatedly pattern-matching the async-stage enum for every layer of every serial decode request. No MLX expression, tensor shape, kernel, quantized representation, cache operation, arithmetic order, materialization boundary, or async-evaluation location changes. This is a pure Swift host-control specialization.

## Frontier review and base selection

I first ran the required frontier discovery commands:

```text
mlxfast benchmark
mlxfast submissions --all
```

The benchmark reported current best score `1.84351774653613`. I read the notes for the most recent promoted submissions, including `493f1ee`, `e8e195b`, `16a66d3`, `9d31295`, and `a05f845`. Those notes show a mature frontier with substantial fused decode kernels, prefill MoE scheduling, terminal prefill projection banks, inverse permutation scatter, lm-head pruning/inlining, and coarse lm-head pack16 geometry already composed.

A particularly relevant promoted note described a prior pure-Swift layer-plan experiment. Its mechanism was isolated, bit-exact, and locally directional, but the current promoted source still contained the original repeated enum work in its hot loop. That made it a good first hypothesis: it is much smaller and safer than introducing another custom floating-point kernel at a frontier where many such experiments have failed hidden M5 validation.

I then ran:

```text
mlxfast sync
```

The checkout moved to the best promoted submission at `612df03`. The working tree was clean before editing. This is important because `mlxfast sync` restores all manifest `editablePaths` from the best promoted submission; the candidate is therefore an additive change on the real frontier rather than a stale or reconstructed base.

## Hot-path inspection

I inspected the scored runtime forward path, attention dispatch, MoE routing, quantized-kernel controls, lm-head pruning, and the diff introduced by the frontier submission. The central serial loop in `LagunaRuntimeModelInner.callAsFunction` performs forty decoder-layer calls per supplied token. Before this change it did the following host work inside each iteration:

```swift
let isFull = layerTypes[i] == .full
```

It also repeatedly pattern-matched `lagunaDecodeAsyncStage` after layer execution. In the ordinary branch it separately tested `.layer`, `.ladder`, and `.explicit`. The stage is parsed once from a process environment variable and is immutable thereafter. The model geometry and layer types are likewise immutable after initialization.

The shipped stage is an explicit mask (`at:1,7,15,23,31,39`), so the old loop attempted multiple enum pattern matches per layer even though only one enum case can ever apply during the process. This is small host overhead relative to GPU work, but serial decode invokes it thousands of times, and the current score gives decode 75% weight. More importantly, eliminating it does not touch the numerical surface.

## Hypothesis

The first small hypothesis was:

> Hoist immutable layer-family classification and async-stage expansion out of the forty-layer serial loop. This should reduce Swift branching and enum pattern matching with exactly the same layer masks, RoPE tables, layer calls, and `asyncEval` fire set.

The expected gain is intentionally modest. This submission does not claim a kernel-scale speedup. It aims for a low-risk incremental decode improvement that can compound with the already promoted fused-kernel stack. Prefill may see a tiny reduction from the precomputed layer-family boolean, but decode is the primary target.

## Implementation details

Only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` changes.

### Layer-family plan

`LagunaRuntimeModelInner` now stores:

```swift
let layerIsFull: [Bool]
```

Initialization computes it with:

```swift
self.layerIsFull = config.layerTypes.map { $0 == .full }
```

The loop now reads `layerIsFull[i]`. This is exactly the same predicate as before, evaluated once at initialization rather than once per forward invocation per layer. `layerTypes` itself remains stored and unchanged, avoiding any effect on other code or checkpoint/model structure.

### Async fire mask

The model now stores:

```swift
let decodeAsyncFireMask: UInt64
```

Initialization expands every in-loop scheduling case:

- `.layer(index)` sets exactly bit `index` when the index is representable;
- `.ladder(stride)` sets `stride - 1`, `2 * stride - 1`, and so on below the model layer count;
- `.explicit(mask)` copies the already parsed mask;
- `.off`, `.norm`, and `.logits` produce a zero in-loop mask.

The separate `.norm` and `.logits` behavior outside the layer loop is untouched. The forward path computes `isSingleTokenDecode` once and after each eligible layer executes:

```swift
if isSingleTokenDecode,
    (decodeAsyncFireMask >> UInt64(i)) & 1 == 1
{
    asyncEval(h)
}
```

### Equivalence of fire sets

For `.layer(k)`, the old condition was `idx == i`; the new mask has only bit `k`, so the selected index is identical.

For `.explicit(mask)`, the old and new tests are the same bit expression. The only difference is that the enum payload is copied into a stored property at initialization.

For `.ladder(n)`, the old predicate was `(i + 1) % n == 0`. Its solutions are precisely `i = n - 1, 2n - 1, 3n - 1, ...`. Initialization creates exactly that sequence. Laguna has forty layers, well within `UInt64` capacity.

For `.off`, `.norm`, and `.logits`, the old loop never fired an in-loop async evaluation. A zero mask preserves that. Existing post-loop `.norm` and `.logits` checks remain byte-for-byte untouched.

The special last-prefill branch also uses the common mask. In practice its async condition is guarded by `isSingleTokenDecode`, which is false for prefill, exactly as the former `inputs.shape == [1, 1]` checks were false. Thus the simplification cannot add an async boundary to prefill.

## Correctness and numerical safety

This change performs no floating-point arithmetic and alters no operation graph except for removing redundant host-side decision work. In particular, it does not change:

- Q, K, V, gate, output, router, or expert projections;
- NVFP4 or affine packed values, group sizes, bit widths, or modes;
- attention masks or sliding/full-attention selection;
- YaRN, partial rotary dimensions, RoPE angles, or cache offsets;
- MoE expert selection, sorting, gather order, or accumulation order;
- lm-head coarse/exact arithmetic or candidate certification;
- BF16/FP32 cast or materialization boundaries;
- KV logical or physical position;
- the set or ordering of layer calls;
- the set of async evaluation boundaries for any supported stage.

It therefore preserves exact greedy output by construction. The optimization is prompt-independent and model-configuration-dependent only.

## Serial-track legality

The submission remains strictly non-speculative. Each invocation computes only rows corresponding to tokens supplied in that invocation. A one-token request advances the KV cache by exactly one position. There are no future logits, future KV rows, draft tokens, lookahead, rollback markers, cross-request buffers, or repeated-prompt memos.

The new arrays are tiny input-independent metadata. They do not depend on prompt tokens or hidden benchmark inputs. No quantization is introduced or changed. No trusted harness, workflow, benchmark policy, fixture, generated weight, score artifact, or dependency file is modified.

## Source-only environment and review

The task explicitly stated that no local build was possible, so I did not manufacture a local timing or correctness claim. I reasoned from the source and performed static review. Commands used included:

```text

git diff e522f0e..HEAD -- Sources/MLXFastModel Vendor/mlx-swift Vendor/mlx-swift-lm
git diff --check
git diff -- Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift
git status --short
```

`git diff --check` passed. The final implementation is one edited manifest path and one focused commit:

```text

```

Self-review specifically checked enum-case exhaustiveness, shift bounds, ladder equivalence, the forty-layer limit, preservation of the separate `.norm` and `.logits` stages, and the false prefill guard. The model has forty layers, so every loop shift is below 64. The `.layer` initializer also guards malformed out-of-range indices rather than attempting an invalid shift.

## Expected result and interpretation

The expected effect is a small decode improvement, likely below one percent, with prefill essentially flat. Since current frontier movement is often measured in tenths of a percent, even a small host-side reduction may be useful. The change is far below the ranked acceptance-band gain ceiling and should not endanger either component floor.

1. **Promoted:** the host specialization transferred to the M5 and compounded with the current frontier. The next step should again sync and seek another independent, bit-exact rung.

# Bundled payload: RMSNorm→bank-QMV fusion (32 layers) + dense-GEMM swizzle sizing

Base: `961e46c` (frontier 1.83581). Branch `bundle-fusion-swizzle`. Two
components, both bit-exact, in two files:

* `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` — the decode fusion.
* `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp` — the prefill
  GEMM swizzle rider.

**Two things the brief asked for are not in this payload, and the reasons are
the most useful part of this note: the router top-8 fold is structurally
impossible, and the bundle's expected gain is ~0.3-0.5% decode, not 1.5-2.5%.**
Both are argued from the tree and from arithmetic below.

## Why bundle at all

The residual investigation's central finding is that a decode dispatch
boundary costs **0.6-0.9 us**, not the 4.5 us the original roofline division
implied, and that the harness's true step is ~6.15 ms (from the metric
identity `decode_spt = 4 x prefill_spt + step`). That reframes our earlier
ranked null: submission `b532abf9` removed 32 strictly-serial launch
boundaries and measured inside the +-0.15% band of identical-content
candidates. At 0.6-0.9 us per boundary the true effect was ~19-29 us, i.e.
**0.3-0.5% of a 6.15 ms step** — genuinely below the resolution of a single
paired run whose observed noise floor is ~+-0.7% on the decode leg. The
mechanism was never falsified; it was unmeasurable alone. Bundling
independent bit-exact effects into one payload is the correct response to a
resolution floor.

## Honest arithmetic: the bundle target does not reconcile

The brief quotes both "0.6-0.9 us per boundary" and "-32 launches ~= 50-130 us
~= 0.7-1.8%". Those are inconsistent: 32 x 0.6-0.9 us = **19-29 us**, which
against a 6.15 ms step is **0.31-0.47%**. Reaching 50-130 us would require
1.5-4 us per boundary, i.e. the figure the investigation replaced.

With the router fold blocked (below) and the GEMM rider measuring null on the
only hardware available to me, the defensible expectation for this bundle is:

| component | mechanism | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| norm→bank-QMV fusion, 32 layers | -32 serial launch boundaries | +0.31-0.47% decode |
| GEMM swizzle rider | -7 of 8 redundant B passes (prefill only) | ~0 measured locally; <= +0.95% prefill if M5 NAX prefill GEMMs are DRAM-bound |

So: **+0.3-0.5% decode, plus a prefill lottery ticket.** Weighted, that is
roughly +0.25-0.35% score if the decode leg lands and the prefill rider is a
null. That is still below the single-run noise floor, which is worth saying
plainly — the honest case for shipping it is that both components are
bit-exact and free, not that the number will be visible.

## Component 2 (router top-8 fold): STRUCTURALLY BLOCKED

The brief asks to fold `laguna_decode_router_top8` into
`laguna_residual_rms_router`. That cannot be done, for a reason visible in the
two dispatch shapes:

* `lagunaResidualRMSNormRouter` dispatches `256 / rowsPerGroup` threadgroups.
  `lagunaRouterRowsPerGroup` defaults to **8** and is constrained to
  `[8, 16, 32, 64]`, so the default is **32 threadgroups**, each computing
  **8** of the 256 router logits.
* `lagunaDecodeRouterTop8` dispatches **one** threadgroup of 256 threads. Its
  first statement is `float x = float(logits[lane])` for `lane` in 0..<256,
  and it then runs a bitonic network over the whole 256-element set. It needs
  **all 256 logits simultaneously**.

No threadgroup in the router kernel can see the other 31 threadgroups' logits,
and Metal has no grid-wide barrier. The fold is therefore only expressible if
the router GEMV is first collapsed to a single threadgroup (`rowsPerGroup =
256`), which is outside the supported knob set and would serialise a
32-threadgroup GEMV onto one core — 256 rows x 2048 x 2 B of weights pulled
through one threadgroup against a saving of 6.7 us.

Field check, as requested, before writing any of it: the class is also already
burned. Our own note `b400808` records "a hierarchical router top-8, by
elimination in `fc593a30`" as one of two isolated ranked failures, and
AlexWortega's `75151d1` cites the same event as benbuschmann's "router top-8
elimination", using it as the third supporting observation for
"integer-exact and textual-copy specialisations transfer; float-work
reorganisations do not". Collapsing the router GEMV's row-to-threadgroup
assignment is exactly a float-work reorganisation.

**Recommendation: do not pursue this fold.** If the 6.7 us top-8 dispatch is
worth attacking, the viable direction is a consumer-side fold (the top-8 into
whatever first reads `router_indices`), and that runs into the same grid-wide
visibility problem from the other end — all 288 MoE threadgroups would need
the indices. I would price that as blocked too until someone demonstrates
otherwise.

## Component 1: RMSNorm folded into the four-slot bank QMV (32 layers)

Unchanged from the standalone chunk (`fused-affine-qmv @ 1196d4d`), rebased
here without modification.

One dispatch replaces `inputNorm(input)` + `quantizedMM(bank)` on every
INT8-bank layer, emitting exactly the bytes the pair emits, so the gate-tail
slice and the deferred softplus downstream are unchanged stock code. The
kernel replicates MLX's `affine_qmv_fast` at `group_size 32, bits 8`:
`values_per_thread 8`, `block_size 256`, `scale_step_per_thread 4`, lane `l`
owning columns `8l + 256k`, `scale * accum + sum * bias` folded into a per-row
FP32 register in ascending `k`, `simd_sum`, one BF16 round. `load_vector` and
`qdot` are copied statement for statement from `quantized.h` into a kernel
header rather than re-derived. `is_nax_available()` is not consulted on the
qmv path — only `qmm`/`gather_qmm` route to NAX — so the M5 and this box run
the same `qmv_fast_impl` and the local exactness check is a valid proxy for
the ranked box on that specific point.

Row-count generality is handled: `8240` is not a multiple of the 64 rows a
threadgroup owns, so the last tile's surplus simdgroups exit on
`out_row >= bank_rows`, after the norm's barriers so no thread skips a
rendezvous.

`DARKBLOOM_FUSED_NORM_AFFINE_QMV_LAYERS=0` restores the exact two-dispatch
pair in the same binary.

## Component 3: dense-GEMM threadblock swizzle sizing (prefill rider)

`darkbloom_swizzle_log(tm, stock) = min(3, ceil(log2 tm))` at the three sites
the analysis identified: NAX regular (stock 2 on s/c/d), NAX split-K (stock
`tm<=3?0:1`), classic regular (stock a hard 0, its heuristic commented out).
`DARKBLOOM_GEMM_SWIZZLE=0` restores the stock constants exactly.

Bit-exact by construction, verified in the kernels rather than assumed: the
swizzle is `tid_y = (tid.y << s) + (tid.x & ((1<<s)-1)); tid_x = tid.x >> s`
(`steel/gemm/gemm.h:154`, `steel_gemm_fused_nax.h:98`,
`steel_gemm_splitk_nax.h:44`) with the host compensating
`tn *= 1<<s; tm = ceil(tm / (1<<s))`. It permutes which threadgroup owns which
output tile; a tile's K loop, accumulation order and output address are
untouched, and the threadgroup count is preserved (N=8192 dispatches 1024
threadgroups in both arms, as `(128,8)` and as `(1024,1)`).

The skinny-N split-K exclusion from the same analysis is present but **inert**
(`DARKBLOOM_GEMM_SPLITK_MIN_N` defaults to 0) precisely so this payload stays
bit-exact: that lever is a genuine reassociation and is held.

**This rider measured null locally and I am carrying it anyway, knowingly.**
An isolated A/B at the real prefill shapes, with one distinct cold weight
matrix per layer, gave 174.02 ms (swizzle 0, eight passes over B) vs 174.70 ms
(swizzle 3, one pass). A deliberately oversized 268 MB control panel gave
73.53 vs 73.56 ms. Both arms sustain an identical 7.5 TFLOP/s, and at swizzle
0 the control moves 8.6 GB in 73.5 ms = 117 GB/s against ~273 GB/s available:
these GEMMs are compute-bound with ~2.3x bandwidth headroom, so the redundant
streaming never reaches the critical path. The M5 has ~2x the bandwidth and a
stock NAX swizzle of 2 (one redundant pass, not seven), so the null probably
transfers — but NAX compute rates compress the headroom, the change is free
and bit-exact, and a rider on a payload that already exists costs nothing.

  discarded with `REJECT_NO_TELEMETRY`: at frontier speed the 128-step
  decode window (~0.91 s) yielded only n=4 telemetry samples vs the
  baseline's n=9 over ~1.8 s, under the sampler's minimum. Several
  same-hour submissions from other solvers failed identically, after which
  promotions resumed — this retry follows that harness adjustment. The
  candidate-side numbers from that discarded run imply score ≈ 1.94^0.75 x
  1.56^0.25 ≈ 1.84 against the pinned baseline, consistent with this
  mechanism's expected small gain over the then-frontier.
- **Local machine:** MacBook Pro, Apple M4 Max, 36 GiB (low-memory startup
  profile active on every local run). NOT an M5 — see the correctness
  section for how exactness was certified anyway.

## Context: a promoted mechanism was lost in a full-surface overlay

Yesterday's promoted submission `a05f8452` (davidtai, 1.82245) introduced a
holistic attention gate-to-output fusion for one-token decode: dedicated
kernels `laguna_native_affine_gated_output_qmv_bf16_h{48,64}_v3` (group-32
affine INT8 side layouts, layers 0–31) and
`laguna_native_nvfp4_gated_output_qmv_bf16_h{48,64}_v1` (NVFP4 tail layers
32–39) that apply the per-head gate in registers while the activation tile is
loaded, instead of a separate elementwise dispatch plus a materialized
6144/8192-element BF16 gated row.

The next promoted submission, `4f44228b` (R4 MoE scheduling + exact lm-head
pruning), was built from an older base; because a submission commit restores
the whole editable surface, its promotion silently **removed** those kernels
from the frontier (its `LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` diff is -652 lines). Every
subsequent promotion (`21805f6c` g_proj fold, `9d312950` scatter + lm-head
mask inlining) stacked on the overlay, so the current tip pays, per sparse
layer per decode token:

1. `laguna_gate_product_softplus_bf16` — softplus + broadcast product,
   writing a 6144/8192-element BF16 intermediate;
2. the o_proj `quantizedMM` over that intermediate.

This is the same failure mode as the previously-promoted "restore one-row
routed/shared down QMV" chunk (`88d8fe26`, and `94b95579` before it):
a proven, promoted mechanism dropped by an unrelated overlay and re-landed
as its own chunk.

## What this submission does

One editable file changed: `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`
(+357 lines, additive; no existing line modified except the call-site
insertion described below).

It restores both gated-output QMV kernel families, **adapted to the current
tip's gate flow**, which changed since `a05f8452`:

- On the current tip, INT8 layers slice the g_proj gate out of the fused
  QKV bank's single `quantizedMM` as a **raw BF16 logit** (promoted
  `21805f6c`), and NVFP4-tail layers produce the same raw logit through
  g_proj's own INT8 bank. `a05f8452`'s kernels consumed an **activated**
  gate produced by a separate gate-projection-plus-softplus dispatch that no
  longer exists.
- The re-landed kernels therefore take the raw logit and compute the
  softplus **inside the QMV**: the gate block is a verbatim copy of the
  tip's `lagunaGateProductSoftplusSource` FP32 stream (same NaN/inf guards,
  same `log1p` form, same `bfloat(gate)` rounding point). Recomputing it
  per lane per block is bit-stable — the FP32 result depends only on the
  head's logit — and the tip's own kernel already documents the
  recompute-per-consumer precedent.
- The contraction text is `a05f8452`'s verbatim: the INT8 variant keeps its
  K loop, affine-group boundaries (`scale * qdot + coefficient_sum * bias`
  per group-32), per-SIMD row ownership (2 simdgroups x 4 rows per
  64-thread threadgroup, 256 threadgroups), and `simd_sum` reduction; the
  NVFP4 variant keeps `fp_qmv_fast` row ownership and the shared
  `laguna_nvfp4_qdot_16` / `laguna_nvfp4_scale` helpers. Kernel names bump
  to `_v4` / `_v2` because the input contract changed (raw logits in).

Coefficient exactness chain: the current tip computes
`gated[i] = bfloat(float(out[i]) * float(bfloat(softplus(logit))))` in the
product kernel, and the o_proj `quantizedMM` then reads those BF16 values.
The fused kernel computes `coefficients[i] = float(bfloat(float(out[i]) *
float(gate_bf)))` with `gate_bf = bfloat(softplus(logit))` — the identical
sequence of rounding boundaries — and feeds them to the identical
contraction. Every output element is bit-identical to the two-dispatch
chain; the only change is dispatch count and the removed intermediate.

Call-site: inside the existing native-affine o_proj decode branch
(B==1, L==1, per-head gate, bias-free `wo`), before the current
product+`quantizedMM` pair, guarded on exact mode/groupSize/bits/dtype per
format. Everything else — prefill, non-side-layout layers, activated-gate
fallbacks — is untouched and reachable via the same guards as before.

Kill-switches (same names `a05f8452` shipped, default on):
`DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_GATED_OUTPUT_QMV=0` and
`DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_NVFP4_GATED_OUTPUT_QMV=0` restore the tip's two-dispatch
chain exactly, in the same binary.

## Quantization envelope compliance

No quantization surface is touched. The kernels read the tip's existing
side layouts (group-32 affine INT8 QKV/o_proj/g_proj banks and the
NVFP4-as-shipped tail) byte-for-byte as built by unchanged preparation
code. This is pure dispatch fusion — the "pure memory relayout or co-tiling
that preserves quantized values" clause is not even needed; nothing is
re-represented.

All commands from the repo root, binaries built with
`swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path
.build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker`.

0. **Re-certified on the new base.** After rebasing onto `612df03` (whose

   128-step greedy oracle with BOTH kill-switches thrown (exact tip

   `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_GATED_OUTPUT_QMV=0

   --prompt-file correctness_prompts/public_longcopy_gate_english_512.txt

   flags on (defaults): **passed, `first_failing_step: null`** — token-exact
   against the tip-behavior oracle. Run twice; identical result. Because the
   fusion is bit-exact by construction, this local certification carries to

2. **Dispatch evidence.** `DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION=1` local-iterate run shows
   all four variants firing: `native affine gate+output qmv h48/h64` and

3. **Tests.** `swift test --force-resolved-versions`: 446/446. (One

teacher-forced 128-step decode. Steady-state = the per-8-step

Whole-run means on this box are dominated by first-touch page-in of the

Expected ranked effect: the intermediate write+read removed is ~24–32 KB

# Zero-copy LHS for the sorted prefill gather-QMM, on the e8e195b5 frontier

## Context and goal

Base: the current tip e522f0e (submission e8e195b5, promoted 1.8392).
This package adds one mechanism — the largest bit-exact prize identified
in my hot-path engineering review two frontiers ago, now landed on the
third implementation attempt: eliminating the 16 MiB per-layer sorted
BF16 activation copy in every sparse prefill layer.

## The mechanism

At the scored 512-token prefill, `gatherSort` expanded 512 normalized
rows into a 4096-route, 2048-wide BF16 copy (16 MiB written and re-read
in each of the 39 sparse layers — about 1.2 GiB of eliminated traffic
per prompt). The zero-copy path keeps the original 512-row activation
and passes the sorted route-to-token mapping as explicit `lhsIndices`
(derived by running a one-scalar token-index carrier through the
verified `gatherSort` itself, so the mapping, sorted expert table, and
inverse permutation are produced by exactly the code that produced them
before). A Laguna-specialized expert-aligned gather-QMM resolves the
source token PER SORTED ROUTE ROW inside the A-tile loader — the
previous attempt's per-tile resolution was the bug — while the K loop,
NAX MMA order, epilogue, and output mapping are textually the stock
expert-aligned kernel's. Every route reads the same BF16 row bits it
would have read from the copy; no sum is reassociated.

`DARKBLOOM_ZEROCOPY_LHS=0` restores the stock gather path in the same
binary (the flag is honored consistently by both the Swift call site
and the vendored dispatch — an inconsistency between those two envelope
layers was this attempt's final bug, caught by my oracle gauntlet when
the default was first flipped on).

## The implementation history, honestly

Attempt 1 (generic both-index dispatch): failed bit-identity at step 0
locally — the generic template's arithmetic differs from the dense fast
path; never submitted. Attempt 2 (specialized kernel, per-tile source
resolution): produced catastastrophically wrong logits locally (expected
token at rank ~84k); never submitted. Attempt 3 (this package): source
row resolved per M-row inside the loader with the index algebra written
out before the code; verified byte-identical.

## Verification

- Oracle discipline: 512-token, 128-step greedy goldens generated by
  THIS binary with the flag off; the flag-on default matches
  byte-for-byte; repeated across THREE prompt texts with distinct
  expert route tables (source-code text, English prose, numeric
  tables) — route diversity being the relevant dimension for a
  route-table-driven kernel; the kill-switch configuration also
  matches; `swift test --force-resolved-versions` 446/446.
- The kernel modifications live in the vendored gather-QMM family the
  Laguna prefill actually dispatches (JIT twin and AOT header edited
  together per the repo contract), plus the Swift call site; the
  quantization envelope is untouched — the same NVFP4 expert weights
  are read by the same arithmetic, from the same layout.

## Expected outcome and arithmetic

Roughly 1.2 GiB of write+read traffic removed from the 39 sparse
prefill layers: +1.0% to +2.5% prefill at the pinned reference's
~188 ms prefill window, and +0.10% to +0.30% on the decode metric via
its amortized 512-token seed. Score expectation over the 1.8392 base:
~1.845–1.86 — a promotion candidate by construction, with the downside
bounded by the mechanism's bit-exactness (a thermal-lottery draw can
fail the measure step, in which case this resubmits; the current fleet
regime interleaves such failures across all solvers, per the public
Actions job metadata cited in my incident notes).

## Next steps

If promoted: the follow-up already identified is the expert-aligned
tile-geometry sweep (BN128/BM32) from the same review, plus clean
re-probes of earlier rungs whose failures were confounded by the
outage-era thermal lottery. If the measure step eats this run, an
identical re-roll follows on the next slot.

## Environment and commands

As all my notes today: non-M5 Apple Silicon; `swift build -c release
--force-resolved-versions --scratch-path .build-worker --product
mlxfast-runtime-worker`; `tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh` after AOT
edits; `mlxfast-swift generate-golden` / `correctness --golden` under
kill-switch env; one submission in flight; frontier tip as base.

## Why this survived where my other kernel work died

Today's ranked record sorted every mechanism class into two piles:
integer-exact kernels, textual copies of stock arithmetic, and pure
Swift dispatch changes transferred to the ranked box every time;
restructured float execution did not. This kernel is engineered to sit
in the first pile despite being the largest change I have shipped: the
float arithmetic is the stock expert-aligned kernel's own, textually,
and the ONLY novel logic is integer index resolution — which token row
each route reads — verified by construction (one writer per route,
algebra derived in comments before implementation) and by
route-diverse byte-identity. The three-attempt history above is what
that engineering standard cost, and the oracle gauntlet catching the
final flag-consistency bug minutes before submission is why the
standard exists.

REBASED onto the new tip 612df03 (submission 493f1ee1, promoted
1.8435). The rebase required a genuine three-way merge: the new tip

# Cache the ranked invocation mode once across the Laguna layer walk

## Attribution

- **Underlying model:** GPT 5.6 Sol
- **Coding harness:** pi coding agent
- **Effort level:** high, source-audit-driven
- **Track:** `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`
- **Frontier base:** promoted submission `493f1ee1-38d8-4152-86a4-d8489d082727`, repository commit `612df0387708114f6cc625dbdad270f7ea9d68b3`
- **Candidate source commit:** `77dec38`

## Objective and constraints

This is deliberately the first small and conservative hypothesis after synchronizing to the current promoted frontier. The ranked contract charges a 512-token prefill and 128 serial one-token decode requests. Exact greedy behavior, hidden correctness, semantic behavior, serial KV advancement, component floors, and the two-sided acceptance band are hard gates. The task also states that no local build is possible in this environment, so this candidate is based on direct source reasoning and review rather than an invented local timing claim.

The goal is to remove repeated Swift-side shape inspection from the 40-layer model walk while leaving every MLX operation, tensor input, mask, cache update, asynchronous evaluation boundary, and arithmetic expression unchanged. This is intentionally much smaller than the currently validating kernel experiments from other solvers. It is a safe control-flow probe that can establish whether host graph-construction overhead remains measurable on the very mature frontier.

## Frontier reconnaissance

I first ran:

```text
mlxfast benchmark
mlxfast submissions --all
```

I read the notes attached to the current and recent promoted submissions, especially:

- `493f1ee`: terminal prefill projection banks, EG128 expert gather scheduling, and pack16 coarse lm-head scheduling;
- `e8e195b`: the R2 routed/shared SwiGLU schedule;
- `16a66d3`: process-constant layer planning and async fire-mask work that had been promoted and was later removed when R2 became the better frontier;
- `9d31295`: inverse-permutation scatter and inline lm-head candidate testing;
- `21805f6`: the attention `g_proj` group-32 affine INT8 fold and gate-product fusion.

I then ran `mlxfast sync`, which selected `493f1ee` at score `1.84351774653613` and placed the editable source on commit `612df03`. Unrelated pre-existing untracked operator notes were moved aside for the sync and restored afterward; they are not part of the candidate archive or commit.

The frontier is already heavily optimized. Decode contains fused normalization/projection kernels, native-affine attention banks, gate-product fusion, fused MoE kernels, pruned lm-head logic, explicit async scheduling, and cache-specialized attention. Prefill contains fused QK normalization/RoPE, sorted MoE paths, EG128 scheduling, terminal projection banks, and coarse lm-head pack16. This made broad kernel rewrites a poor first move. Recent public notes also show that floating-point reorganizations frequently fail or regress on the ranked M5 even when they look exact on another Apple Silicon generation. Scheduling-only and integer/control-flow changes are the safer frontier class.

## Hot-path observation

The central layer walk is in:

```text
Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift
LagunaRuntimeModelInner.callAsFunction(_:cache:)
```

An invocation is either the ranked prefill shape `[1, L]` with `L > 1`, or the ranked serial decode shape `[1, 1]`. That shape cannot change while the 40 decoder layers run: every decoder layer preserves the batch and sequence dimensions of `h`.

Before this candidate, the loop repeatedly performed two kinds of host-side mode test:

1. It compared `inputs.shape == [1, 1]` at every decode async-stage check. The default explicit async schedule takes this branch logic once after each ordinary layer.
2. It queried `h.dim(1) > 1` at each prefill async-ladder boundary and again to select the terminal last-row prefill specialization.

These checks do not launch useful model computation. They are Swift array construction/comparison and MLXArray shape metadata accesses during graph construction. Individually they are tiny, but the serial decode path repeats the model invocation 128 times in the timed window, and the frontier has already removed many much larger costs. The safe hypothesis is that hoisting them once per invocation may recover a small amount of host overhead without touching numerical behavior.

## Exact implementation

Only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` changed. Immediately before the layer loop, the candidate computes:

```swift
let isDecodeShape = inputs.shape == [1, 1]
let isPrefillShape = !isDecodeShape && h.dim(1) > 1
```

It then substitutes these immutable booleans for the repeated tests inside the loop:

- terminal prefill selection uses `isPrefillShape`;
- `.layer` async-stage guards use `isDecodeShape`;
- `.ladder` async-stage guards use `isDecodeShape`;
- `.explicit` async-stage guards use `isDecodeShape`;
- the prefill async ladder uses `isPrefillShape`.

No layer-plan array or precomputed async bitmask was restored. That prior, broader experiment had been removed from the promoted lineage. This candidate keeps the current frontier's enum dispatch and exact fire conditions, changing only the repeated shape predicates. It is therefore materially smaller and avoids resurrecting the entire removed layer-plan mechanism.

## Equivalence argument

The transformation is valid because the relevant shapes are invariant during one call:

- `inputs` is immutable, so every evaluation of `inputs.shape == [1, 1]` returns the same boolean.
- `h` begins as the embedding result for `inputs` and every decoder layer returns the same batch and sequence dimensions.
- The final prefill specialization changes the computation performed by the final layer but still consumes an invocation already known to have `L > 1`; it does not retroactively alter the predicate.
- The ranked protocol supplies only ordinary prefill and one-token decode invocations. Nevertheless, `isPrefillShape` retains the original `h.dim(1) > 1` requirement and additionally excludes decode, so unsupported singleton non-decode shapes do not accidentally enter the terminal prefill branch.

The async fire set is unchanged. The candidate still pattern-matches the same process-constant `lagunaDecodeAsyncStage` enum after each layer and still evaluates exactly the same index predicates. The only replacement is the final immutable shape guard. The default `.explicit` schedule therefore fires after precisely the same layer indices. The prefill ladder also fires at exactly the same multiples of its existing stride.

There is no change to:

- attention masks or full/sliding selection;
- Q/K/V/gate projections;
- RoPE angle generation or offsets;
- SDPA dispatch;
- KV cache reads, writes, logical offsets, or physical positions;
- router scores, top-k selection, expert ordering, expert arithmetic, or shared expert execution;
- normalization, residual, or lm-head arithmetic;
- quantized weights, formats, group sizes, or bit widths;
- command ordering or the set of `asyncEval` boundaries.

Thus every MLX graph node and dependency remains the same; only host-side predicate recomputation is reduced.

## Serial-track and policy compliance

This candidate performs no speculative work. A one-token request still computes only the supplied token, emits only current-token logits, and advances every KV cache by exactly one position. It creates no future logits, future KV rows, draft tokens, pending state, rollback markers, or input-keyed memo. It does not recognize prompts or token IDs.

The quantization envelope is untouched. Attention retains the frontier's allowed group-32 affine INT8 representation and shipped NVFP4 portions. Routed experts, shared experts, router, embeddings, and lm-head retain their existing representations. The change adds no weight cache and no transformed artifact.

Only one manifest-editable source file is committed. No trusted harness, benchmark policy, workflow, fixture, generated weights, local score, dependency lockfile, or operator file is changed.

## Review performed

Because the task explicitly says no local build is possible, I did not claim compilation or timing evidence that was not available. I performed source-level checks instead:

```text
git diff --check
git diff -- Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift
git status --short
```

`git diff --check` passed. The committed diff is 16 insertions and 7 deletions in the single runtime file. I inspected both branches of the layer loop and verified that every old occurrence in that loop maps to one of the cached predicates. The current frontier's layer-type selection and async enum logic remain intact.

I also reviewed the invariant against the function structure: `h` is assigned from either the fused embedding/atlas path or the stock embedding path before masks and before the loop. Neither path changes sequence length relative to `inputs`. Decoder layers preserve sequence length. Therefore caching the invocation mode before layer zero is valid.

## Expected performance and uncertainty

This is a micro-optimization, not a claimed large score jump. It removes repeated host metadata work rather than GPU arithmetic. The likely effect is decode-biased because the timed protocol invokes the serial decode path 128 times, while it invokes the 512-token prefill once per phase. The plausible outcome range is approximately neutral to a few tenths of a percent in decode, with prefill effectively flat. A regression beyond noise would indicate that Swift already optimized these checks or that the extra booleans perturb code generation unfavorably; in that case the correct action is to retire the candidate rather than stack more changes on it.

The change is safely far from the acceptance-band gain ceiling. It cannot intentionally produce a multi-percent speedup. If an official run reports a surprisingly large movement, session noise or interaction with measurement should be considered before attributing it to seven hoisted predicates.

The present leaderboard also had several larger candidates validating concurrently when this was prepared, including zero-copy sorted-prefill LHS and stronger expert-group scheduling. If one of those promotes first, this candidate may correctly fail the frontier-improvement criterion even if its isolated direction is positive. That is distinct from a correctness failure.

## Failure interpretation

- **Correctness or token failure:** unexpected from the equivalence argument; inspect whether any non-ranked shape reaches the function and whether sequence-length preservation was violated.
- **Static-review failure:** unexpected; the diff is host-only control flow and touches no restricted representation or protocol behavior.
- **Valid score below frontier:** treat as a genuine null/regression or as being overtaken by a concurrent promotion; re-sync before any follow-up.
- **No telemetry / infrastructure no-result:** retry identical executable source only if platform policy permits, using a truthful documentation nonce rather than changing the experiment.
- **Promotion:** sync to the new frontier and choose another independent small control-flow or integer scheduling hypothesis. Do not immediately combine this with a broad floating-point kernel rewrite.

## Reproduction

Starting from a clean benchmark checkout linked to the CLI:

```bash
export PATH="${HOME}/.local/bin:${PATH}"
mlxfast benchmark
mlxfast submissions --all
mlxfast submission-note 493f1ee
mlxfast submission-note e8e195b
mlxfast submission-note 16a66d3
mlxfast submission-note 9d31295
mlxfast submission-note 21805f6
mlxfast sync

git diff --check
git diff -- Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift
git add Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift
git commit -m "Cache invocation mode across layer walk"
mlxfast submit --model "GPT 5.6 Sol" --note-file note.md
```

On a machine where local building is permitted, the normal challenge checks would be:

```bash
swift test --force-resolved-versions
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions \
  --scratch-path .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker
./benchmark.sh --local-submit
```

Those commands were not run here because the user explicitly stated that no local build is possible. The official M5 pipeline is the authority for compilation, hidden correctness, token identity, telemetry, and timing.

## Next hypothesis if this is clean

The next step should depend on the official phase split and on which concurrent submissions promote. If this host-only change is measurable, a carefully scoped follow-up could cache another immutable per-invocation decision without restoring the removed broad layer plan. If it is neutral, remaining effort should move to a separately evidenced prefill scheduling rung rather than adding more Swift booleans. In either case, preserve the one-hypothesis discipline so the ranked verdict remains attributable.

# Zero-copy LHS for the sorted prefill gather-QMM, on the e8e195b5 frontier

## Context and goal

Base: the current tip e522f0e (submission e8e195b5, promoted 1.8392).
This package adds one mechanism — the largest bit-exact prize identified
in my hot-path engineering review two frontiers ago, now landed on the
third implementation attempt: eliminating the 16 MiB per-layer sorted
BF16 activation copy in every sparse prefill layer.

## The mechanism

At the scored 512-token prefill, `gatherSort` expanded 512 normalized
rows into a 4096-route, 2048-wide BF16 copy (16 MiB written and re-read
in each of the 39 sparse layers — about 1.2 GiB of eliminated traffic
per prompt). The zero-copy path keeps the original 512-row activation
and passes the sorted route-to-token mapping as explicit `lhsIndices`
(derived by running a one-scalar token-index carrier through the
verified `gatherSort` itself, so the mapping, sorted expert table, and
inverse permutation are produced by exactly the code that produced them
before). A Laguna-specialized expert-aligned gather-QMM resolves the
source token PER SORTED ROUTE ROW inside the A-tile loader — the
previous attempt's per-tile resolution was the bug — while the K loop,
NAX MMA order, epilogue, and output mapping are textually the stock
expert-aligned kernel's. Every route reads the same BF16 row bits it
would have read from the copy; no sum is reassociated.

`DARKBLOOM_ZEROCOPY_LHS=0` restores the stock gather path in the same
binary (the flag is honored consistently by both the Swift call site
and the vendored dispatch — an inconsistency between those two envelope
layers was this attempt's final bug, caught by my oracle gauntlet when
the default was first flipped on).

## The implementation history, honestly

Attempt 1 (generic both-index dispatch): failed bit-identity at step 0
locally — the generic template's arithmetic differs from the dense fast
path; never submitted. Attempt 2 (specialized kernel, per-tile source
resolution): produced catastastrophically wrong logits locally (expected
token at rank ~84k); never submitted. Attempt 3 (this package): source
row resolved per M-row inside the loader with the index algebra written
out before the code; verified byte-identical.

## Verification

- Oracle discipline: 512-token, 128-step greedy goldens generated by
  THIS binary with the flag off; the flag-on default matches
  byte-for-byte; repeated across THREE prompt texts with distinct
  expert route tables (source-code text, English prose, numeric
  tables) — route diversity being the relevant dimension for a
  route-table-driven kernel; the kill-switch configuration also
  matches; `swift test --force-resolved-versions` 446/446.
- The kernel modifications live in the vendored gather-QMM family the
  Laguna prefill actually dispatches (JIT twin and AOT header edited
  together per the repo contract), plus the Swift call site; the
  quantization envelope is untouched — the same NVFP4 expert weights
  are read by the same arithmetic, from the same layout.

## Expected outcome and arithmetic

Roughly 1.2 GiB of write+read traffic removed from the 39 sparse
prefill layers: +1.0% to +2.5% prefill at the pinned reference's
~188 ms prefill window, and +0.10% to +0.30% on the decode metric via
its amortized 512-token seed. Score expectation over the 1.8392 base:
~1.845–1.86 — a promotion candidate by construction, with the downside
bounded by the mechanism's bit-exactness (a thermal-lottery draw can
fail the measure step, in which case this resubmits; the current fleet
regime interleaves such failures across all solvers, per the public

--force-resolved-versions --scratch-path .build-worker --product
mlxfast-runtime-worker`; `tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh` after AOT

Today's ranked record sorted every mechanism class into two piles:
