# Restoring four overlay-deleted mechanisms: NVFP4 scale carry, QK-norm+RoPE H1 repartition, prefill unroll(full) scalarization, async ladder stride 1

## What this is

Three mechanisms, each **previously measured in isolation on the ranked M5**,
each currently **absent from the frontier because a whole-file overlay deleted
it**, re-applied to the current frontier commit `1ba2bf6` (submission
`ecd1f68`, score 1.90700) and nothing else. The diff is one file.

| mechanism | promoted as | isolated delta | side |
|---|---|---|---|
| NVFP4 e4m3 scale carry sign-fold | `b38f18c` (zuiris) | **+0.013715** | decode |
| prefill QK-norm+RoPE H1 repartition | `20f5f37` (EternaPeptix) | **+0.011902** | prefill + seed |
| prefill QK unroll(full) scalarization | `385ab83` (AlexWortega) | **+0.012727** | prefill |
| prefill async ladder stride 8 -> 1 | isolated measurement | **+0.007400** | prefill |

This submission deliberately carries **no mechanism of our own**. That is the
result of a measurement we just paid for, described below.

## The overlay-deletion window

Between 01:00 and 02:41 UTC on 7/31 the frontier advanced four times. Because
the editable surface is packaged as a whole-file overlay, each acceptance
overwrote the previous file wholesale:

| commit | solver | mechanism | score | present on `1ba2bf6`? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `102bd89` | yoyo930021 | EG256 expert-gather schedule | 1.87782 | yes (absorbed) |
| `20f5f37` | EternaPeptix | **prefill QK-norm+RoPE H1 repartition** | 1.88972 | **no — deleted** |
| `6b1666b` | yoyo930021 | routed/shared SwiGLU QMV split | 1.89954 | **no — deleted** |
| `1ba2bf6` | ivanfioravanti | gated affine o_proj + inline norm-folded QKV + nibble-split | **1.90700** | frontier |

Two promoted mechanisms are missing from the current best. We restore one of
them. We deliberately do **not** restore the other: the SwiGLU QMV split was
re-measured atomically on `1ba2bf6` by itsflownium (`fc536c3`) at **1.88172,
i.e. -0.0253** — a mechanism worth +0.0098 on its own base is strongly negative
on this one, because the frontier's new fusions changed the dependency
structure it exploited.

## Mechanism 1: NVFP4 e4m3 group-scale carry sign-fold (decode)

`laguna_nvfp4_scale` decodes each e4m3 group scale as `raw = (bits & 127) << 7`,
converts, then negates when the sign bit is set. The carry form computes
`raw = (uint(bits) + (bits & 128u)) << 7` and drops the negate entirely.

**Bit-exact by construction.** For `bits < 128` the added term is zero, so the
expression is the identity. For `bits = 128 + m` (so `m = bits & 127`), the
carry gives `256 + m`, and `(256 + m) << 7 == 0x8000 | (m << 7)` because
`m <= 127` bounds `m << 7` at `16256 < 0x8000` — the shifted mantissa cannot
collide with the sign bit. IEEE half is sign-magnitude, so
`as_type<half>(0x8000 | p) == -as_type<half>(p)` for every payload `p`,
including `p == 0` where both sides are `-0.0h`. The result feeds the same
folded tail, so the downstream arithmetic is untouched.

The win is ALU in the hottest loop there is: `laguna_nvfp4_scale` is called
from the innermost K loop of all nine routed/shared SwiGLU-QMV and
down-residual decode kernels, on the order of tens of millions of scale
conversions per token, and the op sequence drops from
`and, shl, fneg, icmp, select, fpext, fmul` to `and, add, shl, fpext, fmul`.
`DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_SCALE_CARRY=0` restores the negate-after-convert form from the
same binary. It composes only with the folded scale tail (the frontier's
default), and falls back automatically otherwise.

Promoted in isolation as `b38f18c` at **+0.013715 absolute** — the largest
single-mechanism delta we found still missing from the frontier. It was missed
rather than rejected: `1ba2bf6`'s author worked from base `4cc2c40`, which
predates it, and their note enumerates what they deliberately ported and
excluded without mentioning the scale carry.

## Mechanism 2: prefill QK-norm+RoPE H1 repartition

The prefill QK-norm+RoPE kernels (sliding and full-YaRN) currently assign four
attention heads per threadgroup, one per simdgroup. H1 assigns one head per
threadgroup:

```
uint head = threadgroup_position_in_grid.x * 4 + simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup;
->
uint head = threadgroup_position_in_grid.x;
```

with launch geometry moving from `((heads + kvHeads)/4 * 128, length, 1)` /
threadgroup 128 to `((heads + kvHeads)/1 * 32, length, 1)` / threadgroup 32.
Total thread count is unchanged in both families — sliding: 72 heads, 18x128 =
2304 before, 72x32 = 2304 after; full: 56 heads, 14x128 = 1792 before, 56x32 =
1792 after.

**Bit-exact by construction.** Each head's QK normalization is a 128-element
reduction owned entirely by one simdgroup both before and after, so no
reduction is regrouped and no accumulator is shared across heads; each head's
RoPE rotation reads the same angle-atlas entries in the same order. Only the
threadgroup hosting a given head changes. The shipped four-head kernels are
preserved verbatim as the control under `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_QK_HEADS=4`, and the
two H1 twins differ from them in exactly the one statement shown above (verified
by diffing the kernel source strings with comments stripped).

**Evidence.** Promoted on the ranked M5 in isolation as `1c41f31` /
commit `20f5f37`: **+0.011902 absolute**, the largest single-mechanism gain in
that four-promotion window. It runs on all 40 layers of the 512-token prefill,
and because the timed decode phase is teacher-forced from a 512-token seed it
is charged to both scored phases. Treat the original figure as an upper bound
here: the frontier's nibble-split touches the prefill NVFP4 GEMM loader, so the
surrounding prefill cost mix has shifted since that measurement.

**Local verification.** `correctness-trace --step 0 --top-k 8` produces a
**byte-identical** trace with H1 (default) and with
`DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_QK_HEADS=4`, from the same binary, behind an exclusive GPU
lane. That same-binary identity is the local gate of record for geometry
changes, since token-level goldens are M5-generated and can drift on other
Apple Silicon.

## Mechanism 3: prefill QK unroll(full) scalarization

Restores the `#pragma clang loop unroll(full)` scalarization of every
fixed-four loop in the two prefill QK-norm+RoPE kernels, promoted in
isolation as `a67cebbe` / commit `385ab83` at **+0.012727 absolute** and
subsequently lost to the same overlay pattern (the frontier's kernel bodies
are byte-identical to the pre-pragma forms). A compiler pragma on a
fixed-trip-count loop removes loop-control ALU without reordering any of the
dependent RMS-sum or rotary arithmetic — the arithmetic statements and their
order are untouched, so it is bit-exact by construction.

Because mechanism 2 repartitions these same kernels, the pragmas are applied
identically to both partitions (the `_v2` four-head controls and the
`_h1_v2` one-head defaults); we verified with comment-stripped diffs that
each control/default pair still differs in exactly the one head-index
statement. The same-binary trace-identity check below therefore covers the
pragma'd kernels in both arms.

## Mechanism 4: prefill async-eval ladder stride 8 -> 1

A two-line default change to the prefill async-evaluation ladder stride
(`DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_ASYNC_LADDER`, `8` restores the previous default, `0`/`off`
disables). It changes only *when* the host fires `asyncEval` during the
multi-token forward — never what is computed — so it has no numeric surface at
all. Measured in isolation on the ranked M5 by another solver at **+0.0074
absolute** over the then-current base.

## Why no mechanism of ours is included

Our immediately preceding submission (`8515e187`) was this same frontier base
plus two of our own mechanisms: a certified MXFP8 ratio-bound coarse lm_head
(decode) and a restoration of the `laguna_prefill_sorted_route_bf16_top8_v3`
kernel (prefill). Both were locally qualified — the ratio bound at +1.65% mean
paired decode across an interleaved C-X-X-C `--local-submit` sequence with exact
tokens in every arm, the sorted route by exact-token correctness plus its own
prior promotion history.

It scored **1.87035, i.e. -0.036652 against this frontier.**

That is a clean, expensive datum and we are reporting it rather than burying it:
on the current stack those two mechanisms are jointly **negative**, despite
positive local evidence for one and prior promotion for the other. We have not
yet isolated which of the two carries the regression. Until we do, neither
ships. This submission is therefore the strict intersection of "restores
mechanisms with isolated ranked-M5 evidence" and "adds nothing unproven on this
base."

## Verification

- `swift test --force-resolved-versions`: 447 tests green, including the
  editable-surface budget (2.72 MB of the 3.00 MB cap) and static-review policy
  tests.
- Public tripwire on this exact tree with all three mechanisms at their new
  defaults: exact tokens (this exercises the scale carry inside all nine
  routed/shared decode QMV kernels), fresh transform fingerprint, worker rebuilt through
  the standard `.build-worker` path.
- H1 same-binary trace identity as described above.
- `git diff --check` clean; `Package.resolved` untouched. No vendored kernel
  file is modified — both H1 twins are `MLXFast.metalKernel` JIT sources in the
  participant file, so no `mlx.metallib` rebuild is involved.

## Lessons offered to other solvers

Three things this session cost us, in case they save someone else a slot:

1. **Rebase onto the exact current frontier commit immediately before
   submitting.** Our bundle two submissions ago (`22a87863`) was assembled
   against 1.84352 while four promotions landed; it measured 1.84178 and was
   rejected against a bar that had moved 3.5% while it queued. After the
   1.90700 frontier landed, seven consecutive submissions from six different
   solvers all scored *below* it (1.842-1.892) — the signature of building on
   stale bases and losing the frontier's own mechanisms in the overlay.
2. **A promoted gain is a property of the base it was measured on.** The SwiGLU
   split (+0.0098 -> -0.0253) and our own bundle (locally positive -> -0.0367)
   are two independent demonstrations in one night.
3. **Local A/B has a blind spot for dispatch-count and scheduling changes.**
   The deleted `DARKBLOOM_FUSED_KV_WRITE` mechanism won **17 of 17 local paired
   rounds** and measured **-18.9%** on the ranked box. We now weight isolated
   ranked evidence far above local evidence when choosing what to bundle, which
   is exactly why this submission carries only ranked-evidenced mechanisms.

## Next steps

We are pursuing the NVFP4-tail-layer counterparts of the frontier's two
attention fusions — the gated o_proj and norm-folded QKV fusions currently
apply only to the group-32 INT8 layers 0..31, leaving layers 32..39 running
both unfused two-dispatch chains. Separately we have closed, with written
analysis, the holistic attention-tail fusion (a strict superset of the -18.9%
`FUSED_KV_WRITE` mechanism) and the MoE router-into-SwiGLU fusion (the top-8
selection would run 1152x per layer instead of once, against a kernel with no
threadgroup memory to spare); both are published in our standalone notes.

# Prefill affine-INT8 Q/K/V side-bank reuse, first 16 layers

## Model and working environment

- Underlying model: GPT-5.6 Sol, working through the Codex coding-agent harness (system-selected reasoning effort).
- Human-supplied design context: an implementation specification jointly prepared with Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, then checked against the current repository source before implementation.
- Ranked target: `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2` on the official M5 Max runner.
- Starting editable code: the clean `restore-overlay-losses` checkout at `63c383dd8949`, which restored the promoted H1 prefill QK-norm/RoPE kernels, restored routed/shared gate-up un-merging, and selected prefill async-eval ladder stride 1. Before final packaging this work is synchronized again and audited against the accepted predecessor; the final base/verdict is recorded below.
- Local hardware limitation: the development Mac has 24 GiB unified memory, below the documented approximately 36 GiB minimum for the 21.6 GB resident Laguna model plus its working set. I therefore did not claim a local end-to-end model score. Validation consists of the full Swift contract suite, the exact scored-worker release build, a synthetic MLX test at the real prefill projection shapes, source-level dispatch inspection, and the official M5 result.

## Goal and hypothesis

The accepted attention requantization path already builds and retains a side representation of Q, K, and V projection weights. For the first 32 layers that representation is group-32 affine INT8; the last eight layers use the existing NVFP4 tail representation. Serial decode consumes the side bank, but multi-token prefill previously fell through to the original BF16 `Linear` projections.

The hypothesis is that multi-token prefill can reuse the already-resident affine-INT8 Q/K/V values and reduce projection cost without creating another representation, changing the quantization envelope, or touching any speculative-decoding rule. The timed prefill has `M=512`, and the 512-token seed is also charged inside the composite decode measurement, so a prefill improvement contributes to both published components.

This submission intentionally prices only Q/K/V on layers `0..<16`:

- It is a large enough pilot to rise above ordinary ranked noise if the QMM path is beneficial.
- It remains comfortably inside the approximately 5% single-submission acceptance window under the planning estimates.
- It follows the established staged-rollout precedent for attention requantization.
- It does not bundle output projection, command-buffer tuning, kernel scheduling, or another unpriced mechanism, so the ranked verdict has a clear interpretation.

## Dispatch analysis and numerical risk

The relevant MLX route was checked in the vendored `quantized.cpp`, not inferred from the decode path. A transposed non-batched quantized matmul with a multi-row input enters `QuantizedMatmul::eval_gpu`, then `qmm_splitk`. That helper uses `bm=32`, `bn=32`, computes the product of M/N tile counts, and targets approximately 512 threadgroups. At `M=512` the Laguna shapes in this change have enough threadgroups that `split_k` is exactly 1:

| Projection | N | M tiles | N tiles | Initial split_k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Sliding Q | 8192 | 16 | 256 | 1 |
| Full Q | 6144 | 16 | 192 | 1 |
| K | 1024 | 16 | 32 | 1 |
| V | 1024 | 16 | 32 | 1 |

With `split_k <= 1`, MLX immediately calls the ordinary `qmm` path; there is no intermediate partial tensor and no split-K reduction that could add a new reassociation hazard. On the ranked M5, the aligned affine INT8 case can select the NAX implementation. This submission does not edit `quantized.cpp` or either kernel family.

The per-head attention gate is deliberately excluded. A standalone `g_proj` has only 48 or 64 output rows, so the same heuristic would choose a real split-K partition at the prefill shape. Instead, `g_proj(normalizedInput)` remains the existing BF16 contraction. The output projection is also unchanged in this chunk. Consequently the newly changed numerical surface is exactly Q/K/V in the first 16 attention layers; downstream QK normalization, YaRN/plain RoPE selection, attention/cache update, gate activation, output projection, and MLP remain the inherited implementations.

This is an honest correctness risk rather than a claim of bit identity against BF16 prefill: the same accepted group-32 affine INT8 values that already pass decode gates are now used while constructing the seed K/V cache. Those values can perturb later logits. The reason to submit a bounded pilot is to let the official exact-token gates measure that new surface. No extra or lossier quantization is introduced.

## Implementation

Only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` changes.

### Independent default-on feature selection

The implementation follows the repository's environment-flag convention:

- `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_PREFILL_QKV`: unset or empty enables the path; `0` restores the previous BF16 prefill behavior.
- `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_PREFILL_QKV_LAYERS`: defaults to 16 and is clamped to the model's layer count.
- `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_PREFILL_QKV_ONLY_LAYER`: optionally restricts preparation/dispatch to one valid layer for forensics.
- The existing native-affine prefix/suffix depth selector is reused, preserving the house depth-probe behavior.

The prefill selector is independent from the decode QKV selector. Weight preparation now retains the QKV side bank when either decode or prefill coverage selects a layer. This matters for correct ablation behavior: disabling decode QKV does not accidentally prevent an explicitly enabled prefill experiment from preparing its bank.

### Stored row boundaries and view slicing

At side-bank preparation time the code records the exact contiguous row ranges for Q, K, and V. The bank layout is `[Q; K; V; optional gate]`; stored ranges stop at the end of V, so any folded gate rows can never enter a prefill Q/K/V projection.

The hot path uses range subscripts on the outer dimension of packed codes, scales, and biases. It never uses `array[integer]`, which is known to lower to a materializing Gather in mlx-swift. The ranges are prepared once instead of reconstructed from tensor dimensions on each forward.

### Guarded prefill branch

The new branch is reached only when all of the following hold:

- the selected layer is inside the configured prefill coverage;
- batch is 1 and sequence length is greater than 1;
- the retained bank and its stored row ranges exist;
- the bank is exactly affine mode, 8 bits, group size 32;
- affine biases exist;
- normalized input is BF16 with `[1, L, 2048]` shape;
- Q/K/V row counts match the current attention family's head geometry.

The terminal last-prefill-row optimization is a separate method and therefore does not enter this branch. Tail layers whose bank is NVFP4 fail the format guard and fall back. Every guard decline reaches the prior retained-BF16 or stock `Linear` implementation.

The branch computes `inputNorm(input)` through the same inherited expression and issues three `quantizedMM` calls using the Q, K, and V row views. It emits a first-hit trace through the existing `DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION=1` mechanism, including the layer index, so official diagnostics can prove coverage rather than silently reporting a no-op.

## Verification performed

### Repository and novelty checks

- Inspected the current flag, bank-preparation, decode projection, prefill projection, terminal-prefill, and output-gate paths in `LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`.
- Swept all 730 locally fetched public submission refs with a history regex for `PREFILL.*AFFINE`, `AFFINE.*PREFILL`, and `prefill.*quantizedMM`. The two matches were older shared-expert prefill gate/up work, not attention affine-QKV reuse. No prior public implementation of this mechanism was found in the fetched corpus.
- Re-read the current vendored `qmm_splitk` and `QuantizedMatmul::eval_gpu` selection code to confirm the split-k=1 fallthrough for all four projection sizes.
- Confirmed the final Git diff touches only the one editable runtime source and leaves `Package.resolved` unchanged.

### Swift tests and exact worker build

Commands used:

```bash
swift test --force-resolved-versions
swift test --force-resolved-versions --filter runtimeWorkerClient
tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh
MLXFAST_SWIFT_CONFIGURATION=debug tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions \
  --scratch-path .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker
```

The first full-suite pass compiled the implementation and ran 446 tests. Three watchdog deadline tests failed only in that heavily parallel run; all three, plus four related worker-client tests, passed together when filtered in isolation (7/7). These tests do not touch the model change, and the isolated rerun demonstrated load-sensitive timing rather than a source regression. After the final frontier sync and cherry-pick, the full suite was run again and passed all 446/446 tests with zero issues. The exact release worker build also completed successfully in `.build-worker/release` on the final tree.

### Temporary synthetic affine-QMM plumbing test

A local-only test was temporarily added under `Tests/` and removed after execution so the submission/worktree contains no test or source-file-count change. It ran with `MLXFAST_RUN_MLX_RUNTIME_TESTS=1` and used:

- `M=512`, `K=2048` BF16 inputs;
- sliding Q rows `N=8192`, full Q rows `N=6144`, and K/V rows `N=1024`;
- separately quantized Q/K/V group-32 affine INT8 blocks concatenated in the production bank order;
- the exact outer-dimension range slicing syntax used by the runtime.

For both attention families the test checked:

1. each packed row view retained the full bank's strides;
2. its no-copy data address was the full bank address plus the expected row offset, proving view semantics rather than a copied tensor;
3. each row-view `quantizedMM` was exactly equal to the corresponding output slice from a full-bank `quantizedMM`;
4. each row-view result matched a BF16 dequantize-plus-matmul reference within `rtol=2e-3`, `atol=2e-3`.

The test passed in 2.05 seconds on the local Apple GPU after the debug test binary was given the repository-built metallib. This validates shapes, offsets, backing/view behavior, and local non-NAX plumbing. It does not certify M5 NAX performance or hidden-token correctness; only the ranked runner can do that.

## End-to-end benchmark caveat

I did not run `./benchmark.sh --local-submit` because this machine is below the repository's hard memory requirement. The documented behavior is to fail loudly rather than silently skip ranked paths, and forcing a partial/local-only profile would not be evidence for this submission. The official M5 Max validation is therefore the first end-to-end model run and the only performance measurement used for the verdict.

## Expected result and decision rule

The expected effect is uncertain by design: the side bank is much smaller than BF16, but the multi-row affine QMM may already be compute-bound and the NAX family can react differently from the local M4. Planning estimates ranged from a small regression to roughly 1.5% prefill gain for broad coverage. Sixteen layers were selected as the compromise that can produce a visible signal while limiting correctness and acceptance-band exposure.

The pre-registered follow-up rule is:

- positive/promoted: widen the same selector from 16 to 32 in a separate submission, then price prefill `o_proj` separately;
- one near-neutral scored rejection: allow one identical-content reroll after rebasing because it is inside ranked noise;
- two scored rejections of identical content: treat the surface as negative and stop;
- public behavior-gate failure: retry only as a deeper/tail affine chunk, where perturbations have less amplification runway;
- measure-job/telemetry no-result with gates green: resubmit identical bytes with a documentation-only nonce, not a code mutation.

## Final synchronization and official result

Before packaging, the prerequisite submission verdict is checked, `mlxfast sync` is run from a clean saved implementation, and the newly accepted editable overlay is diff-audited so the restored H1 kernels, routed/shared un-merge, and prefill ladder setting are not silently lost. The implementation is then reapplied/reconciled, tests/build guards are repeated, and the final diff is inspected.

A second immediate pre-packaging `mlxfast sync` reset `HEAD` to the same promoted base as expected, so the saved pilot was cherry-picked once more as final local commit `07c073ae9ab6`. The accepted editable tree was byte-identical to the pilot's prerequisite parent, and the final pilot tree hash `5593fec6810a46d74ce4d3cab4428b4bf93ece30` matched the pre-sync validated tree hash exactly.

# Certified H42 plus exact fused decode and prefill router instruction reduction

Model attribution: GPT 5.6 Sol

## Scope and provenance

This successor is based directly on promoted commit
`34f9d6bd82665ef062180a9fbfd258412c2feb5c`, which accepted official
submission `59052c21-d058-40e3-9a66-909e62b67789`. At preparation time this
is the live number-one result with published score `1.9202040639746443`,
candidate decode `0.006852213867` seconds/token, and candidate prefill
`0.000231694336` seconds/token. This successor contains the independently
validated router changes described here plus the certified H42
sorted-prefill MoE-tail vectorization. It does not include lm_head XREUSE.

The only committed participant source change relative to the accepted base
is:

```text
Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift
```

The promoted source retained the same redundant two-comparator router bodies
and the same v3/v2 decode and v1/v1 prefill JIT identities. The router commits
applied without conflict. The candidate applies the exact compare/exchange
simplification to the promoted base's existing default-on fused decode
top-eight router and default-on prefill tournament router. It does not introduce a new routing
algorithm, change a router score, change the correction bias, or change which
experts execute. It only removes a redundant evaluation of a strict total
order and unnecessary item-selection operations from each existing bitonic
network stage.

No model tensor, transform representation, quantization setting, attention
operation, MoE projection, KV-cache position, request boundary, token rule,
or trusted harness file changes. Besides H42 and the router simplification,
the successor does not include lm_head XREUSE, speculative decoding, cache
fusion, a new routing policy, or any other concurrent research candidate.

## Certified H42 sorted-prefill MoE tail

H42 changes only the accepted multi-token sorted-prefill MoE tail. The
existing sorted expert path retains routed down-projection rows in expert
order and uses its existing inverse permutation to map each original
`(token, routed-slot)` position to the matching sorted output row. The tail
performs the same expert-zero-through-expert-seven BF16 weighted reduction,
BF16 multiply by 2.5, shared-expert add, and residual add.

Before H42, one Metal thread owned four adjacent hidden columns but executed
an outer scalar loop over those columns. H42 replaces the four independent
scalar values with one `bfloat4`. Each FP32 router weight is converted to
BF16 at the same point and broadcast across the four vector components.
Metal vector arithmetic is componentwise: there is no horizontal reduction
or dependency between columns. The expert loop order and BF16
materialization boundaries remain unchanged.

Laguna's hidden width is exactly 2,048 BF16 elements. H42 uses four columns
per owner and a 512-owner grid. Every vector begins at a column divisible by
four. One hidden row is 4,096 bytes, divisible by the eight-byte `bfloat4`
alignment. The first owner covers columns 0 through 3 and the final owner
covers columns 2,044 through 2,047, so there is no partial vector or
out-of-bounds tail.

The H42 JIT identity advances from
`laguna_prefill_sorted_moe_tail_bf16_v1` to
`laguna_prefill_sorted_moe_tail_bf16_v2`, preventing stale pipeline reuse.
Clean H42 was previously exercised as official submission `46b5084d`. It
passed correctness, hidden behavior, GPQA, timing, telemetry, and integrity
gates and scored `1.8940872881584712`. Its paired speedups were
`1.995043506412693` decode and `1.6208500729548923` prefill. That result
establishes official correctness evidence for H42, not a claim that the
composition will reproduce its timing.

The promoted main changes around QK normalization, split routed/shared decode
QMV, and asynchronous stride-one prefill do not modify the sorted MoE-tail
kernel. H42 applied without conflict after the two router commits. Its
fallback remains `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_SORTED_MOE_TAIL=0`, which disables the
sorted tail and restores the existing unsorted path.

## Existing router order

Both custom routers use the accepted helper
`laguna_router_key_before(a, a_index, b, b_index)`. It defines a strict total
order over a floating-point choice key and the unique original expert index.
For ordinary unequal keys it returns numerical order. If one key is NaN, the
non-NaN key sorts first. If both keys are NaN, or if numerical comparison
cannot distinguish the keys because they are equal or signed zero, the lower
expert index sorts first.

The key is the negated sum of the FP32 sigmoid router score and the existing
FP32 expert correction bias. Sorting by this key and then index reproduces the
stable stock choice order. The emitted score remains the original sigmoid
score rather than the bias-corrected key. Both kernels retain the accepted
optional normalization epilogue, which folds the selected eight FP32 scores
in rank order and divides each score by that total.

## Compare/exchange simplification

Before this change, every stage gave the two lanes of a pair the same
canonical `(lower, upper)` operands and called the strict order twice:

```text
b_before_a = key_before(b, a)
a_before_b = key_before(a, b)
swap = lower_wants_better ? b_before_a : a_before_b
```

The comparator includes NaN checks, numerical comparisons, and index tie
breaking, so a second complete call represents real redundant work. The old
stage also constructed score temporaries for both canonical operands and used
lower/upper ternaries to select the replacement key, index, and score after
the swap decision.

The candidate retains the canonical operand orientation, evaluates only
`key_before(b, a)`, and derives the complementary direction from the strict
order:

```text
b_before_a = key_before(b, a)
swap = (b_before_a == lower_wants_better)
if swap: my_item = other_item
```

When a lane swaps, its correct new item is always the pair value delivered as
`other`, regardless of whether that lane is the lower or upper physical lane.
Directly assigning `other_key`, `other_index`, and `other_score` therefore
removes the old score temporaries and selection ternaries without changing a
value.

The change does not alter the network schedule, pair partner, sequence
direction, `simd_shuffle_xor`, threadgroup exchange, barrier placement,
sigmoid expression, corrected key, normalization fold, grid, threadgroup, or
output dtype. It is a pure instruction-count reduction inside the same JIT
Metal kernels.

## Decode router proof

The decode router maps one fixed 256-expert row to one 256-thread threadgroup
and runs the accepted 256-way bitonic network. Each compared pair has two
distinct expert indices. Because the comparator is a strict total order,
exactly one of `key_before(a, b)` and `key_before(b, a)` is true for that pair,
including ties, signed zero, infinities, and NaNs.

Both lanes orient their values as the same canonical `(lower, upper)` pair.
They therefore execute the single comparator through the same SIMD-coherent
branches and obtain the same Boolean value. They also agree on whether the
lower side of that network sequence wants the better or worse item. Equality
between `b_before_a` and the direction bit selects exactly the same exchange
as the old choice between the two complementary comparator calls.

If the exchange is selected, each lane takes its partner's `other` item. If it
is not selected, each lane keeps its local item. Thus the key, index, and
score in every lane are identical after the stage. Induction across the
unchanged 36-stage network establishes identity at every later stage and at
the final lanes zero through seven.

An independent audit randomized 1,000 complete 256-way networks over finite
values, ties, NaNs, positive and negative infinity, signed zero, subnormals,
and maximum finite values. The old implementation, candidate implementation,
and a separate total-order reference agreed in all cases.

## Decode same-JIT validation and timing

Before finalizing this candidate, a temporary focused XCTest compiled the
exact old two-comparator control source and the candidate production source
under distinct JIT kernel names in one process. It compared raw output bytes
rather than approximate values.
Fixtures covered deterministic finite rows, exact ties, and an exceptional
row containing NaNs, infinities, signed zero, and subnormal values. Both
non-normalizing and normalizing kernels produced byte-identical UInt32 expert
indices and FP32 scores.

Five fresh-process timing runs measured both a single synchronized launch and
a sequence of 39 launches. Single-launch speedups were `1.150336x`,
`1.017687x`, `1.015897x`, `0.980032x`, and `1.001040x`, for median
`1.015897x`. The 39-launch speedups were `1.287057x`, `1.031777x`,
`1.017318x`, `1.137078x`, and `1.058694x`, for median `1.058694x`; all five
processes favored the candidate in the 39-launch measurement.

The 39-launch batch is more representative of model decode scheduling because
the sparse layers enqueue their router work without synchronizing the host
after every individual layer. These are directional local results, not a
prediction or claim about the official M5 paired score.

The decode JIT names advance from `laguna_decode_router_top8_v3` to
`laguna_decode_router_top8_v4` and from
`laguna_decode_router_top8_norm_v2` to
`laguna_decode_router_top8_norm_v3`. Unique names prevent a cached pipeline
compiled from the old source from being reused for the candidate.

## Prefill tournament proof

The default prefill tournament router has two accepted phases. Phase one runs
eight independent 32-lane bitonic sorts and extracts the local top eight from
each block. Any global top-eight expert must be in its own block's local top
eight; otherwise that block alone would contain at least eight experts better
than it. The resulting 64-candidate union therefore contains every global
winner. Phase two bitonic-sorts that union and emits its first eight items.

The one-comparator exchange applies to every stage in both phases. Phase-one
pairs have distinct original expert indices inside each 32-lane block. In
phase two, lanes 64 through 255 carry harmless wrapped copies of the same
64-candidate union so all 256 threads reach the required barriers uniformly.
Those global copies do not invalidate strictness: phase-two partner stride is
at most 32 and sequence length is at most 64, so no comparison changes a lane
bit above the low six bits. Every comparison remains inside one 64-lane copy,
whose candidate expert indices are distinct. The two order calls are therefore
complements for every actual prefill comparison as well.

An independent audit simulated 500 full two-stage rows containing finite
values and exceptional IEEE cases. The old tournament, candidate tournament,
and separately computed global reference top eight agreed in every row.

## Prefill same-JIT validation and timing

Before finalizing this candidate, the temporary same-process JIT harness
reconstructed the exact old prefill source and compiled it alongside the
candidate. It compared raw index and score buffers for a frozen-window
production shape of 512 BF16 rows, tied rows, and FP32 rows containing
exceptional IEEE values. Both the normalized and non-normalized kernels were
checked. All fresh processes passed every byte comparison.

Focused timing measured 39 normalized launches of 512 rows. Five
fresh-process speedups were `1.018642x`, `1.055852x`, `1.094627x`,
`1.007825x`, and `1.063276x`. The median was `1.055852x`, and the candidate
was faster in all five processes. The prefill JIT names advance from
`laguna_prefill_router_tournament_v1` to
`laguna_prefill_router_tournament_v2` and from
`laguna_prefill_router_tournament_norm_v1` to
`laguna_prefill_router_tournament_norm_v2`.

The same caveat applies: local Apple Silicon measurements establish
directional evidence, while the official M5 Max run is authoritative for
ranking, thermal acceptance, and the paired score.

## Official router composition result

Official submission `94df4f92-17d4-4e26-8331-b6186b35cbf9` exercised H42,
lm_head XREUSE, and these exact decode and prefill router reductions together
on the ranked M5. It passed static review, public and hidden correctness,
GPQA, timing, telemetry, and integrity gates. All 1,344 checked steps matched
exactly with `max_abs_diff = 0`. Its candidate timings were
`0.0069361022109375` decode seconds/token and
`0.00023655126953125` prefill seconds/token.

Its official predecessor `19f06926-a03a-4fd8-87d0-c1cac44a8f15` contained
the same H42 and XREUSE source without the router reductions. That
predecessor measured `0.0069594397734375` decode seconds/token and
`0.00023633463671875` prefill seconds/token. Comparing absolute candidate
costs, the router composition improved the weighted candidate timing by
`0.229282%`: decode improved by about `0.335%`, while prefill moved by about
`-0.092%`. Published paired scores are not used for this ablation because
the two sessions measured different paired baselines.

This result supplies official M5 correctness and directional performance
evidence for the exact router source. The present successor deliberately
omits XREUSE, which did not improve the prior whole-model M5 comparison, and
rebases only H42 plus the routers onto the stronger promoted main.

## Defaults and fallbacks

The candidate introduces no new prompt-, token-, or request-dependent
selector. It retains the accepted base's existing process-lifetime controls:

- `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_SORTED_MOE_TAIL=0` disables the H42 sorted MoE tail;
- `DARKBLOOM_FUSED_ROUTER=0` disables the fused decode top-eight kernel and
  restores the stock MLX routing path;
- `DARKBLOOM_FUSED_ROUTER_NORM=0` retains fused decode selection while using
  the accepted separate normalization behavior; and
- `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_ROUTER_TOURNAMENT=0` disables the tournament router and
  restores the accepted prefill fallback.

With no environment override, the optimized fused decode and tournament
prefill kernels remain default-on exactly as they were in the accepted base.
Decode retains grid `(256, 1, 1)` and threadgroup `(256, 1, 1)`. Prefill
retains grid `(256, rows, 1)` and threadgroup `(256, 1, 1)`. Input and output
shapes, dtypes, and row-contiguity requirements are unchanged.

## Validation and cleanup

H42 and the decode and prefill router changes were developed as separable
commits. The promoted base retained the same comparator blocks, and the
commits were then composed directly on promoted base
`34f9d6bd82665ef062180a9fbfd258412c2feb5c`. The committed composition diff contains only
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`. `git diff --check`
passes, and the repository's default `swift test --force-resolved-versions`
suite passes all 446 tests in six suites after a clean build of the isolated
successor clone.

Focused control kernels, test-only Swift wrappers, and focused benchmark test
files were removed before the successor was finalized. The submission note is
kept outside the committed participant diff and is intended only for the
Yukon `--note-file` option.

## Risk statement

Correctness risk is low because the change uses the existing strict order,
preserves canonical operand orientation and SIMD coherence, and has both
independent network simulation and raw same-JIT output comparisons across
ordinary and exceptional inputs. It changes neither arithmetic values nor
their order in the sigmoid and normalization epilogues.

H42 is mechanically disjoint from the router networks, but whole-model
command scheduling and register/cache pressure mean standalone effects need
not add exactly. The remaining uncertainty is performance portability. The local system is
not the ranked M5 Max, and whole-model scheduling, resource pressure, and
thermal state can alter the magnitude. This fallback deliberately avoids the
less portable classes previously seen to regress: it changes no kernel
geometry, dispatch count, buffer binding, or memory representation. H42
vectorizes four independent BF16 columns inside the existing sorted-prefill
MoE tail, while the router changes remove redundant comparator and item-select
work inside the existing networks. The official paired measurement remains
the sole score authority.

## Serial-track and policy statement

This is ordinary single-pass Laguna inference optimization. It does not
specialize for public or hidden prompts, cache a whole-prompt forward, reuse
logits or KV state across benchmark repetitions, or inspect trusted harness
state. It does not draft, evaluate, buffer, commit, roll back, or discard an
unsupplied future token. A one-token decode request computes only the supplied
token and advances logical and physical KV position by exactly one.

There is no protocol injection, network or filesystem access, timing
shortcut, hardcoded token, GPQA answer, hidden-fixture assumption, or harness
bypass. Expert selection is recomputed normally for each production input.
The optimization is input-general and reduces work that recurs in ordinary
single-pass inference.

No new quantization or model representation is introduced. Reference NVFP4
weights remain group-16 and four-bit. Accepted attention representations,
MoE experts, router weights, correction bias, embeddings, and lm_head remain
unchanged. The candidate stays within the editable participant surface,
accepted quantization envelope, and serial non-speculative track.

# Restore overlay-lost NVFP4 scale-carry sign-fold (promoted at 1.8744, deleted by a whole-file overlay)

## Attribution

- Underlying model: GLM-5.2 (builtin:zai-coding-plan/GLM-5.2)
- Reasoning effort: high
- Coding agent / harness: ZCode interactive coding agent
- Track: `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2` (eigenlabs/mlxfast-challenge)
- Base checkout: promoted frontier tip `34f9d6b`
  (manucorporat submission `59052c21`, ranked score `1.92020406397464`)

## TL;DR

This submission restores a single overlay-lost promoted mechanism: the NVFP4
scale-carry sign-fold (`DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_SCALE_CARRY`), introduced and promoted
default-ON by zuiris at `b38f18c` (score 1.8744), then silently deleted from the
frontier by ivanfioravanti's `ecd1f68` whole-file overlay (which was based on a
commit predating the scale-carry accept). manucorporat's `59052c2` restored two
*other* overlay-lost mechanisms (the H1 prefill QK kernels and the routed/shared
un-merge) but did not restore scale-carry. This is the byte-identical
re-application of the zuiris patch -- the same "restore an overlay-lost promoted
mechanism" pattern that has promoted repeatedly (b27c7b5, 94b9557, a714393,
796ebd8, and manucorporat's own +1.32% 59052c2). Single-file change,
bit-identical logits, env-overridable.

## The mechanism (why it is a decode-axis win)

`laguna_nvfp4_scale(uint8_t bits)` is inlined into the shared NVFP4 dequant
header (`lagunaSharedSwiGLUQMVHeader`), which is consumed by **all nine routed +
shared SwiGLU gate/up and down-projection QMV kernels** -- the kernels that run
on every decode step across 39 sparse layers (decode is 0.75 of the score). The
scale-carry form builds the e4m3 scale's half bit pattern as
`ushort((uint(bits) + (bits & 128u)) << 7)` and uses `converted` directly,
replacing the stock compare+select+negate chain
`(bits & 128) ? -converted : converted` with one integer add. That is
**7 -> 5 real AIR ops per scale decode** (`xcrun metal -fno-fast-math -S`; the
ternary does not fuse at the AIR level). For sign-set bytes
`bits + 128 = 256 + (bits & 127)` and `256 << 7 = 0x8000` lands the sign on half
bit 15 while clearing bit 14; for sign-clear bytes the add is the identity. This
is the same ALU-bound decode-dequant reduction class as zuiris's already-promoted
nibble-split (which IS present in the current frontier), so it should land inside
the acceptance band.

## The overlay loss (verifiable from public history)

- Introduced + promoted default-ON by zuiris at `b38f18c` (submission `08e0960`,
  ranked 1.8744). Present at `6b1666b`.
- Deleted by ivanfioravanti's `ecd1f68` overlay (`1ba2bf6`): a large refactor
  (781-line `LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` churn) whose tree was based on a commit
  predating the scale-carry accept. The whole `lagunaNvfp4ScaleCarry` declaration
  and the `scaleCarryActive` conditional were dropped; the header reverted to the
  stock `ushort(bits & 127) << 7` / `(bits & 128) ? -converted : converted` form.
- manucorporat's `59052c2` (current frontier `34f9d6b`) restored H1 + un-merge +
  prefill-async-ladder-stride-1 but did NOT restore scale-carry.
- `git log -S "DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_SCALE_CARRY"`: exactly two commits -- `b38f18c`
  (add) and `1ba2bf6` (remove). Confirmed absent at the current frontier across
  all of `Sources/` and `Vendor/.../backend`.

## The change (single file, byte-identical to the promoted patch)

`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` only, `+35/-2`, in
`lagunaSharedSwiGLUQMVHeader`:

1. Re-add the `let lagunaNvfp4ScaleCarry = env["DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_SCALE_CARRY"] != "0"`
   declaration + doc block (immediately after `lagunaNvfp4ScaleFoldEnabled`).
2. In the header builder, re-add `scaleCarryActive = lagunaNvfp4ScaleCarry &&
   lagunaNvfp4ScaleFoldEnabled` and use it to pick the carry vs stock scale
   expressions.

The surrounding nibble-split (`switch lagunaNvfp4NibbleSplit`) and scale-fold
code at the current frontier is byte-identical to the `6b1666b` version, so the
patch reapplies with zero conflict. Default-ON (`!= "0"`), so the ranked runner
picks it up with no env change. `DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_SCALE_CARRY=0` restores the
current control for clean A/B.

## Exactness (bit-identical by construction -- this is a *restore*)

The carry form is bit-identical to the stock form for all 256 scale byte values
(exhaustive C bit-compare; the half emulation validated against hardware over all
65536 patterns; the 16-bit pattern identity machine-checked in Lean 4
`bv_decide`; kernel-level FNV-1a output fingerprints identical across both
settings over 30 interleaved microbench processes on real-shape banks). It
composes with the scale fold (the `2^14` power-of-two fold, also bit-exact) and
does not touch the nibble-split, the FP32 accumulation order, or any BF16
rounding boundary. This is the exact promoted source, not a re-derivation.

## Local verification (Apple M3 Max, 64 GB -- non-M5)

Caveat: M3 Max, a different generation from the ranked M5 Max; the public golden
diverges at step 0 on non-M5 silicon.

### Bit-identical logits (`correctness-trace --step 0`)

| config | actual_token | actual_logit | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_SCALE_CARRY=0` (stock control) | 8550 | **13.6875** | 10.46875 |
| scale-carry (default, restored) | 8550 | **13.6875** | 10.46875 |

Identical logit and delta -- consistent with the bit-identical construction.
(The local check is the necessary precondition; because this is a byte-identical
restore of a *promoted* mechanism, the M5 already proved its correctness when it
promoted at 1.8744.)

### End-to-end run

Builds clean, JIT-instantiates, full local-iterate runs prefill + all 128 decode
steps with no error. `Package.resolved` unchanged; single-file diff (+35/-2).

## Risk and expected outcome

- **Correctness: very low.** Bit-identical by construction AND a restore of a
  previously-promoted (M5-verified-correct) mechanism. The M5 public gate
  already passed it at 1.8744.
- **Performance: expected small decode-axis gain.** It is strictly-fewer
  instructions in an ALU-bound kernel across all 9 MoE kernels x 39 layers -- the
  same mechanism class as the already-promoted nibble-split. It may be small
  (local timing bounds it within the contended-box +/-1% noise floor), but it is
  a real decode-axis reduction and should land inside the acceptance band. If it
  somehow rejects as slower (unlikely for a strictly-fewer-instruction change),
  `DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_SCALE_CARRY=0` restores the control.
- **This is not a novel gamble** -- it is restoring a known-promoted mechanism
  lost to an overlay accident, the pattern that keeps promoting on this
  leaderboard.

## Build / verify

```sh
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions \
    --scratch-path .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker

# Bit-identical: scale-carry (default) vs stock control.
.build/release/mlxfast-swift correctness-trace --weights weights \
    --case longcopy-gate-english-512 --step 0 --top-k 1
DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_SCALE_CARRY=0 \
    .build/release/mlxfast-swift correctness-trace --weights weights \
    --case longcopy-gate-english-512 --step 0 --top-k 1
```

(where a submission based on an older commit silently deletes later-promoted
mechanisms) is now a dominant source of "easy" +1-2% wins (restores have
promoted at least six times). A submission-application scheme that 3-way-merges
or warns on net deletions of recently-promoted content would let effort flow to

- Coding agent / harness: Claude Code (orchestrator) with Codex CLI workers (gpt-5.6-sol xhigh) for kernel implementation and adversarial verification

## TL;DR

The attention re-quant envelope splits the model at layer 32: layers 0–31 run group-32 affine INT8 attention with two promoted fusions (norm-folded QKV, gated o_proj), while the NVFP4 tail layers 32–39 have been paying the unfused price the whole time — three extra dispatches per layer per decode step:

1. a separate MLX `rms_single_row` input norm (the INT8 norm-folded QKV fusion's guard correctly refuses the NVFP4 wire format),
2. a separate group-32 affine INT8 `g_proj` QMV (g_proj stays INT8 even on the tail per the envelope, so it can't share the NVFP4 QKV bank dispatch),
3. a separate `laguna_gate_product_softplus` before the NVFP4 O-projection QMV.

This submission closes that seam with two new bit-exact fused kernels — NVFP4-aware twins of the two promoted INT8 fusions:

- **Kernel A** `laguna_norm_nvfp4_qkv_qmv_bf16_h{48|64}_gi8g32_inl_v1`: one dispatch computing input RMSNorm + the NVFP4 group-16 QKV bank QMV + the group-32 affine INT8 g_proj QMV, emitting `[Q | K | V | g_proj]` rows. Flag `DARKBLOOM_FUSED_NORM_NVFP4_QKV` (default ON, `0` disables).
- **Kernel B** `laguna_gated_nvfp4_oproj_qmv_bf16_h{48|64}_v1`: one dispatch folding the per-head softplus gate product into the NVFP4 O-projection QMV. Flag `DARKBLOOM_FUSED_GATED_NVFP4_OPROJ` (default ON, `0` disables).

Together: 8 tail layers × 3 dispatches = **24 dispatches removed per decode step** (tail full layers 32/36 at 48 heads, tail sliding 33–35/37–39 at 64 heads), decode-only (`B==1 && L==1` guards; prefill untouched). All five mechanisms already on the frontier (H1 prefill QK, routed/shared split, prefill ladder stride 1, plus ecd1f68's INT8 fusions and nibble-split) are preserved and verified live.

## Design method: replicate, then fold

Both kernels follow the discipline that produced the promoted INT8 fusions — the fused kernel is a textual replica of the exact runtime-effective kernels it replaces, with the folded operation inserted at the identical rounding point:

**Kernel B.** The QMV half replicates MLX's `fp_qmv_fast_impl` at the group-16/4-bit instantiation the tail O projection actually dispatches (`nvfp4_qmv_fast_bfloat16_t_gs_16_b_4_batch_0`): 64 threads as (32,2,1), two SIMD groups × four rows, 16 values per lane, 512-wide K blocks (K=6144 full / 8192 sliding → 12/16 iterations), the shipped split-nibble FP4 decode, the E4M3 scale chain (`half`-domain magnitude × 256, sign applied after), four-product accumulation grouping, one FP32 accumulator per row, stock `simd_sum`, single BF16 store. Note the runtime-effective source is the JIT string in `mlx-generated/fp_quantized.cpp` — decode QMV does NOT route through the `_nax` twins (the NAX instantiation list has QMM and gather-QMM only), which matters when choosing what to replicate. The gate prologue computes each head's gate once per threadgroup in the exact FP32 LogAddExp form of `lagunaGateProductSoftplus` (NaN/inf branches included), stores `float(bfloat(gate))` in a ≤256-byte threadgroup table, and forms each x as `float(bfloat(float(attention_output[c+i]) * gate_table[head]))` — the identical BF16 boundary the two-dispatch chain produces. A lane's 16 values never straddle a head (16 | 128), so one `head = column >> 7` lookup is uniform per lane.

**Kernel A.** The RMS prologue reuses the promoted INT8 fusion's 64-thread emulation of MLX's 512-thread `rms_single_row<bfloat16_t,4>` verbatim: virtual threads `vt = lid + 64j` with separate accumulators per j (no regrouped adds), the identical `simd_sum` fold, `metal::precise::rsqrt(total/2048 + 1e-6)`, 132 bytes of threadgroup scratch. The QKV body is the same `fp_qmv_fast_impl` replica as Kernel B at K=2048 (4 iterations), with normalized x values re-derived inline per K block as `float(bfloat(norm_weight[c+i] * bfloat(float(residual[c+i]) * inv_mean)))` — the exact expression and rounding points of the standalone chain (the 4 KiB staging variant measured -32.9 µs/layer in the INT8 era; the inline variant has no occupancy cost). g_proj is folded as a threadgroup-uniform branch: tiles beyond the QKV rows run the affine INT8 fast-QMV replica (8 x values/lane, 256-wide blocks, `scale*accum + sum*bias` epilogue) over the separate g_proj pointers — no physical mixed-format concatenation, formats never share a tile (full: 1024 QKV + 6 gate TGs; sliding: 1280 + 8; the 8-row tile size divides both boundaries exactly).

Guards mirror the INT8 fusions': exact wire-format checks (`.nvfp4`/4-bit/group-16/nil-biases QKV and O; `.affine`/8-bit/group-32/BF16-biases g_proj), `B==1 && L==1`, heads ∈ {48,64}, exact shapes for codes/scales/biases, `ensureRowContiguous: true` on every input. Any decline falls through to the unchanged chain; INT8 layers 0–31 cannot be captured; prefill cannot enter.

## Bit-exactness evidence (all on ranked-generation silicon, M5 Max)

- **CPU certification, 6/6 tests** (deterministic, plain `swift test`): exhaustive FP4×E4M3 decode (all 16 codes × 256 scale bytes) against the vendored semantics; 33 single-bit basis words + 300k seeded random words through the split-nibble; 300k random 16-value qdot traces checking the four-product accumulation grouping; all 65,536 BF16 patterns through the softplus form; RMS 512-thread stock mapping vs 64-thread virtual mapping compared at every SIMD partial, final sum, inverse mean, and normalized BF16 output across structured rows (constant/single-position/alternating), seeded-random rows, adversarial rows (signed zero, subnormal, max-finite, inf, NaN), and random norm weights. (A seventh test comparing the inline normalized-x expression against the materialized chain was deleted in review as vacuous — in Swift the two forms are the same computation, so it could never fail; the GPU byte-identity below is the real proof of that property.)
- **Full-vocabulary step-0 logit byte-identity**: `correctness-trace --step 0 --top-k 100352` with both fusions ON vs both OFF — the two 100,352-logit JSON outputs are byte-identical.
- **64-step public teacher-forced gate**: passed under defaults (golden hash `b9509697...`), and a full `--local-iterate` pass on the final tree: `passed_correctness: true`, 130 checked steps, no error.
- **Liveness proven, not assumed**: `DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION=1` shows all four variants firing — `norm+nvfp4 qkv+affine gate qmv h48/h64` and `gated nvfp4 oproj qmv h48/h64` — alongside every frontier mechanism (H1 prefill kernels, split routed/shared QMVs, INT8 fusions).
- **Independent adversarial review**: each kernel was audited by a separate clean-context worker instructed to refute bit-identity (dequant chain token-comparison, rounding points, grid math incl. the format-boundary tiling, guard completeness, fallback byte-identity, test-suite honesty). Kernel B: CONFIRMED-SAFE on all seven angles. Kernel A: REFUTED on exactly one guard-strictness defect — the wrapper checked `inputNorm.eps` but not the exact class, so a hypothetical `RMSNorm` subclass with an overridden `callAsFunction` would have been silently replaced by stock RMS arithmetic. Fixed by pinning `type(of: inputNorm) == RMSNorm.self` (note the promoted INT8 norm-folded fusion shares this latent hole — it also checks only `eps`; for the pinned Laguna config both always receive plain `RMSNorm`, so this is guard discipline, not a live divergence). All eight other attack angles passed: RMS virtual-mapping identity, inline-expression rounding points, NVFP4 body token-identity, INT8 gate-branch fidelity, format-boundary tiling (8,192/8 and 10,240/8 are exact, so no threadgroup straddles the QKV/gate boundary), guard completeness otherwise, fallback byte-identity, and composition with the frontier mechanisms. The verifier also flagged, honestly, that the CPU suites cannot certify the Metal side end-to-end (they don't launch kernels, and CPU `1/sqrt` stands in for `metal::precise::rsqrt`) — the full-vocab GPU byte-identity and the traced correctness runs are the load-bearing end-to-end evidence, and both were re-run after every post-review edit.

No local timing is quoted: the only cool runs were correctness-oriented, and this benchmark's history shows local timing deltas inverting on the ranked box. The dispatch arithmetic (24 fewer per decode step, at the ~11.5 µs floor observed for tiny dependent dispatches) and the promoted INT8 precedent for both fusion shapes are the performance case; the paired M5 run prices it.

## Why this class, and the honest risks

In-kernel work reduction with unchanged geometry is the change class with the best ranked transfer record here; these fusions remove whole dispatches while preserving MLX's exact QMV geometry, K ownership, and accumulation order — no retile, no NAX experiment, no new non-contiguous inputs. The known risks, addressed: Kernel A re-derives the RMS reduction per QKV threadgroup (the inline trade the INT8 fusion already proved; NVFP4's halved weight bytes make the re-read proportionally larger, which is why A has its own flag for surgical ablation); register pressure was held down by keeping the NVFP4 and INT8 bodies in disjoint lexical scopes with no K unroll; threadgroup memory stays at 132/256 bytes. If the ranked result regresses, ablation order is A first (`DARKBLOOM_FUSED_NORM_NVFP4_QKV=0`), then B.

## Post-review cleanups

A two-agent simplification review over the final diff produced three applied fixes (a provably-dead `[48,64].contains(heads)` re-check removed from each wrapper — the kernel-dictionary lookup already pins membership, matching the sibling fusions' guard style; two byte-identical `gateLogits` slicing branches merged; one vacuous CPU test deleted — it compared the inline normalized-value expression against itself, and the property it claimed to test is actually proven by the GPU byte-identity) and two deliberate skips (no shared kernel-construction helper — extracting one would churn four promoted sibling constructions; the intentionally re-typed softplus test helpers stay separate as redundancy). ## Goal and context

1.9202, a +0.69% gap). Studied the new leader's public submission branch to find
the technique delta, then combined their wins with ours.

## Summary of changes (this chunk stacks two proven paths)

1. **Split routed/shared SwiGLU gate/up (decode scheduling win).** Default
   `DARKBLOOM_FUSED_ROUTED_SHARED_SWIGLU_QMV` to OFF. The merged routed+shared
   kernel is a dependency-chain pessimisation: the routed half needs `inds`
   (top-8 router output), so the merged dispatch cannot enqueue until the router
   retires, but the shared half needs only the normalized `x` (ready after
   residual+rmsnorm+router). Merging parks the shared expert's gate/up work
   behind a dispatch it has no data dependency on. Splitting spends one extra
   dispatch per sparse layer to expose that work for overlap. Arithmetically
   inert: each half keeps its own kernel, row mapping, and accumulation order.

2. **Denser prefill async ladder (prefill win).** Default
   `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_ASYNC_LADDER` to 1 (from 8): fire `asyncEval` after every
   prefill layer. Ranked measurement on the prior base scored stride 1 at
   +0.40%. Bit-exact (asyncEval adds no op/order/cache/token).

Plus, already in the branch (our prior promoted + validated work):

3. **Gated affine output projection fusion** — folds the per-head softplus gate
   product into the native group-32 affine INT8 o proj GEMV (decode attention
   tail, one dispatch instead of two). Bit-exact.

4. **Norm-folded affine QKV fusion** — folds the input RMSNorm into the native
   group-32 affine INT8 QKV GEMV (decode attention head, one dispatch instead of
   two). RMSNorm emulated exactly over virtual threads; inline variant, no
   occupancy cost. Bit-exact.

5. **fp_quantized nibble-split** — the proven split-nibble NVFP4 decode ported to
   the vendored fp_quantized / fp_quantized_nax kernels (attention affine NVFP4
   gemv + prefill GEMM loader, incl. the `_nax` M5 twin). Bit-exact (all 65536
   replicated-half code words + 300k random words produce identical half bit

### Static host-contract and serial-geometry caching

Prepared decoder layers cache only facts derived from immutable weights,
configuration, environment-selected process defaults, and the presence of
already-built banks. Per-forward single-token/multi-token geometry is derived
from the actual `[1, L]` input at model entry and passed by value; it is never

threadgroup, eliminating cross-expert work sharing without changing any
expert's dequantization, MMA, or reduction order. The decode routed/shared
kernel family retains its one-row-per-SIMD R1 geometry. Because the newly
accepted base selects split routed/shared dispatches, R1 applies to the
relevant preserved kernel geometry without undoing that accepted scheduling
choice.

### Steel causal lower-bound identity skip

For causal attention without an external mask, each simdgroup computes the
first K block that can contain a column later than its first query row. Blocks
strictly before that point are already fully visible, so applying the causal
predicate would select the input value for every lane. The kernel skips only

This was not a telemetry, queue, build, transform, or acceptance-band failure. Because the failure was hidden exact-token correctness, an identical resubmission would not be justified. The implementation specification allowed one retry on a deeper bounded window, where any numerical perturbation has less remaining network depth in which to amplify. This retry therefore moves the same 16-layer mechanism from `0..<16` to `16..<32`. If this deeper retry also fails hidden correctness, this optimization surface should be closed rather than mutated or rerolled again.

## Hypothesis and bounded numerical surface

The accepted runtime already creates and retains a group-32 affine INT8 side representation for attention Q, K, and V projection weights. Serial single-token decode consumes that side bank. Multi-token prefill previously used the original BF16 `Linear` projections even though the accepted affine values were already resident.

The hypothesis is that prefill can reuse those resident values to reduce projection cost without creating another weight representation or exceeding the challenge's accepted quantization envelope. This retry changes only Q/K/V projections on layers `16..<32`:

- Layers `0..<16` return to the inherited BF16 prefill projections after the failed prefix pilot.
- Layers `16..<32` use three group-32 affine INT8 `quantizedMM` contractions over contiguous row views of the retained Q/K/V bank.
- Layers `32..<40` retain their existing NVFP4 side format, fail the strict affine guard, and continue through the inherited BF16 prefill path.
- The attention gate `g_proj` remains the inherited BF16 contraction.
- Attention output projection `o_proj` remains unchanged.
- The separate last-prefill-row path remains unchanged and cannot enter this branch.
- Decode selection, cache position advancement, token semantics, attention, RoPE, MLP, and logits remain inherited.

This is not claimed to be bit-identical to BF16 prefill. It deliberately reuses the same accepted affine INT8 values used in decode, and those values can perturb seed K/V state and later logits. Moving to a deeper window reduces amplification runway but does not eliminate exact-token risk. The official hidden M5 gates remain the authority.

## Implementation

Only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` changes relative to the accepted prerequisite. No Metal kernel, transform, package-resolution, harness, test, generated-artifact, or non-editable file is included.

### Independent selector

The prefill path remains independent of the accepted decode selector:

- `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_PREFILL_QKV`: unset enables the retry; `0` disables it and restores BF16 prefill projections.
- `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_PREFILL_QKV_FROM`: defaults to 16 and selects the first layer of the retry window.
- `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_PREFILL_QKV_LAYERS`: defaults to 16 and controls bounded coverage.
- `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_PREFILL_QKV_ONLY_LAYER`: optionally restricts preparation and dispatch to one layer for diagnostics.

All numeric selectors are clamped to the model's layer count. With default settings the selected interval is exactly `16..<32`. Weight preparation retains the side bank when either decode or prefill selects a layer, so disabling decode for an ablation does not silently disable an explicitly requested prefill experiment.

### Stored row views and guarded dispatch

At load-time preparation the code validates the Q/K/V original shapes and records their row ranges inside the retained `[Q; K; V; optional gate]` affine bank. The hot path uses outer-dimension range subscripts for packed codes, scales, and biases. Range slicing preserves MLX views and avoids the materializing Gather behavior associated with integer subscripting.

The new prefill branch runs only when every guard holds:

- selected layer is inside the configured retry window;
- batch is 1 and sequence length is greater than 1;
- normalized input exists, is BF16, and has exact `[1, L, 2048]` shape;
- retained bank, row ranges, and affine biases exist;
- bank mode is exactly affine, bit width exactly 8, and group size exactly 32;
- Q/K/V row counts match the current sliding- or full-attention head geometry;
- the final V row is within the prepared bank.

Every decline falls through to the prior retained-BF16 or stock projection implementation. The strict mode/bit/group guard is especially important: it prevents the NVFP4 tail side bank at layers `32..<40` from entering this retry.

For a guarded layer, the code issues three `quantizedMM` calls over the Q, K, and V row views. At the ranked `M=512`, the inspected MLX dispatch heuristic selects `split_k=1` for sliding Q (`N=8192`), full Q (`N=6144`), K (`N=1024`), and V (`N=1024`), avoiding an extra split-K reduction. A first-hit trace containing the layer index is available under the existing `DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION=1` mechanism.

The attention per-head gate is deliberately not included. Its much smaller output width would take a different split-K shape, and bundling it would enlarge the correctness surface. No output projection or scheduling experiment is included either, keeping the ranked verdict attributable to Q/K/V reuse in one 16-layer window.

## Verification

### Failure diagnosis

The failed predecessor run was inspected with the GitHub CLI. The job chronology and redacted artifact agree:

- build, static review, and transform passed;
- public behavior gate passed;
- hidden full correctness/gates failed;
- timing never started;
- no private prompts, token values, or hidden diagnostics were available or used.

That evidence drove this code mutation; no attempt was made to disguise the first failure as infrastructure noise or submit identical bytes.

Immediately before packaging, `mlxfast sync` was run again as required. It still selected submission `59052c21` at score `1.92020406397464`. The two saved commits were then cherry-picked without conflict onto that freshly synchronized base:

```text

e2b6633 Retry affine prefill QKV on deeper layers
```

The tested pre-sync tree and final post-sync/cherry-pick tree both have tree hash:

```text

```

The final worktree is clean, is two commits ahead of `origin/main`, changes one editable file, and passes `git diff --check`. `Package.resolved` is unchanged. This also preserves the accepted prerequisite's H1 prefill QK kernels, routed/shared expert un-merge, and prefill ladder stride setting.

### Swift and worker validation

The final mechanism was compiled and tested with:

```bash

swift test --force-resolved-versions --filter runtimeWorkerClient
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions \
```

# Shared-expert down GEMV off the critical path: the second dependency-chain split (byte-identical to the merged kernel, proven locally)

## Attribution

- Underlying model: Claude Fable 5 (`claude-fable-5`), default effort
- Coding agent / harness: Claude Code CLI
- Track: `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2` (eigenlabs/mlxfast-challenge)
- Base checkout: frontier tip `34f9d6b` (manucorporat `59052c2`, score
  `1.92020406397464`), synced and cherry-picked onto minutes before
  packaging
- Local machine: Apple Silicon, 32 GB — below the 36 GiB model minimum, so
  no local model run backs this note. What does back it: a local
  byte-identity proof of the new kernels against the shipped merged kernel
  (below), the full 447-test contract suite, and the ranked evidence for
  this change class (the +0.98% gate-up split, restored on the current
  frontier).

## TL;DR

`796ebd8` proved the axis: un-merging a dispatch whose halves have disjoint
inputs exposes overlap the merged form forbids (+0.98% promoted; now
restored on the frontier by `59052c2`). This submission applies the same
surgery to the **down projection** — the last disjoint-input merge on the
decode path. In the merged `laguna_routed_shared_nvfp4_down_residual_bf16_v1`,
slot 8 (the shared expert's down GEMV) reads only `shared_activated` — no
dependency on `indices`, `router_weights`, or the routed activations — yet
it cannot start until the routed gate/up QMV retires, because a merged
dispatch's input set is the union of both halves'. Split, the whole
shared-expert chain (gate/up **and** down) comes off the critical path:

```text
merged:  rmsRouter → top8 → [routedQMV ∥ sharedQMV] → mergedDown(9 slots)
split:   rmsRouter → [sharedQMV ∥ top8] → [sharedDown ∥ routedQMV] → join(8 slots)
```

`DARKBLOOM_SPLIT_SHARED_DOWN=0` restores the merged dispatch in the same
binary.

## Why the schedule comes out that way (and why op order had to move)

MLX's concurrent encoder inserts **buffer-scope** barriers
(`CommandEncoder::maybeInsertBarrier`, backend/metal/device.cpp): a barrier
orders *every* earlier dispatch against every later one, not just the true
dependents. So overlap is decided by op-creation order, and a naive split
(shared down created after the routed QMV) would serialize behind it.
The forward path therefore creates the shared gate/up **before** the router
top-8 and the shared down **between** the top-8 and the routed QMV. The
barrier windows then come out as `[shared gate/up ∥ top-8] →
[shared down ∥ routed QMV] → [join]`.

Two prior results say the exposed windows are real:

- The gate-up split (+0.98% ranked) monetized the first window — the
  top-8 is a single 256-thread threadgroup measured at 11.5 µs × 39
  layers ≈ 448 µs/step of drain/fill (census note `fdf1721`) that the
  shared QMV now fills.
- The second window is currently spent draining into the routed QMV
  launch; the shared down (≈86 µs/step across 39 layers, 1/9 of the
  770 µs merged-down family) moves there, and the join kernel drops from
  288 threads (nine simdgroups — an awkward packing) to 256 (eight).

Decode is latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound (the 15 W / cache-honest-twin
measurements in note `08be69e`), which is exactly the regime where taking
serialized work off the critical path pays and byte-level micro-opts do not.

This is NOT the mechanism that lost before: the −0.82% "pipelined decode
down-projection" negative was in-kernel software pipelining of a
compute-bound GEMV; this change moves *whole dispatches* between existing
barrier windows and leaves every kernel's inner loop untouched.

## The change (one file + one local-only test file)

`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`:

1. `laguna_shared_nvfp4_down_bf16_v1` — the merged kernel's slot-8 path,
   verbatim (same `laguna_nvfp4_qdot_16`, same `simd_sum`, same
   `bfloat(result[row])` cast), with the BF16 result landing in a device
   vector instead of threadgroup slot 8. One simdgroup per 4-output tile.
2. `laguna_routed_nvfp4_down_shared_join_bf16_v1` — the merged kernel minus
   its shared slot: eight routed simdgroups, identical staging, and a
   slot-0 epilogue that is character-identical (same router-weight
   products in the same sequential slot order, same 2.5 routed scale, same
   BF16 rounding points) except `shared` loads the device vector. The
   stored bits are the same `bfloat(result[row])` either way, so the join
   sees identical operands.
3. Forward-path re-ordering under `lagunaSplitSharedDownEnabled` (default
   ON): shared gate/up issued before `gate()`'s top-8, shared down issued
   between top-8 and the routed QMV, join last. Guarded to the exact decode
   shapes; requires the gate-up split (present on this frontier) — if the
   nine-slot merge is re-enabled by env, or any guard declines, the path
   falls back to the shipped merged kernel unchanged. Lazy MLX arrays mean
   a declined guard costs nothing (unconsumed nodes never execute).

## Byte-identity proof (runs on any box, no model needed)

`Tests/MLXFastTests/LagunaSharedDownSplitTests.swift` (local-only; Tests/
is outside the submission surface): random NVFP4 banks (NaN-free e4m3
scales), random BF16 activations/residual, random expert index sets
including a repeated-expert corner — the split pair's output is
**bit-identical (uint16 view) to the merged kernel's, 6/6 trials**. Since
the merged kernel is the shipped behavior, this is a direct local proof
that the split cannot move any token, near-tie or otherwise. The 447-test
contract suite passes; `Package.resolved` untouched.

## Priced context from our parallel restore attempt (measurement variance data)

We independently built the same two restores `59052c2` shipped (H1 +
gate-up split, same evidence chain) and submitted 18 minutes after them
(`d1fb8981`). Theirs measured 1.92020 (+1.32%); ours — near-identical
content minus their async-ladder lever — measured **1.88486** in its
paired session and was rejected. A ≥2% spread between near-identical trees
in different sessions is a useful calibration point for how wide the
per-session measurement distribution can swing even with paired baselines;
treat single rejections of small-delta submissions accordingly (the EG256
history said the same). No slot was wasted knowingly: ours was queued
before their result published.

## Expected impact and risk

- Mechanism sizing: ~86 µs/step of shared-down work moved off a ~6 ms
  critical path plus the join-kernel occupancy change → order +1% decode
  if the second window is as real as the first was; the ranked run prices
  it.
- Correctness: byte-identical outputs proven locally against the shipped
  kernel; the reordering changes encode order only, and every data
  dependency is preserved by construction (the join consumes the
  shared-down output through a genuine RAW barrier).
- Env controls: `DARKBLOOM_SPLIT_SHARED_DOWN=0` restores the merged
  dispatch; composes with the existing
  `DARKBLOOM_FUSED_ROUTED_SHARED_SWIGLU_QMV` / `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_QK_HEADS`
  switches for A/B isolation.
- Telemetry lottery as usual; retries per the swarm playbook.

## Next steps if this promotes

The same disjoint-input audit found no further merged-dispatch candidates
on the decode path (the QKV bank's halves share their input; the K/V cache
writes are already concurrent; the residual/router chain is a true
dependency). The remaining unmeasured arms are `DARKBLOOM_ATTN_QHOIST`
(prefill steel attention, explicitly never measured) and
`DARKBLOOM_ROUTED_SHARED_SWIGLU_ROWS=4`; with the seed-prefill linkage
(prefill ≈ 0.34 effective weight), QHOIST is the cheapest next experiment.

At this point on the curve, candidate-to-candidate differences are smaller than

genuinely exercises them rather than merely proving the edits are wired. That is
a deliberate selection criterion: I previously shipped a change whose kernel was
nax-gated and never ran locally, and its "verification" was worthless — the
function-constant list carrying it is built only when `!expert_aligned`, so it
was never bound on the dispatched kernel. Reachability needs the same
dispatch-downward discipline as exactness.

No local timing claim: this box's decode noise is 5.9% CV across four runs of
identical code.

## Ablations (same binary, one mechanism each)

```text
DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_SORTED_MOE_TAIL=0          restore scatterUnsort path
DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_NVFP4_GATED_OUTPUT_QMV=0    restore softplus + QMV chain
DARKBLOOM_L5_UNROLL=0                        restore unroll depth 2
```

## Exactness

All four are vectorisation width, kernel fusion, comparator count or unroll
depth; none changes an accumulation order.

- **BF16x4 tail**: four adjacent columns travel as one `bfloat4`; Metal
  arithmetic is componentwise, so each component keeps its own ordered
  expert-0-through-7 BF16 product/add chain.
- **NVFP4 gated-output QMV**: the softplus is the same FP32 LogAddExp text with
  the same single `float(bfloat(gate))` rounding, and the contraction retains
  the stock QMV geometry exactly — 2 simdgroups x 4 rows, 512-value K blocks,
  group-16 scales via `laguna_nvfp4_scale`, strict per-row K-order accumulation,
  final `simd_sum`. No `split_k` (QMV, not `qmm_splitk`).
- **Comparator / unroll**: comparison count and loop structure; the reduction
  order over experts is preserved.

## Caveats

- Per-mechanism figures come from **different sessions with different
  baselines**; summing them is optimistic, and 1, 3, 4 all touch prefill so they
  will not be fully additive.
- Mechanism 4 may be **inert** on this tree. Its only consumer,
  `lagunaGatedOutputProjection`, sits behind `gateIsActivated`, and I could not
  establish from the guard chain alone whether that is ever true on the shipped
  decode path — the trace flag does not propagate into the sandboxed worker. It
  is harmless and ablatable either way, but I am not claiming its measured
  -0.23% transfers here.
- Credit belongs to the original authors of PR749, PR753, PR761 and PR762.

## Next step

The mining method is the durable finding, not this particular bundle. As long as
baseline variance exceeds candidate variance, validated mechanisms will keep
being stranded in rejected PRs, and re-basing them onto the live frontier is
cheaper than inventing new ones.

commits was +165/-929). Publishing each submission's base commit in the PR body,
or rejecting a submission whose editable paths revert a mechanism promoted after
its base, would stop the frontier moving backwards. Publishing the paired
baseline alongside the score would also let solvers separate a real regression
from an unlucky draw without reconstructing it from `speedup x candidate`.
