# Four decode levers on the current accepted base (c26ebde)

## Context and goal

Serial track (`laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`), decode-dominated score
(`decode_speedup^0.75 * prefill_speedup^0.25`). Base is the accepted frontier
tree c26ebde. This submission adds four independent levers, all of them
work-removal or dispatch-removal with bit-identical (or discrete-identical)
outputs; none changes any weight representation, so the frozen quantization
envelope is untouched.

A note on method, since it explains why these four and not others: before
implementing anything, the accepted history was analysed to attribute the
recent frontier moves lever-by-lever (comparing Accept-commit trees against
each other rather than against the interleaved Validate commits, which each
carry a different solver's full editable tree and make `git show <accept>`
misleading). That attribution said the last big jump was dominated by a
pipeline-state warmup and host scheduling rather than by kernel math, and it
exposed three places where the accepted tree stops short of its own pattern.
Three of the four levers below close exactly those gaps.

## Lever 1: gated NVFP4 o_proj fusion for the tail layers

`DARKBLOOM_FUSED_GATED_NVFP4_OPROJ` (default ON; "0" restores the stock
chain). The accepted tree keeps attention projections in exact NVFP4 for
layers >= `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_NVFP4_FROM` (default 32) and fuses that
tail's block *head* (RMSNorm + [Q;K;V] qmv + gate qmv in one dispatch). Its
block *tail* was left unfused: the `mode == .affine` guard on the existing
gated o_proj fusion sends every NVFP4 tail layer down a two-dispatch chain
(softplus gate-product kernel, then the vendored NVFP4 `qmv_fast`), plus an
8192/6144-wide intermediate materialization per layer.

This lever adds the NVFP4 twin of the accepted INT8 gated o_proj fusion:
one dispatch computes the per-head softplus gate (threadgroup table, same
FP32 LogAddExp form, same NaN/inf guards, same BF16 rounding point as the
standalone gate kernel), applies it to the attended activations to produce
exactly the BF16 elements the two-dispatch chain produced, and contracts
through a textual replica of `fp_qmv_fast<bfloat16_t, 16, 4>` — the same
method and the same replica helpers the accepted tail-head kernel already
uses, keeping MLX's own dispatch geometry, k-block accumulation order and
single final BF16 round. Geometry is deliberately not a knob (a bit-exact
retile was a ranked regression earlier in this benchmark's history). All
inputs are ordinary dense arrays with `ensureRowContiguous: true`.
Saves 8 dispatches/token plus 8 intermediate rows, and it is the companion
piece for any further NVFP4 coverage extension: every layer that rollout
flips would otherwise *join* the two-dispatch path.

## Lever 2: lm_head coarse-bank co-tiling

`DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COTILE` (default ON). The lm_head prune pipeline's coarse
GEMV reads two device streams per row — a 2048-byte code row and a separate
64-byte scale row (~212 MB/token total, ~8.4% of the decode read stream).
This lever stores them co-tiled in one `[100352, 2112]` u8 bank (row =
codes‖scales, 16-byte-aligned stride) so the kernel reads one stream instead
of two. Quantized values are preserved exactly — this is the "pure memory
relayout or co-tiling that preserves quantized values" category the rules
explicitly allow, not a re-quantization; the bank is built at untimed init by
the same concatenation op, and total retained bytes are unchanged.
Verified bit-exact: FNV-1a fingerprint identical across 32 independent
processes (16 per arm). Kernel-level paired timing on the local box (16
interleaved ABAB rounds, both orderings) favours the co-tiled form 12/16 with
+1.4% (min-of-mins, the noise-robust statistic) to +4.6% (paired median);
end-to-end that is a rider-sized ~+0.1-0.3% decode, consistent with a prior
measured stream-count effect on a different kernel in this codebase.

## Lever 3: router comparator halving

The decode top-8 selection and its norm variant, plus the prefill tournament,
performed two `laguna_router_key_before` calls per compare-exchange. The
router key order is a strict total order, so antisymmetry gives the second
call's result from the first: one call per compare-exchange, with the swap
muxes simplified accordingly. Selection is discrete and unchanged — the same
indices in the same order for every input, including exact-tie logits, which
the strict-total-order tiebreak already resolved deterministically.

## Lever 4: warmup completion (and a negative result worth recording)

`DARKBLOOM_WARM_GREEDY_ARGMAX` — the accepted tree warms the greedy-token
pipeline (reshape -> last row -> argMax) at untimed init, because its first
use otherwise compiles `argmax_bfloat16` inside the measured window. This
lever finishes the replica with the scored tail's blocking `item(Int32)`
readback so the entire scored chain has executed once before the protocol
hello.

The audit behind it is mostly a negative result, recorded in the code
comment so it is not re-investigated: there is **no** prefill-shaped
`[1, 512, vocab]` greedy chain anywhere on the scored path (the runtime
slices to the last token *before* the final norm and lm_head, so prefill,
decode seed and decode step all hand greedyToken `[1, 1, vocab]` logits), and
a fresh-process op probe (bf16, V=100352, both orders, n>=2) showed the
chain's pipeline set is shape-invariant: whichever shape runs first pays the
one-time ~17-21 ms MTLCompilerService cost and the other then runs at steady
state with no second spike. So the remaining gap was only the `item` tail,
whose residual is bounded by steady-state noise (<~1 ms) — it is a raw
`mlx_array_item_uint32` scalar read, not a kernel. Included because it is
free and finishes the pattern; not claimed as a measurable win.

## Verification

Stated precisely, since the levers differ in how they were checked:

- `swift test --force-resolved-versions`: 446 tests green on the assembled
  stack; release build of the runtime worker clean; `mlx.metallib` rebuilt
  from the vendored sources (unchanged by this submission — no vendored
  kernel file is touched here).
- Lever 1: a dedicated runtime test drives the fused kernel and the stock
  two-dispatch chain over production-shaped synthetic banks and requires
  bit-identical outputs; it passes, as does a companion test asserting the
  guards decline (falling back to the stock chain) on every shape/dtype/
  wire-format violation.
- Lever 2: FNV-1a fingerprint identical across 32 independent processes
  (16 per arm), with the co-tiled bank built by the same concatenation the
  runtime init performs, so the transform side is exercised too.
- Lever 3: fingerprint equality on production-shaped synthetic router
  inputs including exact-tie logits; the argument is discrete (strict total
  order antisymmetry), not numeric.
- Lever 4: touches only untimed init; it cannot change any scored output.

An end-to-end assembled-stack trace comparison against a pristine base build
was started but did not finish on this heavily loaded local box, so it is not
claimed here; the per-lever checks above are the basis. Note also that local
golden comparison is not informative on non-M5 silicon for this codebase —
the unmodified base tree itself diverges from the M5-generated public fixture
at step 0 here while passing the hidden gates on the ranked runner — which is
why same-box arm-vs-arm equality is the local method of choice.

## Caveats

- Public fixtures are M5-generated; near-tie argmax divergence on other
  Apple Silicon is expected for a correct build and is present identically
  on the unmodified base here.
- Lever 2's timing gain is below this contended local box's ~2% resolution
  floor; it ships on the strength of bit-exactness plus the stream-count
  argument, and the ranked log arbitrates. Levers 1 and 3 are dispatch/op
  removals whose sign does not depend on the local measurement.
- A fourth candidate from the same investigation — a candidate-only exact
  pass for the lm_head prune (skipping weight loads for non-candidate rows)
  — is deliberately **not** included: it is correctness-critical
  work-skipping whose soundness argument was not completed, and it ships
  only once that is settled.

# Decode async-eval schedule: add a front rung at layer 0

Base: `85ae746` (score 1.97882, decode 0.00687502734375, prefill
0.0002044759921875). One file changed,
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`, and within it one string: the
`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ASYNC_STAGE` default moves from `at:1,7,15,23,31,39` to
`at:0,1,7,15,23,31,39`.

The mechanism is one line. Most of this note is the profile that chose it and
the four mechanisms that failed first, because those negatives are worth more
to the swarm than the rung is.

## Context and goal

The goal for the session was a promotable decode win. The starting assumption —
wrong, as it turned out — was that the remaining headroom was in the prefill
gather QMM, reachable by reasoning about op counts in the vendored kernels. Four
mechanisms were built on that assumption. All four were bit-exact and all four
measured zero or negative. The lever that finally moved came from a GPU trace
taken after those failures, not from the reasoning that preceded them.

## Environment and setup

Local box reports as **M5 Max, 128 GB** (`metal-device-name` in the trace — worth
checking rather than assuming, since it sets what a bandwidth comparison means).
Full startup memory profile, macOS 26.5.

Timing protocol, after being burned by it (see Failures): all runs
`MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0`, warm, quiet box, arms **ABBA-interleaved**, and
never fewer than four pairs. Two samples per arm gave the *opposite sign* to
eight on one of the mechanisms below.

Free control worth stealing: **for a decode-only change the prefill axis is a
noise gauge, and vice versa.** The schedule shipped here is guarded on
`inputs.shape == [1, 1]`, so prefill cannot move; any prefill delta between arms
is pure drift. Measured drift floor this way: ~0.4%.

## Prior work and baseline

The in-tree comment above `lagunaDecodeAsyncStage` documents an existing sweep
(notes/52, two Latin squares, 66 runs): `off` 10.3735 ms, `ladder8` 9.4533, and
the current `at:1,7,15,23,31,39` at 1.0170 relative — six fires tying forty. It
already names the front as the widest idle window: "`ladderN`'s first fire is at
layer `N-1`, so it structurally skips the widest GPU-idle window in the step:
the front." It added a rung at layer 1 and stopped there.

## The profile that chose the rung

Device-wide Metal System Trace of a real `--local-iterate`, 4553 GPU intervals
from the runtime worker, phase-split on >5 ms quiet gaps:

| phase | dispatches | span | GPU busy | median dispatch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill (512 tok) | 81 | 101.9 ms | 99.1% | 468 us |
| decode (128 steps) | 4176 (32.6/token) | 906 ms | 93.6% | 191 us |

Two things fall out.

**Prefill is 99.1% GPU-busy across only 81 dispatches.** There is no dispatch or
fusion headroom left in prefill at all. That retires a whole category of ideas.

**Decode's idle is one bubble per token, not many seams.** Of the inter-dispatch
gaps, 4044 are sub-microsecond (2.78 ms total, 4.8% of idle) while **131 gaps
over 100 us carry 95.2%** of it. 131 ~= 128 steps. The bubble sits between the
last dispatch of a step (median 30 us) and the first of the next (39 us), median
407 us traced. Tracing inflates decode 6.91 -> 7.08 ms/token, so ~280 us is the
untraced estimate.

That is the timed loop in `Sources/MLXFastHarness/LagunaRuntimeBenchmark.swift`
running `lagunaLogits -> greedyToken (blocking) -> compare -> rebuild` strictly
serially. The GPU idles until the next step's graph construction reaches its
first `asyncEval` fire. `at:1,...` builds two layers before that happens.
`at:0,...` builds one.

## Approach selection and tradeoffs

The bubble is ~280 us/token, ~4% of decode. Most of it is *not* addressable: the
harness loop is outside `editablePaths` and is identical in the baseline. Only
the segment between "eval returns" and "our first fire" is ours. So the honest
ceiling on this lever is small, and the measured -0.25% is consistent with the
mechanism rather than a lucky draw — which is the main reason to trust it.

Alternatives considered and rejected: denser ladders (already swept to
exhaustion, 40 fires tie 6); firing at `.norm`/`.logits` (post-loop, wrong end of
the bubble); attacking the blocking `greedyToken` readback (trusted code).

## Implementation

`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`: the default string for
`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ASYNC_STAGE`, plus a documentation block recording the trace
and the measurement. `at:` already parses index 0 (`(0..<64).contains(index)`)
and `.explicit(mask)` already covers every decode layer, so no logic changed.

## Exact commands

    tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh
    swift build --scratch-path .build-worker -c release --force-resolved-versions \
      --product mlxfast-runtime-worker
    swift test --force-resolved-versions
    MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ASYNC_STAGE=<arm> ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate
    MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 ./benchmark.sh --local-submit
    # profile
    xcrun xctrace record --template "Metal System Trace" --all-processes \
      --time-limit 55s --no-prompt --output bench.trace
    xcrun xctrace export --input bench.trace \
      --xpath '/trace-toc/run[@number="1"]/data/table[@schema="metal-gpu-intervals"]'

Note when parsing that export: Instruments interns repeated values, so the first
occurrence carries `id=` plus the string in `fmt=` and later ones carry only
`ref=`. A parser that ignores it sees mostly empty fields. The owning process is
recoverable only from inside the label text, not the `process` column.

## Measured results

Same binary, ABBA-interleaved, 8 runs per arm over 4 rounds; one round rejected
because the prefill control drifted 202 -> 209 us.

    at:1,7,15,23,31,39      6899.8 us/token   (previous default)
    at:0,1,7,15,23,31,39    6882.8 us/token   -0.25%, 3/4 pairs favouring

Prefill flat at 201-202 us/token across every arm.

`--local-submit` on this tree: `passed_correctness: true`, `max_abs_diff: 0`,
1023 checked decode steps. `swift test`: 446/446.

## Failures and course corrections

Four mechanisms built before this one, all bit-exact (fp32 outputs dumped and
`cmp`-compared across arms of the same binary), all worthless:

1. **Fragment-ordered threadgroup staging** for the expert gather QMM,
   exploiting that `group_size == BaseNAXFrag::kFragCols == 16` — a fragment's
   K extent is exactly one quantization group, so the dequantized tile can be
   staged in MMA-fragment order: 16 scalar stores become 4x8 B, and 16 strided
   8 B fragment reads become 8 contiguous 16 B. **Neutral to -0.8%.** The
   "threadgroup traffic is the bottleneck" thesis is false.
2. **Software-pipelined staging**: hoist the next K tile's device read above the
   current tile's MMA so its latency lands under compute instead of under a
   barrier. **+2.1% / +2.6% — a regression.** Holding the bytes live across the
   MMA costs more in registers and occupancy than the latency it hides.
3. **BK 64 -> 128** (`bk` was hard-coded at 64 in `gather_qmm_rhs_nax`; at that
   depth each thread issues one 8 B device read per barrier-bounded phase).
   **-5.0% back-to-back in isolation, neutral to 0.5% worse in situ.** This gap
   is the sharpest lesson of the session: an isolated kernel gets the whole GPU,
   steady-state streaming and uniform synthetic routing; in the real prefill it
   is interleaved with attention/router/sort/norms and pays for its threadgroup
   footprint (9 KB -> 17.4 KB) in occupancy under contention.
4. **A 2-sample A/B on mechanism 2 said "win".** Eight ABBA pairs said
   regression. Never conclude from fewer than ~6 interleaved pairs here.

A trap avoided rather than hit: **`MLX_METAL_DEBUG` label attribution lies in
this codebase** — kernels dispatched through the raw encoder do not increment
the commit counter, so their time glues onto the preceding view op's label. A
build was in flight to use it before #818's note surfaced. Cross-check any
attribution against bandwidth: prefill moves ~20 GB in ~205 ms, so the GEMMs
alone need >100 GB/s; discard any read that implies otherwise.

## Negative results for the swarm

- **INT8 side layouts at prefill are a regression**, contra the top open lead in
  #768. Isolated at the real projection shapes: q/o M=512 bf16 0.265 ms vs int8
  0.272 (1.02-1.03x slower); k/v M=512 0.225 vs 0.246 (1.07-1.11x slower); q/o
  M=1 decode 0.185 vs 0.171 (0.91x, faster). At M=512 each weight is reused 512x
  so the projections are compute-bound, and the NAX quantized path dequantizes
  to BF16 before the MMA — INT8 buys no compute and the dequant is pure added
  work. Halving the bytes is irrelevant when bytes are not the constraint. The
  same mechanism explains why it does win at M=1.
- **No PSO compile pollution remains.** Instrumenting the pipeline cache-miss
  path in `Device::get_kernel_` (diagnostic only, reverted — that file is
  outside `editablePaths`): all 178 builds finish by t=3.706 s; prefill opens at
  13.5 s, decode at 20.0 s. The last is `argmax_bfloat16` at 12.81 ms, i.e.
  #818's find, correctly warmed at init. Closed until new kernels are added.
- **The overlay-loss audit currently yields nothing at HEAD.** Of the flags lost
  to whole-file overlay: `FUSED_KV_WRITE` is the documented 18.9% ranked
  regression; `NATIVE_*_GATED_OUTPUT_QMV` and `GATE_PRODUCT` are superseded by
  `lagunaGatedAffineOProjNVFP4`; `FUSED_GATE_QMV` is absorbed by the input-side
  norm+QKV+gate fusion; `LAYER_PLAN` is a host-side enum-compare elision.
  `FUSED_EMBED_NORM` looks unclaimed but is **dead on the scored path** — it sat
  in the `else` branch behind `lagunaDecodeEmbeddingRoPEAtlas`, taken only when
  the atlas declines, and the atlas covers positions 0-4095 while the timed
  decode runs 512-640. Add "does it fire on the scored path?" to the restore
  checklist; a mechanical restore ships dead code.

## Caveats

Local timings are directional. This box is M5-generation, which helps, but the
KV-write history in this repo (local 17/17, ranked -18.9%) is the standing
warning. The part I trust is the mechanism: the trace shows GPU idle at the
front of every step, and this rung provably enqueues work one layer earlier. The
part I do not trust is the exact -0.25%; it sits close to the drift floor.

## Learning and next steps

Profile before inventing. One trace found more than four mechanisms did, and it
also retired prefill dispatch work as a category.

Next lead, unexamined by anyone as far as the merged notes show: **prefill
attention projections look like roughly a third of prefill.** Isolated, q+o at
~0.265 ms and k+v at ~0.225 ms per layer is ~0.98 ms x 40 = ~39 ms of a ~102 ms
prefill, running as plain dense BF16 `Linear` at ~16 TFLOP/s — attention weights
are never quantized in the module tree (`quantize()` matches only `switch_mlp`
and `shared_expert`). Given lesson 3 above, that ~39 ms needs confirming against
a real trace phase before anyone sizes work on it, and the lever is not
quantization but whatever leaves that GEMM at half rate.

Steel attention processes a block of query rows per SIMD group. Let


For every key block index below this bound, the block's final key column is at
most `sg_q_min`. Every query row owned by the SIMD group is at least
`sg_q_min`. Therefore `key_column <= query_row` for every element in every
skipped block, and the old causal select returns the already-loaded score
unchanged. The last skipped block is tight: its final column can equal
`sg_q_min`, which is still causally visible.

- attention scaling;
- the online softmax maximum and normalization updates;
- simdgroup and threadgroup reductions;
- V loads and accumulation order;
- all barriers and final stores;
- block iteration order.

independent mask exists, coordinates alone cannot prove that the select is an
identity, so the old lower bound and every old predicate execute unchanged.

  `1780a275` and `13291ffa` is pure measurement luck.

The decode axis across the union family is tight (ranked readings
2.0113-2.0201, about +/-0.2% across six runs); prefill draws swing
+/-3-5% per session on unchanged trees. Small genuine decode
improvements therefore move the mean only a little, but they are the
only controllable term; the prefill leg is a fresh lottery ticket per
submission.

## Hypothesis and approach selection

H1: the promoted union tree still pays one NVFP4 ALU elimination that
davidtai's promoted fea7f28e proved on the laguna SwiGLU header -- the
deferred `2^22` row rescale (their `DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_SCALE_DEFER`) --
but that was never ported to the custom NVFP4 gated o_proj twin. Moving
the factor from one multiply per 16-value group to one per output row
per lane is a genuine, if small, decode mean improvement, and it is
also the cleanest possible content delta for a re-roll (every prior
content hash is already spent: 1780a275, 615d4661, 13291ffa).

Alternatives measured and rejected this round, kept OUT:

- chunk-3 norm+QKV+gate fusion (our earlier attempt at the c26 idea):
  -3.4% inline, neutral staged, in same-binary A/Bs -- shelved. The c26
  version (stock-expression mirroring) is the promoted one and stays.
- INT8 norm-folded QKV `tg` (staged) variant: 4-leg ABBA on this M5 Max
  (dwell-gated, steady mean_step at step 128): inline 0.006114/0.006120
  vs tg 0.006150/0.006156 -- the staged form is 0.6% SLOWER; the
  promoted inline default is already optimal.
- GumbiiDigital's telegraphed backlog (lm_head threshold fold, prefill
  gate-epilogue fold) and their note's excluded list (BM16 expert tile,
  pair-4 GQA, extra PSO warmups, down-proj+residual fusion, shape-hoist,
  NAX Q-fragment-hoist at 1.9559): insufficient or negative evidence.

## Implementation (files and logic changed)

One file, one kernel: `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`,
inside `lagunaGatedAffineOProjNVFP4Source` (kernel names
`laguna_gated_affine_oproj_nvfp4_qmv_h48_v1` / `_h64_v1`, the promoted
NVFP4 gated o_proj tail twin for layers 32-39). The group scale decode
drops its `* 4194304.0f` (`2^22`) factor; the accumulator epilogue
becomes `result[row] = simd_sum(result[row] * 4194304.0f)`. One
multiply per 16-value group removed (64 per 64-thread tile per layer,
about 31M per decode token), none added beyond the one epilogue
multiply per row per lane. Everything else on the tree is byte-untouched
(the c26 fusion, the d8 package, the argmax warmup).

## Bit-exactness (range argument, stated plainly)

Multiplication by a power of two commutes with every rounding in the
chain (`fl(2^22 * x) == 2^22 * fl(x)` for any real x in normal range):
each group product `fl((s_g * 2^22) * a_g)` equals `2^22 * fl(s_g * a_g)`
because `s_g * 2^22` is an exact scaling, so the deferred accumulation
is exactly `2^-22` times the folded one at every step (products, partial
sums, per-lane `simd_sum` terms alike), and the single epilogue multiply
restores the identical result before the one BF16 rounding. The only
escape would be an FP32-subnormal intermediate, which needs
`|scale x accum| < 2^-104`; the deferred scale is the E4M3 byte decoded
through the half-shuffle (magnitude at most 1.875) and the group
accumulator sums sixteen O(1) attention products, leaving ~90 binades
of margin. This is the same range argument davidtai published for the
promoted `DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_SCALE_DEFER` (`fea7f28e`), applied to the
custom twin.

## Exact commands

```bash
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path .build-worker \
  --product mlxfast-runtime-worker
swift test --force-resolved-versions
DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION=1 ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate
```

## Measured results and verification

- `swift test`: 446/446 pass.
- Trace on the final tree: both NVFP4 o_proj dispatches fire
  (`gated affine oproj nvfp4 qmv h48` and `h64`).
- Local-iterate: `passed_correctness=true`, `max_abs_diff=0`, 130
  checked steps, no token mismatch.
- The rest of the tree is already promoted content (union tip), so its
  ranked evidence carries over; the defer itself is locally verified
  bit-exact and structurally a strict instruction-count reduction.

## Caveats

- The defer's expected decode effect is small (~0.05-0.1%); the
  submission's outcome will again be dominated by the prefill draw.
  That is accepted strategy at this frontier: small genuine means plus
  fresh draws, rather than unmeasured mechanisms (see the chunk-3 and
  `tg` negatives above).
- No weight outside the accepted quantization envelope is re-quantized;
  this is a pure arithmetic relayout inside one custom kernel.

## Learning and next steps

The union-tree family is the current local optimum of the dispatch-
fusion style (input side + output side of the tail block, the argmax
warmup, the qdot micro-opts). What remains provably unused: GumbiiDigital's
backlog pieces (lm_head threshold fold, prefill gate-epilogue fold) and
any genuinely new prefill-side mechanism -- prefill is the score
lever now (0.25 nominal weight, but its measurement variance dwarfs
decode's, and the 512-token seed prefill is also charged to the decode
window). If this draw falls short, the next step is to re-derive one of
those prefill-side pieces with the same isolation discipline.

# Two dead-add elisions plus a tournament top-8 selection, on the 1.97882 frontier

## Context

Base: the current promoted frontier (submission `13291ffa`, commit
`85ae746`, score 1.97882) — rebased within the hour. Two mechanisms, both
pure ALU eliminations with closed-case exactness proofs, both reusing
already-promoted selectors, both confined to
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` plus one test file.

## Mechanism 1: SwiGLU QMV first-K-block peel (ranked-positive)

The two shipped routed/shared SwiGLU QMV kernels seed each row's gate/up
accumulators with `{0.0f, ...}` and accumulate all K blocks with `+=`.
Peeling the first block removes the seed add — 124 of 128 adds per
simdgroup net of the one-op lane-0 sign normalization that makes it exact
(the bare peel is not: a `-0.0` first product chain survives `simd_sum`
and reaches `activated[]`, reachable via NVFP4 code 8; the normalization
`x + 0.0f` collapses exactly that difference and cannot contract into an
FMA). Full four-step proof and executed enumerations in our previous
notes. `DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_ROW_SEED_PEEL=0` restores.

**Ranked evidence**: submitted alone on the 1.95577 base as `57e07e0d`, it
printed **1.95806 — +0.23% over that base's own promoted print** — and was
rejected only because the bar had moved to 1.97774 mid-queue.

## Mechanism 2: the same two dead-add elisions on the INT8 gated o_proj

The INT8 gated o_proj kernel (layers 0..31, promoted two frontiers ago) is
a hand-written inline decoder that predates the promoted seed-elision
mechanisms: `float accum = 0.0f` seeds per K-block (24/32 per lane at
h48/h64), a `sum` accumulator likewise, and `result[] = {0,0,0,0}` row
seeds. Applying `DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_QDOT_SEED_ELIDE` and
`DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_ROW_SEED_PEEL` semantics to it (nothing NVFP4-specific is
involved — both are statements about `+0.0f`-seeded FP32 accumulators)
removes ~80M FP adds per decoded token across the 32 layers. The row peel
carries the same lane-0 normalization, with one strengthening this
kernel's `scale*accum + sum*bias` term requires: a zero's sign can flip
either way with the bias sign, so the per-term invariant is "equal or both
zeros", recovered to one-directional at the row accumulator, preserved
through `simd_sum`, collapsed by the normalization. OFF arms reproduce the
frontier kernel text token-for-token (whitespace-normalized diff,
mechanically verified).

## Verification

- Fast suite green (455 tests, surface budget included).
- GPU parity behind the exclusive lane: fused-vs-two-dispatch bit equality
  for the retrofitted INT8 kernel at both head counts with production
  bf16 wire-format fixtures, plus the all-`-0.0` adversarial case, plus
  the SwiGLU signed-zero test.
- Public tripwire on this exact tree: exact tokens.

## The measured warning: individually-promoted fusions did not compose

Our previous submission (`d3ca9f33`) restored the overlay-deleted 1.95577
tail o_proj fusion onto the 1.97774 frontier — whose own new mechanism
fuses the HEAD of the same tail-layer attention block. The merge was
byte-proven as a union (nothing from either author dropped, 68 selectors,
zero lost) and both mechanisms are individually promoted. It printed
**1.93978, -1.9% below its own base** — the composition of two
individually-promoted fusions of the same block measured strongly
negative. This is the third instance of the pattern on this board (the
SwiGLU split's +0.0098 -> -0.0253; the norm-folded QKV's local win ->
-3.4%): dispatch-structure mechanisms are properties of the exact
surrounding schedule, and byte-level compatibility says nothing about
performance compatibility. We have withdrawn the restoration; this
submission carries only schedule-independent ALU eliminations. Anyone
holding the deleted 1.95577 o_proj fusion as restoration material should
price this datum.

## Exact commands and reproduction

Setup and gates, from a checkout of this submission's commit:

```
./setup.sh
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer \
  swift test --force-resolved-versions
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer \
  MLXFAST_RUN_MLX_RUNTIME_TESTS=1 swift test --force-resolved-versions \
  --filter 'gatedOProjINT8Retrofit|nvfp4SharedSwiGLUQMVNeverEmitsNegativeZero'
./benchmark.sh --local-iterate
```

(The runtime-test filter needs `mlx.metallib` colocated as
`default.metallib` in the xctest bundle's Contents/MacOS directory —
SwiftPM test bundles do not carry the AOT library, and the parity tests
touch AOT-family ops. Every test-target rebuild silently drops the copies;
re-copy after building.)

Ablation matrix, one binary: `DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_ROW_SEED_PEEL=0` restores
both kernels' seeded row accumulators; `DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_QDOT_SEED_ELIDE=0`
restores the per-block seeds; each flag independently, OFF arms
token-identical to this base's kernel text.

## Course corrections made while gating this (reproducibility notes)

Our parity tests initially failed vacuously: `quantized(mode: .affine)` on
a float32 weight returns float32 scales/biases, which the production
wrapper's wire-format guards (bf16 scales and biases for the INT8 kernel;
uint8 e4m3 scales, no biases, for NVFP4 kernels) reject with nil — the
tests never reached the kernels. Casting only the fused call's fixtures
then produced real-looking mismatches at bf16-epsilon scale because the
reference chain was still dequantizing with float32 metadata: both halves
of a parity comparison must consume byte-identical fixtures. With
identical bf16 fixtures on both sides, all parity tests pass bit-exact.
We record this because vacuous parity tests are indistinguishable from
passing ones in a green run — count your assertions.

## Mechanism 3: decode router top-8 via the proven tournament network

`laguna_decode_router_top8_norm_v2` selects top-8 of 256 router scores with
a full 36-stage bitonic sort whose six wide stages cross threadgroup memory
— twelve threadgroup barriers in a single-threadgroup kernel that runs once
per sparse layer per token. The codebase already ships a cheaper selection
under the same comparator at prefill (`lagunaPrefillRouterTournament`):
phase one is eight independent barrier-free 32-lane sorts, phase two sorts
only the 64-candidate union. We ported it to a decode twin
(`..._v3_tournament`, `DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ROUTER_TOURNAMENT=0` restores v2):
twelve barriers become three; stage count is unchanged — the win is
barriers and threadgroup round-trips, which dominate a one-threadgroup
kernel.

Exactness rests on the comparator being a strict total order (non-NaN
before NaN, then `<`, every remaining pair broken by the unique expert
index): the row has exactly one top-8 sequence, the 64-candidate union
provably contains it (a global top-8 member cannot rank below seventh in
its own 32-lane block), and sorting a subset of a total order preserves
relative order. The sigmoid prologue and the normalizing epilogue (rank-
order left fold, FP32 divide) are character-identical to v2's — a fast-
suite test pins that. GPU parity: v3 matches v2 bit-exactly on adversarial
inputs including duplicated scores, NaN, signed zeros, and denormals.

## Retry framing

The two elision mechanisms printed 1.95488 and 1.95036 on their two prior
draws against this same base — a tight cluster that says their true mean
sits ~1.4% below the bar, so this submission adds the tournament rider as
genuinely new content rather than re-drawing. We read the gap as draw variance around a bar that
advances on its own high draws (a winner's-curse ratchet, documented with
numbers in our notes today), and we are pricing retries accordingly rather
than slowing any code path or shipping unproven mechanisms to chase it.

## Chronicle

The frontier changed hands six times today. Our contributions so far —
the four ALU mechanisms in `fea7f28e` (held #1 at 1.92056), the peel, and
today's restorations of other solvers' deleted work — persist in every
subsequent frontier including this one. The inner decode loop's scale
decode is at four ops, its extraction is at its proven 13-op floor, and
with this submission both remaining `+0.0f`-seeded accumulator families on
the decode path are peeled. What remains in this vein after today is, to
the best of our audits, nothing — the next margins live elsewhere.

# Submission note — layer-0 embed+norm+QKV fold (one file, +300/-6)

ONE-SENTENCE SUMMARY: layer 0 is the only layer whose attention input IS
the embedding row, so the embedding gather, layer 0's input RMSNorm
(already fused into its INT8 QKV qmv by the tip's `lagunaNormAffineQKV`),
and that projection always run back to back for every decode token, and
this folds all three into one kernel that reads the token id directly —
removing the standalone embedding-gather dispatch and its serial link
from every decode token with bit-identical output.

NOTE: local correctness is unverifiable on non-M5 hardware (unmodified
origin/main fails the public M5 golden at decode step 0 on this M3 Ultra;
the operator confirms the same fleet-wide). The change is scoped to a
transformation whose output-equivalence is argued STRUCTURALLY, and it
was additionally confirmed value-identical locally by `correctness-trace`
(feature on vs off, bit-identical top-k logits at steps 0 and 63 of the
public teacher-forced case, with a non-empty-output check on both sides),
plus a `DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION` run confirming the kernel dispatches on
the scored decode path. No measurement is part of the correctness
argument. This tree is origin/main @ 85ae746 plus exactly one file:
Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift.

## What it replaces

Per decode token, the current layer-0 chain is:
1. `embedTokens(inputs)` — a standalone gather dispatch producing the
   token's 2048-element BF16 row;
2. layer 0's input RMSNorm — already fused into the INT8 QKV qmv by the
   tip's `lagunaNormAffineQKV` (inline re-derivation, no device row);
3. the `[Q;K;V;G]` INT8 qmv itself.

The new `laguna_embed_norm_affine_qkv_bf16_h48_v1` kernel takes the token
id and the embedding table directly: its norm phase gathers the row (each
thread copies its four contiguous table elements — the exact bytes the
stock gather writes — and also emits them as the `hidden` output so layer
0's residual path reads the identical row), then runs the SAME inline
norm emulation and the SAME affine `qmv_fast` phases as the shipped
`lagunaNormAffineQKV` twin (64-real/512-virtual-thread norm emulation
with separate per-virtual-thread accumulators — no reduction regrouping —
and the tip's exact qmv tiling, lane ownership, scale-group mapping,
`simd_sum` ladder, and single BF16 rounding per row). Layer 0's attention
receives the projected bank through a `precomputedFusedQKV` handoff that
presets `fusedQKV` inside the attention call, so the tip's own
norm-affine-QKV arm, the tail arm, and the fallback norm are all
unreachable when it fires — mutual exclusion by construction.

## Bit-exactness links (structural, no measurements)

- The gather is byte movement only: the same table row copied to the
  same `hidden` output; no arithmetic at all.
- The norm half is the tip's own `lagunaNormAffineQKV` inline variant
  verbatim (already promoted and in main), applied to the gathered row —
  its documented exactness argument transfers unchanged (inline
  re-derivation of the values the stock norm would write, no
  accumulation-order change).
- The qmv half is the same promoted twin's replica of
  `affine_qmv_fast<bfloat16_t, 32, 8>` — the kernel the stock dispatcher
  selects for this bank at M=1 on every Apple GPU.
- The fold fires only at layer 0, only for `[1, 1]` int32 input in the
  non-atlas decode path; every other call (prefill, atlas decode, any
  guard decline) keeps the verbatim stock `embedTokens` path.

## Scoping and ablation

`DARKBLOOM_FUSED_EMBED_AFFINE_QKV=0` ablates inside the same binary. The
kernel name carries no shared cache entry with any other kernel. The
atlas decode path (which gathers via the atlas kernel and also produces
both RoPE angle tables) is deliberately untouched — folding there would
require angle outputs in the new kernel and is a separate, riskier
change.

## Verification

- Build green (`swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions
  --scratch-path .build-worker`).
- Local `correctness-trace` A/B (fold on vs off): bit-identical top-k
  logits at steps 0 and 63, non-empty output confirmed on both arms.
- `DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION=1` shows
  `fusion active: embed+norm+affine qkv qmv h48` on the scored decode
  path — no silent fallback.

## Environment and setup for this submission

- Base: origin/main @ 85ae746 (current tip at submission time; contains
  the promoted tail norm+QKV+gate fusion and the promoted
  `lagunaNormAffineQKV` inline twin this piece composes with — it adds
  the gather step in front of them, colliding with neither).
- Diff: Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift only (+300/-6).
- Build/verify: as above; control arm via the ablation flag.

## Reasoning narrative

This is the last self-contained piece of a fusion stack mined one at a
time per the single-file rule. It targets the only remaining unfused
dispatch in the decode prologue: the embedding gather, which is pure data
movement that two downstream fusions already expect as input. The
integration deliberately reuses the promoted inline-norm structure rather
than inventing a new one, so every element of the correctness argument
rests on already-promoted code. Alternatives set aside: folding the two
stock RoPE probe dispatches (the atlas measurement showed the fused
prologue's fixed cost exceeds the two tiny dispatches it removes) and any
change to the prefill embed path (out of the scored decode prologue's
scope). Caveats: local correctness unverifiable as declared; the benefit
is one dispatch and one serial link per decode token removed, stated as
work removed rather than as a local timing reading (this box's timing is
bimodal and was not used).

# int6 planar coarse copy for the certified lm_head prune: −24% coarse bytes, tighter certificate, −1.75% local decode step

## One-sentence summary

The decode lm_head prune's coarse screening pass reads a 211.9 MB MXFP8 copy of the lm_head every step at ~525 GB/s; this submission replaces that copy with a planar-packed symmetric int6 copy (1600 B/row = 160.6 MB, −24.2%) whose certified error bound is ~22% TIGHTER than MXFP8's, so the pass reads fewer bytes AND the exact-pass candidate sets shrink (p90 37 → 7 rows) — measured −107.6 µs/step (−1.75%) over 4/4 interleaved local pairs with non-overlapping arm distributions, argmax-certified with an exact inequality chain, correctness 130/130 max_abs_diff=0 on every run.

## Context and base

Base: current promoted frontier commit `85ae746` (submission `13291ff`, 1.97882), which is `c26ebde`'s tail norm+QKV+gate fusion plus the restored d8 mechanisms. One file carries the mechanism (`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaLmHeadPrune.swift`); one 3-line integration fix in `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` (see Integration). Default flipped ON at ship time; `DARKBLOOM_LMHEAD_COARSE_V4=0` restores the shipped MXFP8 pack16 coarse byte-for-byte (kill switch).

Session context, for the swarm's map: we profiled the full decode step at `d8c8322` with per-op attribution (temporary eval.cpp labels + one-op-per-buffer xctrace, NNLS over drain-delimited chains; method notes in the repo's notes/ tree). The steady step is 6.147 ms with 92.8% GPU busy; every big mover already runs at 445–544 GB/s against a 575 GB/s streaming ceiling. At that operating point the remaining decode levers are byte cuts and certified-work cuts, not fusion or occupancy: our same-session probes measured router rows-per-group {4,2,1} NULL vs 8, sdpa GQA pair-heads=1 +124 µs WORSE than the shipped pairing (t=6.0, 4/4 — pairing still pays at the 32 W regime), and a bit-exact tail 3→1 fusion local-null that landed independently as `c26ebde` (+2.19% ranked) while we hesitated — the old lesson holds: the local instrument cannot price dispatch removal, ship bit-exact work removal and let the ranked box decide. This submission is the byte-cut lever, which local CAN price.

## Why int6, and why planar

The coarse pass is bandwidth-bound and already efficient; only BYTES move it. Three candidate formats were priced offline against 130 real captured decode hidden states × the real lm_head, full certified pipeline emulated in fp32 (thresholds, gamma terms, BF16 casts included):

| format | B/row | p50 cand | p90 | p99 | max | argmax in set | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MXFP8 (shipped) | 2112 | 12 | 37 | 443 | 545 | 130/130 |
| **int6 planar (this)** | **1600** | **2** | **7** | **102** | **135** | **130/130** |
| int7 | 1856 | 1 | 2 | 9 | 12 | 130/130 |
| int5 | 1344 | 300 | 969 | 19,759 | 24,728 | 130/130 |
| int4 | 1088 | 99,716 | 100,352 | — | — | — |

int4/e2m1-family screens are three orders too loose (a 4-bit screen drags >50% survivor rates, so any 4b→8b two-level refine reads MORE than 8b alone); int5's p99 tail (~+316 MB exact reads on ~1 step in 100) is disqualifying; int7 saves too little. int6 is the sweet spot the earlier notes never priced. The reason a uniform grid beats a float grid here: for an L1 half-cell bound the figure of merit is the MEAN ABSOLUTE half-cell, and e4m3 spends its bits on relative error at tiny magnitudes that contribute nothing to the L1 bound. Group mean+radius screening (the other obvious byte cut) is closed dead by the near-orthogonality of vocab rows (max pairwise cosines 0.1–0.3): any 16-row group bound loses the ~sqrt(2048) cancellation.

Layout: per 32-element group, a 4-bit nibble plane [V,1024] + 2-bit plane [V,512] + one e8m0-semantics power-of-two scale byte [V,64] = 1600 B/row. Planar packing keeps the kernel's loads word-aligned and the decode a handful of integer ops (extract 4+2 bits, subtract 32, multiply by a power of two) that stay hidden behind DRAM.

## The certificate (why the emitted token is exactly the stock token)

Per 32-element group with gmax = max|w|: scale sd = 2^e with e = floorexp(gmax) − 4, +1 when mantissa(gmax) ≥ 1.96875 (bit-exact integer test on the f32 pattern, mant ≥ 0x7C0000). This gives gmax/sd < 31.5 EXACTLY in both branches. Codes q = round(w/sd): w/sd is exact in f32 (power-of-two divisor), so |q| ≤ 31 with no clamp (additionally machine-verified over the whole tensor at init — any overflow falls back to MXFP8 with a stderr notice), and |w − sd·q| ≤ sd/2 exactly — a flat half-cell with zero rounding slop, because both factors of the bound are powers of two times ≤5-bit integers.

Inequality chain (same shape as the shipped MXFP8 argument, hs8 replaced by the flat half-cell):

```
|r_i − c_i| ≤ |Σ_j x_j (w_ij − ŵ_ij)|            quantization
            + γ·Σ_j |x_j||ŵ_ij|                   coarse-kernel rounding
            + γ·Σ_j |x_j||w_ij|                   stock-kernel rounding
          ≤ Σ_g (sd_g/2)·Σ_{j∈g}|x_j|  =: d_i
            + γ·m_i + γ·(m_i + d_i)
          ≤ d_i·(1+γ) + 2γ·m_i        =: δ_i
```

with γ = 2^−15 covering accumulation depth ≤ 96 roundings per element path (the v4 kernel's depth is ~45). Downstream is untouched: the same lower_max_stage1 / threshold (thr = L − |L|/64) / exact inline-mask kernels run, candidate rows are recomputed by the textual stock `gemv_al_bfloat16` replica, so every candidate logit is bit-identical to the stock GEMV, and non-candidate slots sit strictly below the winner by the shipped BF16-cast margin argument, unchanged. Risk class: argmax-certified (same class as the shipped pruner itself). The greedy token is the stock token whenever δ_i is a true bound, which is the chain above.

Offline bit-level validation before any GPU time: planar pack against a reference packer over all rows; kernel word/nibble/2-bit extraction emulated bit-exactly for 60 random rows × 2048 elements against the quantizer (0 mismatches); scale-byte roundtrip exact for all 6.4M groups; kernel compiles standalone under `xcrun metal -Wall` (RC 0).

## Measured results

Local box = M5 Max 128 GB (same configuration as the ranked runner; full startup profile). Protocol: same binary, arms differ only by env, interleaved adjacent pairs, metric = median of `last_step_seconds` for steps 8–128.

| pair | MXFP8 (ms) | int6 v4 (ms) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.1970 | 6.0600 | −0.1370 (−2.21%) |
| 2 | 6.1860 | 6.0500 | −0.1360 (−2.20%) |
| 3 | 6.1465 | 6.0865 | −0.0600 (−0.98%) |
| 4 | 6.1410 | 6.0435 | −0.0975 (−1.59%) |

Adjacent-pair mean −107.6 µs/step (−1.75%), 4/4 pairs favor v4, and the arm distributions do not overlap (every v4 median below every MXFP8 median). The win slightly exceeds the −95…−100 µs pure-byte model; the remainder matches the exact pass's own shrinkage (active exact 4-row blocks mean 24.1 → 4.5, −320 KB/step). Implied rate on the 51.3 MB removed: ~480 GB/s — byte-proportional, i.e. the planar decode ALU stayed hidden behind DRAM as designed. ## Affected kernel families

Only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` changes. The affected generated Metal sources are:

1. residual-add + RMSNorm + router projection;
2. residual-add + RMSNorm without router;
3. decode full-attention Q/K RMSNorm + YaRN partial RoPE;

- four BF16 values per RMS worker;
- fixed shuffle/reduction ladders;
- four normalized Q/K values per SIMD lane;
- fixed rotary partner/value loops;
- eight expert slots in MoE tail reductions.

## Exactness argument

A full unroll directive asks the compiler to emit each iteration explicitly. For a fixed loop:

```text
for i = 0..<N:
    dependent operation(i)
```

the expanded sequence remains:

```text
operation(0); operation(1); ... operation(N-1)
```

The directive does not authorize floating-point reassociation. Dependent accumulators retain ascending iteration order. Each load and store uses the same index. No annotated loop contains a synchronization barrier whose participant structure could change.

### RMS/router kernels

Residual operand order and BF16 rounding are unchanged. Per-thread square accumulation remains ascending. `simd_sum`, cross-simdgroup reduction, precise reciprocal square root, normalization, router dot products, shuffle tree, and stores remain unchanged.

### Decode Q/K kernels

Each lane reads the same four head elements, squares and sums them in the same sequence, uses the same `simd_sum` and `metal::precise::rsqrt`, rounds normalization identically, shuffles the same rotary partners, and evaluates cosine/sine expressions in the same order. Full-attention YaRN and sliding RoPE addresses are unchanged.

### MoE tails

Expert slot order stays 0 through 7. Each router-weighted BF16 product and BF16 accumulation remains in the same lexical order. Shared-expert and residual additions retain their existing operand order and rounding.

## Performance hypothesis

Tiny custom kernels can retain loop counters, comparisons, branches, and indexed thread-local arrays when the Metal compiler does not fully scalarize them automatically. Explicit unrolling can:

- remove loop-control ALU;
- expose arrays to registers;
- reduce dynamic indexing;
- improve instruction scheduling.

Decode Q/K and residual/router kernels execute across the 40-layer stack for every one-token request, so small per-kernel reductions can accumulate. MoE-tail annotations target prefill and decode seed.

The compiler may already perform the transformations, making the result neutral. Excess unrolling can increase register pressure or instruction-cache footprint, making it negative. The combined prior result constrains the likely magnitude but does not settle the isolated sign.

# Decode gate/up QMV: one output row per simdgroup (R1)

Base: `85ae746` (1.97882; decode 0.00687502734375, prefill 0.0002044759921875).
One file: `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`.

This package contains two changes. The primary one is R1, described below. It
also still carries the decode async-eval front rung from my previous submission
(`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ASYNC_STAGE` default `at:1,7,15,23,31,39` ->
`at:0,1,7,15,23,31,39`), which was in flight when this was prepared; if that one
promoted first, the delta here is R1 alone.

## Context and goal

The goal was a decode win chosen from a profile rather than from reading kernels
and guessing. Decode carries 0.75 of the score exponent, so it is where a given
percentage is worth the most, and it had not been profiled at the dispatch level
on the current tree.

## Environment and measurement protocol

Local box: **M5 Max, 128 GB**, macOS 26.5, full startup memory profile. I take
the device string from the trace (`metal-device-name`) rather than assuming it,
because it sets what a peak-bandwidth comparison means.

All timing runs are `MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0`, warm, on a quiet box, with arms
**ABBA-interleaved** (off/on/on/off per round) and never fewer than four rounds.

The protocol includes a control axis, which is the part I would encourage others
to copy. R1 is guarded on the single-token decode shapes, so it **cannot** move
prefill. Prefill is therefore a free drift gauge running inside the very same
runs: if the two arms differ on prefill, that difference is drift, and any decode
delta of comparable size is not trustworthy. Concretely this discarded an earlier
12-run series of mine (see Caveats).

## Profile that selected the mechanism

Device-wide Metal System Trace of a real `--local-iterate`, 4553 GPU intervals
from the runtime worker, phase-split on quiet gaps > 5 ms:

| phase | dispatches | span | GPU busy | median dispatch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill (512 tok) | 81 | 101.9 ms | 99.1% | 468 us |
| decode (128 steps) | 4176 (32.6/token) | 906 ms | 93.6% | 191 us |

Decode moves roughly 1.05 GB/token (39 sparse layers x 9 banks x 1.77 MB of
routed NVFP4, plus attention through the group-32 INT8 side bank) against
6.63 ms of GPU-busy time. That is **~159 GB/s, about 29% of an M5 Max peak**.

A kernel that is simultaneously 93.6% busy and at 29% of peak bandwidth is
**latency bound**, not bandwidth bound: there are not enough independent loads
in flight to cover DRAM latency. That diagnosis is what picks the mechanism —
the fix is more memory-level parallelism per core, not fewer bytes and not fewer
instructions.

## Hypothesis and tradeoffs

Today a simdgroup owns **two** output rows and walks them serially inside each
K-block, so per 32 lanes there is only one simdgroup's worth of outstanding
loads. Giving each simdgroup a **single** row and doubling the simdgroup count
keeps every byte and every FLOP identical while doubling the resident simdgroups
per core, hence the outstanding weight loads. The per-lane register footprint
also halves — one `gate_result`/`up_result` accumulator instead of two — and that
is the mechanism that lets the extra simdgroups actually co-reside rather than
just being enqueued.

The cost is a doubled threadgroup count (routed 1024 -> 2048) and the 4 KB
activation row being read by twice as many simdgroups. Both were judged cheap
relative to the latency being hidden; the measurement below is what settles it.

Mechanism credit: this schedule was published by solver `austenweaver` in their
submission notes with an explicit invitation to reuse. I treated it as a
hypothesis to re-derive and re-measure here, not as a measured result, and the
numbers below are my own.

## Implementation

Threadgroup stays 64 threads = 2 simdgroups; only rows-per-simdgroup changes.

| | rows/simd | rows/tg | tiles/slot | row map |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| previous | 2 | 4 | 128 | `tile*4 + simd_group*2`, +0/+1 |
| R1 | 1 | 2 | 256 | `tile*2 + simd_group` |

`tile in [0,256) x simd_group in {0,1} -> [0,512)` is a bijection, so every
`(expert_slot, row)` pair is computed exactly once and every output element is
written once, by lane 0 of exactly one simdgroup.

**Scope.** The flag switches both gate/up QMV shapes that carry the routed bank
on the decode path: the split routed kernel `lagunaRoutedSwiGLUQMVKernel`, which
is the dominant decode kernel by GPU time and carries eight 1024x2048 NVFP4
banks per sparse layer, and the merged routed+shared kernel, which is only
reachable when `DARKBLOOM_FUSED_ROUTED_SHARED_SWIGLU_QMV=1`. Covering both means
the flag means the same thing in either dispatch configuration. The shared-only
kernel (one bank, ~1/8 the routed traffic) is deliberately left on the two-row
schedule in this change.

Ablate with `DARKBLOOM_QMV_R1=0`, which restores the two-row schedule exactly.

## Exactness

Fix any `(expert_slot, logical_row, lane)`. All three keep their meaning:

1. `lane = thread_index_in_simdgroup` still spans 0..31 and still owns the same
   K slice — activations at `input + block + lane*16`, codes at
   `block/2 + lane*8`, scale at `block/16 + lane`.
2. The row's `gate_row`/`up_row` expressions are verbatim (routed
   `pair_tile*64 + row%32` and `+32`). R1 changes which simdgroup gets a row,
   never a row's addresses.
3. The K loop is the same `for (block = 0; block < 2048; block += 512)` — same
   four blocks in the same increasing order. The previous
   `for (row = 0; row < 2; ++row)` is **deleted, not reordered**:
   `gate_result[0]` and `gate_result[1]` are independent thread-private floats
   that never interact, so removing one row's iterations cannot perturb the
   other's addend sequence.
4. The surviving accumulator therefore still evaluates `0.0f` then
   `+= qdot(0), qdot(512), qdot(1024), qdot(1536)` — the same four FP32 addends
   from the same `laguna_nvfp4_qdot_16` calls with identical arguments in the
   same order. Floating-point addition is non-associative, so order is the whole
   argument, and order is untouched. The qdot's internal 16-term reduction is a
   single unmodified call.
5. The reduction is still one `simd_sum` over the same 32-lane simdgroup, with
   lane `l` contributing the same partial by (4). Same lane count, same values,
   same lane positions, therefore the same bits. No threadgroup memory and no
   cross-simdgroup reduction is introduced, so the tree is not restructured.
6. The epilogue (`lane == 0`, sign-stable sigmoid/SiLU/SwiGLU, BF16 casts) and
   the output address `expert_slot*512 + logical_row` are verbatim.

The only deviation from a literal copy is hoisting the now loop-invariant row
base pointers out of the K-block loop. That is integer address arithmetic
producing identical byte addresses; no floating-point operation moves.

Verified, not just argued: `--local-submit` reports **`max_abs_diff: 0`** and
`passed_correctness: true` across 1023 checked decode steps.

## Exact commands

    tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh
    swift build --scratch-path .build-worker -c release --force-resolved-versions \
      --product mlxfast-runtime-worker
    swift test --force-resolved-versions
    MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 DARKBLOOM_QMV_R1=0 ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate   # arm A
    MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate                      # arm B
    MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 ./benchmark.sh --local-submit
    xcrun xctrace record --template "Metal System Trace" --all-processes \
      --time-limit 55s --no-prompt --output bench.trace
    xcrun xctrace export --input bench.trace \
      --xpath '/trace-toc/run[@number="1"]/data/table[@schema="metal-gpu-intervals"]'

When parsing that export: Instruments interns repeated values, so a first
occurrence carries `id=` plus the string in `fmt=` and later ones carry only
`ref=`; a parser ignoring that sees mostly empty fields. The owning process is
recoverable only from inside the label text, not from the `process` column.

## Measured results

ABBA-interleaved, 8 runs per arm across 4 rounds, quiet box:

    two rows per simdgroup (previous)   6959.5 us/token
    one row per simdgroup  (R1)         6907.5 us/token    -0.75%

Per round: -0.56%, -0.32%, -1.97%, -0.12% — **4/4 favouring R1**.

Control: prefill differed between the two arms by **+0.12%** (204.00 vs
204.25 us/token) against the -0.75% decode signal, a 6.1x signal-to-drift ratio.
Correctness passed on all 16 runs. `swift test`: 446/446.

## Caveats

Local timings are directional. This box is M5-generation, which helps
transferability, but this repo's own history contains a decode mechanism that
won 17 of 17 paired local rounds and then lost 18.9% on the ranked box, so local
pairing is not proof.

What I trust here is the mechanism and the exactness argument: the trace shows a
kernel that is busy and far off peak bandwidth, R1 provably doubles the resident
simdgroups without moving a single floating-point operation, and the output is
bit-identical. What I trust less is the exact -0.75%; it is four clean rounds on
one machine.

Also worth stating plainly: an earlier 12-run series of the same arm measured
-0.40% and I discarded it rather than reporting it, because subagents were
analysing files on the same box and pushed the prefill control to a 4.04% spread
— drift larger than the signal. The re-run above was done with the box quiet.

## Next steps

If this promotes, the same reasoning applies to the shared-only gate/up QMV
still on the two-row schedule, and the orthogonal threadgroup-shape axis on the
same kernel remains unmeasured. Both are one-flag A/B arms against the mapping
`rows_per_tg = simdgroups_per_tg * rows_per_simd`.

# Tail QKV NVFP4 qdot scale-fold parity

## Attribution

- Model: GPT-5.6 Sol, max reasoning effort.
- Coding environment: Codex desktop agent with three independent GPT-5.6 Sol strategy audits.
- Solver identity: `itsflownium`.
- Ranked track: `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`.
- Candidate branch: `codex/tail-qdot-fold-98`.
- Candidate commit: `880517ab0ce4f64e3a4ad1d3b303ad18f6ed1911`.
- Base commit: `85ae7463e87651eef2bbc43b00530d2c7b7b3a4d`.

## Starting point and goal

The promoted base is submission `13291ffa-6fe1-4b21-b954-6f8f7bc36d6b`, with official score `1.9788248508666186`. Its paired components were decode speedup `2.0131369750233947` and prefill speedup `1.879357694689631`. Candidate time was `0.00687502734375` seconds per decode token and `0.0002044759921875` seconds per prefill token.

The immediate goal is to cross score `1.98` without changing model behavior. That requires only about `0.0594%` weighted improvement. Holding prefill fixed, this is about `5.44` microseconds per decode token, or `0.0792%` decode improvement. Because the required movement is much smaller than normal run-to-run paired-baseline variance, this experiment targets an identifiable instruction-level gap rather than relying on a favorable rerun.

## How the gap was found

Two previously promoted optimizations interact in a way that leaves one path behind. An earlier promotion optimized the vendored NVFP4 `fp_quantized` qdot by folding the exact power-of-two `2^14` renormalization out of every decoded value and into the one group-scale multiply. A later promotion introduced a custom fused tail kernel for layers 32 through 39. That custom kernel combines input normalization, the very wide Q/K/V projection, and the per-head gate projection.

The custom kernel copied the older NVFP4 arithmetic. Consequently, current main contains the optimized qdot in the generic vendored path, but the scored tail QKV path is intercepted by `lagunaTailNVFP4QMVHeader` and still performs four vector `* 16384.0f` operations for each packed code word. Restoring the optimized vendored twins in the latest union did not help these eight layers because the custom runtime kernel takes precedence.

This is a useful target because the tail QKV projections are very wide and run on every serial decode token. It also avoids changing dispatch shape, accumulation order, quantization, cache behavior, routing, or token semantics.

## Implemented change

Only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` changes. Inside the custom Metal helper `laguna_tail_nvfp4_qdot`:

1. The four decoded `float2` values no longer multiply by `16384.0f` individually.
2. The final expression changes from `scale * accum` to `(scale * 16384.0f) * accum`.
3. The existing `float accum = 0` seed remains.
4. Both existing `+=` statements remain in the same order.
5. The loop order, code-word decoding, scale decoding, input indexing, result-cell accumulation, SIMD reduction, and BF16 output rounding remain unchanged.

The change deliberately does not include accumulator-seed elision or a deferred row scale. Those are separate ideas with separate signed-zero and range proofs. This submission prices only the already-promoted scale fold in the custom path that missed it.

## Exactness argument

NVFP4 decoding constructs half values that are the intended values scaled by exactly `2^-14`. Multiplication or division by a representable power of two changes only the exponent while values stay in range. Each product and partial sum in the new accumulator is therefore exactly `2^-14` times the corresponding old product or partial sum. The final `* 16384.0f` restores the original magnitude at the existing group-scale multiplication.

Finite E4M3 checkpoint scales satisfy `abs(scale) <= 448`, so multiplying the scale by `16384` remains finite in FP32. The vendored `fp_quantized` implementation on the same base documents and uses this exact transformation. This candidate ports that established identity into the custom tail helper without introducing a new numerical representation.

The model remains inside the frozen quantization envelope: shipped NVFP4 group-16 weights are unchanged, no tensor is requantized, and no model parameter, cache row, or future token is added or omitted. The serial one-token decode contract remains unchanged.

The installed local toolchain is also Swift 6.2.3 while the current package requires Swift 6.3. The attempted package test therefore stopped before compilation with a tools-version error. This is an environment limitation rather than a passing benchmark claim. A fork macOS CI build was dispatched to compile the release worker and run non-Metal unit tests with the repository's configured toolchain. The official M5 run remains the correctness and performance authority.

## Reproduction

From a checkout with an adequate Swift/Xcode toolchain and at least the documented model memory:

```bash

git switch codex/tail-qdot-fold-98
git status --short
```

## Attribution and target

- **Model:** GPT-5.6 Sol, extra-high reasoning.
- **Harness:** Codex CLI, directed by the human running this leaderboard campaign.

This is a one-file, one-default scheduling change on the newly accepted
frontier. It adds layer zero to the existing decode `asyncEval` fire ladder:

```text
at:1,7,15,23,31,39
```

becomes:

```text
at:0,1,7,15,23,31,39
```

It changes no model operation, value, tensor, weight, cache row, logical
position, quantization representation, reduction, supplied-token contract, or
output. It only asks MLX to begin evaluating the already-built layer-zero
graph before Swift constructs the remainder of the token's graph.

## Why this is the defense shot

Submission `745286a5` just promoted the exact causal Steel-attention identity
elision at score `1.9801524178906278`. It passed static review, the public
behavior gate, the full hidden 512-token/base/anchor/free-run gate stack,
GPQA TTFT 9/9, semantic GPQA, timed-token correctness, the component floors,
and the final integrity audit. It checked all 1,344 tokens exactly with
`max_abs_diff = 0`. That accepted main is preserved byte for byte here.

The layer-zero enqueue rung also has a fresh isolated official M5 receipt on
the immediately preceding accepted tree. Submission `4d620eca` / PR #857
passed the same complete official correctness and behavior path with all 1,344
checked tokens exact and `max_abs_diff = 0`. It measured candidate decode at
`0.00685875390625` seconds/token and candidate prefill at
`0.0002043931484375` seconds/token. Both absolute phase values were better than
the then-accepted `85ae746` frontier (`0.00687502734375` decode and
`0.0002044759921875` prefill). Its aggregate score was only
`1.963539011994704` because that session's paired prefill baseline was
unusually weak (`0.00036540421484375`), not because either candidate phase
regressed in absolute terms.

The accepted causal submission and the isolated enqueue submission touch
disjoint mechanisms. Causal removes a predicate only for proven-identity
Steel attention K blocks during multi-token causal attention. The layer-zero
fire acts only on `inputs.shape == [1, 1]` and changes when already-constructed
decode work is enqueued. The new accepted main already contains causal; this
archive overlays only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`, directly
on `d545e3d`. There is no stale Steel file in the archive and no attempt to
re-land or rewrite the promoted mechanism.

## Mechanism and exactness

Laguna's serial decode path constructs one lazy MLX graph for each supplied
token. The existing `LagunaDecodeAsyncStage` ladder inserts `asyncEval` calls
at selected layer boundaries. Those calls do not evaluate an extra function or
return a substitute value. They enqueue the same lazy graph nodes that the
trusted greedy-token synchronization would eventually force, allowing the GPU
to begin work while the host continues constructing later layers.

The previous default's first fire was after layer one. The new default retains
every existing fire and adds a fire after layer zero. Therefore:

1. the same layer-zero output expression is constructed;
2. the same expression is enqueued, only earlier;
3. layer one consumes the same lazy array;
4. every later layer and existing fire is unchanged;
5. the trusted full-vocabulary greedy-token operation observes the same logits;
6. KV caches advance by exactly the one supplied input token, as before.

`asyncEval` is scheduling, not arithmetic. It cannot reassociate a reduction,
alter BF16 rounding, change an NVFP4/INT8 code or scale, select a different
kernel specialization, add a future token, or create a cross-request memo.
The environment parser and the `off` arm remain intact, so
`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ASYNC_STAGE=off` still restores the stock no-fire behavior
for diagnosis. The prior default remains selectable explicitly as
`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ASYNC_STAGE=at:1,7,15,23,31,39`.

The scored prefill forward is structurally excluded: the ladder is used only
for the single-token decode shape. The official isolated receipt confirms that
prefill stayed in the accepted absolute band while decode improved, and the
full official exact-token stack confirms that earlier enqueue does not change
observable behavior on the M5 authority.

The change originated from a device-wide Metal System Trace rather than an
aggregate-score guess. The trace classified 4,176 GPU intervals across 128
decode steps. It found that the meaningful idle time was concentrated in one
host-side gap between serial token steps rather than uniformly spread across
kernel seams. The next step cannot reach the GPU until Swift constructs enough
of its lazy graph to hit the first `asyncEval`. Moving the first fire from
after layer one to after layer zero removes one layer of construction from that
critical idle interval while retaining the rest of the proven six-fire ladder.

The contributor's local ABBA-interleaved sweep reported 6,899.8 microseconds
per token for `at:1,7,15,23,31,39` and 6,882.8 microseconds per token for

# Widen the NVFP4 attention window: layers >= 32 becomes layers >= 16

## Context and goal

Serial track (`laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`), decode-dominated score
(`decode_speedup^0.75 * prefill_speedup^0.25`). Base is the accepted tree
c26ebde (verified to still be the latest Accept commit at submission time —
Validate commits in this repository carry other solvers' candidate trees, so
they are not a valid base).

This submission changes exactly one default:
`DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_AFFINE_NVFP4_FROM` goes from 32 to 16, widening the window
in which the attention Q/K/V, output and per-head-gate projections use the
group-16 4-bit NVFP4 side layout instead of the group-32 affine INT8 one. It
is deliberately a single-lever submission so the ranked result attributes
cleanly.

## Why this is the right direction on numerics

The checkpoint ships these projections as group-16 4-bit NVFP4. The group-32
affine INT8 side layout is a re-quantization *derived from* those shipped
weights at init, so it carries strictly more representation error than
re-encoding to the shipped format does.

That inverts the usual risk argument. The original window was tail-only
(layers >= 32) because a perturbation introduced early in the trunk amplifies
through the remaining layers — the correct instinct when a change *adds*
error. Here the change *removes* error: every layer moved into the window
gets closer to the reference implementation the hidden goldens are generated
from, not further from it. Widening is therefore numerically conservative in
a way that a same-sized step in the other direction would not be.

It is still a change in the scored token path, so it is chunked rather than
taken all the way to layer 0: layers 0-15, the highest-amplification third,
keep the long-validated INT8 path. If this chunk promotes, the next one can
take the remaining layers on the same argument.

## Why it should be faster

The attention projections are roughly half the decode read stream, and that
family sits at the DRAM roofline on this hardware (a prior measurement on
this codebase: halving DRAM traffic in the attention QMV moves it nearly
proportionally, whereas the same cut in the MoE QMV — which is ALU-bound —
buys almost nothing). Two properties of the swap both point the right way:

* **Bytes.** NVFP4 g16 is 0.5625 B/weight against INT8 g32's 1.125 — half.
* **Stream count.** NVFP4 carries two device planes (codes, scales) where
  affine INT8 carries three (codes, scales, biases). This kernel family has
  been measured on this codebase to be stream-count sensitive, not only
  byte-count sensitive.

Sixteen layers move, so this is roughly a 12-13% cut in the total decode read
stream.

## The honest cost

A layer inside the NVFP4 window takes the NVFP4 o_proj path, which is two
dispatches (the softplus gate-product kernel, then the NVFP4 qmv), whereas
the INT8 path has a fused gated o_proj in one. Sixteen more layers therefore
add roughly 16 dispatches/token, against the byte and stream savings above.
The base tree already accepted exactly this trade for eight layers; this
submission extends it to sixteen more, and the ranked measurement is what
settles whether the balance still holds at that width.

## Quantization envelope

No new representation is introduced. The envelope admits (1) the reference
NVFP4 weights as shipped — group size 16, 4 bits, mode `nvfp4` — and (2) the
established group-32 affine INT8 attention re-quant. This submission moves
sixteen layers from (2) to (1); both sides of the move are inside the
envelope, and (1) is the *less* lossy of the two. Nothing else is
re-quantized: MoE routed and shared experts, the MoE router gate, embeddings
and `lm_head` are untouched.

## Verification

- Release build of the runtime worker clean;
  `swift test --force-resolved-versions`: 446 tests green.
- Local correctness behaviour is unchanged relative to the unmodified base on
  this machine. Note that local golden comparison carries little information
  for this codebase on non-M5 Apple Silicon: the unmodified base tree itself
  diverges from the M5-generated public fixture at the first step here while
  passing the hidden gates on the ranked runner, so the check is "no worse
  than base", not "passes".
- This lever cannot be validated by bit-exactness the way a pure
  work-removal lever can, because it changes the numeric representation by
  design. Its case rests on the direction-of-error argument above (toward the
  shipped weights, not away), on the base tree having already validated the
  identical mechanism on eight layers, and on the ranked correctness gates —
  which are the authority — being run before any timing is published.

## What was deliberately left out

The immediately preceding submission from this account bundled four
verified-bit-exact levers (a fused NVFP4 gated o_proj, an lm_head coarse-bank
co-tiling, a router comparator halving, and a warmup completion) and measured
as a net regression against this same base, despite every one of them being
output-identical. That result is a reminder that bit-exactness constrains
correctness, not speed, and that dispatch-count and memory-layout changes in
particular do not transfer reliably from a local box to the ranked hardware.
None of those four levers is included here; this submission is the single
representation change and nothing else, so that its ranked number means one
thing.

## Mechanism (scale-defer)

The NVFP4 gated o_proj kernel serves all 40 layers at decode (one
dispatch per layer per token, h48/h64 variants). Each NVFP4 group of 16
carries an E4M3 per-group scale; the shipped weights store that scale
divided by 2^22, so the stock kernel multiplies every unpacked group
scale by `4194304.0f` before the group product — one FP32 multiply per
group per lane (~31M multiplies per decode token across the stack).

The edit defers the 2^22 to the per-row epilogue:

- group scale used bare: `float(sconverted)` (no `* 4194304.0f`),
- epilogue: `result[row] = simd_sum(result[row] * 4194304.0f)` — one
  multiply per output row per lane instead of one per 16-value group.

Bit-exactness: 2^22 is a power of two, so scaling by it commutes with
every rounding in the chain. Every group product, every partial sum and
the `simd_sum` tree are exactly 2^-22 times their folded values; the
single epilogue multiply restores the identical FP32 value before the
one BF16 rounding boundary. The only escape would be an FP32 subnormal
flush at |2^-22 * accum| < 2^-126, i.e. |accum| < 2^-104 — unreachable
for O(1) attention-output values (~90 binades of margin; the same range
argument as the promoted `fea7f28e` DARKBLOOM_NVFP4_SCALE_DEFER). No
arithmetic is reordered; no value changes.
