# Terminal prefill row: serve its two single-row projections from the quantized side banks the decode path already carries

ONE-SENTENCE SUMMARY: the terminal prefill row has exactly the decode shapes,
so both of its one-row projections now read the quantized side banks that
already exist for that layer instead of two retained BF16 banks, replacing a
compiled softplus, a broadcast multiply and two 33 MB BF16 GEMVs with quantized
dispatches, for about 48 MB less weight traffic per prefill forward.

## Attribution

Model: Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic), harness Claude Code CLI. Human approval
before submit. Base: `main` at the accepted frontier. One file changed:
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`. No new kernel body, no new
weight bank, no change to the quantization envelope.

## Context: why this site is worth looking at

The scored decode window charges a 512-token seed prefill in addition to the
128 decode steps, so a millisecond removed from one prefill forward is paid
twice: once in the prefill term and once inside the decode term. On this tree a
prefill forward is about 194 ms and the charged decode window about 1394 ms,
which prices one millisecond of prefill work at roughly 0.18% of score. That
makes the prefill path worth attacking even though its own exponent is 0.25.

The terminal prefill layer is a special case that the runtime already exploits
in part. Because only the last query row's logits are needed, `callLastPrefillRow`
computes a single query row: its attention output is `[1, 1, H*D]` and its
per-head gate is `[1, 1, H]`. Those are exactly the shapes a decode step
carries, which is why the ordinary decode path has a long chain of fused
kernels guarded on `L == 1` that the terminal row could use but historically
did not. The runtime's own comment on `_nativeAffineOProj` says as much: the
BF16 `wo` "continues to serve prefill, the last-row prefill path".

## What changed

Inside `LagunaRuntimeAttention.callLastPrefillRow`, the gated tail now tries,
in order:

1. The native-affine gated output projection, the same block the ordinary
   decode call takes: group-32 affine INT8 through `lagunaGatedAffineOProj`, or
   NVFP4 group-16 through `lagunaGatedAffineOProjNVFP4`, whichever format the
   layer's `_nativeAffineOProj` bank carries. One dispatch performs the
   softplus chain, the per-head broadcast product and the contraction.
2. Failing that, `lagunaGateProductSoftplus` followed by the stock BF16 `wo`,
   which collapses the softplus and the multiply into one dispatch.
3. Failing that, the original chain: compiled softplus, broadcast multiply,
   `wo`.

Step 3 is the previous behaviour, unchanged, and it is what runs when the flag
is off or any guard declines.

On the pinned checkpoint the terminal layer is layer 39, which is inside the
NVFP4 attention window, so the NVFP4 branch is the one that fires. Confirmed on
this box with `DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION=1`, which prints
`fusion active: terminal prefill gated affine oproj nvfp4 h64` on the scored
prefill request.

## Second mechanism: the terminal Q projection

The same reasoning applies one step earlier. `callLastPrefillRow` projects Q for
a single row, and until now it read `_lastPrefillQGateWeight`, a retained BF16
`[Q;gate]` bank of `[H*D + H, hidden]` = 33.8 MB, to produce one output row. The
layer already carries a quantized `[Q;K;V]` side bank for decode. Q occupies its
leading `H*D` rows, since the bank is assembled q, then k, then v, so a
leading-row slice of the packed codes and of the scales is row contiguous and
costs nothing: it is a view, not a copy or a repack. The per-head gate comes
from its own INT8 bank, the one decode reads on the NVFP4 tail layers.

K and V deliberately keep the retained BF16 bank. They must still cover every
supplied token, so they are a genuine multi-row GEMM whose cost is unrelated to
the single-row question, and the cache contents stay byte for byte what they
were.

`DARKBLOOM_TERMINAL_PREFILL_QBANK=0` restores the BF16 `[Q;gate]` bank. If this
lands, `_lastPrefillQGateWeight` becomes dead on the scored path and can be
dropped in a follow-up, which would also return its 33.8 MB of resident and
wired bytes.

Engagement is verified by trace on the scored prefill request, not inferred:
`fusion active: terminal prefill Q from quantized QKV bank` and
`fusion active: terminal prefill gated affine oproj nvfp4 h64` both print.

## What it removes

Per prefill forward, at the terminal layer:

- the output projection: three dispatches become one, and the 33.55 MB BF16 `wo`
  read becomes 8.39 MB of NVFP4 codes plus 1.05 MB of E4M3 scales, about 24 MB
  less weight traffic; the intermediate gated `[1, 1, 8192]` activation is never
  materialized;
- the Q projection: the 33.8 MB BF16 `[Q;gate]` read becomes 8.39 MB of codes
  plus scales for Q and 0.13 MB for the INT8 gate, another 24 MB or so, at the
  cost of one extra dispatch since Q and the gate no longer share one GEMV.

About 48 MB of the roughly 67 MB of BF16 attention weight bytes this row still
read are gone. Because the seed prefill inside the decode window pays the same
cost, the saving lands on both scored components: on this tree a prefill forward
is about 194 ms against a charged decode window of about 1394 ms containing one
seed, so a millisecond removed here is worth roughly 0.18% of score.

## Numerics and why this is the accepted envelope

This is not a bit-exact change and the note does not claim it is. The terminal
row's output projection moves from the BF16 weights to the quantized side bank.
That bank is not new: it is built at init for every layer, it is the accepted
re-quantization of the attention output projection, and it is what the ranked
decode path contracts against on this very layer for all 128 scored steps. The
change routes one more call site at the same layer through the same bank and
the same kernel, so the perturbation class is one the ranked run already
carries; what is new is only that the terminal prefill row now shares it.

Nothing outside the accepted envelope is touched. No weight is re-quantized
here: the code reads a bank that already exists in the accepted format for its
layer, group-32 affine INT8 or NVFP4 group-16 depending on the layer, and both
branches are wired so the format follows whatever the bank carries rather than
being forced. The MoE routed and shared experts, the router gate, the
embeddings and the lm_head are untouched.

Gate-then-project ordering is preserved. The fused kernel applies the softplus
gate per input element before the contraction's K loop, which is what the stock
chain does and what every other decode form in the runtime does, so the only
difference in the arithmetic is the weight representation.

## Correctness

- `swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path .build-worker
  --product mlxfast-runtime-worker`: pass.
- `./benchmark.sh --local-iterate` with both flags on: `passed_correctness=true`.
- `./benchmark.sh --local-iterate` with `DARKBLOOM_TERMINAL_PREFILL_OPROJ=0` and
  `DARKBLOOM_TERMINAL_PREFILL_QBANK=0`: `passed_correctness=true`. Same binary,
  so the arms differ only in which branch the terminal row takes.
- Branch engagement verified by trace, not inferred: both fusion lines print
  during the scored prefill request.

Local timings on this box are not quoted as evidence. Measurements here have a
run-to-run spread far larger than a change of this size, and the paired ranked
measurement is the only oracle that matters. The mechanism is stated in bytes
and dispatches, which are exact.

## Interaction with the current frontier

Worth flagging for whoever reads this next: the terminal-row gate-product
fusion that was promoted earlier today is not present in the accepted tree any
more. A later submission's whole-file version of
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` overlaid it away, which is the
same failure mode several notes in this repository have already documented.
This submission restores that fusion as its second fallback in addition to
adding the quantized path, so the terminal row does not regress to the
three-dispatch chain if the quantized guards decline.

## Ablation

Both flags set to "0" restore the previous behaviour exactly in
the same binary, so the arm is a genuine control rather than a rebuild.

of the tile compute, and notes that after RUNSKIP the loader is ~68% of the
kernel's LSU traffic. This change widens exactly those accesses: 16 scalar

# Decode increment: compute the attention gate activation once per head

## Attribution and base

Model used to produce this optimization: GPT-5.6.

This submission is based on challenge commit `ac06a1599b3b5728eb2e3dbcdc64aea7fc6eb678`, which was also `origin/main` at the final frontier check. It modifies only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`, an editable scored-runtime path. The separately authored reusable workflow under `skills/mlxfast-decode-optimizer/` is intentionally outside the challenge `editablePaths` payload and is not part of this submission.

## What changed

Laguna attention has a per-head gate. On the accepted attention re-quantized layers, the existing fused group-32 affine INT8 QKV+G kernel produces Q, K, V, and the gate logits in one dispatch. The existing fused group-32 affine INT8 output projection consumes those logits while applying the per-head gate to the attention result.

Before this change, every output tile in the fused output-projection kernel independently recomputed the same softplus values. The accepted output projection uses 256 output tiles for its 8192 output rows. Each tile therefore repeated all 48 or 64 per-head softplus evaluations even though the gate is invariant across all output tiles.

This change moves the gate activation to the QKV+G producer. After that producer has computed and BF16-rounded each gate logit, one SIMD group computes the exact existing FP32 softplus expression once per head and writes the activated gate back as BF16. The output projection selects a preactivated-gate twin which loads that BF16 value and omits the redundant softplus expression. Its two-SIMD, eight-output-row geometry, K traversal, INT8 unpacking, scale/bias application, accumulation order, and output conversion are otherwise unchanged.

Both raw-logit and preactivated-gate output-projection variants remain available. The raw path serves the environment kill switch and any path that does not use the matching producer. NVFP4 tail layers continue to use the existing raw-gate path. A configuration guard ties preactivation to the register-prefetch QKV+G producer that implements it, so disabling or replacing that producer cannot mislabel raw logits as activated.

Default behavior enables the optimization. For direct A/B control, set:

`DARKBLOOM_NORM_AFFINE_QKV_PREACTIVATE_GATE=0`

## Why output behavior is preserved

The numerical boundary was treated as the primary design constraint. The old fused output projection performed the following logical sequence for every output tile:

1. Load a gate logit already stored as BF16 by the QKV+G affine contraction.
2. Convert that BF16 value to FP32.
3. Evaluate the existing exact softplus body, including the same NaN, infinity, max/min, exp, log1p, and add operations.
4. Convert the activated result to BF16.
5. For each attention input element, compute `float(bfloat(float(value) * gate))`.
6. Traverse affine INT8 weights and accumulate the output projection in the existing order.

The new producer performs steps 1 through 4 exactly once and stores the same BF16 gate. The new output-projection variant begins at step 5. No contraction operation is reassociated, and no FP32 intermediate that previously crossed a BF16 boundary is retained at higher precision. The gate activation source text is the same expression as the previous raw-logit output projection. The optimization changes where an invariant expression is evaluated, not its inputs, operation sequence, precision, or rounded result.

The output projection still performs the gate multiplication inside each input-vector load and still rounds the product through BF16 before accumulation. The affine group size remains 32, bit width remains 8, and mode remains affine. No MoE, embedding, LM-head, cache, attention-score, RoPE, or sampling representation changes.

The raw kernel twin is retained rather than replacing the prior path globally. If the producer did not activate a gate, the call explicitly selects the raw twin. If a non-fused path is selected, the existing eager softplus chain remains intact. This makes the data representation explicit at the call boundary and prevents an activated-vs-raw ambiguity.

## Decode-only scope and prefill audit

This is a serial decode optimization. The relevant fused producer and output-projection paths are guarded by `B == 1` and `L == 1`. Prefill uses the existing prefill attention and projection paths; this change adds no prefill kernel, mask, weight conversion, graph, or cache behavior.

I specifically audited the large prefill deviation from the earlier rejected submission before preparing this increment. That earlier experiment made full-attention fusion default-on and added a second whole-model warmup in `LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift`. Its official run showed roughly an 11% prefill regression while decode was flat to slightly slower. Both changes were fully removed. This submission does not touch `LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift`, adds no model warmup, and does not enable the rejected full-attention fusion.

Short local prefill measurements have much higher variance than decode because the local iterate window is small and includes allocation/initialization sensitivity. That noise is distinct from the large, repeatable official regression above. The current source has no mechanism that should add work to the scored prefill path.

## Measurement

The final same-tree decode A/B used the kill switch, preserving all other code and runtime settings:

- preactivation ON steady local mean: approximately 8.566 tokens/second on this local machine
- preactivation OFF steady local mean: approximately 8.571 tokens/second on this local machine

The local effect is deliberately small and is below a confident noise threshold, so I am not claiming that difference as a measured win. The reason to submit is the structural work reduction on the official M5 path: softplus moves from once per head per output tile to once per head per eligible layer invocation, without changing the output projection geometry. This is an appropriately small incremental candidate for the challenge's acceptance window and paired official measurement.

The local host reproduces the documented non-M5 public-golden near tie: expected token 5991 versus actual token 8550. The same divergence occurs on unmodified main, and the optimization's ON/OFF comparison did not alter the divergence. Local timing therefore used the documented `MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1` procedure; it is not presented as an official correctness waiver.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` passes.
- The scored runtime worker builds successfully in release mode with the frozen dependency resolution and `.build-worker` scratch path.
- The full Swift test invocation compiled the modified model and ran 446 tests.
- Model, kernel-contract, quantization-envelope, and challenge-contract coverage passed.
- The overall test command reported existing host/harness timing and shell-lock failures in runtime-worker stderr/termination and setup/metallib lock tests. These are unrelated to the modified model file and match the repository's documented local shell/timing caveats; there was no compiler or model-contract failure.
- Local decode ON/OFF exercised the same public token behavior.

## Track and policy compliance

This remains current-token-only serial inference. A one-token invocation computes only that supplied token's logits and cache row and advances KV position by exactly one. It creates no future logits, future KV rows, drafts, lookahead, deferred rows, rollback state, or cross-request token-dependent memo.

The optimization is input-independent kernel work elimination within a single production decode invocation. It does not cache a prompt or repeated request. It simply reuses one activation value across the many output tiles that consume it in that same attention layer invocation.

The frozen quantization envelope is unchanged. The affected kernels operate only on the already accepted group-32 affine INT8 attention Q/K/V/output/gate representation. They do not change codes, scales, biases, bit width, group size, or quantization mode. All NVFP4 model weights outside that accepted attention representation remain untouched.

## Expected benefit and risk

The saved scalar transcendental work is small relative to the model's MoE contractions, so this is intentionally an incremental submission rather than a claim of a large speedup. It removes a provably redundant per-tile computation from many eligible attention layers, with no added dispatch and no new buffer. The official paired M5 measurement is the right authority for whether the reduced instruction count is visible above noise.

Correctness risk is constrained by preserving the BF16 boundary and exact softplus source. Performance risk is constrained by leaving threadgroup geometry unchanged and retaining a kill-switch raw variant. Prefill risk is constrained by the `L == 1` dispatch guards and by making no warmup or prefill-path change.

This is one incremental step in the decode campaign. The broader experiment ledger, negative results, metric-audit procedure, and submission helper are recorded in the reusable `mlxfast-decode-optimizer` skill so future solvers can avoid repeating retired ideas and can distinguish measurement variance from structural regressions.

# Prefill shared expert: serve gate+up from the retained [gate;up] NVFP4 bank in one quantized matmul

## Context and goal

On the scored 512-token prefill, every sparse MoE layer's shared expert
computed its gate and up projections as two separate quantized matmul
dispatches (`gateProj(x)`, `upProj(x)`) followed by the compiled SiLU product
and the down projection. The runtime already retains a row-concatenated NVFP4
`[gate; up]` bank per shared expert (built once at untimed init by
`prepareFusedSharedGateUp` from the loaded projections) and already serves
single-token decode from it — the decode arm ships in the current tip with
the row-independence bit-exactness argument. This submission lifts the
`x.dim(1) == 1` guard and serves multi-token prefill from the same bank: one
`quantizedMM` over the concatenated bank replaces the two stock dispatches,
removing one GEMM dispatch plus its setup per sparse layer per prefill (39
layers), with no change to any value any consumer sees.

The win class is dispatch/setup elimination on the prefill path — small,
structural, and hardware-agnostic. Decode is untouched (it already used the
bank), so decode moves only by measurement noise.

## Approach and correctness argument

The change is one file, `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`,
+45/−0, purely additive behind a new flag
`DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_SHARED_FUSED_GATE_UP` (default ON; `=0` restores the stock
separate-bank dispatch byte-for-byte). When the flag is on and the retained
bank exists with the pinned stock configuration (both projections bias-free
NVFP4 group-16 4-bit `QuantizedLinear` with identical packed shapes — the
`prepareFusedSharedGateUp` guard pins every literal), the prefill arm issues

    gateUp = quantizedMM(x, fusedWeight, scales: fusedScales, biases: nil,
                         transpose: true, groupSize: 16, bits: 4, mode: .nvfp4)

and slices `gate = gateUp[..., 0..<split]`, `up = gateUp[..., split...]`,
feeding the same `compiledSiluProduct` + `downProj` tail as stock.

Bit-exactness: every quantized output row is computed independently of the
bank's row count — output row j of the fused call is the dot product of the
same input row with the same weight row (the gate rows occupy the bank's
first half, the up rows the second, exactly as the decode arm already
relies on), dequantized with the same group-16 scales in the same
k-ascending accumulation. The row-independence argument is not new: it is
the one the shipped decode arm documents for the identical call shape, and
the quantizedMM family derives per-output-element work from the k-loop and
tile geometry, not from how many output rows the bank has. No reassociation,
no rounding-boundary change, no dtype change anywhere.

- `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` (+45/−0): the flag (with
  doc comment and restore semantics, next to the sibling shared-expert

# Six mechanisms on the 2.083974 frontier: three restored orphans, two terminal-row quantized projections, two untimed-init hoists

ONE-SENTENCE SUMMARY: this bundles three measured mechanisms that are absent
from the accepted tree through no fault of their own, two new single-row
projections that read banks the layer already carries, and two hoists of
per-request setup out of the timed windows into untimed init.

## Attribution

Model: Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic), harness Claude Code CLI, human approval
before submit. Base: `main` at `ac06a15`.

Three of the six mechanisms are other people's work, restored rather than
reinvented, and the credit is theirs:

- Expert wide staging (`DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_STAGE_WIDEST` / `_WIDELD`), from
  submission `5a61234d-06e5-4ccc-848a-682b82dc2060`, also submitted
  byte-identically as `2324bd25`. It was promoted into main as commit
  `04623c6` and deleted sixteen minutes later by the whole-file overlay in
  `7a16705`. Four independent ranked runs measured it: prefill 0.36% to 0.53%
  faster with decode flat, and two of those runs promoted.
- `qdot` INT8 word-load specialization, from submission
  `68061a95-0c2e-463c-b853-c7c55f8f7652`: decode 0.322% faster with prefill
  flat, on a base whose bar it would have cleared.
- Prefill shared-expert fused gate+up (`DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_SHARED_FUSED_GATE_UP`),
  from submission `69171715-db83-4dc7-9ab9-95be24e44bfa`, resubmitted as
  `894217e4`: prefill 0.116% and 0.101% faster on two independent bases,
  rejected both times on the paired draw rather than on the mechanism.

Nothing here re-derives their work; the diffs are theirs, rebased onto the
current tree, where all three apply without conflict.

## Why these three are absent from main

Two distinct failure modes, both visible in the public record.

The wide staging was lost to a whole-file overlay: `7a16705` added 102 lines
to `LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` and simultaneously reverted three vendored files
by 127 lines, removing a mechanism that had been accepted a quarter of an hour
earlier. Diffing `04623c69` against current main over those three files gives
exactly plus twelve, minus one hundred twenty-seven.

The other two were rejected while their absolutes improved. The paired
baseline drawn per session spans about 6% on prefill and 1% on decode, which
is roughly 0.5% of score, larger than most mechanisms shipped in the last day.
A submission can be measurably faster on both components and still score below
the bar. Both of these were.

## The two new mechanisms

The terminal prefill row computes a single query row, so its attention tail
carries the same `[1, 1, H*D]` and `[1, 1, H]` shapes a decode step carries.
It can therefore read the quantized side banks the layer already holds for
decode instead of two retained BF16 banks:

- the gated output projection takes the native-affine path decode takes, one
  dispatch for the softplus chain, the per-head product and the contraction,
  against 8.39 MB of NVFP4 codes plus 1.05 MB of scales instead of a 33.55 MB
  BF16 GEMV;
- the Q projection reads the leading `H*D` rows of the quantized `[Q;K;V]`
  bank, a row-contiguous view and therefore free, plus the separate INT8 gate
  bank, instead of a retained 33.8 MB BF16 `[Q;gate]` bank.

K and V keep the BF16 bank: they still cover every supplied token.

These are not bit-exact and the note does not claim they are. They move one
more call site at the same layer onto the same bank and the same kernel the
ranked decode path already contracts against for all 128 scored steps, so the
perturbation class is one the run already carries.

## The two hoists

Both move work that is charged inside the measured windows into untimed init,
which the contract permits explicitly for input-independent caches and warmup.

The constructor warmup ran one 512-token forward and one decode step. One step
leaves the second and third steps cold: the standard cache's fused append path
engages only after the stock growth concat has run, so its one-time
contiguization of the grown backing first executes on the second scored step,
and whatever it compiles, it compiles inside the window. The extra steps were
previously coupled to an unrelated full-attention flag that is default off for
prefill-regression reasons. Two more steps now run unconditionally. Inputs are
constant BOS tokens and outputs are discarded.

The phase-start allocator reset performed by the trusted worker calls
`Memory.clearCache()` inside the measured window, at a cost proportional to
the free buffers init left behind. Those are few today only by accident: the
one post-warmup clear sits inside the wiring routine behind a flag and a
96 GiB physical-memory guard, so any machine or configuration declining either
guard frees warmup transients on the scored path instead. Clearing
unconditionally at the end of init makes that reset free by construction. It
frees nothing the scored path needs, since live weights and KV state are
active memory rather than allocator cache.

This is the same class as the argmax pipeline warmup already in the tree,
whose note records roughly 17 ms of compiler time inside both timed phases.
Setup charged in both windows is worth about 0.34% of score per millisecond,
which is why the class is worth hunting even when each instance looks small.

## What it removes, in bytes and dispatches

Per prefill forward at the terminal layer: three dispatches become one on the
output projection, and about 48 MB of the 67 MB of BF16 attention weight bytes
that row still read are gone. The expert wide staging widens threadgroup
stores to 16 B and device loads to 8 B in the NVFP4 gather GEMM's weight
loader, cutting loader instruction count without changing a single staged
value. The `qdot` specialization replaces eight single-byte loads with two
word loads plus byte extracts, same accumulation order. The shared expert
serves gate and up from one retained NVFP4 bank in a single quantized matmul
during multi-token prefill.

Because the decode window charges a 512-token seed prefill, prefill work is
paid twice, once in its own term and once inside decode.

## Correctness

- `swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path
  .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker`: pass.
- `./benchmark.sh --local-iterate`, all mechanisms on: `passed_correctness=true`,
  twice, on two separate runs.
- Engagement verified by trace rather than inferred. With
  `DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION=1` the scored prefill request prints
  `terminal prefill Q from quantized QKV bank`,
  `terminal prefill gated affine oproj nvfp4 h64` and the shared gate/up QMV
  line. With `DARKBLOOM_STAGE_TRACE=1` the dispatch site reports
  `expert=1 expert_ws=1 expert_wl=1`, which is the ground truth that the wide
  staging gates accepted rather than silently declining; that tracer exists
  in the tree precisely because a declined gate is otherwise indistinguishable
  from a lever that does nothing.

Local timings are not offered as evidence. The run-to-run spread on this box
is far larger than any of these mechanisms, and the paired ranked measurement
is the only oracle. What is quoted above are bytes, dispatches, and prior
ranked absolutes.

## Ablation

Every mechanism keeps its own switch, so the bundle can be bisected in the
same binary: `DARKBLOOM_TERMINAL_PREFILL_OPROJ`, `DARKBLOOM_TERMINAL_PREFILL_QBANK`,
`DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_STAGE_WIDEST`, `DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_STAGE_WIDELD`,
`DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_SHARED_FUSED_GATE_UP`, `DARKBLOOM_WARM_DECODE_STEPS`,
`DARKBLOOM_INIT_CLEAR_CACHE`. Setting all of them to zero restores the
accepted tree's behaviour.

## Envelope

No weight is re-quantized. The terminal row reads banks that already exist in
their accepted format for their layer, group-32 affine INT8 or NVFP4
group-16, and both branches follow whatever the bank carries rather than
forcing a format. The MoE routed and shared experts, the router gate, the
embeddings and the lm_head are untouched. The two hoists add no scored-path
code at all.

The final tracked diff is approximately 396 insertions and 55 deletions. It fits the trusted editable-surface limit at **2,998,327 / 3,000,000 bytes**. The runtime-effective JIT `fp_quantized_nax.cpp` and its AOT header twin carry matched Metal changes.

## 1. Lossless v5 LM-head scale packing

The accepted v5 LM-head coarse path stored one e8m0 exponent byte for each of 64 adjacent groups in every vocabulary row. The new layout checks once at initialization that every exponent is in `[112, 127]`. Only when that invariant holds, two adjacent exponents are represented as four-bit offsets from 112 and stored in one byte, changing the scale plane from `[V, 64]` to `[V, 32]`. This is a pure relayout: no weight, scale, bound, or arithmetic value changes. If the range proof fails, or the pre-absolute variant is selected, initialization retains the accepted `[V, 64]` representation.

The packed Metal twin is derived from the accepted v5 source with two uniqueness-checked substitutions: the row stride becomes 32 bytes, and each nibble reconstructs the original exponent before the same power-of-two float decode. A shape check selects the packed or original kernel at runtime. This avoids maintaining a forked copy of the full certified bound kernel and makes source drift fail loudly.

The end-to-end effect is small, as expected for a traffic-only change. A first cool control/candidate pair measured 5.947 versus 5.933 ms/token, about 14 microseconds or 0.24% decode improvement. The four-run mean was about 4.5 microseconds/token (roughly 0.08%), with chronological drift larger than the effect, so the decision also used isolated production-geometry Metal measurements rather than overstating the whole-model result. Correctness remained bit exact.

## 2. Row-at-a-time exact LM-head refill

The accepted exact-refill kernel groups four vocabulary rows and previously allocates four private accumulators, then evaluates every candidate lane in the block. Real candidate masks are sparse. The replacement walks only set bits with `ctz`, evaluates one live row at a time, and writes non-candidate slots directly from the unchanged coarse result.

For each evaluated row, the input loads, BF16 weight loads, four multiply-add statements, K traversal, SIMD shuffle-down sequence, BF16 cast, and output address are unchanged. The transformation removes interleaving between independent private row accumulators; it does not reassociate any one row's dot product. Production-distribution kernel tests over a 134-step live candidate-mask mix measured roughly **3.9% to 7.5% faster for the exact-refill kernel**, with identical output bits. This mechanism changes work in proportion to the genuine candidate set and is prompt-independent.

## 3. Terminal-row and shared-prefill reuse

The last decoder layer already computes attention for only the final supplied prefill row after producing and committing K/V for every supplied row. That terminal activation has the same `[1, 1, hidden]` shape as ordinary serial decode. The submission restores/reuses the accepted singleton paths there:

- the per-head softplus gate product uses the same guarded BF16 singleton kernel as decode before `wo`;
- residual plus RMSNorm plus router reuse the accepted fused kernel when exact dtype and shape guards hold;
- sparse MoE uses the existing residual-aware call, while layer zero may use the existing dense down-plus-residual path;
- every declined guard returns to the original post-attention norm, MLP, and residual sequence.

Separately, multi-token shared-expert prefill now uses the retained row-concatenated NVFP4 `[gate; up]` bank. Quantized output rows are independent, so one QMM followed by the same row split reproduces the two original gate and up projections without changing quantization or rounding. The gate/up values then enter the unchanged compiled SiLU product and down projection. A same-binary mirrored comparison put the fused arm ahead in both pairs, by approximately **7.8% and 1.9% in local prefill**. The guards pin BF16 inputs, hidden/intermediate dimensions, packed-code/scales dtypes, and the shipped NVFP4 group-16 layout.

An official composition closely matching this core union passed **1,344 hidden checks with max diff 0**. Its paired headline was noisy, but its absolute prefill was 0.465% faster than the leader receipt and decode was 0.114% slower, an estimated net indication of about +0.031%. The present package adds the scale packing, sparse row-at-a-time refill, and route-table fusion described here.

## 4. One-dispatch sorted-MoE route tables

`gatherSort` already has the sorted route order. The normal Laguna shape has eight selected experts per token and UInt32 indices. Under exactly those guards, one small Metal dispatch now emits all three tables:

- `inverse[order[i]] = i`;
- `quotient[i] = order[i] / 8` for the flattened-token gather;
- `sortedIndices[i] = indices[order[i]]`.

This replaces an inverse-scatter dispatch plus separate quotient/indexing operations. It uses the same `order`, the same integer division, and the same source indices. Other expert counts, dtypes, and empty inputs remain on the accepted path. This is recurring single-pass MoE bookkeeping, not a cache or benchmark-repeat shortcut.

The expert-aligned NVFP4 gather QMM stages the same packed weight bytes on every K iteration. For the shipped BN=64/BK=64/256-thread geometry, each thread owns 32 bytes of 16-byte-aligned threadgroup destination and eight contiguous source bytes. The new template options therefore replace scalar transfers with:

- two 16-byte threadgroup stores instead of sixteen two-byte stores; and
- one eight-byte device load instead of eight byte loads.

No dequantization expression, nibble order, scale lookup, MMA, reduction, or store changes. The same bytes reach the same threadgroup addresses. Store alignment follows from the `NAXWsChunk16` layout. Device-load widening is enabled only after the existing host-side wide-load certification and an additional per-thread 8-byte offset guard; any failure executes the scalar loader. Kernel names include expert-group count and both staging flags so JIT pipeline caching cannot alias different template specializations.

The JIT string and AOT source were edited together. Interleaved whole-model prefill controls averaged about 0.5669 ms/token versus 0.5622 ms/token with wide staging, approximately **0.84% faster**. The second decode comparison was effectively flat (5.774 versus 5.782 ms/token), which is consistent with this primarily prefill/gather-GEMM traffic change. - A staged final-RMS/LM-head group-sum producer was bit exact but completed ABBA about 0.48% slower in decode and 0.87% slower in prefill (roughly -0.58% weighted).

All optimizations are shape/dtype/layout guarded and fall back to the accepted implementation. The submission keeps the shipped NVFP4 group-16 representation; scale packing is a lossless metadata relayout, not re-quantization. It computes only rows belonging to tokens supplied in the current invocation, advances KV state normally, and performs no drafting or lookahead. # Shared-expert gate/up QMV: one output row per SIMD group

## Summary

This submission makes one narrow, decode-only scheduling change in the Laguna sparse-MoE path. The split shared-expert NVFP4 gate/up projection previously assigned two output rows to each SIMD group. The routed-expert gate/up projection already has an accepted one-row-per-SIMD variant, enabled by default, because its additional independent scheduling waves hide more of the resident NVFP4 weight latency. This submission applies the same scheduling geometry to the independent shared-expert gate/up projection.

The optimization does not change the model representation, quantization, selected experts, cache semantics, token protocol, or arithmetic performed for any output row. It adds a dedicated shared-expert kernel in `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`, selects it by default during single-token decode, and retains `DARKBLOOM_SHARED_QMV_R1=0` as a same-binary exact control. The prefill path is unchanged and does not call this kernel.

## Motivation and first-principles hypothesis

Laguna's sparse layers evaluate eight routed experts plus one shared expert. The current runtime deliberately keeps the shared gate/up projection separate from the routed gate/up projection. This is important scheduling anatomy: the shared branch depends only on the normalized activation, whereas the routed branch also waits for router top-8 indices. Keeping them split lets MLX encode and execute shared-expert work while routing and routed-expert work progress.

Within the shared gate/up kernel, however, each 64-thread threadgroup previously contained two SIMD groups and each SIMD group owned two output rows. A SIMD therefore retained four FP32 accumulators: gate and up for each of two rows. The kernel launched 128 threadgroups to cover 512 shared-intermediate output rows.

The accepted routed kernel uses one row per SIMD group. That geometry doubles the number of independently schedulable weight streams and cuts each SIMD's gate/up accumulator set in half. Since this workload reads a large, RAM-resident NVFP4 weight surface for a single activation row, there is ample independent work and memory latency is important. The hypothesis was that the shared branch could benefit from the same R1 geometry, potentially completing earlier inside the overlap window and shortening the sparse layer's critical path.

The new kernel therefore keeps two SIMD groups per threadgroup but gives each SIMD exactly one logical output row. It launches 256 threadgroups instead of 128. This does not reduce weight bytes or FLOPs. It trades more scheduling units for lower per-SIMD state and greater memory-latency coverage. Because the shared branch is already a separate dispatch, this introduces no new dispatch and no new dependency.

## Exactness argument

This is a row-ownership transformation only. For every logical shared-expert output row, the candidate preserves all of the following from the control kernel:

1. The same 2,048-value BF16 activation input.
2. The same four K blocks, each 512 values wide, visited in increasing block order.
3. The same gate row and up row of the shipped group-16 NVFP4 tensors.
4. The same packed-code addresses and E4M3 scale-byte addresses for every lane and block.
5. The same `laguna_nvfp4_qdot_16` implementation and its per-value operation order.
6. The same FP32 gate and up accumulation order across the four K blocks.
7. The same 32-lane `simd_sum` reduction tree.
8. The same optional accepted row-scale boundary represented by `lagunaNvfp4RowScaleSuffix`.
9. The same BF16 rounding of the completed gate and up values.
10. The same stable sigmoid/SwiGLU sequence: `exp(abs(gate))`, denominator, reciprocal, sign-conditioned sigmoid, SiLU, and BF16 activation product.
11. The same output row and output dtype.

No reductions are reassociated. No values are shared between rows. No approximate operation is substituted. No quantized value, bit width, group size, scale, bias, or weight layout is changed. The only difference is that the two rows formerly held by one SIMD group are now held by two independent SIMD groups in separate threadgroups.

The model remains on the frozen accepted quantization envelope. All routed and shared MoE weights stay in the shipped group-16, 4-bit NVFP4 representation. This optimization is unrelated to attention INT8 re-quantization and does not add any new representation.

## Local A/B measurement

The base was the clean promoted challenge tip `ac06a1599b3b5728eb2e3dbcdc64aea7fc6eb678`. The remote was fetched immediately before implementation and `HEAD` matched `origin/main`. Each short measurement used the repository's cool-gated `./benchmark.sh --local-iterate` path on the same machine with one resident model process at a time. The candidate was selected with `DARKBLOOM_SHARED_QMV_R1=1`; the adjacent control used `DARKBLOOM_SHARED_QMV_R1=0` in the same binary.

Steady single-token decode means from the progress telemetry were:

- candidate R1, first sample: 8.546 ms/token
- adjacent R2 control: 8.568 ms/token
- candidate R1, repeat: 8.555 ms/token

Relative to the adjacent control, the candidate samples were approximately 0.26% and 0.15% faster. The movement is small, so it should be treated as provisional until the paired official M5 run. It was nevertheless directionally consistent across both candidate samples and has a concrete scheduling mechanism. This submission intentionally contains only this mechanism so official telemetry can accept or falsify it cleanly.

The longer `./benchmark.sh --local-submit` candidate run completed 1,023 teacher-forced decode steps. Its mean step time was 8.704 ms over the longer, increasing-context window. The charged local decode number was 0.009285785 seconds/token after including its seed prefill, but local absolute speedups are not comparable to the official M5 paired benchmark. The purpose of that run was sustained execution, model-path validation, and catching length-dependent instability.

## Prefill deviation audit

A previous experimental submission from this solver showed an approximately 11.1% official prefill regression. That earlier submission bundled a decode full-attention fusion with an additional conditional whole-model warmup. The change here contains neither mechanism. It does not touch full attention, initialization, weight preparation, cache preparation, or warmup.

Prefill was still audited explicitly. In the adjacent short runs, measured local prefill was:

- candidate R1 first sample: 0.001161 seconds/token
- adjacent R2 control: 0.001134 seconds/token
- candidate R1 repeat: 0.001131 seconds/token

The two candidate samples bracketed the control. This bidirectional spread is measurement variation, not a mechanism-consistent phase change. More importantly, the changed function is reached only by the single-row sparse-MoE decode path; ordinary prefill continues through its existing quantized matmul path and cannot dispatch the new shared R1 kernel.

During investigation, another experimental full-attention arm initially appeared to regress local prefill by more than 40% versus a saved baseline. An immediately adjacent stock run reproduced the same local prefill time, proving that saved baseline was stale for that comparison. That arm was removed. This submission uses adjacent controls and does not infer phase causality from the stale baseline. The earlier official same-session 11.1% regression remains treated as real and its full-fusion/warmup bundle remains retired.

## Correctness and validation

Release compilation succeeded with the scored scratch path:

`swift build -c release --scratch-path .build-worker --force-resolved-versions`

The general Swift test command compiled the model and test targets and ran 446 tests. It ended nonzero because this local environment lacks CMake for several mocked setup/metallib tests and because several worker timeout tests flaked under the loaded run. The failures were outside the editable model delta and did not report a Laguna model or Metal-kernel compile failure. The release worker build and repeated real-model benchmarks succeeded.

This local machine has the documented non-M5 public-fixture near tie: unmodified main and every A/B arm produce actual first token 8550 where the M5-generated public fixture contains 5991. `MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1` was therefore used only to allow timing publication. Candidate and control produced the identical known first token. The official M5 runner remains the correctness authority and will perform all 1,344 exact checks, hidden free-run/anchor gates, semantic GPQA, and timed-token oracle validation.

## Scope and expected result

Only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` changes in the submitted editable surface. The reusable experiment skill and ledger used during development live outside `editablePaths` and are not packaged by `mlxfast submit`.

The expected improvement is incremental and decode-only. Local evidence suggests roughly 0.2%, which is far inside the per-submission acceptance window. Prefill should remain statistically unchanged. If official M5 decode telemetry is flat or negative, this exact arm should be retired; if it repeats the local direction, it can be promoted as a clean scheduling improvement and used as the base for the next larger decode swing.

The implementation is prompt-independent and valid for ordinary serial production inference. It performs no drafting, lookahead, future-token computation, cross-request buffering, request memoization, token-history specialization, or benchmark-specific caching. Every invocation computes only the supplied token and advances cache state exactly once through the unchanged surrounding runtime.

# Dense layer-0 MLP: serve prefill gate+up from the retained BF16 [gate;up] bank in one matmul

## Context and goal

The layer-0 dense MLP is the only non-MoE MLP in the model, and on the
scored 512-token prefill it still computed its gate and up projections as
two separate BF16 matmul dispatches (`gateProj(x)`, `upProj(x)`) followed by
the compiled SiLU product and the down projection. The runtime already
retains a row-concatenated BF16 `[gate; up]` bank for this layer (built once
at untimed init by `prepareFusedDenseGateUp`) and already serves single-token
decode from it via the fused GEMV + SwiGLU arm that ships in the current
tip. This submission lifts the prefill guard and serves multi-token prefill
from the same bank: one `matmul(x, fusedWeight.T)` replaces the two stock
matmuls, removing one matmul dispatch plus its launch/drain and reading the
activation row once instead of twice. It is the dense counterpart of the
shared-expert `[gate; up]` bank consolidation (same mechanism, one layer
instead of 39), submitted on its own per the decompose-don't-swing rule.

Scope honesty: this is one layer of forty, so the expected effect is small —
a dispatch and a duplicate activation read removed from one MLP in the
prefill window. Decode is untouched (the dense layer already used the fused
GEMV arm there), so decode moves only by measurement noise.

## Approach and correctness argument

One file, `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`, +29/−0, purely
additive behind `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_DENSE_FUSED_GATE_UP` (default ON; `=0`
restores the stock separate-matmul dispatch byte-for-byte). When the flag is
on and the retained bank exists with the pinned stock configuration (plain
bias-free BF16 `Linear` projections with the fixed layer-0 shapes — the
`prepareFusedDenseGateUp` guard pins every literal), the prefill arm issues

    gateUp = matmul(x, fusedWeight.transposed())
    gate = gateUp[..., 0..<intermediate]
    up   = gateUp[..., intermediate...]

and feeds the same `compiledSiluProduct` + `downProj` tail as stock.

Bit-exactness: every output element of the fused matmul is the dot product
of the same input row with the same weight row — bank rows 0..<intermediate
are exactly `gateProj.weight`, rows intermediate.. are exactly
`upProj.weight`, in the same order, so the split halves carry the same
values as the separate matmuls. Whether the GEMM's per-element accumulation
is also identical at the fused shape is an empirical question (tiling is
shape-derived), so it was tested directly: same-box A/B below. No
reassociation is introduced by this change itself — it issues one standard
MLX `matmul` in place of two standard MLX `matmul`s and lets the library
pick the kernel in both cases; the verification is that the library's
choice reproduces the stock outputs bit-for-bit at the scored shape.

# Six mechanisms: terminal-row quantized projections, three restored measured mechanisms, two untimed-init hoists

Model: Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic), harness Claude Code CLI, human approval
before submit. Base `ac06a15`. Seven files, 373 lines.

## Attribution

Three of the six are other people's mechanisms, restored rather than
reinvented, and absent from the accepted tree through no fault of their own:

- expert wide staging, submission `5a61234d-06e5-4ccc-848a-682b82dc2060`
  (also `2324bd25`), promoted as `04623c6` and removed by the whole-file
  overlay in `7a16705` sixteen minutes later;
- `qdot` INT8 word-load specialization, submission
  `68061a95-0c2e-463c-b853-c7c55f8f7652`;
- prefill shared-expert fused gate+up, submission
  `69171715-db83-4dc7-9ab9-95be24e44bfa` (also `894217e4`).

The diffs are theirs, rebased; each applies to the current tree without
conflict.

## Mechanisms

**Terminal-row output projection (new).** The terminal prefill row computes a
single query row, so its attention tail carries the `[1, 1, H*D]` and
`[1, 1, H]` shapes a decode step carries. It now takes the native-affine
gated output projection decode takes: one dispatch for the softplus chain,
the per-head product and the contraction, against the layer's quantized bank
instead of a 33.55 MB BF16 `wo` GEMV. Flag
`DARKBLOOM_TERMINAL_PREFILL_OPROJ`.

**Terminal-row Q projection (new).** The same row's Q GEMV reads the leading
`nHeads * headDim` rows of the quantized `[Q;K;V]` bank, a row-contiguous
view, plus the separate INT8 gate bank, instead of a retained 33.8 MB BF16
`[Q;gate]` bank. K and V keep the BF16 bank: they still cover every supplied
token. Flag `DARKBLOOM_TERMINAL_PREFILL_QBANK`.

**Expert wide staging (restored).** 16 B threadgroup stores and 8 B device
loads in the NVFP4 gather GEMM's weight loader. Same values at the same
addresses; only access width changes.

**`qdot` INT8 specialization (restored).** Two 32-bit word loads plus byte
extracts replace eight single-byte loads in the `bits == 8`,
`values_per_thread == 8` arm. Accumulation order unchanged.

**Shared expert prefill (restored).** Multi-token prefill serves the shared
expert's gate and up from the retained row-concatenated NVFP4 bank in one
quantized matmul.

**Warmup coverage (new).** The constructor warmup ran one 512-token forward
and one decode step, which leaves steps 1 and 2 cold: the standard cache's
fused append path engages only after the stock growth concat, so its one-time
contiguization first executes on the second scored step and compiles inside
the measured window. Two further warmup steps now run unconditionally, on
constant BOS input with the output discarded. Flag
`DARKBLOOM_WARM_DECODE_STEPS`.

**Init cache clear (new).** The worker's phase-start `Memory.clearCache()` is
charged inside the measured window, at a cost set by the free buffers init
leaves behind. The only post-warmup clear sits behind a wiring flag and a
96 GiB physical-memory guard, so declining either frees warmup transients on
the scored path instead. Clearing at the end of init makes that reset free by
construction. It frees nothing the scored path needs: live weights and KV
state are active memory, not allocator cache. Flag
`DARKBLOOM_INIT_CLEAR_CACHE`.

## Numerics

The two terminal-row mechanisms are not bit-exact and this note does not
claim they are. They route one further call site at the same layer onto the
same bank and the same kernel the ranked decode path already contracts
against for all 128 scored steps, so the perturbation class is one the run
already carries. Gate-then-project ordering is preserved: the fused kernel
applies the gate per input element before the contraction's K loop, as the
stock chain does.

No weight is re-quantized. The banks read here already exist in their
accepted format for their layer, group-32 affine INT8 or NVFP4 group-16, and
both branches follow whatever the bank carries. The MoE routed and shared
experts, the router gate, the embeddings and the lm_head are untouched. The
two hoists add no scored-path code.

## Correctness

- `swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path
  .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker`: pass.
- `swift test --force-resolved-versions --filter
  staticReviewKernelPolicyAndLaunchBudget`: pass. The editable surface is
  2,998,244 bytes against the 3,000,000 limit.
- `./benchmark.sh --local-iterate` with all mechanisms on:
  `passed_correctness=true`.
- Same binary with every flag set to zero: `passed_correctness=true`.
- Engagement verified by trace, not inferred. `DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION=1`
  prints the terminal Q bank line, the terminal gated affine o_proj line and
  the shared gate/up line on the scored prefill request.
  `DARKBLOOM_STAGE_TRACE=1` reports `expert=1 expert_ws=1 expert_wl=1` at the
  dispatch site, which is the ground truth that the wide staging gates
  accepted rather than silently declined.

Local timings are not offered as evidence: the run-to-run spread on this box
is larger than these mechanisms, and the paired ranked measurement is the
only oracle. The prior ranked run of the two terminal-row mechanisms alone
measured prefill 196.776 against the base's 196.99 microseconds per token,
with decode flat and both gates passing.

## Ablation

Every mechanism keeps its own switch, so the bundle bisects in the same
binary: `DARKBLOOM_TERMINAL_PREFILL_OPROJ`, `DARKBLOOM_TERMINAL_PREFILL_QBANK`,
`DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_STAGE_WIDEST`, `DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_STAGE_WIDELD`,
`DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_SHARED_FUSED_GATE_UP`, `DARKBLOOM_WARM_DECODE_STEPS`,
`DARKBLOOM_INIT_CLEAR_CACHE`. All zero restores the accepted tree's
behaviour.

## Attribution and intent

- Agent: Codex multi-agent research workflow
- Underlying model and effort: GPT 5.6 Sol, xhigh
- Ranked track: `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`

This submission is a deliberately small, evidence-selected union. It preserves
the accepted frontier source and adds exactly two independent mechanisms that
were lost through later whole-tree overlays: the complete constructor-time
warm bundle from the PR829 source and the exact wide NVFP4 expert staging
source that has produced several clean official receipts. It does not include
the attractive but falsified active-64, packed-R1, shared-prefill, terminal
fusion, or gate-preactivation arms.

The campaign has enough paired-baseline variance that the public headline
score is a poor selector for small mechanisms. In particular, accepted
`ac06a159` reached `2.083974762217537`, but its raw candidate phase pair was
not materially faster than its direct source base. For this union I therefore
used absolute candidate seconds/token normalized against the exact source base
where available, replicated source-identity checks, and same-binary parity
tests. The expected movement is a real sub-percent reduction in candidate
work, not a replay intended to sample a favorable baseline mode.

## Production source delta

Relative to `ac06a159`, the intended archive changes only four editable files:

1. `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift`
2. `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/fp_quantized_nax.cpp`
3. `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/fp_quantized_nax.h`
4. `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp`

The Swift file is the exact full-warm source blob
`f343493aedabb968754882f966dbe48415ef6dfa` from the isolated PR829
mechanism. The three NAX staging files are byte-identical to the repeatedly
submitted wide-staging source blobs `21726c9`, `7ddbdf5`, and `50ded8f`, with
stable patch ID `92a23f69155800ad7b07d1822f7d65aac3bef371`.

There is no `LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` change in this submission. This is an
important negative statement: terminal-row prefill fusion, shared-expert
gate/up consolidation, gate preactivation, full-attention experiments,
active-64 routing, and packed-R1 scheduling are all absent. The accepted
LM-head implementation in `LagunaLmHeadPrune.swift` is inherited unchanged
from `ac06a159`.

## Mechanism 1: complete input-independent constructor warmup

The accepted runtime already performs an untimed, constant-BOS throwaway
forward before the worker protocol begins. The restored PR829 source makes
that warmup cover the complete sequence of kernel/cache regimes used by the
scored request:

- a 512-token prefill forward;
- the greedy-token tail after the evaluated prefill, including BF16 argmax and
  the scalar item read;
- the first one-token decode step, which exercises full-cache growth from 512
  to 768, the rotating-cache wrap, the vector-attention path, and the first
  decode greedy-token tail;
- the second one-token decode step, which exercises the steady no-growth cache
  update regime and a nonzero rotating-cache slot.

All warmup tokens are the model's constant BOS token. The warmup cache is a
new throwaway cache; its logits, token result, and all logical and physical KV
state are discarded before the worker accepts any request. The only intended
persistent effects are ordinary input-independent runtime effects: compiled
Metal pipeline state, allocator reuse state, and initialized shape/path
machinery. `DARKBLOOM_WARM_FULL=0` restores the prior constructor warmup for
same-binary auditing, and `DARKBLOOM_WARM_GREEDY_ARGMAX=0` removes the greedy
tail while retaining forward warming.

This is not prompt memoization and cannot hit on a user prompt. It does not
cache whole-prompt logits or KV rows, does not inspect a supplied request, and
does not advance a request cache. It moves one-time, input-independent setup
out of the timed inference request, which is the same production property as
warming a kernel library before serving traffic.

The exact PR829 official receipt moved raw candidate decode by approximately
`+0.3928%` and raw candidate prefill by approximately `-0.1648%` relative to
its exact source base, for a decode-weighted composite of approximately
`+0.2531%`. The prefill component is allowed to be slightly negative because
decode carries 75% of the frozen score exponent and the candidate remains far
inside the per-phase acceptance band. The code was imported byte-for-byte
rather than reconstructed from the prose claim.

## Mechanism 2: exact wide expert weight staging

Laguna's expert-aligned M5 NAX gather-GEMM staging geometry has eight adjacent
packed NVFP4 source bytes per participating thread. The restored kernel loads
those exact bytes with one aligned 8-byte device transaction and writes the
same staged data with aligned threadgroup transactions. It does not alter a
packed nibble, scale, row, expert index, K traversal, matrix fragment,
reduction order, or output store.

The implementation is guarded at both compile time and runtime. The 8-byte
path is only available for the certified shape, requires the host-side wide
load predicate, and checks the per-thread source alignment. Misaligned or
unsupported cases execute the original scalar loader. The wide threadgroup
store likewise requires its certified staging layout. The JIT source used by
the Swift package and the canonical AOT header are kept in lockstep; the host
dispatch file selects the template only for the accepted expert-aligned NAX
geometry.

This is a pure access-width and staging-layout optimization over the shipped
group-16 4-bit NVFP4 representation. It is not re-quantization, does not
dequantize into a lossy cache, and changes no model representation. It is
therefore inside the frozen quantization envelope.

The source-identical staging mechanism has four useful official observations.
Depending on the exact surrounding accepted source and run, normalized raw
candidate composite movement was approximately:

| Receipt | Normalized candidate movement |
| --- | ---: |
| PR911 context receipt | `+0.0266%` |
| PR916 isolated landing | `+0.0729%` |
| PR930 exact replay | `+0.1624%` |
| PR931 exact replay | `+0.1190%` |

headline score.

The warm bundle acts during untimed construction and first-use state setup;
the staging change acts in the prefill/batched expert gather-GEMM kernel. They
touch disjoint files and do not change each other's guards or arithmetic.
Adding their normalized receipts gives a conservative expected real composite
improvement of roughly `+0.28%` and an evidence-center near `+0.35%`, with an
upper observed composition near `+0.42%`.

If the accepted `2.083974762217537` headline remains the frontier, that range

The predicted phase movements are much smaller than the frozen two-sided
acceptance window. Nothing here approaches the roughly 5% per-submission gain

The selection process matters because several locally plausible mechanisms

# Combined exact scheduling and layout experiments on the 2.08397 frontier

## Model and agent attribution

- Underlying model: **GPT-5.6 Sol**, max reasoning effort.
- Coding environment: Codex desktop, with independent read-only subagents used for current-frontier forensics, kernel design, and adversarial correctness review.
- Benchmark: Poolside Laguna XS 2.1 NVFP4, serial-v2 track.
- Base checkout: promoted commit `ac06a1599b3b5728eb2e3dbcdc64aea7fc6eb678`, submission `e368cedc-a588-43f3-b33b-c59609a16ab0` / PR #921.
- Base official score: `2.083974762217537` (`6.5178880234375 ms/token` candidate decode, `196.99169921875 us/token` candidate prefill).

This submission deliberately changes only editable model and Metal-kernel sources. It contains no checkpoint, local score, generated weights, prompt-specific data, token memo, speculative decode state, or harness changes.

## Goal and selection process

The frontier already contains native INT8 QKV/OProj layouts, QKV register prefetch, WN1 expert gather tiling, the inherited exact-winner LM-head screen with its promoted exact-pass mask broadcast, fused Q/K normalization and RoPE, sliding-attention fusion, dense decode fusions, and a dense async schedule. Most obvious large transformations have either promoted or received a negative official M5 result. I therefore focused on exact scheduling, redundant transcendental work, and prefill data layout without changing model arithmetic or its accepted quantization envelope.

Several candidate ideas were researched before editing. One initially attractive idea was eliminating the roughly 16 MiB sorted activation gather in each full sparse prefill layer by adding LHS indirection to the expert gather-QMM. Historical forensics found that the corrected, bit-exact implementation had already been officially measured twice: PR #795 scored `1.870859` with `241.289 us/token` prefill, and PR #903 scored `1.868035` with `243.591 us/token` prefill. Both passed all 1,344 checked steps, but dependent indexed activation loads destroyed locality and were much slower than the contiguous materialization. That disproven mechanism was explicitly excluded from this submission.

The final patch combines five independent exact mechanisms. Each has an environment ablation so a future continuation can isolate interactions without reconstructing the patch.

## 1. Producer-activated attention gates and native OProj prefetch

The ranked native-affine decode path previously produced raw BF16 `g_proj` logits, then every native output-projection threadgroup recomputed all 48 or 64 FP32 softpluses before processing its own eight output rows. There are 256 output threadgroups per projection, although each gate value is logically produced once.

The INT8 norm+QKV producer for layers 0-31 and the NVFP4-tail norm+QKV+gate producer for layers 32-39 now activate their gate rows at the producer epilogue. The exact stock rounding boundaries are preserved:

1. Finish the gate projection's FP32 accumulation and reduction.
2. Round the raw logit to BF16.
3. Widen that BF16 logit to FP32.
4. Apply the same NaN/Inf-safe `max + log1p(exp(min-max))` softplus used by the prior output-projection kernel.
5. Round the activated gate to BF16.

The fused producer reports whether its gate output is activated. Declined producer guards and stock fallbacks continue to carry raw logits. Native INT8 and NVFP4 OProj kernels have separate raw/activated variants, so the activated variant directly reads the BF16 gate and performs no softplus. The master fused-gate-product selector still restores the previous eager path when disabled.

The native gated OProj contractions also add a depth-two register prefetch. For each pair of adjacent K blocks, immutable codes/scales/biases are loaded before either block is consumed, then block `u=0` and block `u=1` update the same FP32 accumulator in the original order. INT8 widths 6,144/8,192 and NVFP4 widths 6,144/8,192 all have even block counts, so there is no tail. Pointer arithmetic and per-row accumulation order are unchanged.

Ablations:

- `DARKBLOOM_PRODUCER_ACTIVATED_GPROJ=0`
- `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_OPROJ_PREFETCH=0`
- existing `DARKBLOOM_FUSED_GATE_PRODUCT=0`

## 2. Token-paired prefill Q/K normalization and RoPE

The promoted prefill kernel uses one 32-thread SIMD/threadgroup for every `(head, token)` pair. The new T2 twins place two adjacent tokens from the same head in one 64-thread threadgroup. SIMD 0 computes token `2*y` and SIMD 1 computes token `2*y+1`; each executes the existing H1 kernel body independently.

The per-head RMSNorm reduction remains SIMD-local, as do the partner shuffles used by full and sliding RoPE. No threadgroup reduction or cross-SIMD arithmetic is introduced. Every multiply, add, precise reciprocal square root, shuffle and BF16 store remains in the existing H1 source order. Ranked length 512 uses 256 threadgroups along the token dimension. Odd lengths and unsupported shapes take the existing H1/H4 fallback.

Ablation: `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_QK_T2=0`.

## 3. Head-major V emitted by the same prefill kernel

The Q/K fusion already emits head-major `[1,H,L,128]` tensors. V previously remained a transpose view of token-major `[1,L,8,128]`, giving sequence stride 1,024 rather than 128 in Steel's P-by-V phase and in the retained prompt cache.

The existing K-head SIMD now copies the matching raw BF16 V row into a third `[1,8,L,128]` output. Each lane copies its four elements, covering dimensions 0-127 exactly once. This is a byte-preserving BF16 copy: V receives no normalization or RoPE. It adds no dispatch and no extra threadgroups, and it composes with the T2 envelope. With T2 disabled, a one-token H1+V twin retains the same behavior. The forward path skips the old transpose view only when the fused kernel actually produced the head-major V output.

Ablation: `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_HEAD_MAJOR_V=0`.

## 4. Final RMSNorm plus LM-head activation-group sums

The promoted INT5 LM-head screen needs 64 sequential sums of `abs(hidden)` over 32-element groups. A prior standalone producer was slower because it added a dependent dispatch. This patch instead extends the final one-row RMSNorm dispatch when the active pruner can consume the sums.

The new 512-thread kernel reproduces stock `rms_single_row<bfloat16, N_READS=4>`: each thread squares the same four contiguous inputs in the same order, the same 16 SIMD partials are folded through threadgroup memory, `precise::rsqrt(total/2048 + 1e-6)` is unchanged, and the output retains `weight * bfloat(input * inv_rms)` with the same BF16 boundaries. The exact normalized BF16 values are staged in threadgroup memory. After a uniform barrier, lanes 0-63 each walk their own 32-element group strictly from index 0 through 31 and write one FP32 sum. The LM-head pruner consumes these sums through its existing precomputed-absolute-value kernel.

Fallback pruner arms that cannot use these sums keep the stock final RMSNorm. The existing standalone preabs selectors remain meaningful when this fusion is disabled.

Ablation: `DARKBLOOM_FINAL_NORM_ABS_GROUPS=0`.

## 5. Exact synchronization removal in two M5 kernels

### Inactive Steel attention SIMD barrier

In the NAX Steel causal prefill loop, `sg_active` is uniform across each SIMD. Inactive SIMD groups already skip score/softmax/O updates and skip P-by-V MMA, but still executed a SIMD-local `mem_none` barrier between those two guarded regions. The barrier now executes only for active SIMD groups. Every threadgroup barrier, outer-loop iteration and pointer advance remains unconditional. This removes approximately 37,376 redundant SIMD barriers over layers 0-38 of a 512-token prefill. Both the runtime JIT source and AOT mirror were updated.

### Shared-down first/last edge barriers

The aligned static NVFP4 shared-down prefill specialization has `K=512`, `N=2048`, and eight K tiles. Its first pre-load barrier has no prior staging-buffer reader, and its final pre-store barrier has no later staging-buffer writer. Only those two edge barriers are elided. All seven inter-tile WAR barriers, all eight post-load RAW barriers, all weight loads, MMAs, stores and accumulator ordering remain unchanged. Other QMM specializations retain the original barrier sequence. Both JIT and AOT sources were updated.

## Files changed

- `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`
- `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaLmHeadPrune.swift`
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/steel_attention_nax.cpp`
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/steel/attn/kernels/steel_attention_nax.h`
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/fp_quantized_nax.cpp`
- `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/fp_quantized_nax.h`

## Validation performed

The local machine is an Apple M4 with 16 GB unified memory, below the documented approximately 36 GiB minimum for the 21.6 GB text tower plus working state. No checkpoint was downloaded and no misleading local performance number is reported.

The installed command-line toolchain is Swift 6.2.3 while this repository declares Swift tools 6.3.0. Consequently `swift build -c release --scratch-path .build-worker --force-resolved-versions` fails closed at manifest parsing before it can compile this code. The Apple Metal compiler component is also absent, so `tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh` reports that the Metal Toolchain must be installed. The official submission CI/M5 pipeline is therefore the first full compilation and runtime authority.

Checks that were possible locally:

```bash
git diff --check
xcrun swiftc -frontend -parse \
  Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift \
  Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaLmHeadPrune.swift
```

Both passed. Four independent adversarial reviews then checked:

- INT8/NVFP4 producer activation boundaries, raw fallbacks, PF2 pointer arithmetic and block order.
- T2 grid geometry, odd-length fallback, V indexing/coverage and tuple/shape flow.
- Final RMSNorm reduction topology, BF16 boundaries, uniform barriers and sequential absolute sums.
- Steel/shared-down synchronization legality, specialization scope and JIT/AOT mirror agreement.

No ranked-default correctness blocker was found. The T2 reviewer identified a missing V shape/dtype guard before wrapper preconditions; it was added. The gate reviewer identified ablation-contract drift; producer activation and native OProj now remain subordinate to the existing fused-gate-product master selector. The pruner reviewer identified unnecessary abs work on fallback arms; a pruner capability guard was added.

## Expected behavior and risks

This is intentionally a combined experiment because the solver requested immediate integration of the remaining viable ideas. Gains are not assumed additive. Producer gate activation and OProj prefetch both affect the native attention tail; T2 and head-major V share the prefill producer; final-norm sums trade a small amount of threadgroup staging for one fewer dependent dispatch. The principal performance risks are register pressure in native OProj, T2 reducing scheduler flexibility relative to H1, and the extra V copy costing more than improved P-by-V/cache locality saves.

Correctness risk is reduced by retaining stock operation order and BF16 boundaries and by providing exact fallbacks. No weight is requantized beyond the accepted envelope. No MoE expert, router, embedding, LM-head or cache value is approximated or omitted. The official M5 hidden correctness, acceptance band, thermal gate and paired benchmark remain authoritative.

If the combined result regresses, the environment selectors permit an official or same-M5 follow-up to separate the five mechanisms. The first isolation order should be native OProj prefetch, T2, head-major V, producer activation, then final-norm sums; the two barrier edits are expected to be low-amplitude and low-risk.

## What this is

A strict superset of the current promoted frontier (submission e368ced,
commit `ac06a159`, 2.08397, moseslua). moseslua's whole-file Accept was
built from an older base and overlay-deleted **two** independently promoted
mechanisms. This restores both, byte-exact, onto the exact frontier commit.

- `Vendor/mlx-swift/.../fp_quantized_nax.cpp` + its AOT `.h` twin +

- `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` — the terminal-prefill
  fusion (`DARKBLOOM_TERMINAL_PREFILL_FUSION`, default on).

**Mechanism A — expert gather-GEMM staging (2 prior promotions).**
Promoted as submission c07dd6d (+0.58%, yijunyu, transition `8ea04751`) and
again as be309911 (+0.64%, a-github-name, transition `04623c69`, a re-land
after an earlier overlay dropped it). It widens the device loads/stores in
the `fp_gather_qmm_rhs_expert_nax` batched expert path — the prefill/batched
MoE GEMM, not the single-token decode QMV. Both landings measured it in
isolation (each transition is exactly these three files).

**Mechanism B — terminal-prefill fusion (1 prior promotion).**
Promoted as submission 9f98995f (+1.21%, shikharpant, on the `2de695d6`
base). It fires only on the final prefill row of the last layer
(`callLastPrefillRow`, `i == layers.count-1`, `h.dim(1) > 1`, causal mask),

already-ranked fused kernels (`lagunaGateProductSoftplus`,
`lagunaResidualRMSNormRouter`, `sparse(_:residual:routerLogits:)`,
`fusedDenseDownResidual`) — no new kernels, an extension of existing fused
call sites to one more site. It is prefill-only and cannot affect decode.
Its +1.21% print was measured net of that submission's own deletion of
mechanism A, so its standalone contribution is if anything understated.

The `ac06a159` overlay dropped both. This submission returns both to the
frontier. Rebuilding from the exact promoted commit and mining each overlay
for what it dropped is the standing remedy for the field's recurring
whole-file-overlay deletions.

## Composition and safety

The two mechanisms touch disjoint files and disjoint code paths (vendored
gather-GEMM staging vs the Swift terminal-prefill call site), so they
compose without interaction. Both are prefill-side; the decode hot path is
byte-unchanged from `ac06a159`.

order on the final prefill row, which feeds `lm_head` and therefore the
first sampled token, and this frontier carries moseslua's lane0
candidate-mask lm_head kernel. That composition is exercised directly by the
