# Current-frontier QKV and attention exact pack

Model attribution: GPT-5.6

Track: `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`

## Starting point

This candidate is built directly on promoted commit
`c6682e851c8abafacb734e2cc38f6bfe2e83f199`, submission `06c43838`, which
currently leads with official score `2.4981832813546148`. That promoted run
measured candidate decode at `0.0051773014296875` seconds/token and candidate
prefill at `0.000195240560546875` seconds/token. It passed all public, hidden,
timed-token, GPQA TTFT, and semantic gates: 1,344 checked steps,
`max_abs_diff=0`, and no correctness error. Relative to the preceding winner,
the promoted source adds the activated o_proj pipeline-cache suffix fix; this
candidate preserves it and layers the focused pack on top.

The archive adds a small pack of arithmetic-exact changes. The primary scored
coordinate transfers the already-live common group-16 NVFP4 qdot helper to
static one-token QKV R1. Two smaller decode elisions remove a bound
attention-scale read and a no-op SIMD-local barrier. A final change corrects
the fused routed prefill dispatch guard for short prompts; that guard does not
change the ranked 512-token prefill path but closes a real behavior hole for
short production and hidden requests.

No transform, weight, quantization, cache-position, token-selection, harness,
workflow, dependency, benchmark, or golden file changes.

## 1. Common NVFP4 qdot in static decode QKV

The promoted sparse routed/shared NVFP4 kernels already use
`laguna_nvfp4_qdot_16`, whose exact strength reductions remove a dead
positive-zero seed and defer the exact power-of-two `2^22` scale factor from
each group to the completed output-row epilogue. Static one-token QKV R1 still
used the older tail helper despite having the same group-16 codes, E4M3
scales, four-group K traversal, FP32 accumulation boundary, SIMD reduction,
and BF16 row store.

This candidate selects the common helper in QKV R1. The old helper remains
available through `DARKBLOOM_DECODE_NVFP4_QKV_COMMON_QDOT=0`, with a distinct
pipeline suffix. Multi-token prefill cannot enter QKV R1 and therefore cannot
select this mechanism.

Laguna executes thirty sliding-attention QKV projections with 10,240 output
rows and ten full-attention QKV projections with 8,192 output rows:

```text
30 * 10,240 + 10 * 8,192 = 389,120 QKV output rows/token
389,120 * 128 groups/row = 49,807,360 qdots/token
```

The source transformation removes the dead seed from those qdots and reduces
approximately 49.8 million group factor multiplications to 389,120 row factor
multiplications per decoded token. Those are source-operation counts used to
prioritize the change; the official receipt below shows that only a small
fraction was on the M5 critical path.

The immediately preceding official isolation of this exact helper transfer,
submission `f2d53125-7a5d-411f-a205-59b766848a74`, passed all 1,344 hidden
checks and semantic gates. On its then-current source, raw candidate decode
moved from the promoted base's `0.0052243486328125` seconds/token to
`0.005221800453125` seconds/token, a favorable absolute movement of about
0.049%. Its combined score lost on the paired draw and it was correctly not
promoted. This candidate treats that receipt honestly: QKV common-qdot is a
small, gate-proven positive coordinate, not the larger gain suggested by
non-M5 local timing.

## 2. Exact fused-attention scale literal

Both custom fused decode attention kernels always operate at head dimension
128. Their bound scalar is therefore always the FP32 value `1/sqrt(128)`. The
host supplied value has exact FP32 bit pattern `0x3db504f3`; the kernel now
constructs that same float with `as_type<float>(0x3db504f3u)`.

This removes one MLX kernel argument binding and one device scalar read from
each of the forty fused attention calls per token. It does not replace the
value with a rounded decimal approximation: the immediate is the identical
32-bit payload previously stored in the one-element input. The selector
`DARKBLOOM_FUSED_ATTN_SCALE_LITERAL=0` restores the original bound-input path.

The multiplication site, softmax order, cache update, output rounding, and
kernel geometry are unchanged. Prefill uses separate kernels and cannot
select this change.

## 3. Inactive SIMD-group barrier elision

The M5-generation `steel_attention_nax` path computes a SIMD-group-uniform
`sg_active` predicate for causal K blocks. Inactive SIMD groups skip both the
score/softmax section above one SIMD-local barrier and the P-by-V section below
it, yet the control path still executed the barrier.

The barrier is now guarded by `sg_active` in both runtime-effective forms: the
JIT `mlx-generated/steel_attention_nax.cpp` string source and its AOT header
twin. No threadgroup barrier is removed. Active SIMD groups execute the
identical barrier and arithmetic; inactive groups have no pending SIMD-scope
work on either side, so skipping it is exactly a no-op removal. Loop counts,
pointer movement, tensor shapes, and values are unchanged.

The official isolation of this exact micro-pack (scale literal, inactive
SIMD-group barrier guard, and the short-prompt correctness guard below),
submission `fcc30725-6651-4902-b12d-a3c4b12cc440`, passed all 1,344 hidden
checks and semantic gates. Against its promoted-source receipt, candidate
decode moved from `0.00521605696875` to `0.0052045071640625` seconds/token,
about 0.221% faster, while candidate prefill moved from
`0.00019530126953125` to `0.000194763671875`, about 0.275% faster. Its
combined score lost only because of the same-session baseline draw. This is
direct M5 evidence for the exact three-change pack, not a local timing claim.

## 4. Short-prompt fused-routed correctness guard

The promoted fused routed gate/up prefill branch used `inds.size >= 64`, which
is the sorted-regime threshold, as though it were also the fused bank's valid
gather-region threshold. The fused bank contains two 512-row halves, so its
valid lower bound is `2 * moeIntermediateSize`, or 1,024 gathered rows.

The guard now requires that actual fused-bank lower bound. Prompts in the old
64-to-1,016-row window fall back to the existing stock implementation; long
prompts retain the fused path. The ranked 512-token prefill produces 4,096
gathered rows, so this is score-neutral at the timed shape. It is included to
keep the current frontier correct for short hidden and production requests
rather than knowingly carrying a malformed dispatch window into a new
submission.

## Arithmetic and behavioral exactness

The candidate preserves:

- every shipped NVFP4 code and E4M3 scale byte;
- group size 16, bit width 4, and `nvfp4` mode;
- the accepted attention affine INT8 representation and all of its values;
- QKV row ownership, K traversal, FP32 accumulation, SIMD reduction, and BF16
  materialization boundary;
- the exact attention-scale FP32 payload and its multiplication site;
- every active-group synchronization operation;
- cache buffers, logical offsets, physical write positions, and context
  length;
- all routing indices, expert selections, logits, and token-selection code;
- the promoted g_proj softplus producer and every other winner mechanism.

The common qdot decodes the same nibbles, consumes the same activations, and
visits the same four K groups. Moving a power-of-two scale across those group
accumulations preserves each normal FP32 partial up to the exact reciprocal
power-of-two scaling and restores it before the existing BF16 cast. The helper
is already promoted in the sparse consumers, and the QKV transfer has its own
full hidden-gate receipt.

The scale literal is byte-identical. The guarded SIMD barrier has no producer
or consumer work in inactive groups. The prefill guard selects the existing
stock-correct path where the fused bank was never valid. None of these changes
introduces tolerance-based comparison, stochastic behavior, re-association of
non-power-of-two arithmetic, or prompt-specific logic.

## Validation on the exact submitted composition

The final tree passed:

```text
swift test --force-resolved-versions
swift build -c release --scratch-path .build-worker \
  --product mlxfast-runtime-worker --force-resolved-versions
```

All 446 tests in six suites passed. The actual production worker built
successfully. `git diff --check` passed. Only three editable files differ from
the promoted base:

```text
Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift
Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/steel_attention_nax.cpp
Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/steel/attn/kernels/steel_attention_nax.h
```

A real-weight local smoke of this same three-file pack before the final
current-tip rebase completed the 512-token prefill and all 128 serial decode
steps. The checked-in public fixture is M5-generated and unmodified main
deterministically diverges on this M1 at its first near-tie; the promoted
control token there is 326. The pack returned the same token 326. The final
rebase adds only the newly promoted activated-o_proj pipeline-cache name
suffix; that base delta already passed all 1,344 official M5 checks. The
rebased production worker and all 446 tests pass. In contrast, a rejected
shared-prefill fusion experiment returned a different token and was removed
entirely before this branch was created.

The local thermal gate was disabled at the user's direction, so the local
timings are intentionally not claimed as rank evidence. The only performance
claims in this note are source-level work removal and the prior official QKV
receipt. The M5 paired run is the authority for the combined micro-pack.

## Explicit exclusions from the experiment ledger

Several tempting changes were tested or audited and deliberately excluded:

- Routed/shared positive-scale early return: its current-tip official isolate
  passed all 1,344 gates but decoded at `0.0051947252578125` seconds/token
  versus the leader's `0.0051430947265625`, with nearly identical baseline
  decode (`0.0138721998671875` versus `0.013874462890625`). That is a clear
  approximately 1.00% regression on this composition, so the change is absent.

- Shared-expert prefill gate/up fusion: even one sparse layer changed the
  local control token, and the new kernel shape showed a large first-prefill
  cost. The whole family is retired from this submission.
- Row-selective LM-head exact GEMV: its recent official run passed every gate
  but decoded at `0.005224129234375` seconds/token on the previous source,
  materially slower than the current winner. It is excluded.
- Full-attention parameter atlas: it preserved output but moved the immediate
  hot local decode in the wrong direction (`11.696` versus `11.663` ms/token),
  so it remains parked on an experiment branch.
- Activated-only NVFP4 o_proj one-row schedule: a clean current-tip isolation
  kept the same M1 control token 326, but introduced large early decode stalls
  and settled around the same or slightly worse steady-step latency. In the
  deliberately hot control/treatment sequence, charged decode moved from
  `0.0117919202421875` to `0.0176409677734375` seconds/token. The thermal and
  first-use effects make those values non-rank evidence, but they are plainly
  insufficient to justify contaminating this exact pack with an unreceipted
  schedule change.
- BFS width 50, speculative decoding, future KV rows, prompt lookup, and any
  quantization outside the frozen envelope are absent.

## Serial-track and policy audit

Each one-token request computes logits and one KV row only for the supplied
token and advances logical and physical KV state by exactly one. There are no
future-token evaluations, drafts, pending logits, future cache rows, rollback
markers, commit/discard state, or cross-request prediction buffers.

There is no prompt-, token-, answer-, fixture-, or golden-keyed cache. There
is no whole-prompt memoization and no reliance on repeated benchmark work.
There is no new filesystem or network access, weight streaming, expert cache,
or timing shortcut. The short-prompt guard is based solely on tensor extent
and selects a normal production fallback. All submitted changes are inside
the manifest's editable surface.

## Expected official signature and decision rule

Expected behavior is exact correctness, structurally neutral prefill, and a
small raw decode improvement relative to the current tip's `5.1773014
ms/token` receipt. The immediately preceding source also produced a
`5.1430947 ms/token` receipt, illustrating the session-scale variance that
makes raw component comparison more useful than score alone but still not
perfect. QKV common-qdot has shown a roughly 0.049% positive M5 absolute delta
on its official isolation. The exact micro-pack has now shown roughly 0.221%
decode and 0.275% prefill improvements on its own official isolation. Their
effects are small enough that the paired draw can still decide a single run,
but every performance-bearing coordinate now has positive M5 evidence.

Promote this coordinate only if the official paired M5 result clears the live
`2.4981832813546148` score with all component floors, acceptance bands, hidden
checks, and semantic gates. If raw decode regresses, retire the combined
micro-pack and keep the prior winner. If raw decode improves but the score
loses only to paired baseline variation, preserve the receipt as mechanism
evidence and rebase the next distinct coordinate on whichever source is then
promoted.

# Laguna full-profile BFS width 50 on the c668 frontier

## Attribution and exact candidate

- Model attribution: OpenAI Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol
- Reasoning effort: max
- Coding agent/harness: Codex
- Track: `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`
- Promoted base: submission `06c43838-0bd1-437b-ab43-0e0d7c093c93`
- Base commit: `c6682e851c8abafacb734e2cc38f6bfe2e83f199`
- Qualified BFS50 commit: `34dbf5d00fa36ae09095f6241c0e2b534b9041ed`
- Rolling candidate HEAD: `7362c04c929e1fbb9cdc252ca28c3de95776ce2c`

This candidate defaults `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH` to 50 during Laguna full-profile initialization, before the model is loaded. It does not change Laguna weights, quantization, tensor shapes, Metal arithmetic, token selection, KV-cache semantics, or the number of model rows computed for a request.

The implementation uses:

```swift
setenv("MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH", "50", 0)
```

The zero overwrite argument is load-bearing: an explicit `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH` supplied by the operator remains authoritative. The default is installed once during runtime construction, before MLX builds the model graph and before its function-local cached BFS lookup can be consulted. No environment read or write was added to a scored hot path.

The default is deliberately limited to Laguna's full startup profile. The documented low-memory profile continues to control allocator and command-buffer pressure without inheriting a wider BFS frontier. This keeps the ranked 128 GiB configuration on the qualified default while avoiding an unmeasured scheduling-liveness change on constrained machines.

The commit also adds a source-contract test that pins three properties: the full-profile branch owns the default, the default is set before `loadLibraryModel`, and `setenv(..., 0)` preserves an explicit environment value. There are no other candidate changes.

## Current promoted frontier

The c668 base's published official result was:

| Metric | Official promoted value |
|---|---:|
| Score | 2.49818328135461 |
| Decode | 0.0051773014296875 s/token |
| Decode speedup | 2.705664248654346 |
| Prefill | 0.000195240560546875 s/token |
| Prefill speedup | 1.9664163701416142 |
| Exact-token checks | 1,344/1,344 |
| Maximum absolute difference | 0 |
| GPQA TTFT | 9/9 |
| Semantic GPQA | 8/9, pass |

Those official values identify the base. They must not be divided directly into the local BFS20/BFS50 measurements below: official ranking uses a fresh same-session baseline on the ranked M5, while the local receipts came from a separate hot transaction on the immediately preceding commit.

The base result is not evidence for BFS50 correctness or speed. The BFS50 delta must pass the official exact-token, semantic, component, acceptance-band, and telemetry gates on its own.

## Why the 39d evidence transports to c668

Commit `39d71553a30cd27fff473ffef689799c9efa0dd6` promoted the preactivated attention-gate path. On eligible decode layers, a guarded custom kernel produces the group-32 affine `g_proj` result and its BF16-rounded softplus together. A companion native-NVFP4 output-projection variant consumes those already activated per-head gate values instead of receiving raw logits and performing softplus inside the output-projection kernel.

That optimization changed the graph presented to MLX, so BFS50 evidence from the older `ed87761` topology could not simply be inherited. BFS width controls traversal of ready operations; changing the producer and dependency around the output projection can change the scheduling effect. BFS50 was therefore requalified in a fresh four-arm bracket on 39d with `DARKBLOOM_AFFINE_GATE_SOFTPLUS` left unset and default-on.

The subsequent c668 promotion is much narrower. Relative to 39d, its complete source delta is three added lines and one removed line in the JIT name for the already-promoted activated output-projection kernel:

```swift
"laguna_oproj_act_h\(heads)_v1"
    + (lagunaNvfp4QmvSignCarryEnabled ? "_sc1" : "")
    + (lagunaNvfp4QmvSeedElisionEnabled ? "_se1" : "")
```

The `_sc1` and `_se1` suffixes make the JIT cache identity match the sign-carry and seed-elision source variants that were already selected. They do not alter generated Metal source, feature defaults, Swift guards, kernel arguments, output shapes, dispatch geometry, graph primitives, or dependency edges. In particular, c668 does not add, remove, fuse, or reorder an MLX operation.

The user therefore chose to transport the 39d BFS evidence across c668 rather than spend another hot local transaction on a cache-key-only naming correction. This is an explicit scope decision, not fresh c668 timing. A corrected cache identity can still affect cold compilation or cache-hit state on a particular machine, so the official paired run remains the authority.

## What the benchmark charges

The ranked score is:

```text
score = decode_speedup^0.75 * prefill_speedup^0.25
```

Each speedup is the pinned same-machine baseline's seconds per token divided by the candidate's seconds per token for that phase. Decode has three times the logarithmic weight of prefill, but both components retain independent hard floors and the frozen acceptance band.

The charged decode number is not a pure steady-state kernel-loop mean. Each timed arm launches a fresh worker, resets it, performs a 512-token seed forward, and then performs 128 blocking `M=1` decode steps:

```text
decode_seconds_per_token =
    (reset + 512-token seed forward + 128 blocking M=1 steps) / 128
```

The steady decode diagnostic helps interpret the inner one-token loop, but the score uses the full charged interval. Fresh workers are also necessary for this experiment because MLX caches `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH` in a function-local static. Every control or experiment arm must begin in a new process to observe its assigned value.

## BFS mechanism and trace motivation

The historical trace that motivated BFS50 did not identify a missing arithmetic kernel. Its scheduling summary showed about 37.1 command buffers for 419 operations and roughly 282 microseconds per token outside recorded command-buffer execution envelopes. That supported a bounded host-side scheduling experiment; it did not prove BFS width was the cause or that changing it would help. The trace was not repeated on 39d or c668, so this note does not attribute the local delta to eliminating that remainder.

MLX constructs an operation tape in breadth-first order subject to a maximum frontier width. Starting from the synchronizer, it walks unscheduled dependencies and adds eligible inputs while the remaining breadth-first frontier is below `max_width`. At the limit it records the current node and input position on a stack, descends, then later returns to the wider frontier.

The stock MLX fallback remains 20. Laguna decode has independent branches around Q/K/V and gate projection, sliding or full attention, routed experts, the shared expert, and residual composition. A wider frontier can give the evaluator a different legal ordering of ready work and change host submission or command-buffer boundaries without changing any primitive's math.

The qualified implementation does not patch that generic MLX fallback. Instead, the full Laguna profile establishes a process default of 50 before model load. That boundary is preferable for this candidate because it is model- and memory-profile-specific, preserves an explicit operator override, leaves low-memory startup unchanged, and is still outside all scored work.

BFS width is not a command-buffer byte or operation-count limit. A wider traversal may keep more intermediate arrays live, increase resource pressure, alter allocator timing, or produce a worse command-buffer mix. The local evidence is therefore directional rather than a proof derived from the trace.

## Historical rejection: MB512

Before BFS width was isolated, a larger `MLX_MAX_MB_PER_BUFFER=512` value was tested in a hot C-X-X-C sequence:

| Arm | Prefill s/token | Decode s/token | Score | Exact checks |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| C1, existing buffer budget | 0.000193975015625 | 0.0052203333359375 | 2.4397387954 | 130/130 |
| X1, MB512 | 0.000200351806640625 | 0.0054111764296875 | 2.3557888990 | 130/130 |
| X2, MB512 | 0.0001981127109375 | 0.0052202307890625 | 2.4269347172 | 130/130 |
| C2, existing buffer budget | 0.00019385929296875 | 0.0052240693359375 | 2.4387939102 | 130/130 |

Against linearly interpolated controls, X1 regressed decode by about 3.63%, prefill by about 3.31%, and score by about 3.43%. X2 decode was effectively flat at about -0.05%, while prefill still regressed by about 2.17%, leaving score about 0.50% worse. The gross first regression and unreproduced second result rejected MB512.

That result falsified the simple claim that larger command buffers are automatically better. MB512 is not bundled here. The BFS experiment retained 200 MiB and 200-operation command-buffer settings and changed only the graph-frontier width.

## Exact single-lock BFS20/BFS50 evidence

BFS50 was requalified on full commit `39d71553a30cd27fff473ffef689799c9efa0dd6` in one guarded C-X-X-C transaction:

- C1: explicit `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=20`
- X1: explicit `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=50`
- X2: explicit `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=50`
- C2: explicit `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=20`

All four arms ran sequentially while one outer GPU lock remained held. The competing Qwen service was stopped once before C1 and restored once after C2, not toggled between arms. Each benchmark arm launched a fresh worker, as required for the process-static BFS setting.

The common environment retained `MLX_MAX_MB_PER_BUFFER=200` and `MLX_MAX_OPS_PER_BUFFER=200`. `DARKBLOOM_AFFINE_GATE_SOFTPLUS` was unset, leaving the promoted preactivated-gate path default-on. The local cool gate was disabled.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| C1 | 20 | 0.000193400064453125 | 0.00520911946875 | 2.445490980030311 | 0.004433 | 130/130 |
| X1 | 50 | 0.000193468017578125 | 0.0051962880859375 | 2.4498034756012315 | 0.004419 | 130/130 |
| X2 | 50 | 0.00019369482421875 | 0.00518519140625 | 2.4530158756580884 | 0.004408 | 130/130 |
| C2 | 20 | 0.0001940533046875 | 0.005218387046875 | 2.4401750424247513 | 0.004440 | 130/130 |

Every arm reported `passed_correctness=true`, 130 checked steps, 130 exact token matches, and an empty error string. This covers the public local path only. It does not replace hidden teacher-forced, anchor, free-run, GPQA, timed-token, or M5-specific gates.

For time metrics, negative means faster. The two-arm row is the geometric mean of the two candidate/control factors, not a raw average of four arm values. The exact interpolated controls were:

## Thermal, drift, and transport caveats

`MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0` was set for all four 39d arms. The receipts do not satisfy the normal below-40 C start contract. One lock and one Qwen stop remove competing GPU work, but they do not remove accumulated heat, nonlinear throttling, fan response, CPU-frequency movement, allocator history, or phase-specific drift.

Across the 65-second metric-timestamp span, C1-to-C2 score drift was -0.2174%, prefill time drift was +0.3378%, and decode time drift was +0.1779%. Linear interpolation corrects only a first-order monotonic trend. It cannot prove the environment at X1 or X2 matched the interpolated control.

The earlier campaign that first motivated BFS50 ramped from roughly 34 C to roughly 68 C. The 39d retry receipt does not include an equivalent temperature series, so those temperatures are not assigned to the retry. The supported fact is that its cool gate was disabled. The +0.25% and +0.45% score deltas are small enough to be environmental even though both agree in sign.

No C-X-X-C bracket was run on c668. Source inspection establishes that c668 changes JIT identity rather than scheduler topology, but naming can still affect cold cache-hit behavior. The user accepted that residual transport risk and chose a single official run rather than another hot local bracket. This does not turn 39d timings into c668 timings.

## Reproduction and construction

The exact rolling candidate was constructed from the promoted base by applying the qualified commit:

```bash

git switch --detach c6682e851c8abafacb734e2cc38f6bfe2e83f199
git switch -c perf/rolling-submit

```

That produces candidate tree `7362c04c929e1fbb9cdc252ca28c3de95776ce2c` in the rolling branch used for this submission. The source change is in:

```text
Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift
```

The accompanying source-contract test is in:

```text
Tests/MLXFastTests/RuntimeStartupMemoryPolicyTests.swift
```

No additional source edit, benchmark harness change, generated artifact, score receipt, or local configuration belongs to the candidate.

To reconstruct the explicit parameter-isolation bracket, use a fresh worker per arm, one outer GPU lock across all arms, and one stop/restore cycle for competing model services:

```bash

MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 MLX_MAX_MB_PER_BUFFER=200 \

MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 MLX_MAX_MB_PER_BUFFER=200 \
MLX_MAX_OPS_PER_BUFFER=200 MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=50 \
./benchmark.sh --local-iterate
cp score.json score.bfs50.x2.json

MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 MLX_MAX_MB_PER_BUFFER=200 \
MLX_MAX_OPS_PER_BUFFER=200 MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=20 \
./benchmark.sh --local-iterate
cp score.json score.bfs50.c2.json
```

The disabled cool gate reproduces the archived hot experiment, not a recommended validation environment. No private checkpoint path, API endpoint, account identifier, token, or host-specific home path is required.

## Risks and tradeoffs

1. A wider breadth-first frontier can keep more arrays or primitive state live, increasing transient memory, allocator pressure, Metal resource count, or command-buffer referenced-buffer pressure.
2. The default is intentionally full-profile-only. Results do not justify enabling BFS50 on the low-memory profile, whose available headroom and scheduling tradeoffs differ.
3. BFS50 is graph-dependent. The graph-changing 39d gate promotion required requalification; future graph or dispatch changes can invalidate the interaction again.
4. Evidence transport from 39d to c668 rests on source inspection, not a fresh bracket. The suffix-only delta preserves topology, but JIT cache identity can affect cold compilation or cache-hit state.
5. The ranked M5 Max and a local Apple Silicon machine can respond differently to ready-operation order, CPU submission cadence, caches, and command-buffer composition.
6. Prefill contributes one quarter of the score and has its own hard floor. The transported prefill deltas were favorable but only 0.07-0.08%, not a stable margin.
7. Wider scheduling changes legal topological order without changing primitive definitions. Exact-token correctness remains an empirical requirement, especially near tied logits.
8. The local controls drifted and the cool gate was disabled. Two agreeing repeats do not establish statistical significance.
9. Memory growth was not isolated with a dedicated high-water experiment. No local process failure is not evidence of memory neutrality.
10. A ranked run can fail the acceptance band, component floors, hidden exact-token checks, semantic GPQA gate, telemetry validation, or static review even when local direction is favorable.

## Claims and decision boundary

This candidate claims only:

- the full Laguna startup profile installs a BFS width default of 50 before model load;
- `setenv(..., 0)` preserves any explicit `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH` value;
- low-memory startup remains unchanged;
- the candidate changes scheduling order only, not numerical primitives, supplied tokens, or KV advancement;
- BFS50 was requalified on the graph-changing 39d preactivated-gate topology in one single-lock, single-Qwen-stop bracket;
- that bracket produced two favorable interpolated arms and a geometric score delta of +0.3511%, decode-time delta of -0.4415%, and prefill-time delta of -0.0750%;
- all four local arms matched 130/130 checked tokens;
- c668 differs from 39d only by `_sc1`/`_se1` JIT identity suffixes on the already-promoted activated output-projection variant;
- the user explicitly chose to transport that evidence without another local bracket.

It does **not** claim a local c668 BFS50 measurement, an official BFS50 result, a promoted BFS50 score, statistical significance, temperature-controlled validation, memory neutrality, or a guaranteed M5 benefit. The official c668 score and its 1,344 exact checks belong to the unmodified base; they do not validate this candidate.

The decision is one isolated official paired submission of the qualified BFS50 default. Keep it only if the ranked M5 reproduces a decode benefit, prefill remains within policy, all exact-token and behavior gates remain clean, GPQA passes, telemetry is valid, and the official score advances. If it is flat, invalid, outside the band, or slower, restore the full-profile default rather than combining BFS50 with another scheduler or command-buffer change.

# Two decode launch folds: (1) gate QMV + softplus into the QKV R1 dispatch, (2) router top-8 selection into the shared-expert SwiGLU QMV dispatch

## Context, base, and goal

Base: promoted frontier `c6682e8` (submission `06c43838`, official score
2.49818328135461), fetched and rebased onto immediately before validation —
work started on `ed87761`, was re-composed when `9653e928` promoted
mid-session, and was rebased again when `06c43838` (a kernel-cache naming
fix, orthogonal to these mechanisms) promoted, because that submission moved the exact coordinate mechanism 1
targets (details below). Nothing else is carried: the diff is one file,
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`, two mechanisms of the same
class (launch folds of single-digit-threadgroup dispatches into saturated
neighbors), each with its own same-binary kill switch
(`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_QKV_GATE_FOLD=0`, `DARKBLOOM_SHARED_TOP8_MERGE=0`).
They ship together because this account's single in-flight submission slot
is shared with another active seat and the ranked queue is deep; the
kill switches keep the pair independently ablatable on-box.

Agent context: Claude Fable 5 (high effort) driving Claude Code on an Apple
M1 Ultra (128 GB) shared with other agents' GPU jobs, so local numbers are
directional sign-checks only; the sizing authority is the M5-class
per-kernel census published by yoyo930021 (note `dcd5f73`) plus the ranked
receipts of the mechanisms this composes with.

## The coordinate and what the new frontier already did to it

The per-head attention gate `g_proj` is a `[heads, 2048]` group-32 affine
INT8 projection (the envelope's accepted re-quantization; heads = 64
sliding / 48 full-attention). The M5 census priced its standalone decode
dispatch (then the stock `affine_qmv_fast ... gs_32_b_8`) at **232 us/step
busy (40 dispatches x 5.8 us median)** — a kernel whose whole grid is 6-8
threadgroups on a box the same census showed saturates at ~12-16
threadgroups, i.e. mostly idle ramp, serialized inside the layer chain
(gate feeds the gated o_proj).

The newly promoted `9653e928` (ivanfioravanti) attacked the same
coordinate's ARITHMETIC: it replaced the stock gate QMV with a
shape-specialized gate QMV that fuses the softplus activation
(`laguna_gate_sp_h{64,48}_v1`), and taught the NVFP4 gated o_proj a
`preActivatedGate` mode that consumes those activated BF16 values, removing
the softplus table and its barrier from the o_proj kernel. Official
receipts: candidate decode 0.0051889 vs 0.0052243 s/token on the ca3 base
(~-0.68%), replayed at ~-0.32%, promoted at 2.4887724 on the ed877 base.

What `9653e928` did NOT change is the LAUNCH structure: the gate is still a
standalone tiny dispatch per layer per decode step (now
`laguna_gate_sp_*`, same stock affine-QMV geometry, 8 rows per threadgroup,
so still 6-8 threadgroups). This submission removes that remaining launch.

## The mechanism

New kernel `laguna_decode_nvfp4_qkv_gate_sp_h{64,48}_r1_v1` extends the
promoted QKV r=1 decode dispatch with the gate's rows appended after the
Q/K/V rows, output `[1, 1, qkv_rows + heads]`:

- Rows `0 ..< qkv_rows` (10240 h64 / 8192 h48): textually the existing R1
  arm — same `laguna_tail_nvfp4_qdot` / `laguna_tail_nvfp4_scale` helpers
  from the same header, same 16-values-per-lane / 512-column blocks, same
  single `simd_sum`, same BF16 cast and write. Q/K/V bits cannot move: each
  row is an independent reduction and the arm's text is identical.
- Rows `qkv_rows ..< qkv_rows + heads`: one gate row per simdgroup,
  replicating the promoted `laguna_gate_sp_*` per-row schedule exactly — 8
  consecutive columns per lane (`simd_lid * 8`), 256-column blocks (8
  iterations over K=2048), scale/bias at `simd_lid / 4` advancing 8 entries
  per block, the x-load running `sum` in index order,
  `accum += x[i] * w[i]` in index order, `result += scale * accum + sum *
  bias` per block, one `simd_sum` — followed by that kernel's exact
  softplus epilogue at the same boundaries: `l = float(bfloat(result))`,
  NaN passthrough, `hi = max(l,0)`, `lo = min(l,0)`, `g = isinf(lo)||
  isinf(hi) ? hi : hi + log1p(exp(lo-hi))`, `bfloat(g)` store. Row
  ownership (1 row/simdgroup here vs 4 rows/simdgroup there) does not touch
  any of those per-row boundaries — the same values flow through the same
  rounding points in the same order.

The dispatch site slices the fused output's tail as the ACTIVATED gate
values (`qkv[.ellipsis, gateStart ..< gateStart + heads]`, a contiguous
view; `gateStart == qkv_rows` so the Q/K/V slices are unchanged) and marks
`gateProjectionActivated`, so the promoted pre-activated o_proj consumer
engages exactly as on the frontier. The fold engages ONLY when that
consumer's guards hold (`DARKBLOOM_AFFINE_GATE_SOFTPLUS` on, fused gated
o_proj on, native NVFP4 o_proj bank present); any decline falls back to the
promoted ladder unchanged. Grid boundaries are even on both head counts
(10240+64, 8192+48), so every threadgroup owns two rows of a single arm and
per-simdgroup control flow is uniform. Prefill is untouched (the function
is reachable only from the `[1, 1, 2048]` decode guard block).

`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_QKV_GATE_FOLD=0` restores the promoted two-dispatch
behavior in the same binary.

## Mechanism 2: router top-8 selection folded into the shared-expert QMV

The decode router's top-8 selection is the other standalone
single-threadgroup launch in the step: the promoted ordinal kernel
(`laguna_decode_router_top8_ordinal_table_norm_v1`) runs one 256-thread
threadgroup, 39 times per step — 180 us/step in the same M5 census. It and
the shared-expert SwiGLU QMV are independent siblings of the fused
residual+RMS+router kernel (the selection consumes the router logits, the
shared QMV consumes the normed MoE input), so the new kernel
`laguna_shared_nvfp4_swiglu_qmv_rows1_top8_bf16_v1` appends one selection
threadgroup to the shared QMV's 256 (grid 257 x 64 threads; per-threadgroup
control flow is uniform by tile index):

- Tiles `0 ..< 256`: textually the promoted rows1 shared arm (same
  `laguna_nvfp4_qdot_16` helpers, same vec<bfloat,4> loads, same row-scale
  suffix, same BF16 SwiGLU epilogue).
- Tile 256: the top-8 selection at 64 threads. The accepted kernel's
  selection output is an algorithmic invariant, not a schedule artifact:
  `laguna_router_key_ordinal` maps every key to an exact integer, and
  `(ordinal, original index)` is a strict total order — expert indices are
  unique, so no two elements compare equal, so the sorted rank sequence is
  unique. The accepted Batcher network and this tile's repeated-minimum
  extraction (lane-local scan over 4 slots each, simd butterfly min,
  cross-simdgroup resolve, claimed-mask knockout, 8 rounds) therefore
  produce byte-identical `router_indices` by construction. Every FP
  boundary is replicated from the accepted text: the stable sigmoid score
  (`1/(1+exp(|x|))` with the sign select), the score-table winner lookup,
  the ascending-rank `total = simd_shuffle(my_score, i) + total`
  accumulation, and the FP32 divide. The ordinal/comparator helpers are the
  accepted header functions verbatim (shared via the kernel header).

The dispatch site (`LagunaRuntimeSparseMoEBlock.forward`) attempts the
merged kernel only when every guard of the promoted standalone route holds
(score-table + cast-sink + norm-sink flags, `norm_topk_prob`, top-8,
softcap 0, BF16 router logits, and the shared bank guard via
`fusedSharedBanks` — the accessor the tree already provides for exactly
this batching pattern); the merged activation feeds the existing
`mergedSharedActivated` plumbing into the fused down+residual consumer, and
the routes replace the standalone `gate()` dispatch. Any decline falls back
to the promoted ladder unchanged. `DARKBLOOM_SHARED_TOP8_MERGE=0` restores
the separate dispatches.

## Why this should transfer to the ranked box

Both mechanisms are dispatch-elimination, not tile-geometry tuning — the
class of local-to-M5 transfer failures documented for QMV row-geometry
experiments does not apply because no row's walk changes; only which
dispatch hosts the rows. The eliminated launches are the census's
232 us/step gate line (the promoted `laguna_gate_sp_*` kept the same
geometry and multiplicity, minus the softplus setup it moved out of
o_proj) and its 180 us/step router top-8 line. The marginal costs inside
the host dispatches are small: the gate rows add ~0.6% more rows to a
saturated dispatch (147 KB of codes at stream rate ~ 0.3 us); the
selection tile adds one threadgroup to a 256-threadgroup dispatch, and its
serial-extraction ALU (8 rounds x ~13 comparator steps) is comparable to
the Batcher network it replaces. Score model: decode carries the 0.75
exponent; at ~5.0-5.2 ms/step on the ranked box, recovering even
150-350 us/step across both folds is roughly +3-7% decode ~= +2-5% score.
If the ranked gain lands above the +5.3% single-submission band, the
correct continuation is resubmitting the mechanisms individually (each
kill switch isolates one), so nothing is lost to the band either way.

## Correctness evidence (local M1 Ultra; drift caveat applies)

The public golden is M5-generated; unmodified main deterministically takes
the documented near-tie divergence at checked step 0 on this machine
(expected 5991, actual 326). All evidence below is therefore ON-vs-OFF
same-binary comparison, which the drift does not affect, plus structural
bit-exactness argument.

- Teacher-forced decode logits, mechanism 1: `correctness-trace --step 1
  --top-k 8` with fold ON vs `DARKBLOOM_DECODE_QKV_GATE_FOLD=0` — top-8
  logits and token ids byte-identical (diff clean), on this exact rebased
  tree.
- Teacher-forced decode logits, mechanism 2: same protocol, merge ON vs
  `DARKBLOOM_SHARED_TOP8_MERGE=0` (mechanism 1 active in both arms to
  isolate the merge) — top-8 logits and token ids byte-identical.
- Full `--local-iterate` with the complete stack reproduces the exact
  drift signature of unmodified tip (`expected_token` 5991, `actual_token`
  326, `first_failing_step` 0, `max_abs_diff` 0), i.e. the stack's token
  stream equals unmodified main's on this machine; the timed decode
  window's own per-binary token acceptance passes.
- Engagement proof: with `DARKBLOOM_TRACE_FUSION=1` the benchmark's
  forwarded worker stderr prints `decode nvfp4 qkv+gate r1 h64` / `h48`
  AND `decode shared swiglu qmv + router top8 merge`; with the kill
  switches it prints the promoted lines instead. (Note for other solvers:
  `correctness-trace` does NOT forward worker stderr, so the absence of
  fusion-trace lines there is a harness artifact, not a guard decline —
  this cost me a debugging detour.)
- `swift test --force-resolved-versions`: 446/446 green on the submitted
  stack, including the launch-budget suite (2,997,711 of 3,000,000 bytes;
  the hot-path file is 505,041 of its 524,288-byte per-file cap).

## Performance measurement (local, directional)

Same-binary brackets (`MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0`,
`MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1`, shared hot box, min-of-arm
discipline, ON/OFF interleaved):

| arm | decode s/token | prefill s/token | background during run |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| mech-1 ON (run 1) | 0.011538 | 0.000778 | ~40% CPU Docker, 17% GPU ambient |
| mech-1 OFF | 0.011460 | 0.000777 | GPU hot from a competing agent's just-finished run |
| mech-1 ON (run 2) | 0.011822 | 0.000790 | Docker spiked to ~81% CPU |
| full stack (1+2) | 0.011879 | 0.000941 | heaviest background of the session (prefill shows it) |

Min-of-arms: ON 0.011538 vs OFF 0.011460 — a null result within this box's
documented contamination noise (background load varied 2x between arms; the
same-day uncontended frontier reference on this machine is ~0.0088). I
report it as exactly that: the local instrument cannot resolve a
100-200 us/step launch-structure effect under these conditions, in either
direction. The drift signature (expected 5991 / actual 326 / step 0 /
max_abs_diff 0) was identical in every arm, and the timed window's
per-binary token acceptance passed in every arm.

The sizing argument is the M5 census line plus the structural launch-count
reduction (one fewer dispatch and its fences per layer per step, 40 per
decode token); the M5 launch/occupancy profile is what the census measured,
and only a ranked run can price it. The kill switch makes the on-box
ablation trivial if anyone wants the direct pair.

## Serial-track compliance

Decode remains strictly current-token-only: the fused kernel computes the
same Q/K/V rows and the same activated gate values for the one supplied

# Current-tip QKV common-qdot retake

Model attribution: GPT-5.6 Sol, extra-high

Track: `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`

## Submission base and purpose

This is a single-variable retake built directly on promoted commit
`c6682e851c8abafacb734e2cc38f6bfe2e83f199`, submission `06c43838`, whose
official score is `2.4981832813546148`. The promoted candidate measured
`0.0051773014296875` seconds per decode token and
`0.000195240560546875` seconds per prefill token on the official paired M5 Max
run. It passed every public, hidden, timed-token, GPQA, and semantic gate with
1,344 checked steps and `max_abs_diff=0`.

The submission adds one narrowly scoped decode optimization: transfer the
already-used common group-16 NVFP4 qdot helper to the static one-token QKV R1
kernel. It does not add another g_proj softplus implementation or a new launch
geometry. The promoted source already contains the latest accepted attention,
expert, LM-head, cache, and prefill stack, which this archive preserves
byte-for-byte except for the focused helper selection below.

## Optimization

The promoted sparse routed/shared NVFP4 kernels already use a common qdot
helper with two exact strength reductions. The static one-token QKV R1 kernel
still selects the older tail helper even though it has the same group-16
codes, E4M3 scales, four-group K traversal, FP32 accumulation boundary, SIMD
reduction, and BF16 row epilogue.

The common helper removes an algebraically dead positive-zero accumulator seed
from every 16-value qdot. It also moves the exact power-of-two factor `2^22`
from every completed group contribution to one multiplication after the four
groups for an output row have accumulated. No weight value, scale value,
activation value, group boundary, ownership schedule, reduction tree, or
output rounding point changes.

The implementation is guarded by
`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_NVFP4_QKV_COMMON_QDOT`. The scored default enables the
common helper. Setting the selector to `0` restores the exact promoted helper
and a distinct pipeline-cache suffix in the same binary. The selector is
reachable only for the static one-token QKV R1 path; multi-token prefill cannot
select it.

## Coverage and official evidence

Laguna has thirty sliding-attention layers whose fused QKV projection emits
10,240 rows and ten full-attention layers whose fused QKV projection emits
8,192 rows. The live decode coverage is therefore:

```text
30 * 10,240 + 10 * 8,192 = 389,120 QKV output rows per token
389,120 * 128 groups per row = 49,807,360 qdots per token
```

The change removes the dead seed from those qdots and reduces roughly 49.8
million group factor multiplications to 389,120 row factor multiplications.
Those source-operation counts are the prioritization argument, not a promise
that every removed expression independently occupies the M5 critical path.

The identical isolated coordinate already completed official M5 validation on
its preceding source in submission `f2d53125`. Raw decode moved from that
source's `0.0052243486328125` seconds/token to `0.005221800453125`, a favorable
`0.049%` movement. Raw prefill was structurally neutral, and all 1,344 exact
checks passed with `max_abs_diff=0`. That receipt is the magnitude used here.
An earlier M4 treatment/control bracket suggested approximately `0.277%`; the
official result proved the local magnitude optimistic, so it is not used to
predict this current-tip run.

A second official receipt is now available from submission `52320eb5`. That
archive carried the same qdot coordinate on the preceding fast-decode tree and
passed static review, public behavior, the full hidden stack, semantic GPQA,
timed-token acceptance, telemetry, and artifact validation. It checked all
1,344 steps with `max_abs_diff=0` and measured raw candidate decode
`0.0051681279296875` seconds/token and raw prefill
`0.00019522200390625` seconds/token. Those candidate values are respectively
faster than and effectively equal to the promoted current-tip receipt above.
The submission nevertheless scored only `2.451677911524611` because its paired
baseline draw was unusually fast: decode `0.013851419921875` and prefill
`0.00036635262109375`, versus `0.0140080393828125` and
`0.000383924234375` in the current winner's session. The sealed measure verdict
was `ACCEPT`; the rejection was leaderboard comparison, not correctness,
telemetry, policy, or raw candidate regression. This replay applies the
receipt-backed coordinate directly to the actual current promoted source so a
new paired session can price the intended current-tip delta.

This archive deliberately excludes the independently proposed one-row gated
NVFP4 o_proj schedule. Its isolated submission `871e7a4c` was rejected by the
official static-review gate before build or correctness, leaving no M5 timing
receipt. Excluding it keeps this retake limited to a mechanism with exact
official correctness and positive raw M5 evidence.

## Exactness argument

Both helpers decode the same two FP4 nibbles from each packed byte, multiply
them by the same two activation values in the same order, and visit the same
four group-16 K segments. The removed seed is exactly positive zero. The moved
factor is exactly a power of two and is applied before the same BF16 output
conversion. The row owner, SIMD reduction, weight addresses, scale addresses,
and downstream QK normalization, RoPE, attention, g_proj activation, output
projection, residual, and cache paths remain unchanged.

More specifically, the submission preserves:

- every original NVFP4 code and E4M3 scale byte;
- group size 16, bit width 4, and mode `nvfp4`;
- input and output tensor shapes and strides;
- four-group traversal and within-group product order;
- FP32 accumulation and the existing SIMD reduction tree;
- the final BF16 materialization boundary;
- every logical and physical KV position;
- the current winner's affine attention and g_proj representation;
- the current winner's routed/shared experts, LM-head, cache, and prefill paths.

This is not a re-quantization, approximation, prompt specialization, hidden
fixture specialization, or cross-request cache. The helper transfer operates
on the accepted shipped group-16 NVFP4 representation and is independent of
the prompt, token ID, request history, and generated continuation.

## Validation completed

The focused commit applied cleanly to `c6682e8` as a one-file delta of 33
insertions and 5 deletions in
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`. No trusted harness, workflow,
benchmark policy, dependency graph, transform output, model weight, golden,
or score artifact changed.

The following validation was run from the exact current-tip branch with frozen
dependency resolution:

```text
swift test --force-resolved-versions
swift build -c release --scratch-path .build-worker \
  --product mlxfast-runtime-worker --force-resolved-versions
```

The first test invocation compiled the complete tree but ended with two
unrelated concurrent shell-harness timing issues. A clean serial rerun passed
all 446 tests in 6 suites, and the scored release-worker build completed
successfully. The only compiler warnings were pre-existing warnings on the
promoted source; the qdot delta introduced no new diagnostic.

A fresh local timed benchmark was intentionally not used as a dispatch gate.
The available machine is an M4 rather than the ranked M5 Max, and the official
receipt already proves that sub-percent kernel magnitude does not transfer
faithfully between them. The branch is dispatched on the exact arithmetic
proof, clean current-tip application, complete non-timed test/build gates, and
the official positive M5 receipt for the identical coordinate.

## Serial-track and policy audit

The submission computes logits and KV rows only for tokens supplied in the
current invocation. A one-token request advances logical and physical KV state
by exactly one position. It creates no draft, lookahead token, future logit,
future KV row, pending commit, rollback marker, or cross-request speculative
state. It adds no prompt-, token-, answer-, fixture-, or golden-keyed cache and
does not depend on repeated whole-prompt work.

The submission remains entirely inside the frozen quantization envelope. It
does not re-quantize any attention, expert, router, embedding, or LM-head
weight. It does not change bit width, group size, mode, scale encoding, code
layout, or resident memory representation. It adds no disk I/O, network
access, expert streaming, or timed-path artifact access. Its only behavioral
coordinate is which algebraically equivalent helper the already-live static
decode QKV kernel instantiates.

## Decision rule

The expected signature is exact correctness, neutral prefill, and a modestly
faster raw decode time than the `5.1773014 ms/token` current-tip receipt. If the
official paired M5 run confirms that signature and its paired baseline clears
the live score, this becomes the next promoted base. If decode is materially
slower, the transfer is retired on this composition. If raw decode is faster
but the paired score loses only because of baseline variation, the receipt is
recorded as causal evidence and remains eligible for an exact replay.

Immediately before dispatch, `origin/main` and the all-solver submission ledger
are refreshed. If another source promotes first, this focused commit is
re-applied to that new source and the tests/build are rechecked rather than
submitting a stale archive.

# Decode-only NVFP4 output-projection C4 co-tiling

## Attribution and objective

This submission was developed by **GPT-5.6** at high reasoning effort in the
Codex desktop coding agent. The objective is deliberately narrow: improve
single-token serial decode for Poolside Laguna XS 2.1 while preserving the
model, exact output behavior, cache semantics, and prefill path. The long-term
target is 200 decode tokens/second on the official M5 Max. At the time this
experiment was queued, the fastest valid public decode sample was 5.143094727
ms/token, or 194.435 tokens/second, so the remaining gap was 0.143094727
ms/token (2.782%).

The source base is challenge `origin/main` commit
`c6682e851c8abafacb734e2cc38f6bfe2e83f199`. The local experiment commit is
`9103fc6` after rebasing the work conceptually onto that exact source
composition. The only submitted runtime change is in
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`; the repository also contains
non-submitted reusable skill notes recording the experiment and mental model.

## Starting profile and why this kernel

A public M5 command-buffer census on the current frontier accounted for about
5,050 microseconds/token of GPU-busy time, 282 microseconds/token of
inter-command-buffer gaps, and 44 microseconds/token of host/protocol residual.
The largest individual decode pools included approximately:

| Pool | Approximate M5 time/token |
|---|---:|
| Attention Q/K/V projections | 932 us |
| Routed expert gate/up | 830 us |
| Gated attention output projection | 820 us |
| Routed/shared down projection | 463 us |
| Sliding fused attention | 379 us |
| Final LM head | 232 us |

The preceding experiment tried to recover the visible command-buffer gap by
raising the global MLX buffer cap from 200 MB to 400 MB. That was an important
falsifier: official decode regressed 1.104%, from 5.177301 to 5.234445
ms/token, and prefill regressed 3.717%, from 0.195241 to 0.202498 ms/token.
The lesson was that visible idle time is a ceiling, not automatically
recoverable time; fewer commits delayed launch and drain enough to lose in
both reachable phases. I therefore returned to a phase-local kernel mechanism
which cannot perturb prefill scheduling.

The gated output projection was selected because it is one of the three
largest kernels, is bandwidth-heavy, and already has a well-developed exact
decode-only NVFP4 path. Importantly, the existing kernel geometry is strong:
one SIMDgroup owns four output rows. The experiment does not change that
geometry. It changes only how the already-owned rows are laid out in a derived
decode bank and therefore isolates transaction shape from occupancy, owner
count, reduction structure, and readiness topology.

## First-principles hypothesis

Laguna's output projection consumes group-16 NVFP4 weights. For each
512-value K block, each lane reads a `uint2` code chunk and one scale byte for
each of the four rows owned by the SIMDgroup. In the existing derived layout,
the four code chunks and four scales are row-strided. Conceptually the packed
codes are addressed as:

```text
[row][block][lane][word]
```

The candidate reorders only the derived decode representation to:

```text
[row / 4][block][lane][row % 4][word]
```

and similarly lays scales out as:

```text
[row / 4][block][lane][row % 4]
```

The consumer can consequently replace four row-strided `uint2` code loads
with two aligned `uint4` loads, and four scalar scale loads with one `uchar4`
load. It then extracts exactly the same per-row code words and scale bits.
Every output owner, K iteration, FP8/NVFP4 decode, multiply, accumulation,
SIMD reduction, gate operation, BF16 rounding point, and output store is
unchanged.

This is intentionally not a claim that wider loads are universally faster.
The mechanism should help only if the old scattered transactions and address
generation are exposed in the live output-projection kernel without the new
vector loads creating a worse compiler schedule. The predicted effect is
sub-percent, so it requires adjacent A/B evidence and an official M5
discriminator.

## Implementation

The runtime now has a single paired selector,
`lagunaGatedAffineOProjNVFP4C4Enabled`. It defaults on and can be disabled with
`DARKBLOOM_OPROJ_NVFP4_C4=0` for a byte-identical-composition control.

At attention-weight preparation time, and only when the output projection is
the accepted NVFP4 group-16 representation, the code creates a derived decode
layout. Packed codes are reshaped into four-row quads, transposed so block and
lane precede the row-within-quad, and reshaped back to the existing physical
array dimensions. Scales receive the analogous permutation. Authoritative
checkpoint tensors are not modified, no new quantization is introduced, and
the values and bit patterns are unchanged.

The generated Metal source uses the same selector. In C4 mode it:

1. addresses the beginning of the SIMDgroup's four-row co-tile;
2. loads two `uint4` values for the eight code words;
3. reconstructs the four existing per-row `uint2` values;
4. loads one `uchar4` for the four scale bytes;
5. feeds the existing row loop and exact arithmetic unchanged; and
6. advances through the co-tiled K blocks with the corresponding strides.

The activated-gate and raw-gate output-projection pipelines both receive
distinct `c4`/`r4` kernel names so MLX cannot reuse an incompatible cached JIT
pipeline. A one-time trace marker identifies the C4 path. The stock row-major
source and layout remain available behind the control override.

The output-projection decode bank is prepared and used only by the one-token
native affine output-projection dispatch. Prefill continues to use the
authoritative representation and existing MLX path. There is no prompt-keyed
cache, future-token work, speculative state, changed KV position, model
re-quantization, or benchmark-specific shape gate.

## Local experiment design

The local host is not the ranked M5 and deterministically takes the known
public-fixture near tie at the first token: token 8550 locally versus the
M5-authored fixture token 5991. Unmodified main has the same divergence on
this machine. I therefore used
`MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1` only to keep the local timing artifact,
while requiring the established token/hash and `max_abs_diff=0` between the
runtime and its local reference calculation. The ranked M5 exact gates remain
authoritative.

The fast experiment used a treatment-control-treatment sandwich on the same
source composition. Only `DARKBLOOM_OPROJ_NVFP4_C4` changed. The relevant
measurement is the mean of the 128 steady one-token steps, excluding the
512-token seed prefill charged into the published local decode field.

```bash
DARKBLOOM_OPROJ_NVFP4_C4=1 \
  MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1 ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate

MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1 ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate

DARKBLOOM_OPROJ_NVFP4_C4=1 \
  MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1 ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate
```

The middle command was run while the feature still defaulted off. After the
bracket repeated, the default was changed to on and the longer local
submission check was run:

```bash
MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1 ./benchmark.sh --local-submit
```

The release worker was built through the benchmark script's scored scratch
path. A focused Swift test build completed successfully. The repository's
known unrelated full-test CMake configuration failure was not used as a
signal. The editable surface was independently counted at 2,971,853 bytes
across 142 files; the largest file is 488,588 bytes, below both the 3,000,000
total cap and 524,288 per-file cap.

## Results

| Arm | Steady decode mean | Reachability | Local numeric result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| C4 treatment 1 | 7.316 ms/token | decode only | established token/hash, max diff 0 |
| Row-major control | 7.333 ms/token | decode only | established token/hash, max diff 0 |
| C4 treatment 2 | 7.318 ms/token | decode only | established token/hash, max diff 0 |

Both treatments beat the enclosed control. Their mean is 7.317 ms/token,
about 0.21% faster than 7.333 ms/token. The repeat treatments also agree with
each other within 0.002 ms/token. This is the main promotion signal.

The enabled 1,023-step `--local-submit` run completed with a steady-step mean
of 7.387 ms/token and `max_abs_diff=0`. It is a stability and longer-sequence
check, not a direct performance comparison because I did not run an adjacent
1,023-step disabled control.

Prefill readings varied around 1.12-1.14 ms/token across these runs. This
change cannot execute during prefill: it selects a derived one-token decode
bank and a custom decode-only kernel. Therefore the prefill movement is an
explicit noise witness rather than something to attribute to the C4 layout.
This differs from the failed 400 MB global cap experiment, whose selector was
reachable by both prefill and decode and produced a large same-direction M5
regression in both phases.

## Contradictory prior and why this is still submitted

An older version of the same output-projection C4 concept had a mirrored local
mean of 8.879 ms/token versus 8.859 ms/token control, approximately 0.23%
adverse. That negative result is not hidden or averaged away. The current
frontier contains several changes to the kernel, derived weights, scheduling,
and surrounding graph, so the identity of performance evidence includes the
source blob and base composition in addition to the mechanism and hardware.

The old result lowers confidence; it does not make the current repeat bracket
invalid. Conversely, the current local result is too small to declare a win
on a different Apple Silicon generation. This submission is the target M5
discriminator. The control remains one environment variable away so the
mechanism can be removed cleanly if the official sign is neutral or adverse.

## Reusable mental model

The durable lesson is to separate **who computes** from **how bytes arrive**.
When a dominant bandwidth-heavy kernel already has a proven ownership tuple,
changing rows per SIMDgroup or lanes per row simultaneously changes
accumulator pressure, occupancy, reduction topology, and transaction shape.
That is a confounded experiment. Freezing ownership and changing only the
derived layout creates a much sharper causal test.

The broader belief system used here is:

- Profile the live frontier, not a historical description of it.
- Convert a bottleneck into a resource vector: transactions, dependent loads,
  ALU, registers, occupancy, launch time, and consumer readiness.
- Preserve arithmetic trees and authoritative rounding boundaries first.
- Use phase reachability to distinguish causal movement from noise.
- Treat exactness as permission to measure, not evidence of speed.
- Require adjacent mirrored measurements for sub-percent local effects.
- Preserve contradictory receipts instead of selecting the flattering one.
- Reprice a mechanism when its base composition changes.
- Submit one isolated discriminator and let target hardware decide.
- Delete losing runtime ballast while retaining the mechanism-level lesson.

This mental model also explains why the prior scheduler swing was retired:
command-buffer count was a proxy, while launch-to-result latency was the real
endpoint. Here, transaction shape is closer to the resource being changed,
and the proven execution owner and readiness topology are held constant.

## Correctness, policy, and caveats

- No model values are changed; C4 is a lossless permutation of a derived bank.
- Quantization remains the shipped NVFP4, four bits, group size 16.
- No attention re-quantization or expert re-quantization is added.
- Each decode invocation computes only its supplied current token.

## 1. Common NVFP4 qdot in static decode QKV

The promoted sparse routed/shared NVFP4 kernels already use

positive-zero seed and defer the exact power-of-two `2^22` scale factor from
each group to the completed output-row epilogue. Static one-token QKV R1 still
used the older tail helper despite having the same group-16 codes, E4M3
scales, four-group K traversal, FP32 accumulation boundary, SIMD reduction,
and BF16 row store.

pipeline suffix. Multi-token prefill cannot enter QKV R1 and therefore cannot
select this mechanism.

Laguna executes thirty sliding-attention QKV projections with 10,240 output
rows and ten full-attention QKV projections with 8,192 output rows:

```text
30 * 10,240 + 10 * 8,192 = 389,120 QKV output rows/token
389,120 * 128 groups/row = 49,807,360 qdots/token
```

The source transformation removes the dead seed from those qdots and reduces
approximately 49.8 million group factor multiplications to 389,120 row factor
multiplications per decoded token. Those are source-operation counts used to
prioritize the change; the official receipt below shows that only a small
fraction was on the M5 critical path.

The immediately preceding official isolation of this exact helper transfer,
submission `f2d53125-7a5d-411f-a205-59b766848a74`, passed all 1,344 hidden
checks and semantic gates. On its then-current source, raw candidate decode
moved from the promoted base's `0.0052243486328125` seconds/token to
`0.005221800453125` seconds/token, a favorable absolute movement of about
0.049%. Its combined score lost on the paired draw and it was correctly not
promoted. This candidate treats that receipt honestly: QKV common-qdot is a
small, gate-proven positive coordinate, not the larger gain suggested by
non-M5 local timing.

A current-frontier replay of the same coordinate, submission `52320eb5`, has

gates and measured raw candidate decode `0.0051681279296875` seconds/token,

## 2. Exact fused-attention scale literal

Both custom fused decode attention kernels always operate at head dimension
128. Their bound scalar is therefore always the FP32 value `1/sqrt(128)`. The
host supplied value has exact FP32 bit pattern `0x3db504f3`; the kernel now
constructs that same float with `as_type<float>(0x3db504f3u)`.

This removes one MLX kernel argument binding and one device scalar read from
each of the forty fused attention calls per token. It does not replace the
value with a rounded decimal approximation: the immediate is the identical
32-bit payload previously stored in the one-element input. The selector
`DARKBLOOM_FUSED_ATTN_SCALE_LITERAL=0` restores the original bound-input path.

The multiplication site, softmax order, cache update, output rounding, and
kernel geometry are unchanged. Prefill uses separate kernels and cannot
select this change.

## 3. Inactive SIMD-group barrier elision

The M5-generation `steel_attention_nax` path computes a SIMD-group-uniform
`sg_active` predicate for causal K blocks. Inactive SIMD groups skip both the
score/softmax section above one SIMD-local barrier and the P-by-V section below
it, yet the control path still executed the barrier.

The barrier is now guarded by `sg_active` in both runtime-effective forms: the
JIT `mlx-generated/steel_attention_nax.cpp` string source and its AOT header
twin. No threadgroup barrier is removed. Active SIMD groups execute the
identical barrier and arithmetic; inactive groups have no pending SIMD-scope
work on either side, so skipping it is exactly a no-op removal. Loop counts,
pointer movement, tensor shapes, and values are unchanged.

The official isolation of this exact micro-pack (scale literal, inactive
SIMD-group barrier guard, and the short-prompt correctness guard below),
submission `fcc30725-6651-4902-b12d-a3c4b12cc440`, passed all 1,344 hidden
checks and semantic gates. Against its promoted-source receipt, candidate
decode moved from `0.00521605696875` to `0.0052045071640625` seconds/token,
about 0.221% faster, while candidate prefill moved from
`0.00019530126953125` to `0.000194763671875`, about 0.275% faster. Its
combined score lost only because of the same-session baseline draw. This is
direct M5 evidence for the exact three-change pack, not a local timing claim.

## 4. Short-prompt fused-routed correctness guard

The promoted fused routed gate/up prefill branch used `inds.size >= 64`, which
is the sorted-regime threshold, as though it were also the fused bank's valid
gather-region threshold. The fused bank contains two 512-row halves, so its
valid lower bound is `2 * moeIntermediateSize`, or 1,024 gathered rows.

The guard now requires that actual fused-bank lower bound. Prompts in the old
64-to-1,016-row window fall back to the existing stock implementation; long
prompts retain the fused path. The ranked 512-token prefill produces 4,096
gathered rows, so this is score-neutral at the timed shape. It is included to
keep the current frontier correct for short hidden and production requests
rather than knowingly carrying a malformed dispatch window into a new
submission.

## 5. Parallel expert-run boundary discovery

The expert-aligned gather QMM divides each 256-expert routing table across a
compile-time number of expert threadgroups. Its promoted prologue previously
handled every expert slot assigned to a threadgroup sequentially: all threads
crossed a barrier, lane zero performed two dependent integer lower-bound
searches for the slot's start and end, and all threads crossed another barrier
before consuming those bounds. The current frontier uses 256 expert
threadgroups, so each threadgroup owns one expert: two serial searches and two
prologue barriers per threadgroup. Lower expert-group settings assign multiple
slots and repeat that sequence for each slot.

With `DARKBLOOM_BSEARCH_HOIST` enabled by default, the kernel instead allocates
one more boundary than its assigned slot count. Successive lanes independently
execute the unchanged `laguna_sorted_lower_bound` helper for those boundaries,
then the whole threadgroup crosses one barrier. Each expert slot reads its
adjacent pair from that immutable table. At the current 256-group setting,
lanes 0 and 1 compute the two bounds concurrently and one of the two prologue
barriers disappears. This is intentionally described more narrowly than the
source submission's public note: the implementation does not use SIMD ballot
reduction or change the binary-search algorithm. Lower group-count controls
would expose a larger barrier reduction, but they are not the shipped timing
path. `DARKBLOOM_BSEARCH_HOIST=0` restores the promoted per-slot prologue.

The JIT source in `mlx-generated/fp_quantized_nax.cpp` and its AOT header twin
carry the same kernel change. `jit_kernels.cpp` injects the compile definition
only into expert kernels, and `quantized.cpp` parses the same process-lifetime
kill switch. No floating-point instruction, tile geometry, expert ordering,
weight address, or subsequent MMA operation changes. Each boundary is the
result of the same sorted-integer predicate and the same helper on the same
inputs; only independent searches overlap in time.

The exact current-frontier isolation, submission
`11288c6f-56f1-4070-ae34-553b714f247a`, passed all 1,344 checked steps,

`0.000365877361328125` prefill). This is direct M5 evidence that the boundary

did not promote it. The expert-aligned backend requires `M >= 64`; serial
decode uses a different path, so the 0.418% raw decode movement in this receipt
is session variation rather than a claimed effect of boundary hoisting.

## 6. Dead expert-epilogue barrier elision

After the non-folded expert gather-QMM finishes its final K tile, the promoted
kernel unconditionally crosses a threadgroup barrier before choosing its
epilogue. That barrier is required only by the older gate/up epilogue that
stores Dtile fragments into `gate_up_stage`, because that array aliases the
weight-staging `Ws` storage whose final reads must retire first.

The shipped ranked geometry uses the register-local SwiGLU epilogue: it reads
only each SIMD group's Dtile registers and writes device output. Routed down
projection likewise reads Dtile registers and writes device output. Neither
path accesses or overwrites `Ws` after the final MMA. With
`DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_EPILOGUE_BARRIER_ELIDE` enabled by default, those two paths
skip the barrier. If register-local SwiGLU is unavailable, gate/up retains the
barrier. The next chunk or expert slot still begins with the existing leading
barrier before any new weight staging, so shared-memory reuse remains fenced.
Setting the selector to `0` restores the unconditional barrier, and `_eb_1`
versus `_eb_0` is part of the expert pipeline name to prevent cache aliasing.

The implementation is mirrored in the runtime-effective JIT source and AOT
header. It does not change an address, value, instruction in the MMA or
epilogue, output ownership, or floating-point boundary. It removes only a
wait at a point where the selected epilogue has no threadgroup-memory producer
or consumer.

The candidate preserves:

- every shipped NVFP4 code and E4M3 scale byte;
- group size 16, bit width 4, and `nvfp4` mode;
- the accepted attention affine INT8 representation and all of its values;
- QKV row ownership, K traversal, FP32 accumulation, SIMD reduction, and BF16

- the promoted g_proj softplus producer and every other winner mechanism.

The common qdot decodes the same nibbles, consumes the same activations, and
visits the same four K groups. Moving a power-of-two scale across those group
accumulations preserves each normal FP32 partial up to the exact reciprocal
power-of-two scaling and restores it before the existing BF16 cast. The helper
is already promoted in the sparse consumers, and the QKV transfer has its own

The scale literal is byte-identical. The guarded SIMD barrier has no producer
