latest accepted attention, expert, LM-head, cache, and prefill stack, which
this archive preserves byte-for-byte except for those two focused selectors.

## Optimization

The promoted sparse routed/shared NVFP4 kernels already use a common qdot
helper with two exact strength reductions. The static one-token QKV R1 kernel
still selects the older tail helper even though it has the same group-16
codes, E4M3 scales, four-group K traversal, FP32 accumulation boundary, SIMD
reduction, and BF16 row epilogue.

The common helper removes an algebraically dead positive-zero accumulator seed
from every 16-value qdot. It also moves the exact power-of-two factor `2^22`
from every completed group contribution to one multiplication after the four
groups for an output row have accumulated. No weight value, scale value,
activation value, group boundary, ownership schedule, reduction tree, or
output rounding point changes.

The implementation is guarded by
`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_NVFP4_QKV_COMMON_QDOT`. The scored default enables the
common helper. Setting the selector to `0` restores the exact promoted helper
and a distinct pipeline-cache suffix in the same binary. The selector is
reachable only for the static one-token QKV R1 path; multi-token prefill cannot
select it.

## BFS50 scheduler composition

The second coordinate installs `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=50` with `setenv(..., 0)`
inside the full startup-memory profile before the model is loaded. The zero
overwrite argument is load-bearing: an explicit operator-supplied value remains
authoritative. The documented low-memory profile is unchanged. No environment
lookup or mutation occurs in a scored forward; MLX reads and caches the width
while constructing its evaluator state.

BFS width changes only which ready MLX operations are visited first while
respecting the same dependency graph. It does not change any primitive,
weight, tensor shape, reduction tree, supplied token, KV position, or output
materialization boundary. Official isolated current-tip submission `776a79e1`
passed static review, all public and hidden correctness gates, semantic GPQA,
timed-token acceptance, telemetry, and artifact validation with every checked
token exact and `max_abs_diff=0`. Its raw candidate measurement was
`0.005169479171875` seconds/token decode and
`0.00019564225390625` seconds/token prefill. Decode was faster than both the
promoted crown receipt (`0.0051773014296875`) and the first qdot replay
(`0.0051861627578125`); published score `2.4710555768597446` lost because its
paired baseline draw was faster, not because the candidate failed a gate.

The composition is deliberately limited to these two official-clean
coordinates. The qdot helper changes arithmetic strength reduction inside the
static QKV row owner; BFS50 changes host traversal of ready graph operations.
They do not touch the same selector, source generator, tensor, or preparation
state. Both remain independently ablatable in one binary through
`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_NVFP4_QKV_COMMON_QDOT=0` and an explicit
`MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=20` respectively.

## Coverage and official evidence

Laguna has thirty sliding-attention layers whose fused QKV projection emits
10,240 rows and ten full-attention layers whose fused QKV projection emits
8,192 rows. The live decode coverage is therefore:

```text
30 * 10,240 + 10 * 8,192 = 389,120 QKV output rows per token
389,120 * 128 groups per row = 49,807,360 qdots per token
```

The change removes the dead seed from those qdots and reduces roughly 49.8
million group factor multiplications to 389,120 row factor multiplications.
Those source-operation counts are the prioritization argument, not a promise
that every removed expression independently occupies the M5 critical path.

The identical isolated coordinate already completed official M5 validation on
its preceding source in submission `f2d53125`. Raw decode moved from that
source's `0.0052243486328125` seconds/token to `0.005221800453125`, a favorable
`0.049%` movement. Raw prefill was structurally neutral, and all 1,344 exact
checks passed with `max_abs_diff=0`. That receipt is the magnitude used here.
An earlier M4 treatment/control bracket suggested approximately `0.277%`; the
official result proved the local magnitude optimistic, so it is not used to
predict this current-tip run.

A second official receipt is now available from submission `52320eb5`. That
archive carried the same qdot coordinate on the preceding fast-decode tree and
passed static review, public behavior, the full hidden stack, semantic GPQA,
timed-token acceptance, telemetry, and artifact validation. It checked all
1,344 steps with `max_abs_diff=0` and measured raw candidate decode
`0.0051681279296875` seconds/token and raw prefill
`0.00019522200390625` seconds/token. Those candidate values are respectively
faster than and effectively equal to the promoted current-tip receipt above.
The submission nevertheless scored only `2.451677911524611` because its paired
baseline draw was unusually fast: decode `0.013851419921875` and prefill
`0.00036635262109375`, versus `0.0140080393828125` and
`0.000383924234375` in the current winner's session. The sealed measure verdict
was `ACCEPT`; the rejection was leaderboard comparison, not correctness,
telemetry, policy, or raw candidate regression. This replay applies the
receipt-backed coordinate directly to the actual current promoted source so a
new paired session can price the intended current-tip delta.

The first current-tip replay, submission `ab7d5c8f`, has also completed. It
again passed static review, public behavior, the full hidden stack, semantic
GPQA, timed-token acceptance, telemetry, and artifact validation, with all
1,344 checked steps exact and `max_abs_diff=0`. Its raw candidate measurement
was `0.0051861627578125` seconds/token decode and
`0.000194977375` seconds/token prefill. Relative to the promoted receipt, that
single draw was about `0.17%` slower in decode and `0.13%` faster in prefill,
which is the expected shape of a sub-tenth-percent mechanism inside the ranked
box's run-to-run variance rather than evidence of a correctness or policy
failure. The paired decode baseline was again materially faster than the
winner's session (`0.0138568681640625` versus `0.0140080393828125`), producing
score `2.476296720935288` despite a clean `ACCEPT` measurement verdict. With
main still unchanged at `c6682e8`, this note records that mixed current-tip
draw and makes the successor decision explicit: the qdot coordinate remains
unchanged and officially gate-proven, while the only added mechanism is the
separately official-clean BFS50 scheduler whose raw M5 decode measurement was
positive on this exact promoted topology.

This archive deliberately excludes the independently proposed one-row gated
NVFP4 o_proj schedule. Its isolated submission `871e7a4c` was rejected by the
official static-review gate before build or correctness, leaving no M5 timing
receipt. A later isolated replay, `bfc01a41`, passed all correctness gates but
regressed raw decode to `0.00521581640625` seconds/token. Excluding it keeps
this successor limited to mechanisms with exact official correctness and
positive raw M5 evidence on the current topology.

## Exactness argument

Both helpers decode the same two FP4 nibbles from each packed byte, multiply
them by the same two activation values in the same order, and visit the same
four group-16 K segments. The removed seed is exactly positive zero. The moved
factor is exactly a power of two and is applied before the same BF16 output
conversion. The row owner, SIMD reduction, weight addresses, scale addresses,
and downstream QK normalization, RoPE, attention, g_proj activation, output
projection, residual, and cache paths remain unchanged.

More specifically, the submission preserves:

- every original NVFP4 code and E4M3 scale byte;
- group size 16, bit width 4, and mode `nvfp4`;
- input and output tensor shapes and strides;
- four-group traversal and within-group product order;
- FP32 accumulation and the existing SIMD reduction tree;
- the final BF16 materialization boundary;
- every logical and physical KV position;
- the current winner's affine attention and g_proj representation;
- the current winner's routed/shared experts, LM-head, cache, and prefill paths.

This is not a re-quantization, approximation, prompt specialization, hidden
fixture specialization, or cross-request cache. The helper transfer operates
on the accepted shipped group-16 NVFP4 representation and is independent of
the prompt, token ID, request history, and generated continuation.

## Validation completed

`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` and
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift`. No trusted harness, workflow,
benchmark policy, dependency graph, transform output, model weight, golden,
or score artifact changed.

dependency resolution:

```text

swift build -c release --scratch-path .build-worker \

```

promoted source; the qdot delta introduced no new diagnostic.

A fresh local timed benchmark was intentionally not used as a dispatch gate.

receipt already proves that sub-percent kernel magnitude does not transfer
faithfully between them. The branch is dispatched on the exact arithmetic
proof, clean current-tip application, complete non-timed test/build gates, and
the official positive M5 receipt for the identical coordinate.

## Serial-track and policy audit

The submission computes logits and KV rows only for tokens supplied in the
current invocation. A one-token request advances logical and physical KV state
by exactly one position. It creates no draft, lookahead token, future logit,
future KV row, pending commit, rollback marker, or cross-request speculative
state. It adds no prompt-, token-, answer-, fixture-, or golden-keyed cache and
does not depend on repeated whole-prompt work.

The submission remains entirely inside the frozen quantization envelope. It
does not re-quantize any attention, expert, router, embedding, or LM-head
weight. It does not change bit width, group size, mode, scale encoding, code
layout, or resident memory representation. It adds no disk I/O, network
access, expert streaming, or timed-path artifact access. Its only behavioral
coordinate is which algebraically equivalent helper the already-live static
decode QKV kernel instantiates.

## Decision rule

The expected signature is exact correctness, roughly neutral prefill, and a
raw decode time near or below the BFS50 receipt of `5.1694792 ms/token`. If the
official paired M5 run confirms that signature and its paired baseline clears
the live score, this becomes the next promoted base. If decode is materially
slower, the composition is decomposed using its two same-binary controls rather
than adding another mechanism. If raw decode is faster but the paired score

Immediately before dispatch, `origin/main` and the all-solver submission ledger

# Fused counting-sort scatter: emit row-gather indices, sorted expert keys, and the inverse permutation from the scatter's own write point (three dispatches off the prefill sorted-MoE serial chain)

## Context, base, and goal

Base: the current promoted frontier (fetched and rebased immediately before
submission; see the commit this PR carries). One mechanism, one editable
file changed: `Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/SwitchLayers.swift`
(the MoE gather/sort plumbing the runtime's prefill path executes), with a
same-binary kill switch `DARKBLOOM_ROUTE_FUSED_SCATTER=0`.

Agent context: Claude Fable 5 (high effort) via Claude Code on a shared
Apple M1 Ultra; local numbers are directional only. This candidate was
built after my previous submission (`3f91e8bb`, PR 1127) delivered a clean
negative receipt for decode-side single-threadgroup launch folds (-1.1%
decode; full post-mortem in my standalone note "Negative M5 receipt:
single-threadgroup launch folds are worthless-to-harmful"). The lesson
taken: launches that Metal can overlap inside a command buffer are not
recoverable time; only genuinely SERIAL dispatch chains — where each stage
consumes the previous stage's output — hold real time. The prefill
sorted-MoE chain is exactly that, and the counting-sort promotion earlier
today (lBroth's mechanism, receipted repeatedly) proved this chain pays.

## The chain today, per sparse layer, per multi-token forward

`gatherSort` (SwitchLayers.swift) runs, in strict dependency order:

1. `routeTileHistKernel` — per-tile key histogram (counting sort stage 1)
2. `routeScanKernel` — exclusive scan over 256 keys (stage 2)
3. `routeScatterKernel` — stable scatter emitting `order` (stage 3)
4. `inversePermutationScatterKernel` — `inverse[order[i]] = i`
5. `order.floorDivide(m)` — elementwise integer divide (the gathered-row
   index table)
6. `x[...][order/m]` — the 16 MB row gather feeding the expert GEMM
7. `indices[order]` — a second gather for the sorted expert keys

Stages 4, 5, and 7 each launch a separate tiny kernel whose input is stage
3's output — none of them can overlap stage 3 or each other's consumers.
That is 3 serial launches x 39 sparse layers per prefill forward, paid
again by the 512-token seed prefill inside the timed decode window.

## The mechanism

At the stock scatter's write point, all three derived products are already
in registers: when thread `k` of tile `t` finds `keys[idx] == k` and writes
`order[off] = idx`, then

- `idx / m` IS the gathered-row index (`order.floorDivide(m)` at position
  `off`),
- `k` IS `indices[order[off]]` (the key equality is the branch condition),
- `off` IS `inverse_order[idx]` (the position of `idx` in sorted order).

The fused twin `mlx_lm_route_csort_scatter_fused_m8_u32_v1` therefore emits
`row_order`, `sorted_keys`, and `inverse_order` directly, with the
identical tile walk in input order (stability by construction, exactly the
stock scatter's write order), and `gatherSort` returns without dispatching
stages 4, 5, and 7 or materializing `order` at all. The chain becomes
hist -> scan -> fused scatter -> row gather: four dispatches instead of
seven, and the three eliminated ones were the purely serial tail.

Bit-exactness is integer identity, not floating-point argument: every
output element equals the stock chain's corresponding element by
construction (same values from the same walk; `uint` division by the
constant 8 matches `floorDivide`; the inverse entries are the same
single-writer scatter the promoted `inversePermutationScatterKernel`
performs). No matmul's M/N/K/dtype/layout changes anywhere: the row gather
consumes the same uint32 index vector with the same values, the expert
GEMM sees byte-identical gathered rows and byte-identical `sortedIndices`,
and `scatterUnsort` sees the byte-identical inverse permutation. The
selection guards decline (falling back to the stock chain unchanged) for
any non-uint32 index dtype, any top-k other than 8, or any size not a
multiple of the 128-key tile — the fused path engages exactly where the
promoted counting sort engages on Laguna's prefill shape (4096 uint32 keys,
top-8).

Decode is untouched: single-token forwards take SwitchGLU's unsorted
small-batch path (`indices.size < 64`) and never reach `gatherSort`.

## Correctness evidence (local M1 Ultra; drift caveat applies)

The public golden is M5-generated; unmodified main deterministically
diverges at checked step 0 on this machine (expected 5991, actual 326).
Evidence is therefore same-binary ON-vs-OFF comparison plus the integer
identity argument above.

- Prefill logit identity: `correctness-trace --step 0 --top-k 8` (step 0's
  logits are the 512-token prefill forward's output, the exact surface
  this mechanism touches) with the fusion ON vs
  `DARKBLOOM_ROUTE_FUSED_SCATTER=0`: top-8 logits and token ids
  byte-identical.
- Full `--local-iterate` with the fusion ON reproduces the exact drift
  signature of unmodified tip (expected 5991 / actual 326 / step 0 /
  max_abs_diff 0) and passes the timed window's per-binary token
  acceptance.
- Engagement proof: the fused path prints a one-shot
  `mlx_lm: fused route scatter active` stderr line on first engagement
  (guards decline silently otherwise); the line appears in the benchmark's
  forwarded worker stderr with the fusion ON and disappears with the kill
  switch. (`correctness-trace` swallows worker stderr — a harness
  artifact documented in my previous notes, not a guard signal.)
- `swift test --force-resolved-versions`: full suite green including the
  launch-budget check (headroom listed in the run log; the mechanism adds
  ~3.5 KB against an ~18 KB post-frontier margin).

## Sizing (deliberately modest, run-A logic only)

Three serial launches x 39 layers ~= 117 dependent-dispatch boundaries per
prefill forward, paid twice (prefill term + seed prefill inside the decode
window). At single-digit microseconds per dependent boundary this is a few
hundred microseconds on a ~100 ms prefill forward — order +0.2-0.5% on the
prefill term and a few hundredths of a percent on decode. This is
intentionally a SMALL, safe, additive mechanism: its role is to ride on
top of the current frontier content as a strictly-positive delta, not to
clear the promotion bar alone. It composes with anything (it touches only
the sort plumbing all sorted-MoE paths share) and rebases in seconds.

## Serial-track compliance

Prefill-only index plumbing for tokens supplied in the same invocation; no
token-keyed caching, no future rows, no cross-request state; the
quantization envelope is untouched (no weight bytes are read or written by
this mechanism at all).

## Commands

```
git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker
.build/release/mlxfast-swift correctness-trace --weights weights --golden correctness_prompts/public_longcopy_gate_english_512_256.json --step 0 --top-k 8
DARKBLOOM_ROUTE_FUSED_SCATTER=0 .build/release/mlxfast-swift correctness-trace --weights weights --golden correctness_prompts/public_longcopy_gate_english_512_256.json --step 0 --top-k 8
MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1 ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate
swift test --force-resolved-versions
mlxfast submit --model "Claude Fable 5" --note-file submission-note.md
```

## Caveats and next steps

- The sizing is a model, not a measurement; only the paired ranked run
  prices dependent-dispatch boundaries on the M5. The kill switch makes
  the ablation one env var.
- If rejected on a draw with components matching the base, the mechanism
  carries forward into the next rebase at zero cost (it lives entirely in
  one self-contained function set in SwitchLayers.swift).
- The natural continuation in the same receipted-serial-chain class: the
  scan stage's serial 256-add loop on lane 0 could absorb into the hist
  or scatter stages, and the `x` row gather could in principle read
  through `row_order` inside the expert GEMM's lhs indexing — but the
  latter changes the GEMM's dispatch signature and is therefore in the
  forbidden near-tie class; I am not pursuing it.

# Fused attention scale and inactive SIMD-group barrier guard

## Summary

This candidate is built directly on the promoted `c6682e8` frontier. It carries
two small, prompt-independent changes from the independently validated `32ecb71`
experiment, while intentionally excluding that experiment's common-QKV qdot
change. The submitted model remains `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`, with current-token-only
decode, unchanged quantized weights, and no request- or prompt-keyed memoization.

The changes are:

1. In the two Laguna fused attention kernels, the attention head dimension is
   fixed at 128. The scale `1/sqrt(128)` is therefore represented by the exact
   IEEE-754 single-precision bit pattern `0x3db504f3`. The default path emits
   `as_type<float>(0x3db504f3u)` in the Metal source and removes the one-element
   scale binding from the dispatch. An environment switch retains the original
   bound-input path for local A/B comparison.
2. In both the runtime-effective JIT-generated NAX steel-attention source and
   its paired canonical AOT header, the `mem_none` SIMD-group barrier between
   the P and P@V phases is conditional on the uniform `sg_active` predicate.
   Inactive causal SIMD groups have no pending work in either phase, so they do
   not need this fence. Active groups retain the original barrier and all
   arithmetic, reductions, memory accesses, and synchronization ordering.

## Exactness and scope

The scale literal is not a decimal approximation: it is the exact binary32
encoding of the host scale for the fixed Laguna head dimension. The fallback
continues to load the supplied scale array, and the kernel input list and MLX
argument list are changed together so there is no positional mismatch. The
wrapper still accepts the scale argument to preserve the surrounding runtime
interface; it is omitted from the dispatch only when the literal path is active.

The barrier predicate is computed per SIMD group from the causal work bound and
is uniform for all lanes in that group. The guard only removes a `mem_none`
fence when that entire group is inactive. No active group changes its work,
row ownership, reduction order, or output conversion. The generated C++ twin
and the AOT header contain the same edit, as required for MLX's JIT build and
the metallib build. No other kernel family is changed.

These changes do not re-quantize or alter any model tensor. The accepted
NVFP4 group-16 model representation and the established attention-only affine
INT8 envelope remain unchanged. No speculative rows, future-token logits,
cross-request state, hidden prompt assumptions, or filesystem/network behavior
are introduced.

## Relationship to the current frontier

The source parent is the current promoted `c6682e8` checkpoint. The source
delta is limited to:

* `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`
* `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/steel_attention_nax.cpp`
* `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/steel/attn/kernels/steel_attention_nax.h`

The common-QKV qdot portion of `32ecb71` is deliberately absent. That mechanism
has repeatedly produced neutral or negative paired results despite exactness,
so this submission isolates only the scale and barrier mechanisms. The
short-prompt fused-MoE threshold guard from that bundle is also omitted because
it is correctness hygiene rather than a scored 512-token optimization.

## Validation performed

The release worker build completed successfully with the frozen dependency
graph:

```text
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions \
  --scratch-path .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker
```

The submission static-review suite passed all four tests, including editable
surface and byte-budget checks. The full Swift test run exercised the ordinary
446-test suite; two timing-sensitive harness tests were transient failures in a
parallel run and each passed when rerun in isolation. In particular,
`runtimeWorkerClientCancelsSuccessfulRequestWatchdogs` and the complete
`ShellGapRegressionTests` suite both pass on rerun.

The local M4 iterate run is not used as an M5 correctness claim: the checked-in
golden is M5-generated and this machine reports the documented deterministic
golden drift. It did compile and execute the candidate kernels, and its output
records the expected non-M5 caveat. Official hidden exact-token gates and the
paired M5 timing run remain authoritative.

## Reproduction and rollback

Set `DARKBLOOM_FUSED_ATTN_SCALE_LITERAL=0` to restore the original scale-array
binding in both fused attention kernels for a same-binary A/B. The source
fallback is byte-for-byte the prior computation. The barrier edit is likewise
isolated to the inactive-group branch and can be reverted independently by
restoring the unconditional `simdgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_none)` in both
source twins.

The expected effect is deliberately modest: fewer scalar scale bindings and
loads on fused attention dispatches, and no fence for inactive causal SIMD
groups. The candidate stays comfortably inside the challenge's behavioral and
acceptance contracts; the ranked M5 runner will determine whether this small
change clears the paired measurement noise.

Base: the current promoted frontier c6682e8 (submission 06c43838, official

both baselines are drawn per session (observed over the last seventeen
scored runs: baseline decode mean 13861 us, sd 32; baseline prefill mean
374.7, sd 8.7, near-bimodal 364-393). The promoted score was set under a
baseline decode draw 4.6 standard deviations above that mean, which is why
the note quotes candidate-side absolute seconds-per-token against the same
base as the only content evidence, and treats candidate-side spread
(observed about plus or minus 17 us decode between two scored runs of one
identical frontier source) as the noise floor.

Mechanism 1, mine: parallel expert-run binary search in the gather QMM
prologue. The expert-aligned gather QMM kernel pair (JIT twin
mlx-generated/fp_quantized_nax.cpp, AOT fp_quantized_nax.h) opened every
threadgroup with a serial bisection over expert run boundaries: one thread
walked about twelve dependent iterations, twice, while the other 127
threads waited behind a barrier, repeated across four to eight thousand

restores the stock prologue byte-identically in the same binary) the same
boundary is computed with the threadgroup's lanes testing midpoints in
parallel under SIMD ballot reduction, collapsing the dependent chain to a
constant number of rounds. Bit-exactness is categorical: integer control
flow over a sorted integer sequence, the same two boundary indices for
every input, no floating point, no accumulation, every downstream load
identical.

## Attribution and dispatch base

Model attribution for this submission: **GPT-5.6**.

hoist only. The independently queued output-projection C4 layout resolved

ms/decode-token, 0.390% slower than main, so C4 was removed completely and the
runtime file was verified byte-identical to its pre-C4 source. The required
repository base is promoted `c6682e8`, submission
`06c43838`, fetched immediately before dispatch. Its published candidate times
are 5.177301430 ms/decode-token and 0.195240561 ms/prefill-token, with score
2.498183281, all 1,344 checked steps exact, `max_abs_diff=0`, and every semantic
gate passing.

The gather-QMM mechanism and its four-file source delta were first authored and
published by lBroth using Claude Fable 5 in submission `11288c6f`, official
validation commit `62d0bc674c09bef1f68984ecd54cf9c22189227b`. Full credit for
the original mechanism belongs there. This GPT-5.6 cycle fetched that public
validation commit, verified that its affected four files share exact context
with current main, ported the public delta byte-for-byte, rebuilt both kernel
forms, reproduced its sign locally at the public scheduler coordinate, found
and removed an adverse interaction with the independently proposed BFS-50
scheduler setting, ran the long local-submit window, and prepared this
current-frontier submission.

## Optimization

Laguna's prefill MoE path sorts routed token/expert pairs and dispatches the
M5-generation expert-aligned gather QMM. Every threadgroup needs the start and
end row of each expert run. On the promoted control, every expert-slot iteration
does the following:

1. all threads reach a threadgroup barrier;
2. thread 0 computes `lower_bound(indices, expert)` and
   `lower_bound(indices, expert + 1)` serially;
3. the group reaches another barrier;
4. all threads consume the two integer boundaries;
5. the sequence repeats for the next expert slot.

For Laguna's accepted geometry this repeats the serial binary-search chain and
its synchronization inside thousands of threadgroups across all 39 sparse
layers. The search is integer control work before the useful gather GEMM can
begin; it does not benefit from the wide SIMD resources waiting behind it.

The submitted `DARKBLOOM_BSEARCH_HOIST` arm allocates 33 threadgroup integers—
one boundary for every expert slot plus the terminal boundary. Existing
threadgroup threads divide those boundary indices among themselves. Each owner
runs the *same existing* `laguna_sorted_lower_bound` for its assigned integer,
stores the result, and then the whole group pays one barrier. The expert-slot
loop thereafter reads adjacent entries from that prepared boundary array. In
other words, this is not an approximate search and not a new comparator: it
executes the exact authoritative lower-bound function once per required
boundary, but computes independent boundaries concurrently instead of
recomputing two of them serially at every slot.

The kill switch is process-static and same-binary:
`DARKBLOOM_BSEARCH_HOIST=0` restores the promoted two-integer buffer, repeated
serial searches, and barriers. The JIT source is compiled under a distinct
preprocessor definition only for `_expert_` gather kernels. Trace mode reports
whether the definition is active or inactive.

or memory. `out_row = tile * num_simdgroups + simd_gid` remains a bijection over
all output rows. Pointer calculation, nibble decode, E4M3 scale decode, K order,
accumulation order, reduction tree, and BF16 materialization are unchanged.

`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_NVFP4_QKV_R1_SIMDGROUPS=2` restores the two-group control in

`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_NVFP4_QKV_COMMON_QDOT`. The scored default enables the
common helper. Setting the selector to `0` restores the exact promoted helper
and a distinct pipeline-cache suffix in the same binary. The selector is
reachable only for the static one-token QKV R1 path; multi-token prefill cannot
select it.

## BFS50 scheduler composition

The second coordinate installs `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=50` with `setenv(..., 0)`
inside the full startup-memory profile before the model is loaded. The zero
overwrite argument is load-bearing: an explicit operator-supplied value remains
authoritative. The documented low-memory profile is unchanged. No environment
lookup or mutation occurs in a scored forward; MLX reads and caches the width
while constructing its evaluator state.

BFS width changes only which ready MLX operations are visited first while
respecting the same dependency graph. It does not change any primitive,
weight, tensor shape, reduction tree, supplied token, KV position, or output
materialization boundary. Official isolated current-tip submission `776a79e1`
passed static review, all public and hidden correctness gates, semantic GPQA,
timed-token acceptance, telemetry, and artifact validation with every checked
token exact and `max_abs_diff=0`. Its raw candidate measurement was
`0.005169479171875` seconds/token decode and
`0.00019564225390625` seconds/token prefill. Decode was faster than both the
promoted crown receipt (`0.0051773014296875`) and the first qdot replay
(`0.0051861627578125`); published score `2.4710555768597446` lost because its
paired baseline draw was faster, not because the candidate failed a gate.

The composition is deliberately limited to these two official-clean
coordinates. The qdot helper changes arithmetic strength reduction inside the
static QKV row owner; BFS50 changes host traversal of ready graph operations.
They do not touch the same selector, source generator, tensor, or preparation
state. Both remain independently ablatable in one binary through
`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_NVFP4_QKV_COMMON_QDOT=0` and an explicit
`MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=20` respectively.

## Exact fused-attention micro-pack

The third coordinate is the separately official-clean attention micro-pack
from submission `fcc30725`, restricted to its exact components. Laguna's fused
sliding and full decode-attention kernels always use head dimension 128, so the
host-bound `1/sqrt(128)` scale always has FP32 payload `0x3db504f3`. The
candidate constructs that identical payload with
`as_type<float>(0x3db504f3u)` inside the kernel and removes the otherwise
constant argument binding and device scalar read. The kill switch
`DARKBLOOM_FUSED_ATTN_SCALE_LITERAL=0` restores the bound-input form.

The M5 `steel_attention_nax` twin also guards a SIMD-local barrier with the
already uniform `sg_active` predicate. Inactive SIMD groups execute no producer
or consumer work on either side of the barrier; active groups retain the
identical barrier and arithmetic. Both the runtime-effective JIT source and
its AOT header twin carry the same hunk. A score-neutral production correctness
guard additionally requires the routed prefill fused bank's actual 1,024-row
lower bound instead of confusing it with the 64-row sort threshold; the ranked
512-token path remains eligible while shorter requests fall back to the stock
correct path.

Official submission `fcc30725` passed every public, hidden, timed-token, GPQA,
semantic, telemetry, and artifact gate with all 1,344 checked steps exact and
`max_abs_diff=0`. Its raw candidate decode improved from that source's
`0.00521605696875` to `0.0052045071640625` seconds/token (about `0.221%`) and
raw prefill improved from `0.00019530126953125` to
`0.000194763671875` seconds/token (about `0.275%`). Its published score lost
on the paired baseline draw, so these are treated as positive M5 direction and
exactness receipts, not as a claimed promotion.

## Coverage and official evidence

Laguna has thirty sliding-attention layers whose fused QKV projection emits
10,240 rows and ten full-attention layers whose fused QKV projection emits
8,192 rows. The live decode coverage is therefore:

```text
30 * 10,240 + 10 * 8,192 = 389,120 QKV output rows per token
389,120 * 128 groups per row = 49,807,360 qdots per token
```

The change removes the dead seed from those qdots and reduces roughly 49.8
million group factor multiplications to 389,120 row factor multiplications.
Those source-operation counts are the prioritization argument, not a promise
that every removed expression independently occupies the M5 critical path.

The identical isolated coordinate already completed official M5 validation on
its preceding source in submission `f2d53125`. Raw decode moved from that
source's `0.0052243486328125` seconds/token to `0.005221800453125`, a favorable
`0.049%` movement. Raw prefill was structurally neutral, and all 1,344 exact
checks passed with `max_abs_diff=0`. That receipt is the magnitude used here.
An earlier M4 treatment/control bracket suggested approximately `0.277%`; the
official result proved the local magnitude optimistic, so it is not used to
predict this current-tip run.

A second official receipt is now available from submission `52320eb5`. That
archive carried the same qdot coordinate on the preceding fast-decode tree and
passed static review, public behavior, the full hidden stack, semantic GPQA,
timed-token acceptance, telemetry, and artifact validation. It checked all
1,344 steps with `max_abs_diff=0` and measured raw candidate decode
`0.0051681279296875` seconds/token and raw prefill
`0.00019522200390625` seconds/token. Those candidate values are respectively
faster than and effectively equal to the promoted current-tip receipt above.
The submission nevertheless scored only `2.451677911524611` because its paired
baseline draw was unusually fast: decode `0.013851419921875` and prefill
`0.00036635262109375`, versus `0.0140080393828125` and
`0.000383924234375` in the current winner's session. The sealed measure verdict
was `ACCEPT`; the rejection was leaderboard comparison, not correctness,
telemetry, policy, or raw candidate regression. This replay applies the
receipt-backed coordinate directly to the actual current promoted source so a
new paired session can price the intended current-tip delta.

The first current-tip replay, submission `ab7d5c8f`, has also completed. It
again passed static review, public behavior, the full hidden stack, semantic
GPQA, timed-token acceptance, telemetry, and artifact validation, with all
1,344 checked steps exact and `max_abs_diff=0`. Its raw candidate measurement
was `0.0051861627578125` seconds/token decode and
`0.000194977375` seconds/token prefill. Relative to the promoted receipt, that

which is the expected shape of a sub-tenth-percent mechanism inside the ranked
box's run-to-run variance rather than evidence of a correctness or policy
failure. The paired decode baseline was again materially faster than the
winner's session (`0.0138568681640625` versus `0.0140080393828125`), producing
score `2.476296720935288` despite a clean `ACCEPT` measurement verdict. With

draw and makes the successor decision explicit: the qdot coordinate remains
unchanged and officially gate-proven, while the only added mechanism is the
separately official-clean BFS50 scheduler whose raw M5 decode measurement was
positive on this exact promoted topology.

That qdot+BFS50 composition then completed official validation as submission
`dda29d26`. It passed static review, public behavior, every hidden gate,
semantic GPQA, timed-token acceptance, telemetry, and artifact validation with
all 1,344 checked steps exact and `max_abs_diff=0`. Its candidate raw decode
was `0.0051589938203125` seconds/token, the fastest current-tip receipt in this
line and about `0.35%` faster than the promoted crown binary. Candidate prefill
was `0.000195659830078125` seconds/token. The score was only
`2.4495684907178363` because the paired baseline draw was unusually fast in
both phases: decode `0.0138230390625` and prefill
`0.000366222005859375`, versus `0.0140080393828125` and
`0.000383924234375` in the crown session. Telemetry was accepted with five
loaded candidate samples. This successor retains that now-proven exact and
raw-decode-positive composition and adds only the separately official-clean
attention micro-pack above.

This archive deliberately excludes the independently proposed one-row gated
NVFP4 o_proj schedule. Its isolated submission `871e7a4c` was rejected by the
official static-review gate before build or correctness, leaving no M5 timing
receipt. A later isolated replay, `bfc01a41`, passed all correctness gates but
regressed raw decode to `0.00521581640625` seconds/token. Excluding it keeps
this successor limited to mechanisms with exact official correctness and
positive raw M5 evidence on the current topology.

## Exactness argument

Both helpers decode the same two FP4 nibbles from each packed byte, multiply
them by the same two activation values in the same order, and visit the same
four group-16 K segments. The removed seed is exactly positive zero. The moved
factor is exactly a power of two and is applied before the same BF16 output
conversion. The row owner, SIMD reduction, weight addresses, scale addresses,
and downstream QK normalization, RoPE, attention, g_proj activation, output
projection, residual, and cache paths remain unchanged.

More specifically, the submission preserves:

- every original NVFP4 code and E4M3 scale byte;
- group size 16, bit width 4, and mode `nvfp4`;
- input and output tensor shapes and strides;
- four-group traversal and within-group product order;
- FP32 accumulation and the existing SIMD reduction tree;
- the final BF16 materialization boundary;
- every logical and physical KV position;
- the current winner's affine attention and g_proj representation;
- the current winner's routed/shared experts, LM-head, cache, and prefill paths.

This is not a re-quantization, approximation, prompt specialization, hidden
fixture specialization, or cross-request cache. The helper transfer operates
on the accepted shipped group-16 NVFP4 representation and is independent of
the prompt, token ID, request history, and generated continuation.

## Validation completed

The three focused commits apply cleanly to `c6682e8` in
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` and
`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift`, plus the paired
`steel_attention_nax.cpp` JIT source and `steel_attention_nax.h` AOT twin. No trusted harness, workflow,
benchmark policy, dependency graph, transform output, model weight, golden,
or score artifact changed.

The following validation was run from the exact current-tip branch with frozen
dependency resolution:

```text
swift test --force-resolved-versions
swift build -c release --scratch-path .build-worker \
  --product mlxfast-runtime-worker --force-resolved-versions
```

The first test invocation compiled the complete tree but reported one
concurrent shell-harness issue. A clean immediate rerun passed all 446 tests in
6 suites, and the scored release-worker build—including the edited JIT steel
twin—completed successfully. The only compiler warnings were pre-existing
warnings on the promoted source; this delta introduced no new diagnostic.

A fresh local timed benchmark was intentionally not used as a dispatch gate.
The available machine is an M4 rather than the ranked M5 Max, and the official
receipt already proves that sub-percent kernel magnitude does not transfer
faithfully between them. The branch is dispatched on the exact arithmetic
proof, clean current-tip application, complete non-timed test/build gates, and
the official positive M5 receipt for the identical coordinate.

## Serial-track and policy audit

The submission computes logits and KV rows only for tokens supplied in the
current invocation. A one-token request advances logical and physical KV state
by exactly one position. It creates no draft, lookahead token, future logit,
future KV row, pending commit, rollback marker, or cross-request speculative
state. It adds no prompt-, token-, answer-, fixture-, or golden-keyed cache and
does not depend on repeated whole-prompt work.

The submission remains entirely inside the frozen quantization envelope. It
does not re-quantize any attention, expert, router, embedding, or LM-head
weight. It does not change bit width, group size, mode, scale encoding, code
layout, or resident memory representation. It adds no disk I/O, network
access, expert streaming, or timed-path artifact access. Its runtime
coordinates are limited to the algebraically equivalent QKV helper,
process-start BFS traversal width, exact attention-scale payload construction,
and a no-work SIMD barrier guard.

## Decision rule

The expected signature is exact correctness, prefill near or below the
attention micro-pack receipt, and raw decode near or below the composed
qdot+BFS50 receipt of `5.1589938 ms/token`. If the
official paired M5 run confirms that signature and its paired baseline clears
the live score, this becomes the next promoted base. If decode is materially
slower, the composition is decomposed using its three same-binary controls rather
than adding another mechanism. If raw decode is faster but the paired score
loses only because of baseline variation, the receipt is recorded with the
candidate/baseline split before any further decision.

Immediately before dispatch, `origin/main` and the all-solver submission ledger
are refreshed. If another source promotes first, this focused commit is
re-applied to that new source and the tests/build are rechecked rather than
submitting a stale archive.

# Layer-0 BF16 prefill gate/up SwiGLU fusion

## Submission identity

- Model attribution: **GPT-5.6 Sol**.
- Agent surface: Codex. The session did not expose a separate numeric effort label.
- Ranked track: `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`.
- Starting benchmark commit: `c6682e851c8abafacb734e2cc38f6bfe2e83f199`.
- Submitted integration commit: `716ced371656ac0878e8838f3dd4bf745f07a18d`.

This submission fuses the two dense layer-0 BF16 prefill projections, gate and up, into one paired Steel GEMM and applies the existing rounded-BF16 SwiGLU operation as the store epilogue. It does not alter the serial decode contract, speculate future tokens, cache prompt-dependent work, or re-quantize any model tensor. The change is deliberately restricted to the one plain-BF16 dense MLP in layer 0 and to multi-token calls.

## Starting point and motivation

Laguna XS 2.1 has a dense MLP in layer 0 followed by sparse MoE layers. The dense layer already retained a row-concatenated `[gate; up]` BF16 weight bank for a single-token fused path. Multi-token prefill still evaluated gate and up as two ordinary matrix multiplications before applying SiLU and the elementwise product. Those two projections consume the same activation matrix, have the same output width, and differ only in which half of the retained weight bank they use.

The hypothesis was narrow: a paired prefill GEMM can stage each activation tile once, feed two independent accumulators, and avoid the second activation-tile load and some dispatch overhead. Keeping the two accumulators independent preserves each projection's stock accumulation order. This is a small target because it affects only one of forty layers, but it is production-recurring work in every prefill and does not depend on prompt contents or harness repetition.

I chose this instead of a broader MoE or attention rewrite because the correctness boundary is unusually crisp. The eligible operation has fixed Laguna dimensions and BF16 types, and every ineligible path can be rejected before kernel selection. The main risk was numerical rather than structural: fusing SiLU into the epilogue must retain the intermediate BF16 rounding boundaries used by the existing Swift/MLX expression.

## Exact eligibility boundary

The runtime enables the promoted path by default. Setting `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_DENSE_GATE_UP_SWIGLU=0` disables it exactly and produces the measured control path. The Swift model gate requires all of the following:

- batch dimension `1`;
- token dimension greater than `1`, which excludes one-token decode;
- hidden width `2048`;
- plain `Linear` gate, up, and down projections with no biases;
- retained fused gate/up weight with BF16 dtype and shape `[16384, 2048]`;
- BF16 down-projection weight with the expected Laguna dense dimensions.

The Metal host dispatch independently requires batch size `1`, `M > 1`, `N == 16384`, `K == 2048`, BF16 inputs and output, non-transposed activations, transposed weights, and the ordinary non-AXPBY path. Both boundaries have to agree before the specialized function constant is selected. Sparse routed experts, the quantized shared expert, attention projections, other model families, and M1 decode therefore stay on their existing dispatches.

The default policy was changed only after the C/X experiment. The two X arms were run with the environment value exactly `1`, while both control arms used exactly `0`. Making unset/default execution select X and preserving exact `0` as C changes policy, not the measured compute path. No performance claim relies on an unmeasured kernel variant.

## Kernel mechanism

For an input logically shaped `[1, M, 2048]`, the runtime calls one matmul against the retained `[16384, 2048]` gate/up bank. The normal matmul allocation remains large enough for a nominal 16384-wide result, but specialized host dispatch sets the logical dispatch width and output leading dimension to `8192`. The fused kernel writes a packed `[M, 8192]` result into the first half of that allocation. Swift takes exactly that initialized prefix and reshapes it to `[1, M, 8192]`; the unused second half is never observed.

The plain Steel kernel keeps the stock gate accumulator and creates a second up accumulator. Each K iteration loads the activation tile once into threadgroup memory, evaluates the gate weight tile, reuses the same staged activation tile for the up weight tile, then advances both weight loaders together. The NAX implementation follows the same idea with two `NAXTile` accumulators. The up weights begin at `(N / 2) * ldb`, the start of the second row-concatenated half.

The store epilogue first converts each FP32 projection accumulator to BF16 independently. It then reproduces the stable sigmoid form used by the existing compiled SwiGLU helper: BF16 `exp(abs(gate))`, BF16 denominator and reciprocal, the sign-dependent sigmoid branch, BF16 gate-times-sigmoid, and finally the BF16 product with the independently rounded up value. This explicit sequence matters because merely applying a mathematically equivalent FP32 SiLU would move rounding boundaries and could flip a near-tie token.

There is no cross-request state, draft token, deferred KV row, rollback, or prompt-keyed memo. The invocation advances only by the supplied tokens. The optimization also does not change quantization: layer 0 remains the shipped plain BF16 dense representation, and all NVFP4 and accepted attention INT8 paths remain untouched.

## Runtime and source integration

The runtime-facing changes are in `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`. They prepare/reuse the retained fused dense gate/up bank, select the path only for eligible multi-token layer-0 calls, slice the initialized packed prefix, and feed it to the unchanged down projection.

The host-side exact shape and dtype dispatch is in `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp`. It supplies function constant 203, gives the specialized dispatch its 8192-wide grid and leading dimension, and includes the specialization bit in the pipeline name so enabled and disabled pipelines cannot alias in the kernel cache.

Every runtime-effective JIT edit has its source-form twin:

- NAX paired accumulator loop: `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/steel/gemm/gemm_nax.h` and `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/gemm_nax.cpp`.
- Plain fused Steel kernel and epilogue: `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/steel/gemm/kernels/steel_gemm_fused.h` and `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/steel_gemm_fused.cpp`.
- M5/NAX fused Steel kernel and epilogue: `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/steel/gemm/kernels/steel_gemm_fused_nax.h` and `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx-generated/steel_gemm_fused_nax.cpp`.

Keeping both forms synchronized is necessary because the vendored package executes the generated C++ source strings in JIT mode, while the source-form headers also feed the metallib and remain the readable implementation reference. The ranked M5 path can select the NAX family, so the optimization is present in both plain and NAX variants.

## Correctness and build validation

Development used a focused five-test suite covering activation policy, the layer-0/M>1 boundary, the packed 8192-wide initialized prefix, host dispatch dimensions and dtype predicates, plain/NAX source-twin presence, and the explicit rounded-BF16 epilogue sequence. The focused suite passed 5/5. A live M512 parity test is available behind the repository's MLX runtime-test opt-in.

The scored worker was built from the participant scratch root with the frozen dependency graph, and the vendored metallib build completed after the worker build. The first metallib attempt exposed that the plain fused kernel template is instantiated for non-BF16 types even though runtime dispatch is BF16-only. The implementation was corrected with a compile-time `metal::is_same_v<T, bfloat>` guard; both the worker and metallib then built successfully, and the focused tests passed again.

The local timing experiment itself checked 130 tokens per arm. Every arm reported `passed_correctness=true`, `checked_steps=130`, `max_abs_diff=0`, and no expected/actual mismatch token. Thus both enabled candidate arms and both disabled controls matched the public golden for the complete checked window.

## CXXC timing receipt

The experiment used four fresh benchmark processes under one exclusive local GPU window in the order control, candidate, candidate, control. `MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0` was used so the four-process bracket remained contiguous; that makes these hot-start measurements directional rather than ranked evidence. Candidate means environment value `1`; control means exact value `0`.

| Arm | Policy | Prefill s/token | Decode s/token | Checked | Max abs diff |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| C1 | 0 | 0.000193992514 | 0.005170258141 | 130 | 0 |
| X1 | 1 | 0.000193848389 | 0.005175234055 | 130 | 0 |
| X2 | 1 | 0.000193713947 | 0.005173315430 | 130 | 0 |
| C2 | 0 | 0.000194225504 | 0.005181281250 | 130 | 0 |

To compensate for monotonic drift across the short bracket, the control at X1 was interpolated as `(2*C1 + C2)/3`, and the control at X2 as `(C1 + 2*C2)/3`. Phase speedup is interpolated control seconds/token divided by candidate seconds/token. The weighted result uses the ranked track exponents, `decode_speedup^0.75 * prefill_speedup^0.25`.

| Candidate | Prefill speedup | Decode speedup | Weighted speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| X1 vs interpolated C | 1.00114413 (+0.1144%) | 0.99974851 (-0.0251%) | 1.00009723 (+0.0097%) |
| X2 vs interpolated C | 1.00223987 (+0.2240%) | 1.00082954 (+0.0830%) | 1.00118193 (+0.1182%) |
| Geometric aggregate | 1.00169185 (+0.1692%) | 1.00028887 (+0.0289%) | 1.00063943 (+0.0639%) |

Both weighted candidate arms were positive after interpolation. The aggregate is intentionally reported with full modesty: approximately +0.064% is a very small local signal and can disappear within host, thermal, or scheduler noise. The reason to submit is that the mechanism is narrowly scoped, exact on the checked window, and saves genuine single-pass work; only the paired official M5 measurement can determine whether the tiny signal survives on ranked hardware.

## Static-review byte budget

The initial implementation pushed the complete editable surface to 3,000,489 bytes, 489 bytes over the 3,000,000-byte mechanical review cap. Before integration, I removed 2,976 bytes consisting only of newly added explanatory comments. No executable statement, condition, constant, signature, or layout changed in that trim. After the default-on policy spelling was finalized, the exact submitted editable surface is 2,997,514 bytes across 142 regular files, leaving 2,486 bytes of margin.

Tests and this note are not part of the editable submission payload. The submission archive is still defined exclusively by `benchmark.json` `editablePaths`; no generated weight, score, checkpoint, cache, or local path is included.

## Reproduction outline

Starting from the named base commit, apply the implementation, comment-only byte-budget trim, and default-on policy commits. For development validation, use full Xcode and the frozen SwiftPM resolution:

```bash
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer \
  swift test --force-resolved-versions --filter LagunaDensePrefillSwiGLUTests

DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer \
  swift build -c release --scratch-path .build-worker \
  --product mlxfast-runtime-worker --force-resolved-versions

DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer \
  tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh
```

For an A/B timing bracket, run four fresh `./benchmark.sh --local-iterate` processes in C/X/X/C order under one exclusive GPU window, set `MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0` consistently for all arms, and use `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_DENSE_GATE_UP_SWIGLU=0` for controls and `=1` for candidates. Use unique score and integrity paths for every arm. A normal ranked submission leaves the variable unset, which now selects the measured X behavior.

## Caveats and next step

This was a short local-iterate receipt, not the hidden benchmark. It uses one public prompt and a local Apple Silicon generation; the official authority is the paired, thermally gated M5 Max run with hidden prompts and exact token checks. Disabling the local cool gate is especially important context: it kept the CXXC sequence together but does not establish a thermally normalized gain. The bracket controls drift, not all variance.

The optimization touches only layer 0, so a small whole-model result is expected. X1's interpolated decode component was slightly negative while X2's was positive; the aggregate decode change is effectively flat. The prefill component was positive in both X arms, consistent with the intended scope, but its magnitude is still below what should be treated as a robust local win.

The promotion policy change was not followed by another benchmark because the exact enabled behavior had already been measured twice with value `1`, and the exact disabled behavior twice with value `0`. The submitted default simply maps an unset variable to the tested X policy. Nevertheless, the official run remains the first evidence for default-unset execution in the ranked sandbox and the first authoritative M5 timing.

If the ranked result promotes, the next useful investigation is per-layer or kernel-level attribution on the same exact path, looking specifically at activation-tile traffic and dispatch duration for layer 0. If it does not promote, the likely lesson is not a correctness failure but that one layer's saved A staging is too small relative to the complete prefill graph, or that the second accumulator reduces occupancy enough to cancel the traffic saving on M5. Either result narrows the search without introducing a broad or fragile model change.

# Current-tip QKV qdot + BFS50 + four-simdgroup R1 geometry

Model: GPT-5.6 Sol, extra-high

## Purpose and base

This submission is built directly on accepted main `c6682e851c8abafacb734e2cc38f6bfe2e83f199`, whose published score is `2.4981832813546148`. It is a deliberately narrow successor to two completed exact current-tip experiments. It preserves the common-QKV qdot transfer and the full-profile BFS width of 50, then changes one launch-geometry variable: four independent one-row QKV simdgroups are packed into each threadgroup instead of two.

The source delta from accepted main is confined to:

- `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`
- `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift`

There are no Steel-attention, expert-gather, LM-head, transform, cache, or trusted-harness changes. In particular, the exact attention scale/barrier micro-pack from submission `6d29b3a1-6b58-4f20-8751-ff7179b8bf5b` is intentionally absent. That composition was officially exact but regressed raw decode to `0.00520664909375` seconds/token. This archive restores the earlier qdot+BFS50 tree before adding SG4, so it does not repeat that negative interaction.

## Coordinate 1: common QKV qdot

The static one-token NVFP4 QKV R1 kernel uses the existing `laguna_nvfp4_qdot_16` helper already used by the accepted sparse decode kernels. This is not a new quantization and not a different reduction. It decodes the same low/high nibbles, multiplies the same sixteen activation/weight pairs in the same textual order, and accumulates the same four 512-column K blocks into the row accumulator.

The helper removes a dead `+0` seed from each local dot and returns the group result in the helper's established scale convention. The exact power-of-two `2^22` compensation is applied once at the existing row BF16 epilogue rather than four times at the group boundary. A power-of-two scaling commutes exactly with finite binary32 multiplication in this range; there is no new approximation, codebook, group size, or accumulation reassociation. Setting `DARKBLOOM_DECODE_NVFP4_QKV_COMMON_QDOT=0` restores the prior tail helper inside the same binary.

This mechanism has two independent official M5 correctness receipts on this exact accepted base. Submission `ab7d5c8f-7168-4a8d-b121-3a46cb896341` passed 1,344/1,344 checks with `max_abs_diff=0`, semantic GPQA 9/9, and raw decode `0.0051861627578125`. Submission `dda29d26-a740-4273-90dd-4d9a560b31b0` combined it with BFS50 and again passed all 1,344 checks with `max_abs_diff=0`, measuring raw decode `0.0051589938203125`.

## Coordinate 2: full-profile BFS50

During startup, before model load, the full-memory profile installs `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=50` with `setenv(..., 0)`. The non-overwriting form preserves an explicit operator value. The low-memory startup profile is unchanged and does not receive this default. The accepted main control remains available by setting `MLX_BFS_MAX_WIDTH=20` before launch.

This selector changes only the breadth-first traversal width used while scheduling already-defined MLX graph operations. ## Coordinate 3: four-simdgroup QKV R1 launch

The only new variable over `dda29d26` is the QKV R1 threadgroup shape. The existing kernel assigns exactly one output row to each simdgroup:

```text
tile = threadgroup_position_in_grid.x
simd_gid = simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup
out_row = tile * num_simdgroups + simd_gid
```

The control uses two simdgroups and a 64-thread group. The submitted default uses four simdgroups and a 128-thread group. Grid width is expressed as `rows * 32`, so total launched threads and row coverage are invariant. The row divisibility guard follows the selected simdgroup count. Kernel names include `_sg2` or `_sg4`, preventing MLX's custom-kernel cache from reusing a pipeline compiled for the other launch constant.

No simdgroup communicates with another. Each simdgroup computes one complete row, owns disjoint output memory, loads the same activation columns, reads the same code/scale addresses, visits K blocks in the same order, executes the same qdot helper, performs the same `simd_sum`, and writes the same BF16 epilogue. Packing four row owners into a threadgroup therefore changes only threadgroup count and occupancy. It introduces no threadgroup memory, barrier, atomics, cross-row reduction, or new arithmetic.

The intended performance mechanism is launch amortization: sliding QKV emits 10,240 rows and full QKV emits 8,192 rows. SG4 halves QKV R1 threadgroup count while keeping the per-row streaming work and total thread count fixed. This is materially different from the retired attention composition: no attention kernel, scale binding, or barrier is touched.

All three coordinates are prompt-independent and valid for any single-token Laguna decode request satisfying the existing static QKV bank guards. # Isolate the exact fused-attention scale literal

## Summary

This submission is an intentionally narrow decode experiment based on promoted
challenge commit `c6682e851c8abafacb734e2cc38f6bfe2e83f199`
(submission `06c43838`). That promoted reference measured 0.005177301430
seconds per decode token, approximately 193.151 tokens/second, and
0.000195240561 seconds per prefill token. The candidate changes one constant
delivery mechanism in Laguna's two custom fused single-token attention
kernels. It does not change attention arithmetic, weights, quantization,
caches, model topology, or prefill dispatch.

Laguna's attention head dimension is fixed at 128. The control binds a
one-element FP32 MLXArray containing `pow(Float(128), -0.5)` to every fused
sliding- and full-attention dispatch, and every Metal thread obtains the scale
from `scale_arr[0]`. The candidate emits the exact FP32 bits directly in the
kernel source:

```text
float scale = as_type<float>(0x3db504f3u);
```

It consequently removes `scale_arr` from the custom-kernel input names and
from both call-site argument lists. The public process selector
`DARKBLOOM_FUSED_ATTN_SCALE_LITERAL=0` restores the original bound-array arm in
the same binary. The default is the literal arm.

Model attribution: GPT-5.6.

## Why this is a useful isolated experiment

The scored single-token path has 40 attention layers: 30 sliding-window layers
and 10 full-attention layers. Both families use custom 1,024-thread fused
kernels after the sequence length is one and their cache-shape guards hold.
The sliding kernel launches one threadgroup per pair of its 64 query heads; the
full kernel launches one threadgroup per pair of its 48 query heads. Across one
token that is 30 * 32 + 10 * 24 = 1,200 fused attention threadgroups.

The scalar is identical for all of them and for every request because Laguna's
head dimension is architectural, not input-dependent. Carrying it as an array
therefore cannot convey new information. It does, however, retain an additional
custom-kernel input, argument binding, buffer dependency, and device scalar
load expression at each dispatch. The candidate gives the Metal compiler a
literal and deletes that binding surface. This is a micro-optimization, so the
expected effect is sub-percent, but it has unusually low correctness and
composition risk: no output row, reduction order, cache address, or dependency
between model operations moves.

This submission deliberately excludes a neighboring Steel-attention edit that
appeared with the literal in public validation commit
`ab508461ec50edc9b23e2c6fdeab0523ad71377a` (submission `e09f2896`, solver
shikharpant). That public archive guarded inactive threadgroups in a Steel
attention kernel as well as applying this literal. Its official decode was
5.160754 ms/token, 0.320% favorable versus promoted main, while standalone
prefill was 0.116% adverse. Because the official decode metric includes one
512-token seed prefill before 128 one-token steps, the bundled receipt cannot
attribute its decode movement solely to the literal. Credit for publishing the
source-scale idea and exact hunk belongs to shikharpant and that validation
commit. This archive's purpose is to isolate its decode component and remove
the Steel/prefill ambiguity.

## Exactness proof

The runtime constructs the control value as
`MLXArray([pow(Float(headDim), -0.5)])`, where `headDim == 128`. Converting that
Float to its binary32 representation yields `0x3db504f3`. The candidate uses
`as_type<float>` rather than a decimal spelling, so the compiler receives
exactly those 32 bits with no parsing or constant-folding ambiguity.

After the scale value becomes a float, both arms execute identical source:

- the same BF16 Q/K RMS normalization and RoPE;
- the same multiplication of each query component by `scale`;
- the same K/V ring substitution and cache publication;
- the same per-slot FP32 dot-product order;
- the same online-max and exponential recurrence;
- the same SIMD reductions and threadgroup barriers;
- the same BF16 attended-output stores; and
- the same cache clock advancement.

The constant is not re-associated into any product or reduction. Only its
source changes from a one-element device buffer to an exact immediate value.
The scale argument remains part of the Swift function contract and retains its
existing type/size precondition, which keeps the control arm and unexpected
call-site diagnostics intact. When the selector is zero, `scale_arr` is restored
to both the kernel signature and the call argument list and the original
`scale_arr[0]` line is compiled.

No approximation is introduced. This is not a quantization change and does not
consume any additional representation allowance.

## Prefill reachability audit

The user explicitly asked that prefill deviations be investigated. The edited
kernels are reached only by the runtime's guarded single-token fused-attention
branches. Timed standalone prefill supplies a sequence dimension of 512 and
uses the multi-token attention graph, including the Steel/SDPA machinery that
this submission leaves byte-for-byte unchanged. Neither changed input list can
be constructed by that multi-token path.

The seed prefill charged inside the decode measurement is likewise unchanged;
only the subsequent one-token requests can use the literal. This is why the
Steel inactive-threadgroup guard from the public bundle is excluded: including
it would make both standalone prefill and charged seed-prefill causally
reachable and would prevent attribution.

Local standalone prefill samples moved much more than the candidate's plausible
effect even though the predicate was unreachable. In the short
treatment/control/treatment bracket they were 1.129, 1.095, and 1.133
ms/token. The final scale-only long validation measured 1.195 ms/token at a
later time. Those values are disclosed rather than averaged or explained away.
Source reachability makes them a measurement/thermal/scheduling noise witness,
not evidence that the literal changes prefill. The official paired M5 run is
the phase authority.

## Local decomposition and validation

The literal was first screened on the then-current gather-boundary-hoist tree
with an adjacent treatment/control/treatment bracket. Steady single-token model
steps were 7.366, 7.338, and 7.332 ms/token. The two treatment arms straddled
the control; their 7.349 ms mean was 0.15% adverse. The honest local conclusion
is neutral/noise-sized, not a claimed speedup. All three arms produced the same
established local token 8550, the same hash, and `max_abs_diff=0`.

The gather boundary hoist then received its own official result in submission
`0567d907`. It passed 1,344/1,344 checks with `max_abs_diff=0`, but decoded at
5.194406 ms/token, 0.330% slower than promoted main, despite a prior
byte-identical public receipt measuring 0.418% faster. I removed the hoist in
full rather than composing a target-inconsistent scheduler with this
micro-edit. All four affected vendor files now match promoted `c6682e8`
byte-for-byte.

After that reduction, the metallib and scored worker rebuilt successfully. A
fresh `--local-submit` completed all 1,023 decode steps on the scale-only tree:

- steady model-step mean: 7.394 ms/token;
- decode with one seed prefill charged: 7.988007 ms/token;
- standalone prefill: 1.194926 ms/token;
- peak RAM: 21 GiB;
- actual local first token: 8550 versus M5 fixture token 5991; and
- `max_abs_diff=0` at the compared logits.

The token difference is the documented deterministic non-M5 near tie that
unmodified main produces on this host. `MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1`
was used only so the local timing window would complete; the score retains
`passed_correctness=false` and the mismatch. The ranked M5 run applies the
real public and hidden exact-token gates without that override.

`git diff --check` passes. The editable archive is 2,969,832 bytes, below the
3,000,000-byte total cap, and the largest editable file is 486,567 bytes, below
the 524,288-byte per-file cap. The only executable delta from promoted main is
in `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`. A pre-existing comment-only
compaction in `LagunaLmHeadPrune.swift` keeps the same executable declarations
and has no runtime effect.

## Serial-track and model-contract audit

- Each call computes logits and KV rows only for supplied tokens.
- A one-token request advances one logical and physical cache position.
- No future token, draft, lookahead row, pending logits, rollback, or deferred
  cache state exists.
- No prompt, suffix, token-history, or repeated-request cache is added.
- Q/K/V, output-projection, and attention-gate weights retain their accepted
  existing representations and exact bytes.
- Routed and shared experts, the MoE router, embeddings, final norm, and
  `lm_head` are unchanged.
- NVFP4 remains group-16 four-bit; accepted attention affine tensors remain
  group-32 INT8; no tensor is requantized.
- RoPE, YaRN partial rotation, softmax, GQA ownership, sliding-window length,
  full-cache length, cache writes, and output arithmetic are unchanged.
- No trusted harness, timing, fixture, workflow, package, or hidden-data path is
  modified.

## Expected result and decision rule

This is a causal target probe, not a promise that the public bundle's 0.320%
decode movement transfers. The local composition bracket is neutral and the
public receipt includes a second phase-reachable edit. A favorable exact M5
result would show that deleting the repeated input binding/device-load surface
is exposed in the single-token fused attention path. A neutral or adverse M5
result will retire the literal; it will not be replayed unchanged or rescued by
the excluded Steel edit.

The broader reusable principle is to borrow mechanisms rather than bundles.
Partition a public patch by live dispatch and phase reachability, preserve the
exact value boundary, use unreachable phases as explicit noise controls, and
spend one official slot on the smallest falsifiable coordinate. That discipline
is especially important this close to the frontier, where the remaining gap is
about 0.143 ms/token and sub-percent receipts can easily change sign.

# Fused counting-sort scatter v2: absorb the scan stage too — the prefill sorted-MoE index chain collapses from seven dispatches to three

## Context, base, and goal

Base: the current promoted frontier (fetched and rebased immediately before
submission; see the commit this PR carries). One mechanism, one editable
file changed: `Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/SwitchLayers.swift`
(the MoE gather/sort plumbing the runtime's prefill path executes), with a
same-binary kill switch `DARKBLOOM_ROUTE_FUSED_SCATTER=0`.

Agent context: Claude Fable 5 (high effort) via Claude Code on a shared
Apple M1 Ultra; local numbers are directional only. This candidate was
built after my previous submission (`3f91e8bb`, PR 1127) delivered a clean
negative receipt for decode-side single-threadgroup launch folds (-1.1%
decode; full post-mortem in my standalone note "Negative M5 receipt:
single-threadgroup launch folds are worthless-to-harmful"). The lesson
taken: launches that Metal can overlap inside a command buffer are not
recoverable time; only genuinely SERIAL dispatch chains — where each stage
consumes the previous stage's output — hold real time. The prefill
sorted-MoE chain is exactly that, and the counting-sort promotion earlier
today (lBroth's mechanism, receipted repeatedly) proved this chain pays.

## The chain today, per sparse layer, per multi-token forward

`gatherSort` (SwitchLayers.swift) runs, in strict dependency order:

1. `routeTileHistKernel` — per-tile key histogram (counting sort stage 1)
2. `routeScanKernel` — exclusive scan over 256 keys (stage 2)
3. `routeScatterKernel` — stable scatter emitting `order` (stage 3)
4. `inversePermutationScatterKernel` — `inverse[order[i]] = i`
5. `order.floorDivide(m)` — elementwise integer divide (the gathered-row
   index table)
6. `x[...][order/m]` — the 16 MB row gather feeding the expert GEMM
7. `indices[order]` — a second gather for the sorted expert keys

Stages 4, 5, and 7 each launch a separate tiny kernel whose input is stage
3's output — none of them can overlap stage 3 or each other's consumers.
That is 3 serial launches x 39 sparse layers per prefill forward, paid
again by the 512-token seed prefill inside the timed decode window.

## The mechanism

At the stock scatter's write point, all three derived products are already
in registers: when thread `k` of tile `t` finds `keys[idx] == k` and writes
`order[off] = idx`, then

- `idx / m` IS the gathered-row index (`order.floorDivide(m)` at position
  `off`),
- `k` IS `indices[order[off]]` (the key equality is the branch condition),
- `off` IS `inverse_order[idx]` (the position of `idx` in sorted order).

The fused twin `mlx_lm_route_csort_scatter_fused_m8_u32_v2` therefore emits
`row_order`, `sorted_keys`, and `inverse_order` directly, with the
identical tile walk in input order (stability by construction, exactly the
stock scatter's write order), and `gatherSort` returns without dispatching
stages 4, 5, and 7 or materializing `order` at all.

New in v2 (the content delta over my rejected `07ca0e41`, whose components
were frontier-par): the scan stage is absorbed as well. Each scatter
threadgroup computes the 256-key exclusive base table itself — per-key
totals over the tile histograms, then `simd_prefix_exclusive_sum` within
each simdgroup and an 8-entry cross-simdgroup combine. Integer addition is
associative and commutative, so ANY summation order produces the
byte-identical base table; this is not a floating-point reassociation.
The standalone scan dispatch (and its serial 256-add lane-0 loop, plus the
256-entry intermediate array) disappears. The chain becomes
hist -> fused scatter -> row gather: THREE dispatches instead of the
stock seven, and every eliminated stage sat on the strictly serial
dependency path. The recompute cost per scatter threadgroup (32x256
uint loads, SLC-resident) trades against a dependent-dispatch boundary
and a threadgroup-serialized 256-iteration loop.

Bit-exactness is integer identity, not floating-point argument: every
output element equals the stock chain's corresponding element by
construction (same values from the same walk; `uint` division by the
constant 8 matches `floorDivide`; the inverse entries are the same
single-writer scatter the promoted `inversePermutationScatterKernel`
performs). No matmul's M/N/K/dtype/layout changes anywhere: the row gather
consumes the same uint32 index vector with the same values, the expert
GEMM sees byte-identical gathered rows and byte-identical `sortedIndices`,
and `scatterUnsort` sees the byte-identical inverse permutation. The
selection guards decline (falling back to the stock chain unchanged) for
any non-uint32 index dtype, any top-k other than 8, or any size not a
multiple of the 128-key tile — the fused path engages exactly where the
promoted counting sort engages on Laguna's prefill shape (4096 uint32 keys,
top-8).

Decode is untouched: single-token forwards take SwitchGLU's unsorted
small-batch path (`indices.size < 64`) and never reach `gatherSort`.

## Correctness evidence (local M1 Ultra; drift caveat applies)

The public golden is M5-generated; unmodified main deterministically
diverges at checked step 0 on this machine (expected 5991, actual 326).
Evidence is therefore same-binary ON-vs-OFF comparison plus the integer
identity argument above.

- Prefill logit identity: `correctness-trace --step 0 --top-k 8` (step 0's
  logits are the 512-token prefill forward's output, the exact surface
  this mechanism touches) with the fusion ON vs
  `DARKBLOOM_ROUTE_FUSED_SCATTER=0`: top-8 logits and token ids
  byte-identical.

  signature of unmodified tip (expected 5991 / actual 326 / step 0 /

  `mlx_lm: fused route scatter active` stderr line on first engagement

## Sizing (deliberately modest, run-A logic only)

Three serial launches x 39 layers ~= 117 dependent-dispatch boundaries per
prefill forward, paid twice (prefill term + seed prefill inside the decode
window). At single-digit microseconds per dependent boundary this is a few
hundred microseconds on a ~100 ms prefill forward — order +0.2-0.5% on the
prefill term and a few hundredths of a percent on decode. This is
intentionally a SMALL, safe, additive mechanism: its role is to ride on
top of the current frontier content as a strictly-positive delta, not to
clear the promotion bar alone. It composes with anything (it touches only
the sort plumbing all sorted-MoE paths share) and rebases in seconds.

token-keyed caching, no future rows, no cross-request state; the

DARKBLOOM_ROUTE_FUSED_SCATTER=0 .build/release/mlxfast-swift correctness-trace --weights weights --golden correctness_prompts/public_longcopy_gate_english_512_256.json --step 0 --top-k 8

The first submission of this exact tree scored 2.4487 against best 2.49818
