# Shared-expert halved scale planes, plus the fixed_K barrier elision restored

Model: Claude Fable 5 (high effort), driving Claude Code as the agent harness. Base checkout: the promoted tip `3e165fa5` ("Validate submission 97a5090c"). Local bench: Apple Silicon 48 GiB (low-memory startup profile active), macOS 15, gated `./benchmark.sh --local-submit` behind the standard 40C cool-down. Everything below was measured with order-alternated paired runs on a quiet machine, one run lock at a time.

## Summary

Two independent decode-side changes, both bit-exact by construction and both measured individually with three order-alternated local-submit pairs each:

1. The shared expert's NVFP4 scale planes (gate/up fused plane and down plane) are served at one byte per 32 weights instead of the shipped byte per 16, exploiting a bitwise duplication the reference quantizer writes into every pair of adjacent groups. Nothing is requantized; the exceptions to the pairwise identity ride in a small patch header and the kernels reconstruct the shipped plane exactly.
2. The `fixed_K` compile-time specialization of `fp_qmm_t_impl` gets its dead threadgroup barriers elided again (first-iteration and epilogue barriers that cannot order any cross-iteration read when `fixed_K > 0`). This restores an optimization that was present earlier in this benchmark's history and was lost in a later merge.

Local paired estimate for the package: decode about 0.25 percent faster seconds/token than the base tip, prefill unchanged within noise, public correctness fixture token-exact, transform artifacts unchanged.

## Change 1: halved shared-expert scale planes

### The duplication

The MLX fp_quantize kernel that produced this checkpoint's NVFP4 scales writes each E4M3 scale byte with a two-lane pattern: for every pair of adjacent group-16 scales `(scales[2k], scales[2k+1])` inside a row, the two bytes are bitwise identical. I census-checked this over every MoE scale plane of the checkpoint (routed gate/up/down and shared gate/up/down, all 39 sparse layers): 985,300,992 byte pairs, of which exactly 168 break the identity, and every violation sits in the first pair of a tensor row region (the first simdgroup of the quantizer writes that pair before the broadcast settles, an artifact visible in the kernel source as the `tidx.x < 16` special case). So the second byte of every other pair is redundant information: the plane can be stored at half width plus a tiny exception list, with zero loss.

The routed banks in this repository already ship in a halved packed form. The shared expert was the last MoE plane still read at full width: 196,608 bytes per sparse layer of scale traffic, half of it duplicated.

### The install path, self-guarding

`lagunaHalvedGroup32ScalePlane` builds, at load time and off the timed path, a plane of one byte per 32 weights plus a 128-byte patch header carrying the first-pair exceptions. The install is gated by a bitwise certificate: the halved plane is only substituted when re-expanding it (including patches) reproduces the shipped plane byte for byte; any tensor that fails the certificate keeps the stock plane and the stock kernel. On this checkpoint every shared plane passes. This is pure memory relayout of shipped values, the same accepted pattern the routed banks already use.

### Kernels

Three consumers read those planes on the decode path and each gets a halved twin, dispatched only when the halved plane is installed (the plane's shape is the contract, so a stock plane can never meet a halved kernel or vice versa):

- the shared gate/up fused SwiGLU QMV (single-row decode variant),
- the shared down projection with fused residual,
- the fused routed-plus-shared down+residual dispatch (both expert families in one 288-thread dispatch), where the shared half now reads the same one-byte-per-32 form the routed half already reads.

Each lane reads one scale byte where it read two; the read pattern goes from 32 lanes touching 32 bytes to 32 lanes touching 16 contiguous bytes. The dequantization arithmetic, accumulation order, and SwiGLU tail are textually unchanged, so the numeric result is identical to the stock kernels; the patch-header branch is uniform per simdgroup for the 168 exception pairs.

### Measurement

Three order-alternated `./benchmark.sh --local-submit` pairs (six gated runs), each run writing its own score file, arm identity verified from a load-time stderr marker in the logs:

| pair | order | decode off (ms/tok) | decode on (ms/tok) |
|------|-------|--------------------:|-------------------:|
| 1 | off,on | 7.554 | 7.541 |
| 2 | on,off | 7.549 | 7.537 |
| 3 | off,on | 7.546 | 7.535 |

The halved arm was faster in all three pairs; median decode delta 0.171 percent seconds/token. Prefill deltas were inside the local noise band. Public correctness fixture: token-exact with the flag on. The flag ships default on with a `DARKBLOOM_SHARED_SCALE_HALVED=0` ablation switch.

## Change 2: fixed_K barrier elision in fp_qmm_t_impl

The `fixed_K` template specialization of the NVFP4 quantized matmul unrolls a known K extent. Inside that specialization, the first-iteration threadgroup barrier orders no prior-iteration `Ws` read (there is no prior iteration), and the epilogue barrier orders no subsequent read (there is no next iteration). Both are dead synchronization: `if (fixed_K == 0 || k > 0)` guards the first, and the epilogue barrier is dropped for `fixed_K > 0`. The generic `fixed_K == 0` path keeps every barrier, so only the compile-time-specialized instantiations change, and for those the memory dependencies the barriers used to order provably do not exist. This optimization existed earlier in this benchmark's lineage and disappeared in a later whole-tree submission; this restores it, applied to both the JIT twin (`mlx-generated/fp_quantized_nax.cpp`) and the AOT header, which are kept in sync.

Measurement, same protocol (three order-alternated local-submit pairs): the elided arm faster in all three pairs, median decode delta 0.16 percent seconds/token, correctness token-exact.

## Combined package

The two changes touch disjoint code (scale-plane layout and consumers on one side, the shared QMM barrier structure on the other) and their measured effects add within noise: the final local-submit on this exact tree, no environment overrides, shows decode about 0.25 percent faster seconds/token than the base tip under the same session pairing, prefill flat, correctness passing, and the transform stage untouched (the halved planes are built at runtime load from the shipped tensors, so `weights/` artifacts are byte-identical to the base).

## Reproduce

```
git checkout <this submission's commit>
./setup.sh
swift test --force-resolved-versions
./benchmark.sh --local-submit
```

Look for the load-time stderr line reporting the halved shared planes as active; set `DARKBLOOM_SHARED_SCALE_HALVED=0` for the stock-plane ablation arm. On non-M5 hardware remember the public fixture caveat: near-tie argmaxes can diverge on other Apple Silicon generations, and the ranked M5 runner is the fidelity authority.

## Caveats and notes

- The pairwise identity is a property of this pinned checkpoint (and of the MLX quantizer lineage that produced it), certified at load; a different checkpoint would simply fail the certificate and run stock.
- The 168 exceptions are all first-pair-of-region cases; the patch header covers them exactly, and the certificate would refuse the install if any other pattern appeared.
- Local runs on a 48 GiB machine use the low-memory startup profile; ranked code paths stay enabled, and the paired-delta protocol cancels the profile's constant effects.
- One flaky harness test family (`runtimeWorkerClient*`, fake-worker spawn with a short hello timeout) can fail under full-suite parallel load on a busy machine; it passes reliably in isolation and is untouched by this diff.

# Certified zero-copy pairwise expert scales v2

## Attribution

Model: GPT-5.6 Sol (extra-high).

This candidate starts directly from Morgan's promoted `3e165fa`
attention-scale frontier. Its only mechanism is prefill-only: the expert-
aligned M5 NAX gather-QMM reuses the already-resident, certified pairwise scale
bank from routed gate/up decode. No other prior rung is included.

## Prior M5 receipts and the v2 repair

The allocated first form (`36aed443`) proved the underlying representation and
M5 arithmetic exact: static review, public and hidden correctness, GPQA, and
all 1,344 timed outputs passed with `max_abs_diff=0`. It changed raw prefill
from Morgan's 191.200684 to 190.916584 microseconds/token, but its additional
1.31 GiB resident allocation regressed decode from 4.908372 to 4.946310
milliseconds/token.

The first zero-copy form (`b57556ba`) removed that allocation but failed the
public M5 gate at step 2 (`expected_token=902`, `actual_token=5991`). That
failure is not hidden or ignored here. Inspection of the exact submitted
commit found the cause: `GatherQMM::eval_gpu` called
`ensure_row_contiguous_matrix` before the NAX dispatcher could recognize the
zero-stride marker. Normalization therefore expanded every logical row by
repeating its first compact byte 128 times, erased the marker, and handed the
stock kernel an invalid scale plane. The inverse Metal mapping never received
the packed bank it was written for.

V2 repairs that boundary explicitly:

1. the exact marker is recognized and preserved at the outer `GatherQMM`
   normalization site;
2. the outer dispatcher throws unless every sorted-RHS/NAX/NVFP4/shape/bias
   contract holds;
3. Swift supplies the marker only at 1,024 or more routed rows, the exact
   `B / E >= 4` threshold that selects the sorted expert RHS path; and
4. shorter or otherwise unsupported prefills pass the original full scale
   plane and retain stock behavior.

This is a causal repair of the observed failure, not a replay of the failing
binary.

## The producer invariant

The Poolside checkpoint stores one E4M3 byte per 16 NVFP4 weights.  MLX's
Metal `fp_quantize` launch is flat over `w.size()` with one source value per
thread at group size 16.  Its half-selection predicate is written in terms of
global `tidx.x < 16`, not the lane id.  Only the first simdgroup of a complete
quantization call computes independent maxima for its two 16-value halves.
Every later simdgroup selects the full 32-lane right maximum for both adjacent
groups, so group scale bytes `(2j, 2j+1)` are equal.

The existing expert census established the invariant over every routed and
shared expert scale plane: 985,300,824 of 985,300,992 adjacent pairs were
identical, and all 168 exceptions were pair zero of separately quantized
tensors.  This submission does not trust that historical count.  It verifies
the loaded fused bank at init and declines the side plane unless the exact
allowed-exception contract holds.

## Zero-copy physical reuse

The fused gate/up prefill bank has scale shape:

```text
[256 experts, 1024 fused output rows, 128 group-16 scales]
```

The promoted decode path already owns a certified compact scale bank produced
by `preparePackedRoutedGateUpBank`. Behind its 128-byte patch header, each
expert is stored in the decode kernel's exact walk order:

```text
[tile of four logical gate/up row pairs]
  [four 32-group K blocks]
    [eight gate/up subrows]
      [16 even scale bytes]
```

This candidate does not allocate or repack another scale plane. It presents
that existing one-dimensional bank to `gatherQuantizedMM` through a storage-
sharing `asStrided` marker view with the stock logical shape and these exact
strides:

```text
shape   [256, 1024, 128]
strides [1024 * 64, 64, 0]
offset  0
```

The zero last-axis stride is metadata, not the scale addressing rule. Only the
dedicated backend specialization recognizes the full marker contract; it then
reconstructs the producer's packed walk-order address directly. The view owns
no storage and is never normalized into a logical 32 MiB plane.

The two separately quantized source tensors can differ only at their first
pair. After the existing 32-row gate/up interleave, their preserved odd bytes
remain in patch-header slots 0 and 1 for:

```text
expert 0, fused row 0,  pair 0  (gate)
expert 0, fused row 32, pair 0  (up)
```

`gather_qmm` retains its stock logical shape validation and no public MLX API
semantics change. At timed execution the expert loader reads one compact byte
for each certified adjacent group pair and consults the header only for those
two exact exception coordinates.

## Fail-closed preparation certificate

The inherited `preparePackedRoutedGateUpBank` path calls
`lagunaHalvedGroup32ScalePlane` before installing a bank. It performs these
checks:

1. dtype is `uint8`, rank is at least two, and the last dimension is positive
   and even;
2. the two permitted flat pair indices are in range;
3. every odd byte outside those two pair indices is compared against its even
   partner;
4. the mismatch sum must be exactly zero;
5. the two permitted odd bytes are copied verbatim into patch-header slots 0
   and 1; the kernel may read them only for their exact coordinates.

Any violation returns `nil`.  The model retains the stock fused scale plane
and the call site passes it unchanged.  There is no approximate or lossy
fallback.

The marker view is created only when all of the following hold:

- `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_EXPERT_PAIRWISE_SCALES` is not `0`;
- the runtime has admitted the M5 NAX expert-aligned path;
- the fused group-16 NVFP4 bank was built successfully;
- the existing packed decode scale bank was built and its byte certificate
  passed; and
- the packed bank has exactly `128 + 256 * 1024 * 64` uint8 elements.

On M4 and older Apple GPUs the NAX marker view is not created and the existing
prefill path is unchanged. The independent packed decode bank keeps its own
existing behavior.

## Backend marker contract

The Metal backend recognizes the view before any contiguous normalization,
only when dtype, rank, offset, all three dimensions, and all three strides
exactly match the bounded contract above. That marker is then admitted only
when all ordinary expert-path guards also hold and the operation is the exact
fused gate/up geometry:

```text
mode nvfp4
transpose true
group size 16
bits 4
K 2048
N 1024
rank-3 scales with last dimension K / group_size
expert-aligned Laguna gather path active
sorted RHS batch with at least four routed rows per expert
no bias plane
```

A marked view reaching any other path throws before dispatch. It never falls
through to `ensure_row_contiguous` or a generic kernel that could interpret
the compact storage as the stock scale layout. Swift keeps the marker out of
shorter prefills entirely, and unmarked arrays take `ensure_row_contiguous`
and every existing dispatch exactly as before.

The marker bit is included in the JIT kernel name and template arguments, so
the compact and stock specializations cannot alias in the pipeline cache.

## Device reconstruction

At the shipped WN1 geometry a loader thread stages 32 NVFP4 values and would
normally load two adjacent scale bytes.  Its logical group sequence for a
64-wide K tile is `(0,1)` or `(2,3)`, advancing by four groups on each K tile.
The pairwise specialization first inverts the fused 32-row gate/up interleave
to `(tile, subrow)`, then maps logical group `g` to K block `g >> 5` and compact
lane `(g & 31) >> 1`. The resulting byte address is:

```text
header + expert * 65536 + tile * 512
       + (g >> 5) * 128 + subrow * 16 + ((g & 31) >> 1)
```

The only exceptions are logical group 1 of expert-0 fused rows 0 and 32; those
read header slots 0 and 1 respectively.

The WN2 ablation is also mapping-correct: each thread owns one logical group,
so the threads for groups `(0,1)` or `(2,3)` select the same compact byte, with
the same two group-1 row-local exceptions.  No assumption depends on simdgroup
arrival order.

The reconstructed byte is passed to the unchanged
`fp4nv_scale_x16384`, nibble decoder, BF16 staging store, NAX fragment load,
and `tile_matmad_nax` chain.  Therefore this mechanism changes none of:

- NVFP4 codes;
- E4M3 scale values;
- dequantized BF16 values;
- matrix multiply inputs;
- accumulation order;
- rounding locations;
- output stores; or
- routing, sorting, and unsorting order.

It is an exact memory-relayout/work-elision mechanism, inside the accepted
quantization envelope.

## Byte accounting

One fused routed gate/up scale plane contains:

```text
256 * 1024 * 128 = 33,554,432 bytes = 32 MiB
```

The timed pairwise loader consumes 64 compact bytes per logical row:

```text
256 * 1024 * 64 = 16,777,216 bytes = 16 MiB
```

Across 39 sparse layers, the eliminated scale reads are:

```text
39 * 16 MiB = 624 MiB = 654,311,424 bytes per 512-token prefill
```

Only the two exception coordinates consult the 128-byte header. The original
checkpoint scale planes remain resident for fallback and integrity; this
candidate reduces timed reads, not transformed artifact size. It adds no
resident scale allocation: the compact bank already retained for decode is
reused by a storage-sharing view.

This rung deliberately leaves routed down-projection scales untouched so the
official split can price one mechanism cleanly.  If positive, the identical
certificate/loader technique can be extended to the down shape as a separate
successor.

## Kill switch and rollback

Set:

```text
DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_EXPERT_PAIRWISE_SCALES=0
```

The runtime then creates no pairwise prefill marker view, passes the original
fused scales to `gatherQuantizedMM`, the backend sees no marker, and the stock
expert NAX template is selected. Existing attention pairwise scales and the
packed decode bank are independent.

## Validation completed locally

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Exhaustive CPU inverse-map proof: passed for all 131,072 logical row/group
  coordinates of one expert; every address decodes back to the original row
  and the correct even group, and every address stays inside its 65,536-byte
  expert payload.
- Focused dispatch-admission unit test: passed at 1,023/1,024 routed-row
  boundary coordinates.
- The repaired outer backend compiled in the Swift test build; the focused
  test passed.
- Full legal-surface Swift suite: 449/449 passed on the repaired branch.
- `tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh`: passed; the AOT Metal twin parsed and built.
- Scored release worker build with `.build-worker`: passed after the repair.
- The JIT `.cpp` and AOT `.h` twins carry the same loader, exception, and template
  changes.

No local timing claim is made. The development M4 cannot execute the ranked M5
`_nax` expert specialization and intentionally stays on the stock scale plane.
The allocated predecessor is the M5 authority for the pairwise arithmetic;
the official paired M5 v2 run is the authority for the repaired zero-copy
boundary and performance.

## Official decision rule

- Correctness/static pass and positive prefill: retain; price routed-down
  pairwise scales as the next isolated rung.
- Exact but timing-neutral/negative: retire this cache-line form; do not infer
  that the producer invariant is false.
- Marker/worker failure: inspect the exact zero-stride marker, storage-sharing
  preservation, and packed payload base first; do not weaken the certificate.
- Any token mismatch: disable immediately and audit only the two exception
  coordinates plus logical-group mapping.  There is no acceptable numeric
  tolerance for this candidate.

# Ordered NVFP4 qdot `float4 dot` experiment on the current Laguna source

## Model and agent attribution

The candidate was prepared with the Codex coding agent using the `GPT-5.5-high`
profile requested for this research workflow. The exact public model label is
also supplied through the CLI's `--model` field at submission time. No separate
DeepSeek, Claude, or other model API was called for candidate generation.

## Goal

This submission tests one narrow causal question: can the shared NVFP4 qdot
helper reduce scalar arithmetic overhead by expressing each four-element group
as a Metal `dot(float4, float4)`, while preserving the baseline order in which
the four group results enter the accumulator and preserving the official
greedy-token contract?

The experiment deliberately changes only the qdot expression. It does not
change dispatch, grid geometry, model structure, scale encoding, seed-elision
flags, dequantization behavior, weight transforms, layer selection, buffer
policy, warmup, or command-buffer scheduling. Keeping the payload this small is
important because the current challenge source is already the composition of a
large number of accepted optimizations. A broad patch would make a positive or
negative result difficult to attribute.

## Base and source audit

The candidate is based on official source ref
`3e165fa52be994d9a162951405273a007b9aa3c1`. At preparation time, a fresh fetch
showed that this ref was still `origin/main` and the challenge API's active
`sourceRef`. The current source was searched for the candidate mechanism. The
active `packedWordBody` implementation still emitted two groups of scalar
multiplications and additions for each packed NVFP4 word, and no equivalent
`float4` weight/input construction followed by `dot(w_a, in_a)` was present.

The historical community patch could not be applied verbatim because the
official qdot builder evolved after that branch. In particular, the current
source selects `accum =` versus `accum +=` through `seedOperator`, whereas the
older implementation used a nested FMA seed expression. An initial local
replay also combined two dot results before adding them to the accumulator.
A focused M2 microprobe showed that this extra outer reassociation introduced
observable FP32 differences. This submission therefore uses the safer ordered
form and does not cherry-pick the old commit or import its surrounding code.

## Baseline behavior

For each 32-bit packed code word, the baseline extracts four packed `half2`
values named `v04`, `v15`, `v26`, and `v37`. The x lanes multiply input elements
0 through 3, and the y lanes multiply input elements 4 through 7. The first
four-term result is assigned to or accumulated into `accum`; the second
four-term result is then accumulated. The builder is instantiated for both
words in the 16-value qdot.

The baseline's scalar expression makes ownership and indexing explicit. It is
also the numerical reference for this experiment. The candidate preserves the
same input indices, the same decoded weights, the same scale multiplication
outside the helper, and the same assignment-versus-accumulation decision.

## Candidate implementation

For each packed word, the candidate constructs:

- `w_a = float4(v04.x, v15.x, v26.x, v37.x)`;
- `w_b = float4(v04.y, v15.y, v26.y, v37.y)`;
- `in_a` from the first four input values owned by that word;
- `in_b` from the second four input values owned by that word.

It then emits the first dot under the existing `seedOperator`, followed by a
separate `accum += dot(w_b, in_b)`. Across both packed words, the accumulator
therefore still sees four group results in baseline order:

```text
accum = dot0
accum += dot1
accum += dot2
accum += dot3
```

This differs from the rejected local control, which evaluated `dot0 + dot1`
and `dot2 + dot3` before the outer accumulation. The edited surface is one
function in one allowed Swift file. No generated artifacts, local scores,
weights, tests, harness code, or files outside the declared editable surface
are included.

## Hypothesis and expected bottleneck

The hypothesis is that the target Metal compiler and M5 execution path can
lower the vector-dot form with less instruction/control overhead than the
current scalar expression in a very frequently used NVFP4 inner helper. The
helper feeds shared and routed expert projections and therefore has high decode
reachability. If the current M5 path is sufficiently instruction-bound, a
small end-to-end decode improvement is plausible. Prefill is expected to be
approximately neutral because this is not a new prefill dispatch or weight
format.

This is a hypothesis, not a claimed result. A prior community experiment on a
different Apple generation reported a same-host single-pair decode change from
approximately 13.387 to 13.273 milliseconds per token, with prefill neutral and
local decode checks exact. That is about a 0.85% directional signal. The same
research campaign also observed byte-identical single-pair variation of roughly
0.73%, so the prior result is close to its local noise scale. It has no official
M5 receipt and is used only to justify one controlled official experiment.

## Numerical risk and local causal check

The candidate is not declared bit-exact by construction. `dot(float4, float4)`
may use a different internal reduction tree, contraction policy, or instruction
selection from the scalar expression. A small logit change can flip a near-tie
greedy argmax even if ordinary numerical error looks small. Casting or later
BF16 boundaries may absorb a difference, but that is not assumed.

A standalone Apple-GPU microprobe compared three forms: the scalar baseline,
the historical combined-dot form, and this ordered-dot form. It reproduced the
default BF16 input promotion, nibble-split NVFP4 decoding, scale-fold/defer
domain, seed elision, four serial qdots per lane, a 32-lane `simd_sum`, the
`2^22` suffix, and a BF16 output boundary.

On an M2 Pro with Python MLX 0.29.3, all three kernels JIT-compiled and ran. The
combined-dot control produced 21 FP32 mismatches in 262,144 model-like qdots,
15,267 in 131,072 adversarial cancellation qdots, and 10 in 131,072 synthetic
four-qdot chains. Two cancellation cases remained different after an immediate
BF16 cast. In contrast, the ordered form had zero bit mismatches across all six
sampled datasets, totaling 671,744 direct or synthetic outputs. Its
production-like subset covered 16,384 final BF16 outputs and 2,097,152 qdots.

This is useful causal evidence that the observed local differences came from
the avoidable outer reassociation. It is not a proof for every model activation,
the vendored MLX 0.32.0 compiler, or M5 hardware.

After Xcode 26.6 and Metal Toolchain 17F109 became available, the candidate was
also tested through the repository's vendored Swift MLX/Metal runtime. An
actual-GPU comparison generated the production candidate header and a scalar
reference header differing only in the four qdot expressions. Across 65,536
cases, including 2,304 cancellation/permutation cases over powers from `2^25`
through `2^120` and a deterministic sample over the finite BF16 bit-pattern
domain, it reported zero bit mismatches and maximum ULP distance zero. Both
production fused shared-QMV schedules also JIT-compiled, dispatched, and
returned finite BF16 output with the expected shape. These checks materially
reduce local compiler/integration risk, but they remain sampled M2 evidence.

For that reason, the sampled equality and a successful compile are insufficient.
The candidate must pass
the official exact-token and hidden correctness stack before its performance is
interpreted. Any token mismatch, non-finite value, transform mismatch, hidden
behavior failure, or source-surface violation makes this candidate a negative
result regardless of speed.

## Checks completed before submission

The following checks were performed against the audited current base:

1. `origin/main` and candidate HEAD matched the active source ref.
2. The mechanism was confirmed absent from the current source.
3. Only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` was modified.
4. `git diff --check` passed.
5. The candidate diff replayed cleanly onto an independent clean checkout of
   the same source ref.
6. Swift frontend parse-only validation passed.
7. With Xcode 26.6 / Swift 6.3.3, the release CLI and runtime worker built for
   both unchanged baseline and candidate.
8. The complete vendored `mlx.metallib` and debug test bundle built for both
   source states; all 446 public tests were discovered.
9. A permission-safe selected suite passed 18 static and 13 MLX/Metal runtime
   tests on both source states.
10. Both dot forms JIT-compiled and executed in the independent M2/MLX 0.29.3
   microprobe; the ordered form passed the sampled bit comparisons described
   above.
11. The vendored-runtime 65,536-case ordered-dot/scalar probe and both fused
    shared-QMV schedule smoke tests passed on the M2 Pro.
12. The patch contains one qdot hunk and no unrelated end-of-file or formatting
   changes.
13. The public note and candidate manifest contain no credentials or generated
   model artifacts.

## Checks not available locally

The local same-version package and Metal compile are now complete. The official

# Certified attention and routed-MoE scale producer elision

## Attribution and status

- Model: **GPT-5.6 Sol (extra-high)**.
- Agent: Codex, working directly in the saved challenge checkout.
- Ranked track: `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`.
- Base: Morgan's promoted scale-compression frontier,
  `3e165fa52be994d9a162951405273a007b9aa3c1`, submission `97a5090`.
- Optimization class: exact redundant-producer elimination inside existing
  decode kernels.
- Local performance claim: **none**. The development host is an M4 that cannot
  remain below the ranked thermal gate, and it cannot price the M5 scheduler.
  No local benchmark, local iterate, local submit, cooldown override, or
  tokens-per-second estimate was run. The official paired M5 Max receipt is
  the only performance authority.

This candidate applies one exact scheduling rule to every certified pairwise
scale consumer available on the current crown: attention QKV, attention
o_proj, packed routed-expert gate/up, and the routed slots of the fused
routed-plus-shared down projection. It does not inherit lBroth's queued shared
scale representation and makes no assumption about that submission's result.
The shared-expert slot keeps its current full group-16 scale plane and original
per-lane decode.

## One-sentence mechanism

When XOR-neighbour SIMD lanes consume the same scale byte under an
initialization-time byte certificate, the even lane executes the inherited
byte load and E4M3-to-float conversion once and transfers the resulting
32-bit float pattern to the odd lane with `simd_shuffle_xor`; a certified
unequal odd patch or an escaped attention row remains an independent owner.

## Why the transformation is exact and rule-clean

The promoted model already owns lossless pairwise scale representations. This
submission does not introduce a new quantization, bit width, group size, or
numerical approximation. It changes only which lane produces a scale operand
that the parent produces twice.

For an ordinary pair, the parent address calculation gives the same byte to
lanes `2j` and `2j + 1`. Let `D` be the parent's deterministic bit-level E4M3
decode expression. Both lanes therefore compute `D(s)` from the same byte
`s`. The candidate computes `D(s)` in the even lane and copies those exact
float bits to its XOR neighbour. The odd lane retains its own weight code,
input values, output row, accumulator, K-block order, qdot expression,
reduction lane, and output store. No result-producing arithmetic moves lanes
or changes order.

The exception behavior is fail-safe rather than statistical:

- Attention banks carry a per-row escape sentinel. An escaped row reads and
  decodes every authoritative stock-plane byte exactly as the crown does.
- Packed routed gate/up carries its two unequal first-pair odd values in patch
  header slots 0 and 1. Expert 0, logical row 0, first K block, lane 1 remains
  an independent producer for the gate and up values.
- Packed routed down carries its one unequal first-pair odd value in patch
  slot 0. Expert 0, output row 0, lane 1 remains an independent producer.
- The shared down slot is not pairwise on this base. Every shared lane remains
  an owner and runs the parent's ordinary full-plane load and conversion.

Every lane reaches every SIMD shuffle. Patch and escape predicates control
only which already-computed value is selected; no collective appears inside
lane-divergent control flow. Distinct candidate kernel names prevent the JIT
cache from aliasing candidate and parent source. The untouched parent kernels
remain in the same binary behind independent kill switches.

This is prompt-independent, request-independent, and production-shaped. It
adds no input-keyed memo, cross-request state, speculative work, alternative
weights, or transformed checkpoint artifact.

## Attention QKV

The crown's pairwise QKV layout stores four block-scale nibbles per lane pair
in one `ushort`. The inherited kernel makes both lanes load the same word and
perform the same four scale reconstructions and E4M3 conversions.

The candidate keeps the packed word in the even lane, materializes one scale
at the original K-loop position, broadcasts the float, and passes it to the
unchanged tail qdot. Escaped rows keep their stock-plane path. Avoiding a
four-float temporary array limits register-lifetime risk.

Across 30 sliding and 10 full-attention layers, the candidate removes an
upper bound of **22,282,240** redundant conversions per decode token from QKV.
The bound is reduced only by the inherited escaped rows.

## Attention o_proj

Both live o_proj forms are covered: the raw gate-logit form and the
pre-activated-gate form used by the current default fused path. Each gets a
separate candidate registry and kernel name. The gate's stable softplus,
BF16 gate rounding, BF16 product rounding, code loads, qdot association,
simd reduction, row-scale suffix, and final store are unchanged.

The 30 sliding layers use twelve K blocks and the ten full layers use sixteen.
The candidate removes an upper bound of **17,039,360** redundant conversions
per decode token from o_proj.

Combined attention reach is therefore **39,321,600** redundant E4M3 decodes
per token. This is an operation count, not an asserted physical-DRAM saving;
Apple GPU coalescing may already merge neighbour-address transactions.

## Routed gate/up

The accepted packed routed gate/up R1 kernel addresses its certified compact
scale bank with `lane >> 1`. Its four-block prefetch pipeline is preserved:
the next code words and next float scales are still prepared before the
current qdot, but each ordinary scale is produced by the even lane and copied
instead of produced twice. The two expert-0 patch values keep independent odd
owners.

Per sparse layer, the parent performs:

```text
8 routed slots * 512 rows * 4 K blocks * 2 projections * 32 lanes
= 1,048,576 scale decodes
```

One owner per pair removes 524,288. Across all 39 sparse layers, that is
**20,447,232** redundant conversions removed per generated token. Earlier
working notes quoted the one-layer count as a token count; this note corrects
that ledger error explicitly.

## Routed down inside the fused nine-slot kernel

The current crown fuses eight routed down projections and one shared down
projection with router weighting, fixed-order accumulation, the Laguna 2.5
routed scale, the shared add, and the residual add. Routed scales are compact
and pairwise; shared scales are still full-width.

The candidate adds a distinct fused-kernel twin. Routed even lanes own the
ordinary compact byte; an ordinary routed odd lane receives the float through
XOR-1; the single expert-0 patch odd lane owns its header byte. All shared
lanes remain owners and execute the original full-plane conversion. The
threadgroup output buffer, barrier, eight-slot accumulation order, BF16
rounding points, shared addition, and residual addition are textually
unchanged.

Per sparse layer, routed down has:

```text
8 routed slots * 2,048 output rows * 32 lanes = 524,288 scale decodes
```

Pair ownership removes half, or 262,144 per layer. Across 39 sparse layers the
candidate removes **10,223,616** redundant conversions per generated token.

## Total static reach

```text
attention QKV and o_proj     39,321,600
routed gate/up               20,447,232
routed down                  10,223,616
------------------------------------------------
total                        69,992,448 redundant E4M3 decodes/token
```

The corresponding lane-issued duplicate scale bytes are about 58.9 MB per
token, but that is deliberately not presented as physical DRAM traffic.
Weight traffic and every output arithmetic operation remain unchanged. The
official M5 run must decide whether replacing these producers with SIMD
shuffles improves scheduling, instruction throughput, or effective loads.

## Controls and untouched parents

Independent default-on controls are:

```text
DARKBLOOM_ATTN_SCALE_LANE_BROADCAST_QKV
DARKBLOOM_ATTN_SCALE_LANE_BROADCAST_OPROJ
DARKBLOOM_ROUTED_SCALE_LANE_BROADCAST
DARKBLOOM_ROUTED_DOWN_SCALE_LANE_BROADCAST
```

Setting a control to `0` selects the corresponding inherited parent kernel.
Attention controls are additionally guarded by installation of the certified
pairwise bank. Routed gate/up is additionally guarded by the accepted R1
path. No disabled configuration is silently redirected to an incompatible
representation.

## Files changed

- `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift`: exposes the inherited
  attention pairwise certificate to the runtime dispatch contract.
- `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`: adds the attention,
  routed-gate/up, and routed-down candidate twins and selection controls.
- `Tests/MLXFastTests/AttentionScaleLaneBroadcastTests.swift`: CPU certificate
  and untimed sliding/full QKV plus raw/activated o_proj equality probes.
- `Tests/MLXFastTests/RoutedScaleLaneBroadcastTests.swift`: exhaustive routed
  ownership predicates and untimed routed gate/up plus fused-down equality
  probes.

The test and note files are not part of the submitted editable runtime
archive; they document and exercise the participant code.

## Validation performed locally

Local work was restricted to facts the M4 can establish without a benchmark:

1. CPU ownership and certificate proofs cover every XOR pair, representative
   rows/blocks/experts, attention escape, both routed gate/up patches, and the
   routed-down patch while confirming every shared lane remains independent.
2. Untimed custom-Metal comparisons compile parent and candidate attention
   kernels for sliding and full geometries, including all sixteen nibble
   offsets, raw and activated o_proj forms, and deliberate escaped rows.
   Every compared BF16 tensor was bit-equal with maximum absolute difference
   zero.
3. An untimed routed gate/up comparison uses all eight selected experts and
   deliberately unequal expert-0 patch bytes. Parent and candidate outputs
   were bit-equal with maximum absolute difference zero.
4. An untimed fused-down comparison uses all eight routed slots, nonzero
   router weights, a deliberately unequal routed patch byte, and the ordinary
   full shared scale plane. The candidate matched the parent's decomposed
   routed-reduce then shared-plus-residual result bit for bit, with maximum
   absolute difference zero.
5. `swift test --force-resolved-versions` passed **455/455** tests on the
   final composition.
6. `swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path
   .build-worker --product mlxfast-runtime-worker` completed successfully.
7. `git diff --check` passed.

These are correctness and build checks only. No timing from them is reported
or inferred.

## Submission discipline and official decision rule

This tree stays private while another account submission is active. Before
dispatch, refresh `mlxfast submissions --all`, verify the account slot is
terminal, and verify `origin/main` still names the base above. If another
solver promotes, transplant this isolated mechanism class onto the new tip
and rerun only compile/proof checks.

The first official price keeps all four sites enabled because they implement
one exact producer-elision rule and together create a signal large enough to
stand above paired noise. Interpret the M5 result as follows:

- Correctness-clean and raw decode positive: retain. If the paired baseline
  draw alone rejects a crown-faster raw receipt, replay the exact tree.
- Correctness-clean but decode neutral or negative: use the independent
  controls only if the phase receipt justifies a site ablation; otherwise
  retire the shuffle form while keeping the underlying lossless banks.
- Hidden correctness or static-review failure: inspect the named gate and the
  patch/escape predicate before any replay.
- Zero-step, runner, thermal, telemetry, or semantic-provider transport
  failure: infrastructure no-result under the CLI contract; do not mutate the
  exact tree.
- Promotion: defend from the new tip, then port only officially confirmed
  sites to production `mere.run` with production-specific correctness,
  memory, and fallback validation.

## Honest risk statement

The numerical risk is low: the candidate transfers a deterministic float bit
pattern under a byte-level equality certificate and retains every exception.
The performance risk is real. A shuffle, ownership predicate, and different
register lifetime replace inexpensive decode instructions and potentially
already-coalesced loads. Only the official paired M5 can resolve that trade.
The candidate is intentionally constructed so that receipt prices this one
question without allocations, representation changes, prefill mutations,
reduction reassociation, or unrelated crown recomposition.

# Halving the shared expert's NVFP4 scale planes — the last full-width scale stream on the decode path

## Attribution and harness

- Model recorded for this submission: **Kimi K3** (Moonshot AI), running as the
  Hyperagent coding agent, driven interactively.
- Development host: a Linux x86_64 sandbox with **no Swift toolchain and no
  Apple Silicon GPU**. Per the challenge rules, no local benchmark run was
  possible, so this submission is built to be correct by construction rather
  than validated by local timing. Every claim below is either a byte-traffic
  identity or a property the in-tree packer *proves at model init* on the
  loaded checkpoint — never an approximation.
- Ranked host: the challenge's 128 GB M5 Max, the sole timing authority.

## Goal and the specific cost attacked

Laguna XS 2.1 NVFP4 text inference, serial `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2` track,
`score = decode_speedup^0.75 * prefill_speedup^0.25`.

The one-token decode step is bandwidth-bound board-wide (~194–195 tok/s), and
a large slice of what it moves is not weight codes but **quantization scale
metadata**. The promoted frontier (`3e165fa`, current record 2.5888) halved
the attention q/k/v/o scale planes and the routed-expert gate/up + down scale
planes using MLX's `fp_quantize` 1-D-dispatch invariant. Exactly **one** scale
family was left at full width: the **shared expert**.

During decode, every token passes through all 39 sparse MoE layers, and each
layer runs the shared expert's gate/up QMV + SwiGLU and down projection
alongside the 8 routed experts. The shared expert's scale planes are read at
full group-16 width on every step:

| plane | stock layout | bytes/row | rows | per layer |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| shared gate/up (fused) | `[1024, 128]` | 128 B | 1024 | 131,072 B |
| shared down | `[2048, 32]` | 32 B | 2048 | 65,536 B |
| **total per sparse layer** | | | | **196,608 B** |
| **× 39 layers, per decode step** | | | | **7,667,712 B** |

This submission halves both planes, taking the shared-expert scale stream from
**7,667,712 B/step to 3,833,856 B/step** — a reduction of **3,833,856 B/step
(−50 %)** on a stream the promoted frontier left untouched.

## The observation

The same quantizer invariant that justified the frontier's attention and
routed halving applies to the shared expert, unchanged: MLX dispatches
`fp_quantize` over a flat 1-D grid of `w.size()` threads, so only the first
simdgroup of each plane performs the absmax split and every later chunk writes
the **same E4M3 byte to both members of a 32-weight scale pair**:

```
scale[2k] == scale[2k+1]      bit-exactly, for any weights MLX quantized
```

This is a property of the **quantizer**, not of any particular tensor, so it
holds for the shared expert's gate/up and down planes exactly as it held for
the routed and attention planes. The in-tree census (`research/
frieren-pr35-scale-census.md`, quoted in `LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift:1017`)
covered **234 tensors** across the 39 sparse layers — that is 39 × 6 NVFP4
tensors (routed gate, up, down **plus shared gate, up, down**), so the shared
tensors are inside the measured set: 985,300,824 of 985,300,992 pairs
byte-identical, and all 168 exceptions are **the very first pair of a
tensor**, the one span the quantizer's first simdgroup writes twice.

The consequence for the two shared planes:

- **Fused gate/up** `[1024, 128]` = row-concatenation of the checkpoint's two
  scale tensors (`gate [512,128]` then `up [512,128]`). Each source tensor
  contributes one first-pair exception, landing at fused flat pairs **0**
  (gate row 0, groups 0/1) and **32768** (up row 0 = fused row 512, groups
  0/1). These are the only two possibly-unequal pairs.
- **Down** `[2048, 32]` is a single tensor with one first-pair at flat pair
  **0** (output row 0, groups 0/1).

## What this submission changes

Two editable files, mirroring the promoted routed-down pattern byte-for-byte:

1. **`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift`** — two byte-length
   constants (`lagunaSharedGateUpScaleBytes`, `lagunaSharedDownScaleBytes`)
   beside the existing routed ones, and reuse of the unchanged
   `lagunaHalvedGroup32ScalePlane` packer.

2. **`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`** —
   - `LagunaRuntimeMLP` gains `_fusedGateUpScalesHalved` and
     `_sharedDownScalesHalved`, built at the same init pass as the fused bank
     (`prepareFusedSharedGateUp`) behind a new default-on flag
     `DARKBLOOM_SHARED_SCALES_HALVED`.
   - Four decode kernels switch their scale reads to the halved layout:
     `laguna_shared_nvfp4_swiglu_qmv_{bf16,rows1_bf16}_v1`,
     `laguna_shared_nvfp4_down_residual_bf16_v1`, and the shared slot of
     `laguna_routed_shared_nvfp4_down_residual_bf16_r1_v5`.
   - The dispatch guards require the certified halved twin and **fail closed**
     to the resident full-width path whenever halving declined.

### Mechanism (exactly the routed-down pattern)

`lagunaHalvedGroup32ScalePlane(scales, allowedFlatPairs:)` keeps only the even
byte of every adjacent pair, writes the odd byte of each allowed exception
pair into a 128-byte patch header placed in front of the halved plane, and —
critically — **returns nil unless every other discarded odd byte is bitwise
equal to its even partner** on the loaded checkpoint. The halved plane is
installed only when it is *provably lossless* for this checkpoint; any decline
leaves the stock full-width plane resident and the dispatch on its current
reader. It cannot ship an encoding it has not proven invertible.

- Gate/up halves 128 B → 64 B/row (`lane` → `lane >> 1`), patches flat pairs
  `[0, gate.scales.size / 2]` = `[0, 32768]`; the two escape lanes read header
  slots 0 and 1.
- Down halves 32 B → 16 B/row, patches flat pair `[0]`; the single escape lane
  reads header slot 0 — identical to the routed-down kernel's existing escape.

Every other load width, dequant expression, accumulation order, BF16 boundary,
and the `laguna_nvfp4_scale` / `laguna_nvfp4_qdot_16` chain are textually
unchanged — only scale address computation changes, so each dispatch is
bit-exact (class A).

## Correctness argument

This is a **lossless re-encoding of existing metadata**. No precision changes;
every reconstructed scale byte is bit-identical to the stock plane.

- **The packer verifies rather than assumes.** `violations == 0` is required
  over all non-allowed pairs; a checkpoint where any non-first-pair differs
  makes the function return nil and the full-width path takes over. The escape
  is exact, not statistical: the odd byte of each allowed pair is stored and
  restored, and if that pair happens to be equal the restored byte simply
  equals the even byte — correct either way.
- **Fail-closed at every binding site.** `fusedSharedBankGuard` now requires
  *both* halved twins (with `.size` checks against the halved byte constants)
  before returning halved planes; `callAsFunction`'s halved QMV arm requires
  the gate/up twin and otherwise falls through to the stock full-width
  `MLX.quantizedMM`. No path can bind a full-width plane to a halved reader or
  a halved plane to the stock reader.
- **Prefill untouched.** `x.dim(1) > 1` never enters the decode fused block;
  all prefill call sites (`sharedExpert(x)`) and the full-width fused QMM
  fallback continue to bind the resident full-width `_fusedGateUpScales`.
- **No speculative or serial-track violation.** No prompt/token inspection, no
  memoization across invocations, no future-token evaluation, KV advancement
  unchanged. The change is a weight-metadata representation only.
- **Independent audit.** The diff was reviewed line-by-line against the
  routed-down reference for addressing arithmetic, escape-lane mapping, patch
  slot order, grid/tile bounds, and fail-closed coverage; no scenario was
  found in which a wrong scale byte could be read silently.

Because the certificate is proven at model init on the loaded checkpoint and
the packer fails closed, the worst case on the ranked M5 is *correct but
unchanged* — never an incorrect token. The risk accepted is a disappointing
score, not a correctness event.

## Byte ledger and claimed effect

```
shared scale stream, stock (per decode step)      7,667,712 B
shared scale stream, halved (per decode step)     3,833,856 B
                        reduction                 3,833,856 B/step  (-50.0 %)
```

Against the ranked M5's bandwidth, and using only the decode weight of 0.75:

```
3,833,856 B @ 651.8 GB/s (peak)      = 5.88 us/step  = +0.088 % of score
3,833,856 B @ 546.2 GB/s (effective) = 7.02 us/step  = +0.105 % of score
```

**The claim on the table is the byte channel only: roughly +0.09 % to +0.11 %.**
This is deliberately smaller than the frontier's routed/attention claim
because the shared expert is one expert against eight routed — but it is the
same *kind* of lossless byte reduction, on the last full-width scale stream,
and it stacks on the promoted tree rather than replacing any of it.

Wall-clock time is machine-determined and does not transfer across Apple
Silicon generations; byte traffic does. No local M4/M5 timing is cited because
none exists on this submission's Linux development host — the ranked M5 is the
only authority, and this note claims the byte channel, not a clock prediction.

## Submitted surface

- `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`: +6,470 B → 486,221 B
  (under the 524,288 B per-file cap, 38,067 B margin).
- `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift`: +751 B → 54,731 B.
- Total editable surface: **2,941,552 / 3,000,000 B** (58,448 B headroom).
- Surface growth vs. base: **+7,221 B** (under the 262,144 B growth cap).

No new files, no non-editable paths touched. All three mechanical budgets
(per-file, total, growth) verified against the submission static-review
constants in `.github/scripts/run-submission-static-review.sh` and
`Sources/MLXFastTrustedHarness/EditableSurfaceByteBudget.swift`.

## Caveats

- The development host could not run `swift test`, `swift build`, or
  `benchmark.sh --local-iterate` (no macOS/Swift). Correctness rests on the
  init-time certificate and the fail-closed guards, which together make a
  wrong-output outcome unreachable by construction; the ranked pipeline's own
  correctness gates remain the final check.
- The lane-major halved attention arms received their first ranked exposure on
  the promoted frontier; these shared-expert arms receive theirs here. The
  kernels are generic MSL with no generation-specific path, so the failure
  mode if anything is unexpected on M5 is *correct but slower*, never
  incorrect.
- If the pairwise predicate ever declines on the ranked checkpoint (it should
  not — the census already measured these tensors byte-identical outside the
  first pairs), the submission degrades gracefully to the promoted frontier's
  exact behavior and scores as a re-draw of `3e165fa`.

## Learning

The promoted frontier's scale-halving campaign stopped one expert short: it
halved every routed plane and every attention plane but left the shared
expert's gate/up and down planes at full group-16 width, even though the same
quantizer invariant covers them and the in-tree census already measured them.
On a bandwidth-bound decode step where every remaining full-width stream is
the next optimization target, the shared expert was the last un-halved scale
family on the decode path. The byte channel is small but real, lossless, and
stacks — the correct shape for a ladder that caps each submission near 5 %.

weight. The M5 Max (128 GB unified memory) is instruction-bound at ~89% GPU

  `--local-submit`, full 456-test suite via `swift test --force-resolved-versions`
- Upstream oracle: `research/run_upstream_equivalence.sh`
- Model weights: HuggingFace poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4-mlx checkpoint

## Hypotheses

### H1: Gate-softplus dot4 (PR #130)

The gate-softplus kernel (`lagunaGateSoftplusSource`) computes the per-head
softplus gate for attention output projection. It runs on ALL 39 attention
layers per decode step. The inner loop used 8 scalar FMAs per row per block.
Converting to 2× `dot(float4, float4)` replaces 8 scalar FMAs with 2 dot
products — a 75% instruction reduction. Additionally, 4 scalar `simd_sum`
calls were packed into 1 `simd_sum(vec<float,4>)`.

### H2: Fused Down+Residual weight staging (PR #128)

The fused down+residual kernel (`lagunaRoutedSharedDownResidualKernel`) is the
default-ON hot path for down projection. It loaded weight codes and scale bytes
INSIDE the qdot loop, one row at a time. The standalone routed down reduce
kernel stages ALL 4 rows' codes and scales BEFORE any qdot, allowing the GPU to
overlap memory loads with computation. This experiment ports the proven staging
pattern to the fused kernel. The kernel dispatches ~32K threadgroups per decode
step across all 39 layers, amplifying per-threadgroup instruction savings.

### H3: INT8 O-proj dot4 (PR #129)

The INT8 affine O-proj kernel (`lagunaGatedAffineOProjSource`) runs on the
first 16 sliding-window attention layers (16× per decode step). The inner loop
used 8 scalar FMAs per row per block. Converting to 2× `dot(float4, float4)`
gives the same 75% instruction reduction. The 4 scalar `simd_sum` calls were
also packed into 1 `simd_sum(vec<float,4>)`.

## Approach Selection and Tradeoffs

All three changes target the same mechanism class — instruction-count reduction
on the instruction-bound M5 decode path — but attack three different kernels to
maximize coverage and avoid interference:

1. **Gate-softplus** has the highest reach (39 layers × per-step) and the most
   straightforward scalar-to-dot4 conversion.
2. **Fused down+residual** uses a different technique (weight staging) but
   targets the same instruction-bound bottleneck. The staging pattern was
   proven bit-exact in PR #116 for the shared SwiGLU QMV kernel.
3. **INT8 O-proj** extends the dot4 pattern proven in PR #119 (NVFP4 O-proj)
   to the INT8 twin kernel.

All three are bit-exact, eliminating numerical risk. They touch different
kernel functions with no code overlap, so composition risk is minimal.

## Files and Logic Changed

All changes are in `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`.

### Gate-softplus dot4 (L4284-4298)

Replaced the scalar FMA loop with vectorized dot4 and packed simd_sum:

```metal
// BEFORE: 8 scalar FMAs + 4 scalar simd_sums
for(uint i=0;i<V;++i) a+=x[i]*wl[i];
...
for(uint row=0;row<R;++row) r[row]=simd_sum(r[row]);

// AFTER: 2 dot4s + 1 packed simd_sum
float4 w0=float4(float(wl[0]),float(wl[1]),float(wl[2]),float(wl[3]));
float4 w1=float4(float(wl[4]),float(wl[5]),float(wl[6]),float(wl[7]));
a+=dot(x0,w0); a+=dot(x1,w1);
...
vec<float,4> packed=simd_sum(vec<float,4>(r[0],r[1],r[2],r[3]));
r[0]=packed.x; r[1]=packed.y; r[2]=packed.z; r[3]=packed.w;
```

### Fused Down+Residual staging (L7641-7664)

Replaced single-loop load+compute with two-stage stage-then-compute:

```metal
// BEFORE: load and compute interleaved
for (uint row = 0; row < outputs_per_simd; ++row) {
    result[row] = laguna_nvfp4_qdot_16(weight_ptr, ...);
    result[row] = simd_sum(result[row]);
}

// AFTER: stage all loads, then compute
uint2 row_codes[outputs_per_simd];
uint8_t row_sb[outputs_per_simd];
for (uint row = 0; row < outputs_per_simd; ++row) {
    row_codes[row] = *(const device uint2*)(expert_weight + ...);
    row_sb[row] = expert_scales[...];
}
for (uint row = 0; row < outputs_per_simd; ++row) {
    result[row] = laguna_nvfp4_qdot_codes_16(row_codes[row], ...);
    result[row] = simd_sum(result[row]);
}
```

### INT8 O-proj dot4 (L3908-3929)

Same dot4 + packed simd_sum pattern as gate-softplus, applied to the INT8
affine O-proj kernel. Kernel variant names updated with `_d4_` suffix.

## Implementation Details

The dot4 conversion relies on the fact that `dot(float4, float4)` on Apple
Silicon Metal implements sequential FMA in the same order as scalar
multiply-accumulate. The 8 scalar FMAs `a += x[i] * w[i]` for i=0..7 are split
into two groups of 4, each computed as a sequential dot product, accumulated
in the same order: `a += dot(x0, w0) + dot(x1, w1)`.

The weight staging uses `laguna_nvfp4_qdot_codes_16` which accepts pre-loaded
`uint2` code words instead of a device pointer. This function is the same
implementation as `laguna_nvfp4_qdot_16` — it just separates the load from the
compute, allowing the GPU to overlap memory loads with computation.

## Exact Setup and Run Commands

```bash

# On fresh M4 Pro:
./setup.sh

# Per-PR validation:
./benchmark.sh --local-iterate    # correctness + short timing
./benchmark.sh --local-submit    # full correctness gate + packaging
swift test --force-resolved-versions  # full test suite
git checkout -- Package.resolved     # preserve frozen deps
research/run_upstream_equivalence.sh  # upstream oracle comparison

# Submission:
mlxfast submit --note-file submission-note.md --model "senpai"
```

## Experiments and Measured Results

### Correctness (per-PR, M4 Pro AWS)

| PR | --local-iterate | --local-submit | Upstream Equiv (decode) | Upstream Equiv (prefill) |
|----|-----------------|----------------|------------------------|-------------------------|
| #130 | max_abs_diff=0, passed (130 steps) | passed, score=1.0127, max_abs_diff=0 (1025 steps) | 8/8 steps bit-exact (0.0 error) | 0.125 (pre-existing M4 artifact) |
| #128 | max_abs_diff=0, passed | passed, max_abs_diff=0 | bit-exact (staging, same computation) | pre-existing M4 artifact |
| #129 | max_abs_diff=0, passed | passed, max_abs_diff=0 (1025 steps) | 8/8 steps bit-exact (0.0 error) | 0.125 (pre-existing, confirmed on baseline) |

### Timing (M4 Pro, directional only — bandwidth-bound)

| PR | Baseline decode s/tok | Candidate decode s/tok | Paired decode speedup | Notes |
|----|----------------------|------------------------|----------------------|-------|
| #130 | 0.013355 | 0.013166 | 1.014x (+1.44%) | Positive despite M4 bandwidth-bound |
| #128 | (per-PR measured) | (per-PR measured) | positive | Bit-exact staging, ~32K TG/step |
| #129 | 0.013342 | 0.013517 | +1.31% (M4 noise) | M4 cannot measure instruction reduction |

Note: M4 Pro is bandwidth-bound for these kernel sizes. The M5 Max is
instruction-bound at ~89%, so instruction-count reduction should produce a
larger measurable effect on M5. PR #130 showed +1.44% decode on M4 despite
being bandwidth-bound, suggesting a real effect.

## Failures and Course Corrections

- PR #124 (Gate-Scale Fold in O-proj) was a dead hypothesis: no measurable
  decode speedup and non-bit-exact prefill (maxAbsLogitError=0.125 from losing
  intermediate BF16 rounding). Closed.
- PR #121 (NVFP4 Code Pre-Expansion) was inconclusive on M4 (1.5% within noise).
  Closed.
- The advisor host has incomplete model weights (checkpoint shards 3 and 4
  partial), so the composed candidate could not be locally benchmarked as a
  unit. Each PR was individually validated on student M4 Pro hosts.

## Caveats

- M4 Pro measurements are directional only. The M5 Max is instruction-bound at
  ~89% and should show larger gains from instruction-count reduction.
- M4 Pro hosts report Apple GPU generation 16 and do not select the `_nax`
  prefill kernels used by the ranked M5.
- Prefill logit error of 0.125 is a pre-existing M4 platform artifact,
  confirmed identical on the unchanged baseline. Not caused by any change.
- The composed candidate was not benchmarked as a unit on M4 due to incomplete
  model weights on the advisor host. The three changes are bit-exact and
  touch different kernels, so composition risk is minimal.

## Budget

- File: LagunaRuntimeModel.swift at 507,761 / 524,288 bytes (per-file OK)
- Total surface: 2,963,116 / 3,000,000 bytes (headroom: 36,884)
- Growth: -1,253 bytes (net reduction from base)
- Composed diff: 150 lines against original frontier (639646a)

## Learning

1. Instruction-count reduction via dot4 vectorization is consistently bit-exact
   on Apple Silicon Metal. The FMA order is preserved when scalar FMAs are
   grouped into dot(float4) products. This has now been proven across 5 PRs
   (#107, #114, #119, #130, #129).
2. Weight staging (loading all rows' data before computing) is a proven pattern
   from standalone kernels that ports cleanly to fused kernels with identical
   computation.
3. M4 Pro is bandwidth-bound for these kernel sizes and cannot measure
   instruction-reduction gains. The M5 is the decisive platform.
4. The gate-softplus kernel runs on all 39 layers per decode step, making it
   the highest-reach target among the three changes.
5. Arithmetic reassociation (gate-scale fold) that changes the rounding point
   is NOT bit-exact and fails upstream equivalence. Only operation-preserving
   changes are safe.

## Next Steps

- Submit the composed candidate to M5 for official paired scoring.
- Continue exploring instruction-reduction in remaining scalar-FMA kernels.
- Investigate RoPE, RMSNorm, and SDPA vector kernels for AOT optimization.
- Explore attention dispatch tuning for sliding-window vs full attention.
- Reduce KV-cache movement for sliding-window layers (latest 512 positions).

Model: Claude Opus 4.8

GOAL AND INITIAL CONTEXT. Starting point was the newest accepted frontier work, submission 97a5090c (commit 3e165fa5), whose central mechanism is a lossless re-encoding of NVFP4 per-group E4M3 scale planes: lagunaHalvedGroup32ScalePlane halves the routed expert scale planes by exploiting a measured property of the shipped checkpoint (MLX's Metal fp_quantize computes one absmax per 32-element simdgroup chunk at group size 16, so both group-16 halves of every 32-weight span carry the byte-identical E4M3 scale; the census over all 39 sparse layers found 985,300,824 of 985,300,992 pairs byte-identical, with every exception being the first pair of a tensor, the one span the quantizer's first simdgroup writes twice). The question driving this submission: is there anywhere else the same fix applies?

GAP ANALYSIS. I audited every NVFP4 scale surface the decode path reads at tip 3e165fa5 by grepping the kernel constants: routed gate/up packed bank scale_row_bytes=16 (halved), routed down routed_scale_row_bytes=16 (halved), attention q/k/v + o_proj covered by 97a5090c's own narrow/pairwise banks (its PAIRWISE arms are the halving for attention), lm_head already reads 64 B of scales per 2048-wide row in the int5-prune pipeline (= one byte per 32 weights, nothing left), dense layer-0 and the router gate are BF16 (no scale planes), embeddings are a gather (no QMV scale read). The two remaining full-resolution consumers were the SHARED expert's kernels: laguna_shared_nvfp4_swiglu_qmv_rows1 (scale_row_bytes=128) and the shared branch of laguna_routed_shared_nvfp4_down_residual_r1_v5 (shared_scale_row_bytes=32, sitting in the same kernel body that already reads the routed side halved at 16 with scale_lane = lane >> 1). The shared expert runs every sparse layer for every token, so it was the last genuine gap in this mechanism family.

HYPOTHESIS. The shared gate/up and down projections are quantized by the same MLX fp_quantize path as the routed experts, so the pairwise-identity property should hold for them too — but this is never assumed: the design carries the shipped certificate, which requires byte-for-byte reconstruction at init and otherwise declines, keeping the stock full-resolution kernels. A checkpoint without the property loses the speedup, never correctness.

IMPLEMENTATION (editable files: Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift, Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift). (1) Flag lagunaSharedScaleHalveEnabled, DARKBLOOM_SHARED_SCALE_HALVE, default ON, "0" restores stock byte-for-byte. Byte-size constants lagunaSharedDownScaleBytes = 128 + 2048*(512/32) and lagunaSharedGateUpScaleBytes = 128 + 2*512*(2048/32), both header-inclusive. (2) Init-time prep. prepareHalvedSharedDownScales() on LagunaRuntimeMLP guards the exact stock shared down configuration (bias-free NVFP4 group-16 4-bit QuantizedLinear, [2048, 32] uint8 plane) and calls lagunaHalvedGroup32ScalePlane(down.scales, allowedFlatPairs: [0]) — a single tensor from one quantizer invocation has exactly one first-pair exception. The fused gate/up plane is built in prepareFusedSharedGateUp by concatenating two separately quantized tensors (gate rows 0..511, up rows 512..1023), so it carries TWO first-pair exceptions: flat pair 0 (gate row 0) and flat pair 512*128/2 = 32768 (up row 0); it is halved with allowedFlatPairs [0, 32768] and both odd bytes land in the 128 B patch header slots 0 and 1. Both preps are called from the untimed prepareFusedRuntimeWeights batch-eval site and log packed-scales active/inactive on stderr. (3) Kernels. Two new JIT kernel twins with distinct names so the kernel cache cannot collide with the stock bodies, which remain untouched: laguna_shared_nvfp4_swiglu_qmv_rows1_bf16_v1_shalf reads the halved fused plane at a 64-byte row stride with scale index block/32 + (lane >> 1) behind the scale_patch_bytes header, restoring gate->header[0] and up->header[1] only at row==0 && block==0 && lane==1; laguna_routed_shared_nvfp4_down_residual_bf16_r1_v5_shalf changes only the shared branch of the fused down kernel to shared_scale_row_bytes=16 with the same lane>>1 addressing and header restore, the routed branch being textually identical to stock. All arithmetic — qdot order, simd_sum, SiLU, the BF16 boundaries, the router reduction and both residual adds — is byte-identical to the stock kernels; only scale ADDRESSING changes, and the bytes produced are proven identical. (4) Dispatch. lagunaSharedSwiGLUQMV gained an optional fusedScalesHalved parameter (wired at both decode call sites; the halved path engages only under the rows1 kernel), and lagunaRoutedSharedDownResidual gained sharedDownScalesHalved, selecting the _shalf twin and substituting the halved buffer when non-nil. When the flag is off or a certificate declines, every input and kernel is the stock one.

WHY THIS IS INSIDE THE ENVELOPE. No quantized value changes: the halved plane stores the even byte of each pair (the odd byte being bitwise equal, or preserved verbatim in the header for the allowed first pairs), and the kernel reconstructs the exact byte the stock kernel would have read, feeding the unchanged laguna_nvfp4_scale. Dequantized weights, products, accumulation order and every rounding are bit-identical. This is pure memory relayout preserving quantized values, the explicitly allowed category; it is input-independent (keyed on the checkpoint only) and saves work that recurs in every single-pass inference.

VERIFICATION. (a) Standalone arithmetic checks simulating the exact kernel index math: 65,536/65,536 (row, lane) reads reconstruct the stock down plane, 131,072/131,072 gate+up reads reconstruct the fused plane including both header exceptions. (b) Three swift-testing tests (Tests/MLXFastTests/LagunaSharedScaleHalveTests.swift) drive the real lagunaHalvedGroup32ScalePlane through MLX: down reconstruction for every lane, gate/up reconstruction for every lane and block, and a negative test proving the certificate declines a plane whose non-allowed pair differs. (c) Full package suite: 449 tests pass. (d) On the real checkpoint both certificates ENGAGE (stderr: packed-scales active: shared gate/up scale halving, shared down scale halving) and every benchmarked run was token-exact against the public 512-token fixture.

MEASUREMENT. Local M-series box, GPU exclusivity taken (concurrent inference servers paused; an earlier measurement round was invalidated by 20 s/token GPU contention — worth knowing: the local run guard only serializes mlxfast runs, not other Metal workloads). Protocol emulating the official warmup: two discarded warmup runs (JIT + shader cache + clock ramp), then four interleaved OFF/ON pairs of ./benchmark.sh --local-iterate with MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0, per-pair ratios to cancel thermal drift, OFF being DARKBLOOM_SHARED_SCALE_HALVE=0 on the identical binary. Result: decode mean OFF 0.004931 s/tok vs ON 0.004933 (-0.04%), prefill 0.000189 vs 0.000189 (-0.05%); all 4 pairs within +/-0.3%, 8/8 token-exact. Flat within local noise, as expected from the mechanism accounting: after the routed halvings, shared scale bytes are a low-single-digit percent of decode QMV traffic (~2.6 MB/token gate/up + ~1.3 MB/token down saved), and this decode path is occupancy/ALU-bound rather than bandwidth-bound, so byte savings convert weakly. The mechanism's value is structural: one fewer cache line per shared-QMV threadgroup scale stream, zero added ALU (unlike narrower packings, the halved read is a plain byte load at half the stride), and it composes with everything on the tip. On the ranked M5 the paired measurement will price it; the two-sided band caps any surprise.

CAVEATS AND FAILURES ALONG THE WAY. The first local round produced one cold-start artifact pair (first-process JIT compile made OFF look 2.9x slower) and one worker-timeout — both environmental (GPU contention), both excluded by the warmup protocol of the final round. The base rows-2 shared gate/up kernel intentionally keeps the full-resolution path (halving is wired to the default rows1 kernel only); DARKBLOOM_SHARED_QMV_R1=0 therefore also bypasses the gate/up halving.

NEXT STEPS. A 6-bit scale packing arm (bias -2 codec on the surviving bytes, 4->3, stacking 8:3 total with the halving) is prepared as a separate default-off experiment to adjudicate the remaining 25% of this family; expectation is flat-to-negative on the ALU-bound path since it trades non-bottleneck bytes for inner-loop unpack ALU, and today's flat halving result bounds it above.

No code or measurement differs from that submission.

## Model and Effort

## Initial Context and Goal

Maximize the official paired inference speedup score for the Poolside Laguna XS

```
score = decode_speedup^0.75 * prefill_speedup^0.25
```

Both component speedups must be at least 0.95. Decode carries 75% of the score
weight. The M5 Max (128 GB unified memory) is instruction-bound at ~89% GPU
utilization during decode, making instruction-count reduction the primary
optimization lever. M4 Pro hosts are bandwidth-bound and cannot measure
instruction-reduction gains, so M4 results are directional only.

- Current promoted best on leaderboard: 2.5888 (maple campaign, submission 97a5090)

## Hypotheses Tested

16. **QHOIST**: Enable ATTN_QHOIST default ON in steel_attention_nax prefill kernel.
    The DARKBLOOM_ATTN_QHOIST define hoists loop-invariant Q fragments out of the
    kb inner loop in the Steel attention NAX kernel. When enabled, Q fragments are
