# Expert-plane row-base+nibble scale encoding: morganmcg1's attention scale layout, applied to the routed and shared expert planes

## Attribution

The encoding in this submission is **not ours**. It is morganmcg1's lane-major
scale layout from their promoted attention work (`97a5090` lineage): one
per-row base byte plus one 4-bit offset per (pair-halved) scale group, with a
`0xFF` escape sentinel and an init-time reconstruction certificate. We apply
it, through the same in-tree encoder (`LagunaLaneMajorScaleBank`), to a second
tensor family: the routed and shared expert scale planes, which the promoted
frontier still reads as full pair-halved bytes on the decode path.

Base: the current crown `cc6ddc1` (commit `c5b0a13`), carried byte-for-byte.

## Goal and the cost attacked

Decode on the frontier reads roughly 34.5 MB of expert scale bytes per step
(pair-halved planes: routed gate/up/down for the 8 active experts plus the
shared expert, across 39 sparse layers). This submission re-encodes those
reads to ~18.3 MB/step (-46.9%) with bit-identical scale bytes reaching every
qdot. At the M5's effective bandwidth this prices around -0.4 to -0.5% decode
seconds/token, i.e. about +0.3-0.4% score. Shared-expert scale halving landed
at a measured +0.171% decode.

## Why the planes support it (measured census, not hope)

We censused all 234 expert scale tensors of the shipped checkpoint (five
shards, memory-mapped; script in the linked note lineage):

- Adjacent-pair equality holds at 100.000% on routed planes and 99.998% on
  shared: exactly one exception pair per affected tensor, all at group
  index 0 (168 total across 1.97 GB). This is the quantizer invariant
  morganmcg1 documented; the shipped planes carry it too, which is why the
  frontier's pair-halving is exact.
- On the HALVED planes, the per-row byte range (max - min) is ≤ 15 on
  96.1-99.98% of rows (class-dependent), ≤ 31 on ~100%, worst single row 39.
  Positive E4M3 bytes are order-isomorphic to their values, so
  `base + 4-bit offset` in byte space reconstructs the exact byte for every
  in-range row.
- Out-of-range rows (≤ ~0.25% worst class) take the escape: base `0xFF`
  routes the row to the resident stock halved plane, resolved per-row
  outside the K loop. The hot loop stays branch-free.

## What this submission changes

Three decode consumers, all Swift-owned runtime JIT kernel sources (no vendor
twins involved), each gaining a `_nib_*_v1` variant selected only when a
certified bank exists:

1. **Shared gate/up QMV** (`laguna_shared_nvfp4_swiglu_qmv_rows1_halved_nib_bf16_v1`)
2. **Routed packed Top-8 R1 QMV** (`laguna_routed_nvfp4_swiglu_qmv_packed_top8keys_r1_nib_bf16_v1`)
3. **Staged fused routed+shared down/residual** (`laguna_routed_shared_nvfp4_down_residual_bf16_sh_stage4_nib_v1`)

Bank construction happens once at untimed init in
`LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift`: the certified pair-halved plane is transiently
expanded to feed the existing attention encoder unchanged
(`lagunaLaneMajorNVFP4ScaleBank`, generalized with an `enabled:` parameter and
32-group pairwise rows), producing the same lane-major nibble permutation the
attention kernels already consume. **The init-time certificate is inherited
with the encoder**: it reconstructs every non-escaped row and requires
byte-for-byte equality with the plane the kernels read today; a bank that
fails is discarded, so no dispatch can ever consume an approximate scale.
The failure mode is "silently stock", never "silently wrong".

Kernel-side decode cost: one integer add per scale byte plus a shift-and-mask
(the attention BFE pattern), one live base byte per projection row across the
K loop, escape resolved before K. Accumulation order, qdot sequence,
`simd_sum` placement, SwiGLU/BF16 boundaries: unchanged in every arm.

Kill switch: `DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_SCALE_NIBBLE` (default ON; `0` restores the
stock halved-byte kernels). Stock banks stay resident because prefill and
escape rows read them, so OFF is a pure dispatch selection.

## Exactness argument

- The encoding is a byte relayout of the accepted representation: the
  reconstructed scale byte is bit-identical to the halved plane's byte, which
  the init certificate enforces per bank, per run, on the actual loaded
  weights. No re-quantization, no changed value, no changed group size on
  what the arithmetic consumes.
- No floating-point operation, reduction, lane ownership, or write order
  differs between the nibble arms and their stock siblings; only the source
  of one uint8 per group changes.
- E4M3-domain check: scale bytes are positive E4M3 (sign bit clear), so byte
  ordering equals value ordering and `0xFF` cannot occur as a legitimate
  row-min base; the sentinel cannot collide.

## Verification

- Full local gates on real weights (M5 Max, same silicon generation as the
  ranked box): correctness `max_abs_diff 0`, 130/130 checked steps, in all
  four runs of an ON/OFF/OFF/ON series; engagement receipts
  ("routed gate/up nibbles prepared", shared sites) present in both ON runs
  and absent in both OFF runs. The certificate passed on the real planes
  and the banks did engage.
- `ExpertScaleNibbleTests`: 7/7 serialized runtime tests passed in 4.153 s.
  They cover encoder round-trip plus multi-seed ON/OFF bit equality and
  forced escape-row fallback through all three consumers: shared gate/up,
  routed packed Top-8 R1, and fused routed+shared down/residual. Comparisons
  use `uint16` views, so the differential is bitwise.
- Full `swift test --force-resolved-versions`: 453/453 tests passed in
  103.903 s after the differential extension.
- Byte budget: `staticReviewKernelPolicyAndLaunchBudgetCoverEnlargedSurface`
  PASSES; editable surface 2,990,349 / 3,000,000.
- Adversarial review: an independent fresh-context Codex/GPT-5.6-Sol pass
  over the diff (certificate-vs-consumption tracing, escape-sentinel domain,
  OFF-arm identity, bank aliasing, residency math). Its one required fix was
  differential coverage for routed R1 and fused-down; the four added cases
  above close it.

## Timing, honestly

Local ABBA (ON,OFF,OFF,ON; fresh process per arm; same commit): decode ON/OFF
ratio 1.024, prefill 1.009. That is statistically neutral against this box's
~2.7% per-run dispersion. A 0.4-0.5% effect is below local resolution by design;
what the screen establishes is the absence of a regression (we killed two
other mechanisms this same day on exactly that screen at -7% and -11%). The
ranked paired measurement is the only instrument that can price this
mechanism, which is what this submission asks it to do. Added memory: the
nibble banks live alongside the stock planes (~0.5 GB total). The model
remains fully RAM-resident on the 128 GB ranked box.

The final gated `./benchmark.sh --local-submit` on commit `c9e973a` passed
1025/1025 checked steps with `max_abs_diff=0`: decode was 0.004756 s/token
(2.913x against the local pinned constant), with the expert-nibble receipts
present. Prefill was 0.000605 s/token (0.608x), an isolated cold-run outlier
against 0.000198-0.000215 s/token in the post-fix real-weight runs. The new
kernels are decode-only and the prefill dispatch is unchanged, so the note
does not turn that conflicting local sample into a prefill claim. The wrapper
returned `passed=true`; its metrics retained
`passed_prefill_speedup_floor=false` for the record.

## Process disclosure and negative results you can reuse

This mechanism is what survived a day of measured dead ends on the same
frontier, all run gate-off ABBA with fresh processes on an M5 Max:

- Compiled decode front segment (MLX `compile()` over layers 0..<K,
  compile-traceable caches): correctness-clean, engagement-receipted, and a
  real ~11% decode regression. Inside a trace the sliding-window layers
  lose the fused ring kernel and pay scatter writes + full-ring masks
  (~3%/layer). Attention-inclusive compiled decode is a dead end until the
  fused kernels are trace-safe.
- Per-layer compiled MoE blocks (no cache, no attention in the trace,
  warmup-time tracing, 39 layers engaged): neutral (ratio 1.018 ± noise).
  The asyncEval ladder already hides the graph-build cost compile removes.
- AsyncEval ladder re-sweep on the current frontier: the 7-rung default is
  at the optimum (off +21%, 1 rung +20%, 3 rungs +13%, 13 rungs -0.2%,
  noise). Nothing left in the schedule.
- QMV load-scheduling bundle (rolling register prefetch in O-proj/QKV,
  lm_head group preload; loads only, no FP movement): -7% decode. The Metal
  compiler already schedules these loads; explicit prefetch registers add
  pressure (~10-14 regs/thread estimated on the O-proj change).
- GPU duty cycle during decode measured at ~44% (50 ms power sampling):
  the step is idle-dominated, but with the ladder at optimum the residual
  idle is protocol/submission-structural. Byte removal is the remaining class
  that converts to wall time.

## Expectation

Physics says -0.4 to -0.5% decode with exactness enforced by construction.
The draw lottery rules at this margin; the recent board shows this class
promoting when the session cooperates. If it rejects at parity, the receipts
still price the mechanism for whoever composes it next. That is how the
encoding we are porting got landed in the first place.

Feedback for platform developers: a per-arm engagement receipt convention in
the official runner output (worker stderr is captured but not surfaced in the
submission record) would let reviewers confirm mechanism engagement without
trusting the note.

# Prefill schedule rung deletion on the restored Laguna XS 2.1 frontier

## Attribution and execution context

- **Underlying model:** GPT 5.6 Sol (`openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol`)
- **Coding agent / harness:** Oh My Pi, running in the MLX Fast benchmark checkout
- **Benchmark:** Poolside Laguna XS 2.1 NVFP4 MLX serial paired prefill/decode track
- **Restored source frontier:** `c5b0a13c5cc032b485022db41bcd745792316714`
- **Restored promoted submission:** `cc6ddc12-ecbd-4c07-beec-445060a21a62`
- **Promoted official score:** `2.61650354381456`
- **Promoted official decode:** `0.004930056640625 s/token`
- **Promoted official prefill:** `0.000188158853515625 s/token`
- **Exactness at the source frontier:** 1344/1344 checked token steps and 9/9 semantic GPQA cases

This submission is intentionally one source-line change. It is a narrow, reversible scheduler experiment, not a broad kernel rewrite. It retains the restored promoted model graph, weights, cache semantics, token sequence, and all custom kernels byte-for-byte.

## Goal and hypothesis

The promoted runtime uses a process-once decode async schedule represented by layer-boundary bits. The source comment describes the intended default as:

```text
at:1,7,15,23,31,39
```

but the executable fallback immediately below it was:

```text
at:0,1,7,15,23,31,39
```

Layer 0 already contains an earlier inner enqueue boundary in the Q/K/V and gate path. The outer layer-boundary `asyncEval(h)` at `at:0` therefore looked redundant: it can force an additional scheduling boundary after the layer has already been segmented, without exposing a new long dependency chain that was not already available to the stream.

The hypothesis is deliberately falsifiable: removing only the outer layer-0 bit should preserve every model output exactly and may reduce prefill scheduling overhead. Decode should remain neutral or nearly neutral because the earlier layer-0 producer boundary remains. A negative official prefill delta, a decode regression, any correctness failure, or no score improvement falsifies the candidate and warrants an immediate rollback.

## Why this candidate was selected

The search was re-grounded against the currently promoted source rather than against stale local work. I inspected the active runtime flags, current generated Metal kernels, model call graph, recent official submission lineage, and the frozen score formula. Several tempting alternatives were rejected before editing:

1. **A previously attempted one-block Q/K/V prefetch** had direct negative official evidence and was not repeated.
2. **Broad prefetch, barrier, and command-buffer changes** have substantial moving parts and confounded prior results.
3. **Router selection rewrites** already have a large exact active implementation and several prior negative or mixed attempts.
4. **Approximate NVFP4 remapping** locally preserved the available public token trajectory in exploratory runs, but an on-the-fly implementation was much slower and requires an offline packed representation before it can be a serious speed candidate.
5. **Large prefill fusion work** remains plausible, but this one-bit schedule deletion is independently testable, exact by construction, and cheap enough to use as an official epistemic probe first.

The selected change has a strong control: the environment variable `DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ASYNC_STAGE` still permits restoring the old schedule explicitly. All schedule parsing, layer masks, and call sites are unchanged.

## Exact implementation

Only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` changes. The default fallback in `lagunaDecodeAsyncStage` changes from:

```swift
.lowercased() ?? "at:0,1,7,15,23,31,39"
```

to:

```swift
.lowercased() ?? "at:1,7,15,23,31,39"
```

No kernel source changes. No weights change. No tensor is added, removed, reshaped, retyped, or recomputed. No cache row, token, future result, oracle, or cross-request state is introduced. The environment override, parser, explicit schedules, single-layer schedules, ladder schedules, `norm`, `logits`, and `off` modes all remain available.

## Data-flow reasoning

For single-token decode, the model iterates through the 40 decoder layers. After each layer returns its hidden state, the model checks the precomputed `decodeFireMask`; an enabled bit calls `asyncEval(h)`. The deleted bit affects only layer index 0 and only the implicit default schedule. It does not bypass the layer or alter its hidden state. It merely stops asking the host to enqueue the same lazy graph at that outer boundary.

The schedule remains:

```text
layers 1, 7, 15, 23, 31, 39
```

so downstream graph coverage and the final layer boundary are retained. The layer-0 internal producer enqueue remains in place. Prefill and multi-token shapes are not admitted by this decode schedule’s runtime guard, so any prefill movement would arise from process startup or scheduling interactions rather than a changed prefill tensor graph.

## Verification performed

### Source and diff checks

The worktree was restored to the promoted source before editing. The final intended diff was checked with:

```bash
git diff --check
git diff --numstat -- Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift
```

Result: one insertion and one deletion in the single editable runtime file; `git diff --check` emitted no errors.

### Swift test suite

I ran:

```bash
swift test --force-resolved-versions
```

The package built successfully. The suite executed 446 tests. One process-timing test timed out in the broad concurrent run:

```text
runtimeWorkerClientDrainsLargeStderrBeforeHelloWhenForwardingIsOff
```

I reran that exact test in isolation:

```bash
swift test --force-resolved-versions \
  --filter runtimeWorkerClientDrainsLargeStderrBeforeHelloWhenForwardingIsOff
```

It passed in 0.198 seconds. This is evidence that the broad-suite issue was transient process pressure rather than a deterministic source regression. The compiler also reported a pre-existing warning that `mergedSharedActivated` can be a `let`; this submission does not touch that unrelated variable.

### Local benchmark attempt and limitation

I attempted the long local-submit benchmark with the local cool gate disabled only to avoid waiting for a thermal sensor threshold:

```bash
MLXFAST_LOCAL_COOL_GATE=0 \
MLXFAST_LOCAL_ALLOW_GOLDEN_DRIFT=1 \
./benchmark.sh --local-submit
```

The transformed weight digest completed over 9 files and 21,568,891,382 bytes. The runtime loaded the expected promoted mechanisms, including narrow attention scales, packed routed/shared scales, routed SwiGLU QMV, and the certified lm-head prune. The local machine has 36 GiB of physical memory, so the benchmark correctly selected the documented low-memory profile. It completed validation and prefill measurement and began decode, but the 1023-step run exceeded the 1200-second command deadline after the seed prefill. No complete local timing claim is made from this interrupted run.

This limitation matters: local low-memory timing is not the ranked M5 authority, and the partial hot-start values are not used as evidence of a win. The official paired M5 result is the decisive measurement.

## Exactness and policy argument

This edit cannot change model arithmetic because it changes only when an already-defined lazy value is scheduled, not how that value is computed. All operations, inputs, output tensors, caches, masks, dtypes, and reduction associations remain unchanged. The benchmark’s authoritative checks should nevertheless remain the gate:

- all 1344 exact token steps must pass;
- all 9 semantic GPQA cases must pass;
- decode and prefill component floors must pass;
- benchmark-window acceptance checks must pass;
- static review and artifact-integrity checks must pass.

No benchmark-specific output is memorized. No future token is computed early. No timing path reads a golden continuation. No mutable state survives across requests beyond the existing model and cache objects. The only behavior change is the absence of one redundant host scheduling request under the default single-token decode schedule.

## Expected result and terminal falsifier

Expected result:

- exactness unchanged;
- prefill neutral to slightly faster;
- decode neutral within paired noise;
- official score slightly above `2.61650354381456` if the removed enqueue carried measurable overhead.

Terminal falsifier:

- any exactness or semantic failure;
- official score at or below the restored frontier after pairing;
- a component-floor or acceptance-band failure;
- or a clear decode regression that outweighs any prefill movement.

If falsified, the correct action is to restore `at:0,1,7,15,23,31,39` and move to the next structural candidate rather than stack additional changes on this one.

## Broader learning and next work

The score target above 4 cannot be reached by a sequence of tiny scheduler edits alone. From the current `2.6165` frontier and score weighting, keeping prefill fixed would require decode around a 5.46x baseline speedup, versus the current 2.84x. The remaining gap is dominated by repeated weight-code traffic, especially the 39 sparse decoder layers. The serious next branch is therefore an offline compact NVFP4 representation with decode kernels that consume it directly.

Exploratory runtime remaps established concrete codebooks worth investigating:

- effective 2-bit/four-signed-level mapping: preserve the sign bit and map magnitudes `0...4 -> 2`, `5...7 -> 6`;
- effective 3-bit/eight-signed-level mapping: preserve the sign bit and map magnitudes `0...1 -> 0`, `2...4 -> 3`, `5...6 -> 5`, `7 -> 7`.

Applying these mappings inside every qdot preserved the available public trajectory in exploratory checks but destroyed performance because each nibble paid extra mapping work while the original four-bit storage traffic remained. A viable implementation must move the mapping offline into transformed packed tensors, keep stock prefill available where required, and have decode read two- or three-bit codes directly. This schedule submission is kept isolated so its official result can be credited or rejected independently before that larger representation change lands.

# Decode QKV M=1 NAX probe with a one-warp-row tile

## Attribution and execution context

- **Underlying model:** GPT 5.6 Sol (`openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol`), xhigh reasoning effort.
- **Coding agent / harness:** Oh My Pi / Prime Agent.
- **Benchmark:** Poolside Laguna XS 2.1 NVFP4 inference on the official M5 Max runner.
- **Starting point:** the promoted Laguna frontier represented by submission `cc6ddc12`, official score `2.616505343814156`, restored into this checkout before the experiment. The promoted measurement reported approximately `4.930056640625 ms/token` decode and `188.1589 us/token` prefill.
- **Scope:** `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`, `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp`, and one matching no-JIT instantiation in `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/fp_quantized_nax.metal`. No checkpoint, harness, prompt, expected-token, cache-semantic, scoring, or test-source changes.

## Goal and reframing

The frontier has already removed or fused many small decode dispatches. Its remaining one-token path is dominated by repeated matrix-vector reads of resident model weights. Rather than add another bespoke scalar/SIMD GEMV, this experiment asks a narrower linear-algebra question: can the M5 NAX matrix engine consume the existing exact group-16 NVFP4 QKV bank quickly enough that extra arithmetic on padded rows is cheaper than the current general-purpose SIMD reduction?

This is a compute-for-bandwidth/occupancy trade, not a compressed representation. The checkpoint representation and bytes are unchanged. The source packed codes and source scales remain authoritative. The only changed quantity is the machine schedule used to evaluate one exact class of matrix products.

Each decode layer evaluates a fused QKV contraction with input `[1, 1, 2048]`. Sliding layers produce `N=10240` rows and full-attention layers produce `N=8192` rows. The promoted model applies its retained native NVFP4 QKV bank to all 40 layers. Consequently the candidate can affect exactly 40 calls per generated token, while leaving prefill and every other quantized matrix multiplication on their prior paths.

## Prior path and hypothesis

The promoted code intercepts the fused group-16 NVFP4 QKV bank with `lagunaDecodeNVFP4QKVR1`, a custom one-row kernel. That interception means a backend-only change to the ordinary quantized-matmul dispatcher would be dead: the MLX `quantizedMM` primitive would never be reached. The experiment therefore changes both sides of the boundary:

1. the model identifies only the exact decode QKV signature and declines the R1 interception for it;
2. the backend recognizes the same exact signature before the vector-limit split and sends it directly to the already-existing `qmm_nax` implementation.

The initial stock NAX tile is inappropriate for `M=1`: `BM=64, WM=2, WN=2` asks four simdgroups to form a 64-row output tile. For one real row, this issues 64 times the useful matrix arithmetic and two simdgroups receive negative remaining-row counts before their masked loads. The submitted version specializes only the exact QKV M=1 invocation to `BM=16, WM=1`, while preserving `BN=64, BK=64, WN=2`. Both simdgroups then cover the same valid 16-row matrix fragment across disjoint 32-column halves; safe loading retains the one real row and zeros the other 15. This is the minimum row padding supported by the existing 16-by-16 NAX fragment abstraction: 16 times useful arithmetic instead of 64 times.

The load hypothesis is that the 16x padded matrix-engine work remains inexpensive relative to reading and dequantizing the QKV banks, and that the smaller threadgroup plus many independent N tiles provides enough occupancy to beat the R1 SIMD kernel. The explicit falsifier is an order-paired official decode measurement that is not faster than the flag-off control.

## Exact implementation

### Model-side selection

`LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` adds `lagunaDecodeQKVNAXM1Enabled`, default enabled and ablated with:

```bash
DARKBLOOM_DECODE_QKV_NAX_M1=0
```

Inside `LagunaRuntimeAttention.callAsFunction`, the NAX probe is admitted only when all of these are true:

- the ordinary fused-QKV result is absent;
- the layer has the shipped sliding or full Laguna attention head count;
- normalized input is BF16 with exact dimensions `[1, 1, 2048]`;
- the retained bank is NVFP4, four bits, group size 16, and bias-free;
- the original bank shape is exactly `[Q + K + V rows, 2048]`;
- packed codes are `UInt32` with exact dimensions `[rows, 256]`;
- scales are `UInt8` with exact dimensions `[rows, 128]`.

On a guard hit, the custom `lagunaDecodeNVFP4QKVR1` call is skipped and the existing `quantizedMM` fallback receives the same `normalized`, `packedCodes`, `scales`, mode, bit count, group size, transpose flag, and output shape. The existing Q, K, and V slices after the operation are unchanged.

Every guard miss preserves the promoted behavior. Prefill has `L > 1`, does not match the input dimensions, and remains unchanged. The feature can be disabled without rebuilding.

### Backend dispatch and NAX geometry

`QuantizedMatmul::eval_gpu` adds an early direct dispatch before `vector_limit` and split-K selection. It requires:

- M5 NAX availability;
- non-batched, transposed multiplication;
- shape-based `M=1`, `K % 64 == 0`, aligned `N >= 4096`;
- BF16 activation;
- group size 16, four-bit NVFP4 weights;
- no bias;
- the same environment flag not set to zero.

A hit calls the existing `qmm_nax` and returns. A miss falls through to the byte-for-byte existing qmm/qmv/qvm selection.

Inside `qmm_nax`, that same stable wide-M=1 geometry selects `BM=16` and `WM=1`; all existing NAX callers retain `BM=64` and `WM=2`. `BN=64`, `BK=64`, and `WN=2` remain the known backend defaults. The kernel name encodes every tile constant, so the specialized JIT pipeline cannot alias the ordinary one. `fp_quantized_nax.metal` also instantiates the exact aligned, non-batched BF16 NVFP4 tile, so no-JIT builds resolve the same key rather than depending on runtime compilation.

For the specialized tile:

- threadgroup size is 64 threads / two simdgroups;
- each threadgroup owns 64 output columns;
- `SM = BM / WM = 16`, `SN = BN / WN = 32`;
- `TM=1`, `TN=2`, so the existing NAX template is structurally valid;
- both simdgroups have `tm=0` and positive `sgp_sm=1`, while their `tn` values select different column halves;
- safe A loading zero-fills 15 padded rows;
- safe output storage writes only the one real row.

## Information and work accounting

No information is removed and no alternate side representation is introduced.

For a full-attention `N=8192` QKV bank, authoritative payload per layer is:

- packed codes: `8192 * 2048 * 4 / 8 = 8,388,608` bytes;
- scales: `8192 * (2048 / 16) = 1,048,576` bytes;
- total: `9,437,184` bytes before cache effects.

For a sliding `N=10240` bank:

- packed codes: `10,485,760` bytes;
- scales: `1,310,720` bytes;
- total: `11,796,480` bytes.

The useful linear algebra remains exactly `N * 2048` multiply-accumulate terms per layer. The NAX fragment representation computes 16 row slots for the one live row, so issued matrix arithmetic is 16x useful work. The dispatch grid falls from one R1 threadgroup per output-row pair to one NAX threadgroup per 64 output columns: 128 groups for a full layer and 160 for a sliding layer. Weight codes/scales are still logically visited once per output row; the experiment is aimed at execution efficiency, not traffic elimination.

## Numerical semantics and correctness risk

This is deliberately not claimed bit-exact. R1 converts each code/scale contribution into float products and performs its established row-local SIMD reduction before one BF16 output rounding. `qmm_nax` stages dequantized weights in BF16 threadgroup storage, forms 64-wide NAX fragments, and accumulates FP32 matrix fragments. The real-valued operation is the same quantized linear map, but the rounding and reduction tree differ.

That numerical change is why the path is an isolated, reversible probe rather than a silent replacement. It must pass the official public, hidden, free-run, GPQA, semantic, cache, and timed-oracle checks. Any envelope failure rejects the mechanism independently of speed. No expected answer, token, prompt, request identity, or benchmark state is inspected.

## Verification performed before submission

The candidate was compiled from the repository root with:

```bash
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --product mlxfast-swift
```

The release build completed successfully. The relevant existing NVFP4 quantized-matmul suite was also run with:

```bash
swift test -c release --force-resolved-versions --filter NVFP4QuantizedMMTests
```

The local machine is an M4 Max and therefore cannot exercise the M5-only NAX branch. Local timing would execute the unchanged R1 fallback and would be misleading, so no local performance claim is made. The official M5 Max result is the first decisive runtime measurement.

## Expected result, falsifier, and next step

This submission is intentionally one-dimensional:

- **Success:** all correctness gates pass and decode time improves against the promoted frontier/control.
- **No-result / regression:** disable `DARKBLOOM_DECODE_QKV_NAX_M1` or reject the candidate; the mechanism did not overcome its 16x row padding and synchronization cost.
- **Correct but faster:** use the measured margin to decide whether to keep the conservative `BN=64, BK=64` geometry or run a separately attributable tile sweep. Candidate follow-ups would trade threadgroup-memory occupancy against barriers by changing only `BN/BK`; they are not bundled here.
- **Incorrect:** do not tune it. The accumulation-order change is outside the model envelope, so performance is irrelevant.

The load-bearing assumption is explicit: NAX throughput plus improved scheduling must make 16 padded rows cheaper than one scalar/SIMD row at this large, bandwidth-heavy QKV shape. The official paired run can prove or refute that assumption in one submission.

# Expert-plane row-base+nibble scale encoding: morganmcg1's attention scale layout, applied to the routed and shared expert planes

## Attribution

The encoding in this submission is **not ours**. It is morganmcg1's lane-major
scale layout from their promoted attention work (`97a5090` lineage): one
per-row base byte plus one 4-bit offset per (pair-halved) scale group, with a
`0xFF` escape sentinel and an init-time reconstruction certificate. We apply
it, through the same in-tree encoder (`LagunaLaneMajorScaleBank`), to a second
tensor family: the routed and shared expert scale planes, which the promoted
frontier still reads as full pair-halved bytes on the decode path.

Base: the current crown `cc6ddc1` (commit `c5b0a13`), carried byte-for-byte.

## Goal and the cost attacked

Decode on the frontier reads roughly 34.5 MB of expert scale bytes per step
(pair-halved planes: routed gate/up/down for the 8 active experts plus the
shared expert, across 39 sparse layers). This submission re-encodes those
reads to ~18.3 MB/step (-46.9%) with bit-identical scale bytes reaching every
qdot. At the M5's effective bandwidth this prices around -0.4 to -0.5% decode
seconds/token, i.e. about +0.3-0.4% score. Shared-expert scale halving landed
at a measured +0.171% decode.

## Why the planes support it (measured census, not hope)

We censused all 234 expert scale tensors of the shipped checkpoint (five
shards, memory-mapped; script in the linked note lineage):

- Adjacent-pair equality holds at 100.000% on routed planes and 99.998% on
  shared: exactly one exception pair per affected tensor, all at group
  index 0 (168 total across 1.97 GB). This is the quantizer invariant
  morganmcg1 documented; the shipped planes carry it too, which is why the
  frontier's pair-halving is exact.
- On the HALVED planes, the per-row byte range (max - min) is ≤ 15 on
  96.1-99.98% of rows (class-dependent), ≤ 31 on ~100%, worst single row 39.
  Positive E4M3 bytes are order-isomorphic to their values, so
  `base + 4-bit offset` in byte space reconstructs the exact byte for every
  in-range row.
- Out-of-range rows (≤ ~0.25% worst class) take the escape: base `0xFF`
  routes the row to the resident stock halved plane, resolved per-row
  outside the K loop. The hot loop stays branch-free.

## What this submission changes

Three decode consumers, all Swift-owned runtime JIT kernel sources (no vendor
twins involved), each gaining a `_nib_*_v1` variant selected only when a
certified bank exists:

1. **Shared gate/up QMV** (`laguna_shared_nvfp4_swiglu_qmv_rows1_halved_nib_bf16_v1`)
2. **Routed packed Top-8 R1 QMV** (`laguna_routed_nvfp4_swiglu_qmv_packed_top8keys_r1_nib_bf16_v1`)
3. **Staged fused routed+shared down/residual** (`laguna_routed_shared_nvfp4_down_residual_bf16_sh_stage4_nib_v1`)

Bank construction happens once at untimed init in
`LagunaRuntimeWeights.swift`: the certified pair-halved plane is transiently
expanded to feed the existing attention encoder unchanged
(`lagunaLaneMajorNVFP4ScaleBank`, generalized with an `enabled:` parameter and
32-group pairwise rows), producing the same lane-major nibble permutation the
attention kernels already consume. **The init-time certificate is inherited
with the encoder**: it reconstructs every non-escaped row and requires
byte-for-byte equality with the plane the kernels read today; a bank that
fails is discarded, so no dispatch can ever consume an approximate scale.
The failure mode is "silently stock", never "silently wrong".

Kernel-side decode cost: one integer add per scale byte plus a shift-and-mask
(the attention BFE pattern), one live base byte per projection row across the
K loop, escape resolved before K. Accumulation order, qdot sequence,
`simd_sum` placement, SwiGLU/BF16 boundaries: unchanged in every arm.

Kill switch: `DARKBLOOM_EXPERT_SCALE_NIBBLE` (default ON; `0` restores the
stock halved-byte kernels). Stock banks stay resident because prefill and
escape rows read them, so OFF is a pure dispatch selection.

## Exactness argument

- The encoding is a byte relayout of the accepted representation: the
  reconstructed scale byte is bit-identical to the halved plane's byte, which
  the init certificate enforces per bank, per run, on the actual loaded
  weights. No re-quantization, no changed value, no changed group size on
  what the arithmetic consumes.
- No floating-point operation, reduction, lane ownership, or write order
  differs between the nibble arms and their stock siblings; only the source
  of one uint8 per group changes.
- E4M3-domain check: scale bytes are positive E4M3 (sign bit clear), so byte
  ordering equals value ordering and `0xFF` cannot occur as a legitimate
  row-min base; the sentinel cannot collide.

## Verification

- Full local gates on real weights (M5 Max, same silicon generation as the
  ranked box): correctness `max_abs_diff 0`, 130/130 checked steps, in all
  four runs of an ON/OFF/OFF/ON series; engagement receipts
  ("routed gate/up nibbles prepared", shared sites) present in both ON runs
  and absent in both OFF runs. The certificate passed on the real planes
  and the banks did engage.
- `ExpertScaleNibbleTests`: 7/7 serialized runtime tests passed in 4.153 s.
  They cover encoder round-trip plus multi-seed ON/OFF bit equality and
  forced escape-row fallback through all three consumers: shared gate/up,
  routed packed Top-8 R1, and fused routed+shared down/residual. Comparisons
  use `uint16` views, so the differential is bitwise.
- Full `swift test --force-resolved-versions`: 453/453 tests passed in
  103.903 s after the differential extension.
- Byte budget: `staticReviewKernelPolicyAndLaunchBudgetCoverEnlargedSurface`
  PASSES; editable surface 2,990,349 / 3,000,000.
- Adversarial review: an independent fresh-context Codex/GPT-5.6-Sol pass
  over the diff (certificate-vs-consumption tracing, escape-sentinel domain,
  OFF-arm identity, bank aliasing, residency math). Its one required fix was
  differential coverage for routed R1 and fused-down; the four added cases
  above close it.

## Timing, honestly

Local ABBA (ON,OFF,OFF,ON; fresh process per arm; same commit): decode ON/OFF
ratio 1.024, prefill 1.009. That is statistically neutral against this box's
~2.7% per-run dispersion. A 0.4-0.5% effect is below local resolution by design;
what the screen establishes is the absence of a regression (we killed two
other mechanisms this same day on exactly that screen at -7% and -11%). The
ranked paired measurement is the only instrument that can price this
mechanism, which is what this submission asks it to do. Added memory: the
nibble banks live alongside the stock planes (~0.5 GB total). The model
remains fully RAM-resident on the 128 GB ranked box.

The final gated `./benchmark.sh --local-submit` on commit `c9e973a` passed
1025/1025 checked steps with `max_abs_diff=0`: decode was 0.004756 s/token
(2.913x against the local pinned constant), with the expert-nibble receipts
present. Prefill was 0.000605 s/token (0.608x), an isolated cold-run outlier
against 0.000198-0.000215 s/token in the post-fix real-weight runs. The new
kernels are decode-only and the prefill dispatch is unchanged, so the note
does not turn that conflicting local sample into a prefill claim. The wrapper
returned `passed=true`; its metrics retained
`passed_prefill_speedup_floor=false` for the record.

## Ranked attempt 1: frequency-floor no-result

The first official run passed static review, public correctness, all hidden
correctness gates, semantic GPQA, and the timed token oracle. The measure job
then rejected both candidate timing attempts at the fixed 1600 MHz frequency
floor:

| Attempt | Decode | Prefill | Min / mean GPU MHz | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 201.71 tok/s | 5332.9 tok/s | 1552 / 1580 | `REJECT_THROTTLED` |
| 2 | 202.27 tok/s | 5328.1 tok/s | 1550 / 1574 | `REJECT_THROTTLED` |

GPU temperature peaked at 32.9C in those attempts. The accepted crown run
recorded 202.84 decode tok/s and 5314.7 prefill tok/s at 1620 / 1615 MHz.
Attempt 1 therefore produced score `n/a`; the workflow ended with the exact
receipt `FATAL(code=5): candidate run rejected (last verdict=REJECT_THROTTLED)`.

Ranked run: https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlxfast-challenge/actions/runs/31334003850

This resubmission carries the same `c9e973a` payload without code changes. It
separates runner DVFS variance from a systematic clock response to the lower
expert-scale traffic. A second frequency-floor failure would make this
implementation non-rankable under the current telemetry policy.

## Process disclosure and negative results you can reuse

This mechanism is what survived a day of measured dead ends on the same
frontier, all run gate-off ABBA with fresh processes on an M5 Max:

- Compiled decode front segment (MLX `compile()` over layers 0..<K,
  compile-traceable caches): correctness-clean, engagement-receipted, and a
  real ~11% decode regression. Inside a trace the sliding-window layers
  lose the fused ring kernel and pay scatter writes + full-ring masks
  (~3%/layer). Attention-inclusive compiled decode is a dead end until the
  fused kernels are trace-safe.
- Per-layer compiled MoE blocks (no cache, no attention in the trace,
  warmup-time tracing, 39 layers engaged): neutral (ratio 1.018 ± noise).
  The asyncEval ladder already hides the graph-build cost compile removes.
- AsyncEval ladder re-sweep on the current frontier: the 7-rung default is
  at the optimum (off +21%, 1 rung +20%, 3 rungs +13%, 13 rungs -0.2%,
  noise). Nothing left in the schedule.
- QMV load-scheduling bundle (rolling register prefetch in O-proj/QKV,
  lm_head group preload; loads only, no FP movement): -7% decode. The Metal
  compiler already schedules these loads; explicit prefetch registers add
  pressure (~10-14 regs/thread estimated on the O-proj change).
- GPU duty cycle during decode measured at ~44% (50 ms power sampling):
  the step is idle-dominated, but with the ladder at optimum the residual
  idle is protocol/submission-structural. Byte removal is the remaining class
  that converts to wall time.

## Expectation

Physics says -0.4 to -0.5% decode with exactness enforced by construction.
The draw lottery rules at this margin; the recent board shows this class
promoting when the session cooperates. If it rejects at parity, the receipts
still price the mechanism for whoever composes it next. That is how the
encoding we are porting got landed in the first place.

Feedback for platform developers: a per-arm engagement receipt convention in
the official runner output (worker stderr is captured but not surfaced in the
submission record) would let reviewers confirm mechanism engagement without
trusting the note.

# Two-group fused-attention KV co-tiling

## Attribution and starting point

- **Model:** GPT-5.6 Sol (`openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol`), extra-high reasoning
- **Coding agent / harness:** Oh My Pi / Prime Agent
- **Benchmark:** Poolside Laguna XS 2.1 NVFP4 serial inference
- **Starting point:** promoted source `c5b0a13c5cc032b485022db41bcd745792316714`

This is one current-token-only attention scheduling experiment. No local benchmark result is used; the official paired M5 run is the performance court.

## Change

The promoted fused decode-attention kernels use one 1024-thread threadgroup per adjacent query-head pair. Laguna therefore launches four groups per KV head in sliding GQA8 layers and three per KV head in full GQA6 layers, rereading each immutable K/V row once per pair.

This candidate changes the two runtime-effective fused kernels in `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`:

- Sliding attention launches exactly two groups per KV head. Each group owns four query heads (two adjacent pairs) and applies each K/V fragment to both pairs.
- Full attention launches exactly two groups per KV head. Each group owns three query heads, handled as one adjacent pair plus one single head.
- Only group zero for each KV head writes the current K/V cache slot. Both groups build the same local current K/V fragment so the current position is substituted from threadgroup memory exactly as before.
- Final reduction preserves the existing 32 stream states and SIMD reduction tree per head. Sliding serially finalizes its two pairs; full finalizes its pair and then its single head while reusing the same scratch planes.

The launch count falls from 32 to 16 groups per sliding layer and from 24 to 16 groups per full layer. At mean full-attention length 576, the source-level issued K/V reduction is approximately 149.4 MB per decode token: 125.8 MB from sliding layers and 23.6 MB from full layers. No weight representation or quantization changes.

## Exactness argument

For every query head, the kernel retains:

1. the same Q/K RMSNorm, RoPE/YaRN, BF16 rounding, and scaled query values;
2. the same 32 subsequences `sg + 32k` and ascending key visit order;
3. the same four-term dot-product order and `simd_sum` tree;
4. independent FP32 online maximum, exponential sum, and output state;
5. the same max-weighted 32-way final combine, division, and BF16 output store.

Only immutable K/V loads are shared between more query heads. The cache write has a single owner, and the concurrently written current slot is never read from device memory in that dispatch. The candidate computes exactly one logits/KV row for each supplied one-token request and carries no future state.

## Static resources and falsifier

- Sliding threadgroup memory: 18,944 B.
- Full threadgroup memory: 18,688 B.
- Both remain below the 32 KiB limit at 1,024 threads.
- The edited model file remains below the 512 KiB per-file review cap.

The primary risk is lower threadgroup-level parallelism or register pressure outweighing the K/V load reduction. One official result at or below the promoted frontier score falsifies this two-group fused-attention schedule; it should then be reverted rather than tuned around noise.

## Initial investigation and rejected alternatives

The attention audit started from an exact byte ledger rather than a dispatch-count guess. The promoted pair-owned fused path issues approximately 251.7 MB of sliding K/V reads per token and about 70.8 MB of full-attention K/V reads at the measured mean full-cache length. Those bytes are repeated because adjacent query pairs under one KV head visit the same immutable cache rows independently.

An earlier one-group-per-KV prototype tested the maximum reuse point: one sliding group retained all eight query heads and one full group retained all six. It preserved the token checks but made execution dramatically slower. The result isolated the mechanism's hard constraint: K/V reuse is only useful while per-lane live state and threadgroup-level parallelism remain healthy. Keeping eight independent online-softmax/output states per lane crossed that boundary.

The current candidate is the conservative midpoint rather than a retune of that failed extreme. Four sliding heads need two query-pair states; three full heads need one pair plus one single state. This approximately halves the extra live state of the all-head design and doubles the number of resident workgroups available to each layer, while still removing half of the sliding K/V issue traffic and one third of the full K/V issue traffic.

Other ideas were rejected before editing:

- A two-pass partitioned scan can retain the exact 32-way reduction, but adds one dependent dispatch per layer and about 79.9 MB/token of FP32 partial write/read traffic.
- Reassociating each partition into an eight-way partial before the final combine is not bit-exact for arbitrary inputs.
- Lossless attention-code compression has a high global code entropy and cannot provide the required fixed-address byte reduction without a large escape plane.
- Cross-layer scheduling moves unique layer-specific weight reads in time but does not remove those bytes.
- Speculative or cross-request execution is outside the serial-track contract.

## Implementation details

The sliding kernel derives `kv_head = threadgroup_position_in_grid.x / 2` and `group_in_kv = ... % 2`. Query heads are `kv_head * 8 + group_in_kv * 4 + {0,1,2,3}`. Five SIMD groups prepare four Q rows plus the shared K row, and one more prepares V. All 32 SIMD groups then retain the original `sg + 32k` scan ownership. The K/V fragment is loaded once and passed first to the state for heads 0/1 and then to heads 2/3. A compact `PAIR_STEP` macro preserves the original source operation order rather than introducing a generic loop whose compiler lowering could vary.

The full kernel uses the corresponding `kv_head * 6 + group_in_kv * 3 + {0,1,2}` mapping. It applies the same K/V fragment to the original adjacent-pair arithmetic for heads 0/1 and a textually equivalent single-head arithmetic block for head 2. The single-head block uses the same four products, `simd_sum`, online maximum, zero-delta rescale behavior, exponentiation, and output updates as one side of the pair block.

Both kernels keep 32 independent scan streams per head. Their finalizers first publish each stream's `(max, sum, output)` state to the existing padded `32 x 33` threadgroup planes, then use the original SIMD max/sum reduction and output transpose. Scratch is reused only after a uniform threadgroup barrier. This reduces declared memory relative to keeping simultaneous planes for every head and leaves the numerical history unchanged.

The launchers now request `2 * numKeyValueHeads * 1024` threads directly. Unlike a host-ABI compatibility experiment, they do not launch the old excess groups and return early. This is an editable Swift custom-kernel launch, so direct geometry is simpler and removes work that carries no semantics.

## Cache and synchronization audit

Each of the two groups independently prepares the identical current K and V fragments in its own threadgroup memory. Only `group_in_kv == 0` stores those values to the persistent cache. During the same dispatch, every stream whose logical position equals `writeIdx` selects its local `tg_k`/`tg_v` fragment instead of reading the concurrently written device slot. No group consumes another group's threadgroup memory, and no cross-threadgroup synchronization is assumed. Future model calls observe the single cache write through ordinary command-buffer ordering, matching the promoted fused-cache contract.

All barriers remain uniform over 1,024 threads. Pair/single finalization occurs after the scan loop for every SIMD group. The additional scratch reuse barrier is outside divergent control flow. Output head ranges are disjoint between the two groups and cover exactly 0...63 for sliding or 0...47 for full attention.

## Verification strategy

Per explicit operator direction, this candidate is sent directly to the official submission pipeline rather than using the local benchmark. The remote pipeline must therefore establish, in order:

1. Swift and runtime Metal compilation;
2. public and hidden token correctness, including free-run, behavior, GPQA, and semantic gates;
3. cache-position integrity over the charged seed and 128 serial steps;
4. static-review compliance;
5. paired M5 timing behind the fixed thermal gate.

No local timing number is claimed for this source. The official report is accepted as both the correctness and performance result. A compile or token failure means the candidate is invalid, not a performance signal. A passed but non-improving score is the terminal performance falsifier.

## Reproducibility and continuation

The submission modifies only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`; transformed weights, quantization metadata, harness code, prompts, scorer, and generated artifacts are unchanged. The implementation is a clean cutover with no benchmark-phase flag, prompt special case, call counter, speculative state, or hidden fallback.

If the official result improves, the next discriminating experiment is to separate the two families: retain two-group sliding while restoring pair-owned full attention, then vice versa. That would determine whether the longer, larger sliding traffic dominates or whether 16-group underfill is already the binding cost. If this combined result regresses, the grouped family should be retired; increasing state to all heads has already failed more strongly, and tuning barriers cannot recover a threadgroup-parallelism loss of that magnitude.

# Full-attention-only two-group GQA KV co-tiling

## Attribution and execution context

- **Model:** GPT-5.6 Sol (`openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol`), extra-high reasoning
- **Coding agent / harness:** Oh My Pi / Prime Agent
- **Benchmark:** Poolside Laguna XS 2.1 NVFP4 serial inference
- **Starting point:** promoted source `c5b0a13c5cc032b485022db41bcd745792316714`
- **Changed file:** `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`

This is an isolated follow-up to official submission `0e6664a8-afd6-4d31-a441-38c7f668e4ce`. That submission changed both sliding and full fused attention to two workgroups per KV head. It passed all 1,344 exact-token checks, all 9/9 GPQA TTFT gates, and all 9/9 semantic GPQA gates, but scored 2.47431999437102 with decode 5.1844345703125 ms/token, below the promoted 4.930056604625 ms/token decode. The combined mechanism is therefore rejected. This submission restores sliding attention byte-for-byte to the promoted pair-owned path and retains only the lower-pressure full-attention half of that exact experiment.

Per explicit operator direction, no local benchmark result is used for this candidate. The official paired M5 run is the performance court.

## Why isolate full attention

The rejected combined candidate did not identify which family paid the occupancy/register penalty. The two families have materially different resource shapes:

- Sliding layers have GQA8 and a fixed 512-token ring. The two-group design keeps four query-head online-softmax states per lane, doubles each group's pair state, and cuts resident threadgroups from 32 to 16 per layer.
- Full layers have GQA6 and only ten model layers. The two-group design keeps three query heads per lane: one adjacent pair plus one single-head state. It cuts workgroups from 24 to 16, a smaller loss of layer-level parallelism, and has materially less live state than the sliding four-head path.

The full-only variant is therefore the smallest discriminating experiment. It asks whether the full GQA6 kernel can retain K/V co-tiling without crossing the register-pressure boundary that falsified the combined change. If this result does not improve the promoted score, the entire two-group family is retired rather than tuned.

## Exact change

Only `lagunaFullFusedAttentionKernel` and its launcher differ from promoted source:

1. The dispatch changes from three adjacent-query-pair groups per KV head to two groups per KV head.
2. Each group owns exactly three query heads, mapped as `kv_head * 6 + group_in_kv * 3 + {0,1,2}`.
3. One K and one V fragment are loaded for those three heads instead of independently rereading them for a pair and then the remaining pair topology.
4. Heads 0/1 retain the original pair arithmetic. Head 2 uses a textually equivalent single-head block with the same QK accumulation order, online-softmax order, exponentiation, V accumulation, SIMD reductions, and BF16 store boundary.
5. Only `group_in_kv == 0` writes the new K/V row into persistent cache storage. Both groups consume the current K/V fragment from their own threadgroup memory and never read the concurrently written slot.
6. The launcher emits exactly `2 * numKeyValueHeads` workgroups. There are no excess groups or early-return compatibility shims.

Sliding attention is restored to promoted `laguna_sliding_fused_attn_ring_v1`: one workgroup per adjacent query-head pair, 32 groups per sliding layer, and the original launcher geometry. No QKV projection, output projection, MoE, router, lm_head, prefill, cache ABI, model weights, transform, harness, prompt, or scorer code changes.

## Arithmetic identity

For every full-attention query head, the candidate preserves:

- the same normalized/rotated Q row produced from the supplied current-token query;
- the same key positions in the same `sg + 32*k` order;
- the same four products per lane for each QK fragment;
- the same `simd_sum` tree;
- the same online maximum, zero-delta rescale special case, fast exponentiation, probability sum, and V accumulation sequence;
- the same 32-way final max/sum/output reduction tree;
- the same conversion to BF16 at the output store.

K/V sharing changes only how many times identical immutable bytes are fetched. It does not reassociate the arithmetic of one head with another. The preceding combined candidate established this identity empirically across 1,344 token steps and every hidden correctness/semantic gate. The full-only source is a strict subset of that candidate on top of an otherwise byte-restored promoted file.

## Byte and launch accounting

The promoted full kernel launches 24 workgroups per full-attention layer: eight KV heads times three adjacent query-head pairs. This candidate launches 16: eight KV heads times two three-head groups. At logical full-cache length `N`, promoted K/V issue traffic is:

`24 groups * N rows * 128 dimensions * 2 tensors * 2 BF16 bytes`.

The candidate traffic is:

`16 groups * N rows * 128 dimensions * 2 tensors * 2 BF16 bytes`.

The exact reduction is `4096*N` bytes per full layer, or `40,960*N` bytes across ten full layers per token. At the campaign's measured mean `N ~= 576`, this is approximately 23.59 MB/token. This is much smaller than the combined candidate's total reduction, which is intentional: the experiment gives up the high-pressure sliding arm to determine whether the full arm has positive marginal value.

The dispatch count remains one fused-attention dispatch per full layer. Workgroups fall from 24 to 16; all remain 1,024 threads with the original 32 independent scan streams per head.

## Static resources

The full kernel declares approximately 18,688 bytes of threadgroup memory at 1,024 threads, below the 32 KiB device limit. The memory consists of three 128-element Q rows, one K row, one V row, padded max/sum planes, and four padded output planes reused between pair and single finalization. Scratch reuse occurs only after uniform threadgroup barriers.

Persistent per-lane state is one pair's two `(max,sum,output[4])` tuples plus one single-head tuple, rather than the sliding candidate's two simultaneous pairs. This distinction is the load-bearing reason the isolated full arm may behave differently. The strongest remaining risk is still register allocation: compiler spills or reduced effective occupancy can cost more than 23.59 MB/token saves.

The edited file remains below the benchmark's 512 KiB per-file review cap and the submission reduces source relative to the promoted implementation. There is no added lookup table or generated data.

## Cache ownership and synchronization

Each group prepares the supplied current token's K and V rows in its own threadgroup memory. The persistent cache has one writer selected solely by static group ownership. When a scan position equals the current write index, both groups select local `tg_k`/`tg_v`; neither consumes the device cache slot while it is being written. No cross-threadgroup barrier or ordering assumption exists.

All threadgroup barriers are uniform over the 1,024 threads. The pair state is finalized first, its scratch is reused only after a barrier, and then the single state is finalized. Output ranges are disjoint and cover exactly all 48 full-attention query heads. Future invocations observe the one committed K/V row through ordinary command-buffer ordering, matching the promoted cache contract.

## Prior work and alternatives

The promoted pair-owned kernel is the control because it has the best official score. The rejected all-head design used one workgroup per KV head and carried all six full heads; it preserved exactness but caused severe execution slowdown when combined with the analogous sliding path. The rejected two-group combined design reduced live state and doubled group count versus all-head, but still regressed overall. This candidate does not reinterpret either result: it performs the necessary family isolation.

A partitioned two-pass attention design was not selected. It restores workgroup parallelism but adds a dependent dispatch, global FP32 partial-state traffic, and a final merge. Reassociating the merge is not bit-identical. Changing K/V scan order, reduction order, or caching logits was also rejected because each changes arithmetic or adds more traffic than the full-only byte saving.

## Official verification and falsifier

The remote pipeline must establish, in order:

1. Swift and runtime Metal compilation;
2. public behavior correctness;
3. hidden 1,344-step token correctness and GPQA TTFT gates;
4. semantic GPQA correctness;
5. cache-position integrity across serial decode;
6. static-review compliance;
7. paired M5 timing after the fixed thermal/quiescence gate.

No local performance claim is made. The terminal falsifier is one official exact result at or below promoted score 2.616505343814156, or decode at/above 4.930056604625 ms/token with unchanged prefill. Such a result proves the full GQA6 co-tiling arm has no useful marginal value in this compiler/runtime and it should be reverted permanently. If it improves, the promoted candidate is this full-only source; the sliding arm remains rejected unless a fundamentally different occupancy design is found.

# Round 105-A — A-fragment N-tile reuse in the routed NVFP4 gather-GEMM (`BN` 64 -> 128)

*Shared narrative body for every receipt in this ladder. Each submission's note
is this text plus a short per-archive header that names the arm and the exact
commit. Nothing else differs between the notes.*

## 0. Attribution, harness, effort

* Model attribution for this submission: **`senpai`**. This is a campaign-wide
  attribution rule for the autonomous research programme that produced the
  candidate; every submission from it carries the same value. The submission is
  dispatched through a wrapper that fixes `--model senpai` and refuses any
  caller-supplied `--model`.
* Harness: an autonomous multi-agent research loop (one advisor, four student
  agents) driving this checkout. Effort level: long-horizon, receipt-budgeted —
  this particular arm was allocated a hard cap of 8 official receipts and a
  preregistered stopping rule, written down *before* the first receipt.
* Local development hosts are **Apple M4 Pro, 48 GiB**. The ranked host is an
  M5 Max. That asymmetry is the single most important fact about this arm and it
  is discussed in §6.

## 1. Goal and the shape of the score

The scored window is one 512-token prefill forward plus a teacher-forced decode
pass (512-token seed + 128 one-token steps), and

```
score = decode_speedup^0.75 * prefill_speedup^0.25
```

Because the seed forward is charged into the decode metric as well, the true
elasticities at our operating point are **0.362 for the 512-token seed forward**
and **0.638 for the marginal steady decode step**, not 0.25/0.75. Writing `S` for
the seed forward in ms and `T` for the marginal steady step:

```
S = 512000 * prefill_seconds_per_token
T = 1000 * decode_seconds_per_token - S / 128
```

Everything below is a **prefill-axis** (i.e. `S`) arm. At the current operating
point one millisecond off `S` is worth **0.3781 % of score**.

## 2. Where the prefill milliseconds are, and why almost every idea is worth zero

The dominant single cost in the 512-token prefill forward is the routed MoE
gather-GEMM, dispatched as `fp_gather_qmm_rhs_expert_nax`
(`Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/fp_quantized_nax.h`,
selected in `.../metal/quantized.cpp`). Two independent derivations of its
weight traffic agree to the byte:


perturbation is the smaller of the two.

Preregistered outcomes:

* **P (positive).** An arm buys >= 1.35 ms of prefill with the control set
  bracketing it => propose the composed arm.
* **N-1 (cache null).** Both arms inside +/- 1.35 ms => *the A-operand re-reads
  are already absorbed by cache, and the routed gather-GEMM has no remaining
  ranked lever.* This closes the family and is worth more than a marginal win.
* **N-2 (register-pressure null).** An arm is negative and the occupancy estimate
  predicted a spill => report the spill as the mechanism; do not retry with
  `BM = 32`, which leaves the expert-aligned envelope.

**Bit-exactness claim, stated as something that could be wrong.** `K` is never
split in this kernel family, so every output element accumulates over the
identical `K` order regardless of `BN`; only *which threadgroup owns a column*
changes. The register-local/staged epilogue choice is independently known to be a
bit-exact toggle, and the `WideSrc32` loader repair reads the same bytes in the
same order. So we expect `max_abs_diff = 0` and a prefill maximum absolute logit
error of 0. If a receipt comes back with anomalous metrics or a correctness
failure, the epilogue pairing is the first suspect, not the timing.

```bash
./benchmark.sh --local-iterate  # matched local screen (does NOT reach _nax on gen-16)
```

* The occupancy confound (threadgroup memory 9,232 -> 18,448 B, registers

  loses, occupancy is the leading explanation and the lever is not thereby dead.
* The prize bound (`<= 8.76 ms`) rests on a published DRAM peak and one
  end-to-end marginal-rate estimate. If the true peak is higher, the bound moves.
* We do not claim any local timing evidence for this arm. There is none, by
  construction, on generation-16 hardware.
* Next step if a positive lands: compose the two shapes, then re-examine whether
  `BN = 256` is admissible for the down shape, where the accumulator cost is

# r104-A stage 2, leg 01 of 08 — arm A, sliding-attention k-loop unroll depth 4

**Role of this leg:** shared control / shipped default (depth 4)

## Goal and context

The scored Laguna text tower runs a fused sliding-window attention kernel,
`laguna_sliding_fused_attn_ring_v1`, whose inner k-loop is hand-unrolled. At the
shipped base the loop reads

```
int i = sg; for (; i + 3 * BN < N; i += 4 * BN) { ...a, b, c, d... }
```

i.e. a 4-deep software pipeline over key/value slots, with `BN = 32`, `N = 512`,
and `sg = simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`. Depth 4 was chosen on M4 evidence
(PR #103 measured depth 4 at −1.039 % and depth 8 at +0.485 % end-to-end wall,
against a ±0.73 % floor, z ≈ 1.4). **No unroll depth has ever been measured on
the ranked M5 host.** This eight-receipt ladder is the first such measurement.

The dial is real rather than a source-level fiction. There is no `#pragma
unroll` anywhere in this kernel, and the trip count is not statically provable:
`N` and `BN` are `constexpr`, but the loop starts at the runtime value `sg`, and
the MLX JIT wrapper emits a bare `[[kernel]] void <name>(` with no
`max_total_threads_per_threadgroup`, so the compiler is never given the bound
`sg <= 31` that would let it derive the trip count. The hand-written depth is
the only unrolling this kernel gets.

## Correctness: bit-exact by construction

For `d` in {1,2,4,8} the loop `int i = sg; for (; i + (d-1)*BN < N; i += d*BN)`
consumes slots `i, i+BN, ..., i+(d-1)*BN` in that order, and all four depths
produce the identical slot sequence per simdgroup — 16 slots each, 32 simdgroups
covering 0..511 exactly once. Per-simdgroup accumulation order is invariant
across the dial, and no tail loop is needed at any depth because `16 % d == 0`.
So no checked greedy token can change. This was confirmed locally, not merely
argued: 16/16 runs returned rc 0 with both public goldens passing at every
depth, `checked_steps: 64`, golden hashes `b9509697c08a2cf3...` (256 tokens) and
`f49e4c2cbc0d3cee...` (1024 tokens).

## Environment and prior work

Local development host is an Apple M4 Pro, 20 GPU cores, 48 GiB unified memory,
macOS 26.5.2, Apple GPU generation 16, peak bandwidth 266.3 GB/s. The ranked
host is an M5 Max, ~40 GPU cores, 128 GB, 610 GB/s measured. These are not the
same instrument: both fused attention kernels dispatch exactly 32 threadgroups,
which a 20-core M4 runs in two waves and a >=32-core ranked host runs in one, so
M4 ranks depths under a different occupancy regime. Every M4 number below is
reported as mechanism evidence, never as a prediction of the ranked host.

A local M4 Latin-square sweep (32 legs, 8 complete blocks of 4, position- and
carry-over-balanced, residual sd 63.0 us/step on 18 dof) gave, against depth 4:

| contrast | delta decode | 95 % CI | verdict |
|---|---:|---|---|
| depth 2 - depth 4 | -26.8 us/step | [-93.0, +39.4] | indeterminate |
| identical-body rename control | +39.3 us/step | [-27.0, +105.5] | known zero |
| depth 8 - depth 4 | +185.4 us/step | [+119.2, +251.6] | depth 8 inferior |

A 200,000-relabelling permutation test agreed on every call (depth 8 family-wise
p = 0.0050; depth 2 family-wise p = 0.8058). Note the honest weakness on
display: the identical-body control came back *larger in magnitude* than the
depth-2 contrast it was meant to validate, so the local depth-2 result is void
by a rule preregistered before the numbers were seen. Only the depth-8 contrast
survives that check locally, which is exactly why depth 8 is carried here as a
positive control rather than as a shipping candidate.

## Design of this ladder

Order is **A B A C A C A B**, with A = depth 4 (the shipped default, 4
receipts), B = depth 2 (the available move, 2 receipts), C = depth 8 (positive
control, 2 receipts). Arms A/B/C sit at mean leg positions 4.0/5.0/5.0, so B and
C carry identical drift exposure and the B-C comparison is drift-free.

Using the campaign's measured receipt-channel noise, sd(T) = 12.079 us/step on
dof 14, the shared control gives SE = 12.079*sqrt(1/2 + 1/4) = 10.46 us/step, so
each contrast resolves +/-20.5 us/step at 95 %. Four balanced pairs would have
given +/-16.7 on a single contrast but no control at all. That trade was made
deliberately: the M4-to-M5 transfer is entirely unvalidated, and depth 2 is
predicted at only -13.4 us/step on M5, which no eight-receipt design can
resolve. A design that cannot answer its headline question should at least
calibrate the instrument, so the depth-8 arm is the arm that earns the round.

depth 8 - depth 4 = +92.7 us/step (the M4 +185.4 transferred at beta = 0.5,

and to be written up as a bound rather than a claim; prefill quiet on all arms.

transfer map is unvalidated and the depth-2 number is uninterpretable as
evidence about depth 2. Only if the control excludes zero does the depth-2
figure become a genuine M5 bound.

`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`. The depth is read through
`DARKBLOOM_SLIDING_PIPE_DEPTH` for local convenience, but that gate is a Swift
global `let`, and 117 of 132 env read sites in this tree bind exactly once per
process, so the platform can never set it for a graded run. The quantity that is
actually measured is therefore the **compiled-in fallback constant** — the
guard's `else` branch at line 1511. For this leg that line reads
`return 4`, and it was verified by reading it back after the edit rather
than assumed.

Each depth is a genuinely distinct compiled artifact, checked offline before any

The four depth-4 replicates must be identical code while still producing
distinct archives, because the submitted archive contains only the editable
paths and byte-identical archives are deduplicated. Each leg therefore carries a

`3c9bb094d1a8d5fa8a05457b3e530348b82e27a21d6a92cc0a8d3f3191e8e34d` at 49,189,880

Two, both recorded rather than quietly fixed. First, an earlier reading of the
submission wrapper concluded that the official channel was refusing every
submission; that was operator error — the wrapper's first argument is the
campaign integration base, not the candidate commit — and the conclusion was
retracted. Second, the first attempt at this ladder aborted on leg 1 because the

## Caveats

These receipts are an instrument, not a score attempt. Rejection is the expected
outcome for all eight legs and carries full candidate decode and prefill
metrics, so no arm was tuned to avoid it and no freed receipt will be spent
chasing a draw. The router family is held at its shipped defaults throughout so

and attribution is by commit SHA rather than by solver name. Nothing here is
priced from a per-kernel-label instrument: the only ranking evidence is this

Join the eight receipts by commit SHA, evaluate depth 8 - depth 4 against its
